## Block H — The Agent Gateway (agent-native reorientation, SH74)

- **SH134** — **`post.move`**, the seventh op. The vocabulary could create, update and delete an address but not *change* one, and the workaround an agent reaches for first — upsert at the new address — creates a second post and orphans the original with its id, its SH51 audit trail and its SH14 version history. `post.move` re-addresses in place ([ShPostUnifiedWriteService#move](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/migration/unified/ShPostUnifiedWriteService.java), [ShAgentBatchService#postMove](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/agent/ShAgentBatchService.java)) with a new `to` field on `ShAgentBatch.Op`. The design calls: (1) **both state rows move together** — moving only the draft would leave the live page at the old URL while every draft-preferred read reported the new one, so a published post's live URL changes *without a publish step* and the change set says `the live URL changes immediately` rather than letting the human find out (P7); (2) **source absent + destination present is a `noop`** — a move is the one op whose precondition its own success destroys, so without this rule no document containing one could be applied twice, and SH82's re-runnability would be a lie; (3) **never overwrites** an occupied address and **never crosses a site boundary** (separate folder trees, ACLs and tenants), both teaching errors naming the honest two-step; (4) the destination folder resolves its owning site via SH128's walk, so a move into a nested folder does not blank the post's site. Inbound `ShReference` rows are id-keyed and survive; URLs written into another post's body as prose do not, and SH100 is where that gets caught. Manifest flag `postMove`. 9 tests in [ShAgentMoveAndPruneTest](../shio-app/src/test/java/com/viglet/shio/api/agent/ShAgentMoveAndPruneTest.java). → IMPROVEMENTS §VIII.7.
- **SH136** — **byte stability is a build guard** ([ShByteStabilityLintTest](../shio-app/src/test/java/com/viglet/shio/api/agent/ShByteStabilityLintTest.java) + [ShStableMap](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/utils/ShStableMap.java)). SH130 caught `tools/list` serializing differently on every boot; this generalizes it, and **the generalization found four more live instabilities on the day it was written** — the same yield SH122 and SH128 produced, which is now three guards running.
  <br>**The reason this had to be a lint is the finding worth keeping.** `Map.copyOf`/`Map.of` iterate in an order derived from a salt `ImmutableCollections` initialises **once per JVM**, so the obvious assertion — build the payload twice, compare the bytes — *passes over broken code in every test process there will ever be*. It is the same shape of tautology SH130 deleted from the version check: an assertion that cannot fail at the moment it has a job to do. So the guard is textual, per §VIII.10, with a `byte-stable-exempt: <reason>` hatch (one site uses it: a keyed lookup that is never iterated).
  <br>**What it found.** Five `Map.copyOf` call sites, four of them defects, every one the identical shape: build a `TreeMap` or `LinkedHashMap` *deliberately, for determinism*, then discard that order in the return expression. Ranked by damage: **SH101's render digest** hashed landmarks in map-iteration order, so the same page hashed differently after a restart — and *only for a single-field post*, because the multi-field path re-sorts on merge, which is half-broken determinism and worse than none (the first counter-example reads as a real change). Then the **MCP error `data`** — the payload whose entire job is to teach — reordering `fix`/`allowed`/`didYouMean` per boot, and uncanonicalized at the writer besides. Then SH103's diagnostics counts and SH109's review summary, both of which feed SH116 ETags that would stop matching after a restart.
  <br>**Two fixes, not one.** `ShStableMap.copyOf` preserves whatever order the source had, and the digest now **sorts at the hash site** rather than trusting its caller — because a hash is the one place "the caller sorts it" is not good enough: the failure is a wrong answer, not an exception. That second fix is what makes the per-payload assertion *deterministic*: hand `digestOf` the same landmark counts in deliberately reversed order and require the same digest. **Verified by breaking it** — reverting the sort makes that test fail (`d:635ab9de…` vs `d:99b6b8ef…`), which is the check every guard in this block should have to pass before it is trusted. 4 tests. → IMPROVEMENTS §VIII.11.
- **SH137** — **`folder.move`**, the ninth op ([ShFolderWriteService#move](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/folder/ShFolderWriteService.java), [ShAgentBatchService#folderMove](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/agent/ShAgentBatchService.java)). SH134's defect one level up and strictly more destructive: without it, renaming a section meant `folder.upsert` at the new path plus `folder.delete` of the old, and that delete cascades over every post beneath it — where the post-level workaround orphaned one page, this one destroyed a subtree. SH134 is also what made the gap conspicuous, since an agent that has learned `post.move` will assume the folder verb exists. Takes `to` as the whole name chain (that is what addresses a folder, SH79); the last segment is the new name, so rename and relocate are one op. Manifest flag `folderMove`.
  <br>**No post's URL changes, and that is why it needs no confirm token.** A friendly URL is unique per site and independent of the folder chain, so the pages inside a moved section keep the addresses they had — the opposite of a path-shaped CMS, worth stating because it is the assumption a caller brings. Nothing is destroyed and nothing goes dark, so the op is deliberately **not** in `DESTRUCTIVE_OPS`: it is the safe verb that exists to replace the destructive workaround, and making it demand SH108's two-step would push callers back to what they were doing. The folder's own `furl` *does* follow a rename, unlike a post's (SH139) — a post's is its address and its live URL, a folder's is neither, and deriving it from the name is what `create`, `update` and `folder.upsert` already do.
  <br>**It shipped as one writer both surfaces call, which is SH139's rule paying out — and that is how the live defect surfaced.** The console's own re-parent had no cycle check, and its move dialog navigates *down* from the site root, so a curator could reach a child of the folder they were dragging in three clicks. That does not fail: it succeeds and produces a cycle, detaching the subtree from the root (so every address walk stops finding it) and sending the recursive delete round the loop until the stack runs out — a tree unrepairable through the UI that broke it. Both guards (`ShFolderMoveException.Cycle`, `.Root`) live on the writer so they cannot be present on one path and missing on the other, and `checkMovable` exposes them without writing so a `dryRun` reports what the real run would refuse (SH82: a plan that lied is worthless). Cross-site and occupied-target refusals are shared with `post.move` and are now **kind-aware** — two folders answering one name chain is not the delivery ambiguity two posts on one URL is, and an error describing the wrong consequence teaches something false (P6).
  <br>Adding the op took `tools/list` 3 tokens over its 2200 ceiling; `shio_write`'s description was **trimmed instead of the ceiling raised** (P3: lean the payload first), landing the list back under budget while covering one more verb. The MCP golden's diff is a single line — the op enum — because the goldens collapse free text to type tokens. 8 tests in [ShAgentMoveAndPruneTest](../shio-app/src/test/java/com/viglet/shio/api/agent/ShAgentMoveAndPruneTest.java) plus a console stage in [ShFolderAPITest](../shio-app/src/test/java/com/viglet/shio/api/folder/ShFolderAPITest.java). → IMPROVEMENTS §VIII.7.
- **SH138** — **a deletion plan is never silently shortened** ([ShAgentChangeSet](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/agent/dto/ShAgentChangeSet.java), [ShAgentBatchService](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/agent/ShAgentBatchService.java)). Filed as a truncation hazard; **the truncation was not the live defect, and looking for it found the real one.** Nothing on the plan path cut a row — but plan/apply compile a document into ops and then hand them to the *hand-written batch's* validator, so a prune that swept up 300 undeclared posts failed with `batch-too-large`: "split the work into batches of at most 200 ops". A caller cannot follow that. They never wrote the ops, and a converge cannot be hand-split — so a legitimate large prune, and any `shio push --content` over a tree of more than ~100 posts, had **no path forward at all**. A ceiling with no usable way past it is the same dead end as a silent cut, reached from the other side.
  <br>The fix is the roadmap's two sanctioned options, each where it belongs. **Exempt:** compiled ops get their own ceiling, `shio.agent.batch.max-document-ops` (2000, beside the unchanged `max-ops` of 200), because a document's op count is not a measure of what the caller asked for — a three-post document compiles to four hundred ops when the site holds four hundred undeclared posts. Which ceiling applies is a `Source` argument only `ShAgentDesiredStateService` may pass, deliberately **not** a field on `ShAgentBatch`: on the wire a caller could claim the document ceiling for a typed batch. **Refuse:** past it, a new `document-too-large` teaching 400 names how many of the ops are *deletions* (the number that explains the size) and points at narrowing `folders`, never at splitting batches.
  <br>**And the invariant is now structural rather than observed.** `ShAgentChangeSet`'s compact constructor rejects `results.size() != ops`, so the type cannot express a cut — a guard per §VIII.10 rather than a resolution to be careful, and the thing that will still hold when someone adds a `limit` parameter nobody has thought of yet. The reason a plan gets this treatment while every other unbounded section gets `truncated: true` is that the patterns are not interchangeable: a shortened sitemap reads as incomplete, and a shortened list of deletions reads as a complete review of what is about to be destroyed. The manifest deliberately does **not** publish either ceiling — the agent cannot know in advance how many undeclared posts a prune will find, so the number is only actionable after a refusal, and the refusal carries it (P3: a field paid every session to save one rejected call in a rare case is the wrong trade). 5 tests ([ShAgentDeletionPlanTest](../shio-app/src/test/java/com/viglet/shio/api/agent/ShAgentDeletionPlanTest.java)), including one asserting the unusable advice does not come back. → IMPROVEMENTS §VIII.7.
- **SH139** — **the console move no longer rewrites a post's URL** ([ShObjectWriteService](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/object/ShObjectWriteService.java)). `moveTo` re-slugged `furl` from the title on every move, so dragging a published page between folders silently changed its live URL and discarded any hand-set one — the exact question SH134 spent its design budget on for the agent path, wrong on the path a human triggers by accident. **The fix is a delegation, not a deleted line:** the post branch now calls `ShPostUnifiedWriteService#move`, the code SH134 already got right, so the two surfaces move a post the same way instead of forking on it — which is also what the console was missing (both state rows moving together, `modifiedDate`/`modifier` stamped, and the move landing in the SH51 audit, hence visible to the SH88 feed and the SH109 review queue). A URL is assigned **only when the object has none**, the one case where a move discards no decision; `reparent` stops re-slugging folders for the same reason (a copy still assigns its own). Keeping the URL makes a collision possible on the one move that crosses a site boundary, so that is refused with a teaching 409 (`ShMoveUrlConflictException`, mirroring the agent path's `MoveTargetOccupiedException`) rather than quietly uniquified — which would be the old behaviour in a narrower case. The dialog had no failure path at all, so an unhandled rejection left it open with no explanation; it now surfaces the problem `detail`. 3 stages in [ShFolderAPITest](../shio-app/src/test/java/com/viglet/shio/api/folder/ShFolderAPITest.java). → IMPROVEMENTS §VIII.7.
- **SH135** — **prune covers folders**, not only posts ([ShAgentDesiredStateService](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/agent/ShAgentDesiredStateService.java)). Without it a desired-state document stopped describing its own scope the moment a section moved: the posts went, the empty folder stayed, and the next plan reported `changed:0` over a site that no longer matched the document — which erodes convergence, the only property that justifies declarative apply at all. Scope is unchanged (the declared folders' subtrees; declaring none and asking to prune is still an error). The ordering question — *is a folder prunable while it still holds undeclared content?* — is answered structurally: posts are pruned first and folders **deepest-first**, so a `folder.delete` never relies on its own silent cascade, and a whole emptied subtree collapses in one apply. Three kinds of folder are protected: the declared ones, every ancestor of one, and any folder a declared *post* names as its home (placing a post somewhere is a declaration about that folder too). Manifest flag `folderPrune`. 6 tests. → IMPROVEMENTS §VIII.7.
- **SH128** — **build-time guard for the "site-less object" defect class** ([ShFolderSite](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/object/ShFolderSite.java) + [ShFolderSiteInvariantTest](../shio-app/src/test/java/com/viglet/shio/object/ShFolderSiteInvariantTest.java)). Only a site's **root** folder carries `shSite`, so resolving an arbitrary folder's owning site means walking to the root; reading `folder.getShSite()` compiles, reviews clean, and silently yields `null` for anything nested. Four copies of the walk existed and a fifth call site was missing it. The guard is a textual lint over `src/main` — any `getShSite()` on an identifier the same file declares as an `ShFolder` fails the build — because a behavioural test proves only the paths it happens to exercise, and the *next* write path is where the next instance lands. **Writing the lint immediately found four more live defects, all fixed here:** `ShAddressResolver#addressOf(ShFolder)` addressed nested folders as `folder:null/…` (an address that resolves to nothing); `ShCdaService#siteIdOf` saw `null` for every non-root folder and `allowsSite(null)` is `false` under an allow-list, so a **scoped CDA token could not list the children of, or resolve the path to, any folder below a site root**; `#buildPath` returned a null site on nested paths; and `ShPreviewTokenAPI`'s folder fallback read only the immediate folder, 404-ing a preview link for any post in a subfolder. Two call sites read the field deliberately (the exchange export records it root-only; the console XP endpoint touches it to force a LAZY proxy) and carry a `ShFolderSite-exempt` comment naming why — an exemption costs a line of prose in review, which is the right price. → IMPROVEMENTS §VIII.10.
- **SH130** — **MCP wire conformance** ([ShMcpWireConformanceTest](../shio-app/src/test/java/com/viglet/shio/api/agent/mcp/ShMcpWireConformanceTest.java) + goldens in `src/test/resources/mcp/golden/`). The behavioural tests would all still pass after renaming `inputSchema`, moving `isError` inside `content`, or answering `resources/read` with `content` instead of `contents` — and every MCP client would break. A hand-rolled protocol has no compiler checking it against the spec. The goldens are **shape transcripts**: every key and its nesting, with the literal value kept for the fields that are themselves contract (`jsonrpc`, `protocolVersion`, `type`, `mimeType`, `role`, error codes, the op `enum`, the method list, and the tool/prompt/resource **names**, which are the public API), while free text collapses to a type token so a copy edit is not a golden update. Regenerate with `-Dshio.mcp.golden.update=true`. The version claim is checked against the **observable obligations** of MCP `2025-06-18` — batching refused, structured capability objects, `serverInfo.title`, `content[]`+`isError` results, plural `contents`, templates on their own method — rather than compared with itself, which is what `assertThat(V).isEqualTo(V)` was doing. **Found a P5 break in the process:** `inputSchema()` is built from `Map.of`, whose iteration order follows the JVM hash seed, so `tools/list` serialized differently from one boot to the next — unstable bytes on the one payload re-sent every turn, defeating client and prompt-cache reuse. `ShMcpServer` now canonicalizes schema key order, and a test asserts byte stability. → IMPROVEMENTS §VIII.11.
- **SH131** — **the full-text bind contract moved inside the repository** ([ShPostUnifiedRepository](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/persistence/repository/post/ShPostUnifiedRepository.java)). `FULLTEXT_PREDICATE` needed its `:q` pre-lowercased and `%`-wrapped and said so only in a comment; SH83 read the comment, wrote the caller, and still got it wrong — and the symptom was an *empty result set*, which reads as "nothing matched" and therefore survives review and manual testing alike. The raw `@Query` methods are now suffixed `…Like` (the parameter name says what it wants) and every caller goes through `search*` default methods that normalize exactly once. A contract that can only be honoured by remembering, and whose breach looks like valid data, belongs inside the method rather than beside it. → IMPROVEMENTS §VIII.11.
- **SH132** — **the MCP tool list is a measured budget** ([ShMcpToolBudgetTest](../shio-app/src/test/java/com/viglet/shio/api/agent/mcp/ShMcpToolBudgetTest.java) + `src/test/resources/token-budgets.properties`). The 12-tool cap is a *proxy*; what costs money is the serialized size of `tools/list`, re-sent on every turn of every session before any work happens — eight tools with essay-length descriptions are worse than twelve terse ones and a count test cannot tell the difference (P3). Ceilings live in a properties file with a note on what each guards, so raising one is a reviewable diff with a reason attached rather than an edited magic number; **SH113 extends the same file** with the REST response budgets. Estimation is `ShTokenBudget`'s 4-chars-per-token heuristic, the same number the instance reports in `X-Shio-Est-Tokens`. Measured 2026.3: 1655 est. tokens over 8 tools (ceilings 1750 total / 400 per tool / 200 handshake). → IMPROVEMENTS §XIII.2.
- **SH129** — **`shio apply [file]`** ([cli/src/commands/apply.mjs](../cli/src/commands/apply.mjs)), with `--dry-run`, `--check` and `-` for stdin. Law P1's order is MCP → files/CLI → REST, and SH82's content verbs had landed at MCP and REST but not the CLI, so a JS developer with a content document had to `curl` it — which also meant losing the SH80 teaching errors to a wall of raw JSON. `--check` is a plan by definition (a drift guard that could write would not be a guard) and exits non-zero when anything would change, printing *what* drifted so CI is actionable — the same green light `shio push --check` gives for post-types (SH65), now over content. Stdin support is what lets a document be generated by the step before it. This is still a command over a JSON blob, which is a worse authoring surface than a directory; SH87's `shio push --content` is the ergonomic form and will run on this same plan/apply engine once SH86's projection lands, and the command's own header says so. 11 tests ([cli/test/apply.test.mjs](../cli/test/apply.test.mjs)). → IMPROVEMENTS §VIII.7.
- **SH84** — Every Block H surface refuses a second tenant, and a publish now reaches Turing's index on AFTER_COMMIT through the ecosystem's own SDK, off by default.

- **SH77** — **Context pack** (`GET /api/v2/agent/context`). The one call that replaces a session of exploration (design law P2): content **model** (post-types with fields, reusing the SH11 `ShCdaSchemaField` shape so an agent learns one field shape across the product), **sitemap** as a flat depth-first row list keyed by path, derived **conventions**, a **digest**, and a **budget** report. Composition, not a new contract (P10): the model comes from the existing `ShCdaMapper` and site visibility reuses the SH2 per-site token allow-list, so the pack can never show content the CDA would hide from the same credential. [ShAgentContextService](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/agent/ShAgentContextService.java) + [ShAgentContext](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/agent/dto/ShAgentContext.java) (one document type, nested records) + [ShAgentContextSection](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/agent/ShAgentContextSection.java) + [ShAgentProperties](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/agent/ShAgentProperties.java) (`shio.agent.context.*`: default/max budget, default depth, max nodes). Every parameter is optional — the single-site case is a bare GET. **Determinism is load-bearing, not cosmetic:** the `digest` (SHA-256 over the canonical terse body, `c:` + 12 hex) is what lets an agent skip re-reading, so every collection is explicitly sorted (types by name, sites by name, folders by position→name→id, posts by title→id) and the digest deliberately **excludes** the budget/measurement lines so it tracks content only and is identical for the JSON and terse renderings. Folder posts are deduped **draft-preferred**, matching the CDA's `/list`, so the two views of a folder never disagree. **Honest truncation:** only the sitemap is budget-gated (a partial model is not a smaller answer, it is a wrong one — an agent that sees 6 of 9 types invents the other three), cuts are reported with a resumable `from=` cursor, and `truncated` with a `null` cursor is the explicit "nothing fit, raise the budget" signal. Conventions are **derived from the instance** (managed/system type counts, unused types, the DRAFT-then-publish rule, path addressing, multi-site hint) — author-written conventions arrive with SH114. Two new grouped count queries on `ShPostUnifiedRepository` count `distinct p.id` (the unified model stores up to two rows per post) — see the SH22 note below. 21 tests ([ShAgentContextTest](../shio-app/src/test/java/com/viglet/shio/api/agent/ShAgentContextTest.java)). Concept: [specs/SH74-agent-native-cms.md](specs/SH74-agent-native-cms.md) §4.3.
- **SH78** — **Token-lean responses.** The mechanics behind law P3. [ShTokenBudget](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/agent/ShTokenBudget.java) (≈4-chars-per-token estimate, `tryAdd` refuses a chunk without charging it so output is always cut at a row boundary, `overBudget` reports a mandatory-section overrun instead of hiding it), [ShTerse](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/agent/ShTerse.java) (`format=terse` line grammar: one quoting rule — quote iff empty or containing a space/quote — with absent attributes and zero counts omitted entirely), [ShAgentContextTerse](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/agent/ShAgentContextTerse.java) (also the canonical digest input, so what is measured is exactly what is emitted), `include=` section projection with a teaching 400 on an unknown section, and [ShEstTokensHeaderFilter](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/agent/ShEstTokensHeaderFilter.java) stamping `X-Shio-Est-Tokens` on every `/api/v2/agent/*` response (measured on the serialized body, so it covers both encodings and cannot drift). **Three findings, each now a test:** (1) *the terse win is per-row, not per-payload* — JSON pays for braces and every key name on every row while terse states the shape once in the verb, so the saving scales with row count (~25–35% per row) and is diluted on a small pack by fixed prose; the assertion therefore measures the **marginal** cost of a row, which is what would catch a node row being "enriched" back into a blob. (2) The residual per-row cost is dominated by the **36-char UUID**, not by the encoding — which makes **SH79 path addressing the larger token lever**, now quantified rather than assumed (→ new SH121). (3) Agent JSON was itself paying for `"folders":0,"posts":0` and four explicit `null`s on every row; `@JsonInclude(NON_DEFAULT)` on the agent DTOs applies the same "don't pay for what you don't say" rule to JSON, so the comparison is against a lean alternative rather than a rigged one (→ new SH125 to make it policy). **Two bugs the tests caught in the implementation itself:** an unbounded budget short-circuited `tryAdd` *without charging*, so `estTokens`/`X-Shio-Est-Tokens` silently under-reported the entire sitemap on every `budget=0` call; and conventions were charged **after** the sitemap gate opened, letting the walk admit rows that the later charge pushed over the ceiling the caller had asked for. Both fixed with regression tests. A misleading `omittedNodes` count was **removed** rather than fixed — the walk stops at the budget so it cannot know how much remains, and the only number it had ("1 more") understated the truth; the scale of what is left is already derivable from the `folders`/`posts` counts on each emitted folder row. 9 tests ([ShTerseAndBudgetTest](../shio-app/src/test/java/com/viglet/shio/api/agent/ShTerseAndBudgetTest.java)) + the SH77 suite. **Scope note:** per-field `fields=` projection on *content* reads is **not** in this task — there are no content reads on the agent surface until SH79/SH83, so it is tracked as SH123. Concept: [specs/SH74-agent-native-cms.md](specs/SH74-agent-native-cms.md) §4.4.
- **SH79** — **Path addressing.** A content address — `post:<site>/<friendly-url>`, `folder:<site>/<name-chain>`, `site:<name>`, `id:<uuid>` — so a UUID stops being the agent's working currency (design law P5). [ShAddress](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/agent/ShAddress.java) (parse/normalize/canonical form) + [ShAddressResolver](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/agent/ShAddressResolver.java) + `GET /api/v2/agent/resolve?address=…` → [ShAgentResolved](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/agent/dto/ShAgentResolved.java), plus `shio resolve <address>` (`--id` for pipelines) and `site=` on the context pack now accepting a `site:` address. **The shape decision that kept this from being a token regression:** the obvious reading of "path addressing" is to emit an `address` on every context row — but a row already carries its site, path and url, so a built address duplicates derivable information and *adds* tokens to the very endpoint this task was supposed to make cheaper. Instead the grammar is stated **once**, as a convention line, and the resolver makes those addresses actionable; a test asserts no row carries an `address=` attribute. The token win itself lands in SH121, which removes the id. **Two namespaces are kept deliberately apart:** a folder path is a chain of folder *names*, while a post's `furl` is arbitrary and need not relate to its folder — so the scheme names which is meant, and the lenient `site:` form (post-first, then folder) raises a **400 naming both explicit addresses** when a path is occupied by both rather than silently picking one. That case is real and is in the fixture: a post whose `furl` is `/blog` alongside a `/blog` folder. Resolution reuses the CDA's own furl candidates (so an address and a delivery URL never disagree about the same post), is draft-preferred like `/list`, honors the SH2 allow-list, and reports a disallowed site as **absent rather than forbidden** — a scoped key must not be able to use a 403 to prove a site exists. `addressOf(…)` is the inverse, tested as a round trip because SH121 depends on it. Failures teach: a malformed address returns the schemes and a corrected example; an unresolved one lists the sibling paths with a nearest match (`/blg` → `/blog`). Known limit, documented: a site whose *name* contains `/` must be addressed by id. 22 new backend tests + 6 CLI; suites 360 and 39 green. → §VIII.5
- **SH122** — **Build-time guard for the `@TenantId` JOINED-join hazard — and three production bugs it uncovered.** [ShTenantJoinHazardTest](../shio-app/src/test/java/com/viglet/shio/tenant/ShTenantJoinHazardTest.java) characterizes the failure by *executing* each query form, and that mattered because reasoning got it wrong twice. The first hypothesis was "only projections and `GROUP BY` are affected", since shipped queries navigated `p.shPostType.name` in a `WHERE` clause with green tests. Executing the predicate form showed it fails identically — the generated SQL explains why: Hibernate joins **only the subclass table** (`join "ShPostType" spt1_0 on …`) and still emits `and spt1_1.tenant_id = ?` against a root alias it never declared. An explicit `join` does not rescue it either. So the rule is the widest one: **never navigate past `.id`** of an `ShObject`-subclass association, in any clause. **The green tests were green because they never reached the finder** — which means three shipped paths were broken in production and nothing said so: `GET /api/v2/cda/query?siteId=&postType=` (a *documented* SH1 endpoint), and `GET /api/v2/cda/search?q=&siteId=` for any site with `searchablePostTypes` configured (SH52) — the existing search tests passed because no fixture configured one. Fixed by filtering on the post-type **id**: `ShCdaService.pageBySiteAndType` resolves the public `?postType=<name>` to an id first (unknown name → empty page, never a 500), and `searchablePostTypeNames` became `searchablePostTypeIds`; four repository finders were re-keyed. The identical fix had been sitting three lines above them in the same file since SH61, which is precisely the argument for a guard rather than a comment. [ShTenantJoinLintTest](../shio-app/src/test/java/com/viglet/shio/tenant/ShTenantJoinLintTest.java) scans repository sources — both `@Query` strings and derived method names — and fails the build on any navigation past `.id`, skipping comments (so the rule can be documented without tripping itself) and native queries (no tenant predicate is added to those). Its own regexes are self-tested, because a lint that silently matches nothing is worse than none: word boundaries turned out to be useless on **both** sides of a derived name — the association is glued to `By`/`And` (no boundary before) and the next property starts with a capital, so `Id\b` does not hold in `_IdAndState` (which would have flagged every safe finder). 4 new tests + 6 characterization tests; regression cover in [ShCdaTenantJoinRegressionTest](../shio-app/src/test/java/com/viglet/shio/api/cda/ShCdaTenantJoinRegressionTest.java). → §XIV.4
- **SH124** — **Cost instrumentation on the delivery path.** `X-Shio-Est-Tokens` now covers `/api/v2/cda/*` as well as `/api/v2/agent/*` — instrumenting only the agent namespace would have measured the cheap half of an agent's traffic and missed the expensive one, leaving SH112/SH113 blind to the reads that actually dominate. `ShEstTokensHeaderFilter` → [ShEstTokensHeaderFilter](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/agent/ShEstTokensHeaderFilter.java) (the name was surface-specific; the concern is not), registered once for both patterns at `LOWEST_PRECEDENCE - 30` — deliberately **outside** the SH3 ETag filter, so a conditional `304` is measured as the zero-byte response it really is. That ordering is what will let SH116's claim ("an unchanged context costs nothing") show up as a number rather than an assertion. → §XIII.2
- **SH125** — **Null/default omission as policy, with the counter-rule.** Nulls are always waste (`"url": null` and an absent `url` say the same thing), so every agent-owned DTO omits them — enforced by [ShAgentJsonLeanTest](../shio-app/src/test/java/com/viglet/shio/api/agent/ShAgentJsonLeanTest.java), which serializes real responses and fails on any `:null`. **The interesting half is what the policy refuses to do.** A blanket `NON_DEFAULT` — the obvious "make it smaller" move, and what the task originally proposed — would have stripped the `false` entries from the manifest's `features` map and `truncated: false` from a budget report. Those are not defaults, they are *answers*: an absent feature flag sends a caller probing (the exact cost the manifest exists to remove) and a missing `truncated` reads as "unknown". So the rule is **NON_NULL as the baseline, NON_DEFAULT only where a default is genuinely uninformative** (row-shaped DTOs, where `folders: 0` on a post row says nothing) — leanness is never a licence to drop an answer, and both counter-cases are pinned by tests. Two scoping decisions recorded rather than glossed: (1) **the CDA is untouched** — its TypeScript mirror declares nullable fields as `string | null`, *not* optional, so omitting a null would turn a declared `null` into `undefined` and break typed consumers; leaning the delivery path needs a coordinated SDK type change (→ new SH127). (2) The context pack's `model` section therefore still ships the CDA shape's nulls, which is the measurable price of composing over a frozen contract (P10) — asserted by a characterization test so it stays visible instead of reading as an oversight. An earlier draft of this test read whatever the shared test database happened to hold and passed or failed by class ordering; it now owns its fixture, because a leanness rule that only holds in one test order is not a rule. → §XIII.2
- **SH126** — **`shio context` CLI.** Completes SH77's stated surface: `shio context [--format terse|json] [--site] [--include] [--depth] [--budget] [--from] [--out]`, over a new [ShioAgentClient](../cli/src/agent-client.mjs) (console Basic auth — the pack reports the *authoring* view, so it is an admin read; kept separate from `ShioAdminClient`, which hard-codes the `/api/v2/post-type` prefix). Two deliberate choices: **`terse` is the default here** (unlike the endpoint, whose default stays JSON — the caller of a CLI is an agent), and the body is streamed through as **text, never parsed and re-serialized**, because the pack's digest is computed over exactly those bytes and reformatting would break `--out` diffs. `--out` writes a committable artifact a later session or a reviewer can diff; an unknown `--format` is rejected with the allowed set in the message, mirroring the server's teaching-error contract (SH80). 8 new `node:test` cases ([context.test.mjs](../cli/test/context.test.mjs)) incl. byte-for-byte passthrough, flag forwarding, blank-flag omission, and no artifact written on an HTTP failure; CLI suite 33 green. → §VIII.3
- **SH121** — **Id-free agent reads.** The context pack no longer emits an object id on any site or sitemap row; `?ids=true` (and `shio context --ids`) restores them. This is where SH78's measurement is finally collected: the terse encoding's residual per-row cost was dominated by the 36-char UUID, and SH79 made every row addressable without one, so the id had become the most expensive thing a row carried and the least necessary. [ShAgentContextService](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/agent/ShAgentContextService.java) threads the flag through the walk; [ShAgentContext](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/agent/dto/ShAgentContext.java)'s `NON_NULL`/`NON_DEFAULT` policy (SH125) then drops the field from the wire with no extra machinery. **Three decisions worth keeping:** (1) the **resume cursor stays an id** — it is one value per *response*, not one per row, so it costs nothing measurable and needs no namespace disambiguation to be exact; `offer()` therefore takes the object id as a parameter instead of reading it back off a row that no longer has one. (2) The **digest moves with the flag**, unlike with `budget`/`format`: `ids` changes what the pack *says*, not how the same statement was measured, and SH116 will hand that value straight to `If-None-Match`, where two representations must not share an entity tag. (3) An id is still accepted **as input** (`?site=<uuid>`) — the asymmetry is deliberate; a caller holding an id should never be made to translate it first. A convention line tells the agent how to get ids back, said once instead of 36 chars per row. → §VIII.5
- **SH81** — **Batch transactional mutation** (`POST /api/v2/agent/batch`). N addressed ops — `folder.upsert` · `folder.delete` · `post.upsert` · `post.publish` · `post.unpublish` · `post.delete` — applied as one transaction, with `dryRun`. [ShAgentBatchService](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/agent/ShAgentBatchService.java) + [ShAgentBatch](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/agent/dto/ShAgentBatch.java) + [ShAgentChangeSet](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/agent/dto/ShAgentChangeSet.java). P2 on the write side: a twelve-page structure is one call instead of ~24, and because every op is **addressed** (SH79) rather than id-keyed, no UUID has to survive between steps — which is the failure mode SH79 was written to end. **Composition, not a third contract (P10):** nothing here touches the database; folders go through `ShFolderWriteService` and posts through `ShPostUnifiedWriteService`, so the SH51 audit, SH12 webhooks, SH55 trash semantics and title/summary derivation behave exactly as they do from the console. The §XII invariant is enforced now rather than deferred to SH84 — the SH54 content ACL and SH22 quota are checked on the same objects the console checks them on. **Why dry-run simulates instead of writing-and-rolling-back:** by the time a rollback is decided, audit rows, lifecycle events and quota counters have already happened, and a plan that perturbs the instance is not a plan; so a dry run writes nothing and keeps a *pending set* of what earlier ops would have created — otherwise "create /blog, then put a post in /blog" reports a spurious 404 on its second line and the plan is useless for exactly the structures the endpoint exists for. That shortcut is **dry-run-only**: an early version took it in real runs too and silently skipped the publish, making apply disagree with its own plan. Writes refuse the lenient `site:` address and the `id:` form (a read may guess a namespace because a wrong guess costs a retry; a write may not). Idempotency is structural — `post.upsert` writes the **furl from the address** (new `ShPostUnifiedWriteService#setFurl`, applied to both state rows) so the second run finds the same post, and publish reports `noop` when the live rendering would not differ. 17 tests. → §VIII.7
- **SH82** — **Desired-state plan/apply for content** (`POST /api/v2/agent/plan` · `/apply`). [ShAgentDesiredStateService](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/agent/ShAgentDesiredStateService.java) + [ShAgentDesiredState](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/agent/dto/ShAgentDesiredState.java). A batch is imperative, so the caller must know what it already did — precisely the knowledge an agent loses to context compaction. A document is a *fact*: applying it twice is applying it once, and the second plan is empty. That empty plan is the content **drift guard**, the same green light `shio push --check` gives for post-types (SH65) — SH65's shape, one engine, a second resource type. The document is **compiled into SH81 ops** and handed to the same engine, so plan and apply cannot drift from each other (`plan` *is* `apply` with the dry-run flag) or from batch. Compile order is load-bearing and fixed: folders → upserts → publishes → prunes, so a page never goes live referencing a sibling that does not exist yet and a deletion never races its replacement. **`publish` is a tri-state on purpose:** absent means "leave the live state alone", because treating absence as `false` would unpublish live pages the moment someone trimmed a field from the document (P7). **`prune` is scoped to the declared folders**, and declaring none is an error rather than a licence to delete everything — a prune whose blast radius depends on what the author forgot to mention is the definition of a surprise. 12 tests. → §VIII.7
- **SH75** — **MCP server host.** `POST /mcp` speaks the Model Context Protocol (JSON-RPC 2.0, streamable HTTP, revision `2025-06-18`) over a tool/resource/prompt registry; `shio mcp` in the CLI bridges stdio to it, so local setup is `claude mcp add shio -- shio mcp` with no CORS, token or proxy ceremony. [ShMcpServer](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/agent/mcp/ShMcpServer.java) (protocol) + [ShMcpAPI](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/agent/mcp/ShMcpAPI.java) (transport) + [ShMcpTool](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/agent/mcp/ShMcpTool.java)/[ShMcpResource](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/agent/mcp/ShMcpResource.java)/[ShMcpPrompt](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/agent/mcp/ShMcpPrompt.java) (registry contracts) + [mcp.mjs](../cli/src/commands/mcp.mjs) (bridge). **The protocol is implemented, not imported**, and the reason is the task's own constraint that the host be transport + registry only: the MCP Java SDK is Jackson-2 and Spring-Boot-3 based while this app is Boot 4 + Jackson 3 (`tools.jackson`), so importing it would trade a few hundred lines of envelope handling for a second JSON stack and a standing version risk on the product's front door. **The decision that shapes everything else: two error channels.** A JSON-RPC `error` means the *message* was unusable (unknown method, unknown tool) and is the client's problem; anything the caller could fix — a bad address, an unknown post-type, a failed batch — comes back as a normal result with `isError: true`, rendered as text. Only the second reaches the model, so routing an SH80 teaching error the other way would throw away the `didYouMean` that makes the retry succeed. **Scope, stated rather than discovered:** `GET /mcp` returns `405` because this server sends nothing unprompted — no subscriptions, no progress, no sampling — and a stream that never emits is indistinguishable from a broken one; the day SH90's watch mode exists it can start answering with no client change. A session id is minted on `initialize`, returned as `Mcp-Session-Id`, and stamped into the SH51 audit actor as `alice (agent:7f3c…)` — the human stays visible because an agent acts *as* someone, and the id is what makes SH109's review queue expressible. A column for it belongs to SH106, which owns the credential model and can migrate once. The bridge is deliberately dumb (frames stdio into POSTs, copies answers back, parses nothing) so there is exactly one implementation of the protocol and it cannot drift; its tests assert the properties that actually matter for a bridge — one line out per request, silence on `202`, an id-carrying error when the network fails, and never an embedded newline. 20 protocol tests + 8 CLI tests. → §VIII.1
- **SH83** — **The agent tools** — `shio_context` · `shio_find` · `shio_read` · `shio_write` · `shio_apply` · `shio_publish` · `shio_assets` · `shio_changes`, plus resources (`shio://manifest`, `shio://context`, `shio://schema/{postType}`) and prompts (`new-site`, `add-section`, `translate-site`, `audit-content`). Every tool is a **shape** over a REST surface that already exists (P10) — `shio_write` over SH81's batch, `shio_apply` over SH82's plan/apply — so a bug has one possible home and it is never the MCP layer. New underneath them: [ShAgentReadService](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/agent/ShAgentReadService.java) with `GET /api/v2/agent/find` and `/read`, because `find`/`read` had no REST equivalent and inventing one inside a tool would have broken exactly the rule the block is built on. **`find` returns identifiers, never bodies:** a search that returned twelve matches' content has spent the agent's context on the eleven it did not want, and that cost scales with how badly the query was aimed. **Reads are DRAFT-preferred, not CDA-backed:** composition is the rule, but the CDA only sees `PUBLISHED`, and an agent that cannot read back its own unpublished work is not a composition worth having; the SH2 allow-list is still enforced, from the same place. **Eight, not nine, and the missing one is deliberate:** `shio_verify` waits for SH99's content lint, because a verify that only pretends leaves the agent believing its work was checked — strictly worse than knowing it was not. `shio_changes` ships as a *window* over the SH51 audit and says so; SH88 adds the cursor, and faking one over `date` would look resumable while silently dropping same-timestamp entries. Schemas are hand-written and short because a tool schema is context re-sent every turn — a test fails the build past 12 tools. Prompts render **procedures**, never content or tone (§0.7 stands: Shio hosts no model and no prompts in the sense that matters); each one plans with `dryRun` before writing and treats publishing as a separate named step, asserted by test, because a procedure that skips those teaches an agent to work in the way P7 exists to prevent. → §VIII.8
- **SH123** — **Per-field projection on agent content reads.** `fields=` on `GET /api/v2/agent/read` and on `shio_read`; the response echoes which fields came back, which removes the "is this all of it?" round trip for a few tokens. Waited for SH83 exactly as planned — there were no content reads to project before it. **The one decision worth recording:** a field the post-type does not declare is a **teaching error**, not an empty result. `fields=headine` returning `{}` is indistinguishable from an empty post, and the agent's next move is to overwrite real content with nothing — the only way this feature could cause damage, so it is the one case it refuses. A field the type *has* but the post has not set is simply absent; that is data. → §VIII.4
- **SH83 follow-up (found by its own test)** — **the full-text search bind parameter was passed raw.** `ShPostUnifiedRepository.FULLTEXT_PREDICATE` lower()s the *columns* but not the `:q` parameter and does no wildcarding — both are the caller's job, as they are in `ShCdaService`. `find(q=…)` passed the term unprocessed and matched nothing, which reads as an empty index rather than a bug and is why it survived a first review. Now normalized at the call site, with the contract stated where the mistake was made. The general shape is [SH131](ROADMAP.md).
- **Refactor (found by SH83)** — **the SH2 per-site allow-list was implemented three times.** Identically and by hand, in the context pack, the address resolver and the batch engine. Extracted to [ShAgentSiteAccess](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/agent/ShAgentSiteAccess.java). Duplication of an *access rule* is worth removing even while every copy is correct, because the failure mode is silent and it is a security one.
- **SH81 follow-up (found while building it)** — **posts created below a site's root folder had a null `shSite`.** `ShFolderWriteService` deliberately nulls `shSite` on non-root folders (only the root carries it, and `ShObjectNavigationService#siteOf` walks up for the rest), but `ShPostUnifiedWriteService#create` read `folder.getShSite()` directly. Every post created in a subfolder — from the console too — was therefore site-less: invisible in the console, which navigates by folder, and fatal to anything querying by site (CDA `/query`, the by-url lookup, the SH79 resolver). Fixed by walking up, as the navigation service already does. Same class of defect as SH122: valid code, wrong at runtime, silent until something queried along the other axis.
- **SH22 follow-up (found by SH77)** — **the `@TenantId` JOINED-join hazard.** A JPQL query that navigates *past the id* of an association whose target is an `ShObject` subclass (`ShSite`/`ShFolder`/`ShPostType`) makes Hibernate emit the tenant discriminator predicate against the **subclass** table alias, which carries no `tenant_id` column (it lives on the JOINED `ShObject` root) — the query dies at prepare time with `Column "spt1_1.tenant_id" not found`. Valid JPQL, invisible until runtime. Both new count queries group on the association **id** instead, which uses the FK column already on `sh_post_unified`: no join, no tenant predicate, cheaper SQL. Documented in `agents.md` → Common Issues and in `ShPostUnifiedRepository`; a build-time guard is tracked as SH122.

- **SH76** — **Agent manifest** (`GET /api/v2/agent/manifest`). The instance describing itself to a coding agent, so the dominant agent failure mode — *guessing* an endpoint, a capability or a parameter name — costs one cached call instead of a 404 and a retry (design law P2). New `com.viglet.shio.api.agent` package: [ShAgentAPI](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/agent/ShAgentAPI.java) + [ShAgentManifestService](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/agent/ShAgentManifestService.java) over three records ([ShAgentManifest](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/agent/dto/ShAgentManifest.java) / [ShAgentEndpoint](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/agent/dto/ShAgentEndpoint.java) / [ShAgentLimits](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/agent/dto/ShAgentLimits.java)). Payload: product + build version (jar `Implementation-Version`, `dev` in an IDE) + a **`protocol` revision** that versions the *agent surface shape* independently of the product; a sorted `features` map; `limits` (rate-limit bucket, default page size, cache max-age) so a client paces itself instead of learning the ceiling from a `429`; a **curated** endpoint index (16 entries, each with `purpose`, the required credential, and a runnable `example`); and `startHere` — the opening three calls, model before content. Two deliberate design calls: (1) **features are three-valued in origin but binary on the wire** — *configured* flags read the live properties (`multiTenant`, `oidc`, `webhooks`, `scheduledPublish`, `previewTokens`, `rateLimit`, `signedImageUrls`), *build* flags are constants of the artifact, and **unshipped capabilities are reported `false`, never omitted** (an absent flag sends the caller probing, which is the cost the manifest exists to remove); (2) the index is curated, not generated from the full API — it is read every session, so a token budget applies (P3), enforced by a test that fails if it grows past 30 entries. `ShApiTokenFilter` gains `/api/v2/agent` as a **third** token-authenticated prefix (after `/api/v2/cda` and `/graphql`) so a delivery key can read the manifest without a console credential — the SH2 method gate is untouched, so this widens *reads* only, and a `READ` key still gets `403` on a POST there. No security-config change: the namespace falls under the existing `anyRequest().authenticated()`, so a console session and HTTP Basic (the `shio` CLI) work too. 9 tests ([ShAgentManifestTest](../shio-app/src/test/java/com/viglet/shio/api/agent/ShAgentManifestTest.java)) assert the *contract* rather than the contents — byte-stability across calls, sorted keys, unshipped-as-`false`, every endpoint self-sufficient, the index stays small — plus 2 in `ShApiTokenFilterTest` (16 total) for the prefix widening. Concept: [specs/SH74-agent-native-cms.md](specs/SH74-agent-native-cms.md) §4.2.
- **SH80** — **Teaching errors** (RFC 9457 + `fix`/`allowed`/`didYouMean`/`example`). Design law **P6 — errors are instructions**: every field on the wire is a round trip the caller does not spend re-deriving the contract. New `com.viglet.shio.api.error` package: [ShProblem](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/error/ShProblem.java) (immutable builder over Spring's `ProblemDetail`; `type` = `https://shio.viglet.com/errors/<slug>`; **blank/empty extensions are omitted entirely** rather than serialized as `null`/`[]`, so a response never pays for what it doesn't teach), [ShTeachingException](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/error/ShTeachingException.java) (a domain error carries its own problem, so adding one is a constructor — not another handler), [ShDidYouMean](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/error/ShDidYouMean.java) (commons-text Levenshtein over a case/separator-insensitive normal form, gated at `max(2, len/3)` — a wrong suggestion is worse than none — and tie-stable on the candidate order), and [ShApiExceptionHandler](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/error/ShApiExceptionHandler.java) (`@RestControllerAdvice`; renders domain problems and enriches four framework exceptions: missing parameter, type mismatch, unreadable body, wrong verb). **Statuses are unchanged from the framework defaults — only bodies gain content** — so nothing that branches on a status code is affected. Two enrichments are worth naming: a `MethodArgumentTypeMismatchException` on an **enum** parameter returns the constants as `allowed` + the nearest match (the most common "which values does this take?" round trip), and a `405` returns the mapped verbs as `allowed`, which is what stops a caller probing verbs. The three existing post-type exceptions (`ShUnknownWidgetException`, `ShSystemPostTypeException`, `ShManagedPostTypeException`) now extend `ShTeachingException`; both throw sites load the widget catalog **on the error path only** so a 400 can teach the installed names. **The interesting finding:** nearest-string matching is silent on exactly the guess an agent is most likely to make — `RichText` is 4 edits from `Text` and further from everything else, because it is a *vocabulary* mismatch, not a spelling one. Hence [ShWidgetAliases](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/post/type/ShWidgetAliases.java): ~90 foreign widget names from Contentful / Sanity / Strapi / Payload / JSON-schema (`richtext`, `symbol`, `reference`, `relation`, `media`, `asset`, `array`, `enumeration`, `boolean`, `portabletext`…) mapped onto the 14-widget catalog, consulted **before** the distance fallback and **only ever suggesting a target that is actually installed**. 15 tests ([ShTeachingErrorTest](../shio-app/src/test/java/com/viglet/shio/api/error/ShTeachingErrorTest.java), network-free) cover omission of empty extensions, the four teaching fields, alias translation per source platform, the typo fallback, tie determinism, the never-suggest-an-uninstalled-widget invariant, and message/detail agreement between logs and the wire. Concept: [specs/SH74-agent-native-cms.md](specs/SH74-agent-native-cms.md) §4.6.
- **SH598** — ShAgentP2ConformanceTest walks discoverability as graph reachability -- seed with an entry point's response, open every door it names, repeat to a fixed point -- from both cold starts the product has, GET /agent/context and MCP initialize. All 71 targets (11 tools, 7 resources, 4 prompts, 28 routes, 11 ops, 10 elsewhere pointers) are named from both, so the gap list lands empty and says so rather than manufacturing entries; the finding is the depth, asserted beside it, because a capability can stay findable and still get further away.

**Follow-ups — the edges the first end-to-end build exposed.**

- **SH168** — **A write refuses a field the post-type does not declare** ([ShAgentBatchService](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/agent/ShAgentBatchService.java), [ShAgentVerifyService](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/agent/verify/ShAgentVerifyService.java)). `post.upsert` stored any key handed to it, and because an upsert declares *whole state* a mistyped field name did not add a key — it **replaced** the one that was meant with one nothing reads. The write reported `changed:1`, the console could not render it, `shio types` could not type it, and `shio verify` was green: the only defect on record that destroyed content without saying anything. It is now a 400 carrying the post-type's field list as `allowed` and the nearest name as `didYouMean` (the SH80 matcher, not a second notion of "close").
  <br>**It binds new keys only.** A post that already holds undeclared keys — SH152's post-type collisions, older instances' `File` posts — stays writable, because refusing those would mean an agent could no longer fix such a post at all. The `unknown-field` lint rule reports the ones already there, as an **error**: the CMS can prove this one from the inside, so SH99's rule applies honestly even though it turns a pre-SH168 instance red. "Known and accepted" is SH142's job, not a softer severity.
  <br>**A plan warns where a real run refuses.** The first cut threw on a `dryRun` too, and the blueprint test caught what that costs: a plan that dies on the first bad field hides the rest of its report, including SH152's list of which fields the existing post-type lacks — the more actionable half. So a plan reports `undeclared field(s) … — a real run will refuse this write` on the row and keeps going. A refusal that can only be discovered by attempting the write is exactly what a plan exists to prevent.
- **SH171** — **A multi-address read fails per row, not per call** ([ShAgentReadService](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/agent/ShAgentReadService.java), [ShAgentDoc](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/agent/dto/ShAgentDoc.java)). `GET /agent/read` with N addresses 404'd the whole call when any one was unresolvable, which inverted the saving the batch form exists for: the agent then re-read the addresses one at a time to find the offender. Now each row comes back positionally — the SH80 slug, title and fix in place of its content — and the **single**-address form still 404s, because callers depend on that.
  <br>**One transactional subtlety made it real.** Catching a teaching exception inside `@Transactional(readOnly = true)` is not enough: the inner interceptor had already marked the shared transaction rollback-only, so the successful rows blew up at commit with `UnexpectedRollbackException`. `noRollbackFor = ShTeachingException.class` on the resolver and the read service fixes it, and is safe precisely because both are read-only lookups — an enclosing *write* transaction has no such exemption, so a batch op that cannot resolve still rolls the whole batch back.
- **SH172** — **An address names one post, or it is an id** ([ShAddressResolver](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/agent/ShAddressResolver.java)). A post with no friendly URL has no address under SH79's scheme, and `find` rendered it as `post:<site>/` anyway — so three URL-less `File` posts came back as three rows carrying the *same* address, none of them actionable, none of them saying anything was wrong. SH100's lint had already answered this correctly by falling back to `id:<uuid>`; the two surfaces disagreeing was the defect. The fallback now lives in `addressOf`, the one place both of them ask, so `find`, `changes`, the change rows and the review queue agree by construction — the invariant is enforced rather than restated (§VIII.10's rule). A site-less post (the SH128 class) falls back for the same reason.
  <br>The response says so once, at the top (`notes`), rather than marking every row: a File-heavy site would otherwise pay for the same sentence on every row, and the `id:` prefix is already visible where it applies.
- **SH175** — **A conditional requirement is stated on the argument** (`shio_write`'s schema). `type` said it was needed only when creating; `folder`, needed on exactly the same op, described itself as a hint — so the most common write on the surface, an agent's first create, paid a round trip to learn it from the error. The schema is the one document a model reads *before* calling. Deliberately a sentence rather than JSON Schema's `if`/`then`: a conditional keyword an MCP client may or may not surface is a worse deal than a description the model definitely reads.
- **SH196** — Every folder write records one audit row — create, rename and move joined delete and restore — and `ShHistory.subject_kind` says whether a row is about a post or a section, so the change feed reports a site's shape and not only its contents, a purged section's own entry still reads as a section, and reverting a run undoes the folders it created as well as the pages.
- **SH140** — A move that changes a live URL now names the published pages whose authored markup still links to the old one, with their addresses and one fix, on the move's own row.
- **SH197** — The stability helper can no longer be handed a hash-ordered literal, which it was in ShAgentOps; banning Map.of outright is refused by a count, not an argument.
- **SH393** — The manifest ships an `elsewhere` map naming where each unreachable capability does live, asserted equal to the P1 exception list, so the boundary is a lookup and not a seventh derivation.
- **SH453** — Both branches of site.upsert now read data.postTypeLayout: the create branch serializes the bindings it was handed through ShSiteWriteService rather than the protocol layer, and reports them - "a blank site, binding postTypeLayout.Article" - because saying "a blank site" either way is what kept this invisible to the one caller who could notice. Applied rather than refused, since P2 asks one op to mean one intention; the conformance suite's two-op workaround becomes one op and the guard.
- **SH463** — site.delete removes a site and everything in it with the SH108 confirm token, saying in its plan line that it is purged rather than trashed — and the instrument half landed with it: a siteDelete feature key forces the P1 classification, and an AGENT_EQUIVALENT entry now names the HTTP verbs its agent form covers, which found two more undeclared decisions on its first run.
- **SH544** — an audit description is bounded where it is built, and a database refusal reaches the wire as a teaching 400/409 naming the op instead of a 500
- **SH545** — an agent read reports whether a page is live in a published field, conditional and measured, so state can keep meaning which row was returned
- **SH546** — shio publish makes drafts live from the CLI, --all names every post from a find, and the batch ceiling comes from the refusal rather than a constant
- **SH547** — an empty desired-state document is refused as empty-document, teaching the document's own keys and naming the endpoint an ops array belongs to
- **SH596** — `shio://diagnostics` is on `resources/list` — the failure report folded by cause, with the count, the fix and the frames, terse, a read with no arguments rather than a twelfth tool against a `tools/list` paid every turn. The half worth keeping is why the conformance check was green over it: `ShAgentP1ConformanceTest` classified the feature as `shio_changes` on the true observation that incidents ride the change feed, because its `Reach` vocabulary had no way to say *a resource delivers this and no tool needs to*, so the honest answer had nowhere to go. A classification can only be as honest as its categories allow — `MCP_RESOURCE` now exists, is checked against the registered beans rather than believed, and carries its own vacuity guard.
- **SH599** — ShAgentCapabilityJoinTest joins the three registries in one key space and fails naming any tool, resource, prompt or route that no `features` flag claims and nothing declares flagless -- the reverse of ShAgentP1ConformanceTest's walk, which SH463 had already noticed for one case and nobody generalised. The claimed side is read from P1's table rather than copied, so the two cannot drift; of 50 entries `features` claims 16, and the other 34 are declared with a reason in seven families rather than claimed by a neighbouring capability, which is SH596's mistake in the other direction.
- **SH600** — The manifest now carries `omitted` -- section name and entry count for everything `include=` removed, absent on a full document -- so ?include=identity stops answering 200 with all 57 capability flags silently gone. Counts and section names only, never content: listing what was dropped would cost most of what the projection saved. It reaches the context pack for free, because the manifest folded in at include=manifest is itself a projection, so a session opening with one call is now told the twenty-eight-route index exists; three assertions that used the word `endpoints` as a proxy for its absence were tightened to the section's opener, which is the same confusion one level up.
- **SH413** — site.upsert data.reindex:true indexes a site's already-published posts through the same indexItem the publish listener uses, so there is one mapping. Paged - data.limit 200 max 1000, data.from resumes - because SH84's sender is single-threaded and a large site would be an outage of the publish path. It is a data key and not a twelfth op name: ShAgentOpsReachTest priced the vocabulary at 600 and refused the name, which is SH326's trade.
- **SH523** — PUT /api/v2/post-type/{name}?dryRun=true answers what a model change would cost instead of making it: which published posts would violate a field being made required, which templates read a field being removed, which declared fields nothing reads, and which stored keys no type declares - SH474's defect asked as a question rather than found by a lint firing 66 times. A dry run on the write an agent was making anyway, not an endpoint of its own, for SH262's reason at the same fork.
- **SH524** — field-reachability.test.mjs classifies every declared field of the section vocabulary the way ShAgentP1ConformanceTest classifies a capability: does a component draw it, and does the drawing annotate it. All 25 section fields render, so SH465's class is closed and asserted rather than remembered; the types the package does not draw are a signed list, not a naming rule that would absorb a section somebody forgot. The annotation half came back 25 of 25 missing and is SH638.
- **SH525** — shio propose --from <address>... asks the question propose already answers, about content the reader wrote: what post-type are these instances of. A flag rather than a verb because the capability was built and only its input was hard-wired to a capture. It carries the two things conversion does not need - which instances lack each field, and a minority field reported rather than swept into the type - and the report says it is evidence about the instances it read.
- **SH553** — The sitemap's post nodes carry published, so an agent opening with the pack is no longer told every page of a fully published site is a draft. Free of queries here, unlike the two surfaces SH545 fixed: the walk already fetched both state rows to drop one, so the fact was in hand and discarded. Conditional, so addressing@scale is unmoved at 62 tokens - and because Node uses NON_DEFAULT rather than NON_NULL, the omission is asserted on the wire.
- **SH601** — startHere branches: two facts true whatever the intent, then six rows of question to one call, keyed by what a reader arrives with rather than by capability. ShAgentIntents is the table and the discovery benchmark reads it, so what is scored is what an agent is told - SH601's own instruction, build once, score against it, route with it. Paid for by deleting three lines the routing now answers per intent.
- **SH608** — The pack reports which sections include= removed, so ?include=instance no longer answers 200 while dropping the model, the sitemap and the conventions in silence. Names rather than SH600's counts, because a pack section it drops is never built and counting would cost what the projection saved. Built from the parsed section set, since after assembly an empty list and an unasked section are the same thing. Separate from budget.truncated: one is the caller's lever, the other the instance's.
- **SH621** — GET /api/v2/post-type/{name} answers an unknown name with an RFC 9457 document carrying allowed, didYouMean and a fix naming both next moves, where it sent 404 with Content-Length 0. P6 was implemented on the agent surface only, which is the wrong half: post-types are the one name-keyed surface since SH117, so a name is all a caller can get wrong and a typo is the likeliest arrival. With zero bytes a renamed type and one that never existed were the same answer.
- **SH622** — The 401 entry point and a chain-wide 403 handler write the same problem document the controller advice does, with a fix naming the credential that path wants and the call that mints one. P6 lived in ControllerAdvice and a rejected credential never reaches a controller, so every endpoint had one 4xx with no instructions - the one a caller meets first. The reason nobody noticed is that no test asked an unauthenticated question and read the body; four now do.
- **SH638** — Every section field a component renders now carries data-shio-prop, so a page composed from the package is editable in place. The host contract is one optional postId prop: only the host knows the id, because it fetched the section over the CDA and React drew it - and omitting it renders byte-identical markup, so a public page pays nothing. SH524's instrument was checking data-shio-field, an attribute this product does not have; it was right by accident and now checks the real one.

## Block K — Perception & verification loop (SH74)

> The block removes the *first* of the three human round trips in a typical build: the
> one that exists only because the agent cannot check its own work. Everything here is
> answered from state the instance already holds — no rendering, no crawling, no browser
> — because the cheap textual proof is the one that gets run.

- **SH99** — **Content lint** (`GET /api/v2/agent/verify`, `shio verify`, `shio_verify`). The content-side `tsc`: [ShAgentVerifyService](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/agent/verify/ShAgentVerifyService.java) walks the readable content once and reports `required-field-empty`, `dangling-reference`, `missing-asset`, `unpublished-dependency`, `duplicate-url`, `orphan-post`, `orphan-folder` and `empty-folder` as [ShAgentReport](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/agent/verify/dto/ShAgentReport.java) findings, each with an SH79 address and an SH80-style `fix`. The design calls: (1) **`ok` tracks errors, never warnings** — an error is broken from a visitor's point of view, a warning is something the CMS cannot prove from inside itself (an empty folder may be a section under construction), and an exit code that failed on the second kind is an exit code that gets wrapped in `|| true`; (2) **truncation is never silent** — `found` counts the whole run while `findings` carries what fitted, the same hazard SH138 records for deletion plans; (3) **a cross-site reference is not called dangling** — a target the credential cannot read is re-checked by id first, so the allow-list never manufactures a defect; (4) **one read pass, both states** — the duplicate-URL rule is only meaningful between `PUBLISHED` rows and "published depends on unpublished" cannot be asked without knowing which ids have one. A new repository finder, `findWithoutSite`, exists solely so the lint can see the **SH128 defect class** — a site-less post is invisible to every other finder by construction, and a lint blind to the defect its own guard was written for is not much of a lint. Ships the **ninth MCP tool**: `shio_verify` was held back from SH83 for want of something real to verify, and this flips the manifest's `contentLint` from the `false` it reported through all of Block H. 15 tests ([ShAgentVerifyTest](../shio-app/src/test/java/com/viglet/shio/api/agent/verify/ShAgentVerifyTest.java)) build every defect through the SH81 batch surface, so the rules are proved against content an agent could actually have written. → was §IX.1
- **SH100** — **Route/link verification**, as the `routes` check group of the same report: `url-missing` on a published post with no friendly URL, `link-unresolved` for a site-relative href matching no published URL, `asset-missing` for a `/file_source/<id>/<name>` with no bytes on disk, and `image-no-alt`. **It does not crawl.** "Internal links return 200" is answered against the content graph — the set of published furls, compared through `ShAddress.normalizePath` (made public here so there is exactly one canonical path form in the instance, P5) — rather than by fetching a front end that may not be running, may be a different deployment, and legitimately owns routes the CMS has never heard of. That last point is also why `link-unresolved` is a **warning**: on any real site the front end owns generated routes, and reporting those as errors would make the gate useless. Only `PUBLISHED` rows are route-checked (a draft's broken link is work in progress) and only the two markup widgets are scanned (a plain Text field holding something path-shaped is not a link). → was §IX.2
- **SH101** — **Render digest** (`GET /api/v2/agent/render`, `shio digest`, `shio_digest`). [ShHtmlOutline](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/agent/verify/ShHtmlOutline.java) scans markup into a heading outline, landmark counts, a link inventory and an image inventory **with alt text**, plus a word count; [ShAgentRenderService](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/agent/verify/ShAgentRenderService.java) shapes it into [ShAgentDigest](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/agent/verify/dto/ShAgentDigest.java). Four calls worth naming: (1) **two sources** — `address=` digests the markup Shio holds (no front end needed, usable immediately after a write) and `url=` digests what a visitor actually gets; (2) **fetching is off by default** (`shio.agent.render.allow-fetch`) and restricted to the origins of *readable* sites, because an endpoint that fetches an arbitrary URL on the server's behalf is a request forgery with a friendly name — and the origin check keeps the agent path from being a privilege escalation, the Block L invariant; (3) **the `digest` hash covers structure only** — heading levels and text, landmark counts, link hrefs, image sources and whether each has alt — so a typo fix does not move it and a lost heading does, which is what makes "did this page change shape?" a string comparison instead of a re-read; (4) **a missing `alt` attribute and `alt=""` are kept apart**, because the second is how decorative markup is *correctly* declared and collapsing them would train the agent to "fix" it. A scanner rather than an HTML parser, with the trade stated in the class doc: a digest is not a DOM, and the failure mode of a scanner is a slightly wrong outline, never invented structure. `visualSnapshot` (SH102) is reported `false` on purpose — a PNG costs orders of magnitude more tokens and tells the agent less. 10 tests ([ShAgentRenderTest](../shio-app/src/test/java/com/viglet/shio/api/agent/verify/ShAgentRenderTest.java)). → was §IX.3
- **SH103** — **Agent diagnostics** (`GET /api/v2/agent/diagnostics`). The asynchronous half of the loop: SH80's teaching errors answer the call that failed, this answers the failures that happen *after* the agent moves on. [ShAgentIncidentLog](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/agent/diagnostics/ShAgentIncidentLog.java) is a bounded in-memory ring buffer wired into the four places that previously only logged a warning: the webhook dispatcher (a delivery that never arrived is the difference between *published* and *visible*), the Thumbnailator pipeline (a failed transform serves the original and surfaces nothing), the publish scheduler (nobody is watching at 03:00), and a new `ShAgentErrorRecordingFilter` for 5xx — a filter rather than a catch-all `@ExceptionHandler`, so no existing client's error body changes, and registered outside the security chain so a rejected scan is not recorded as an instance fault. Two properties do the real work: **repeats fold** into one row with a count (one broken webhook retried on every publish would otherwise evict every other incident from a 50-slot window — the one way a diagnostics log actively misleads), and the response **states its own bound** via `since`/`dropped`/`notes`, because "no incidents" otherwise reads as a clean bill of health when it may mean "nothing is remembered". A disabled webhook subsystem says so explicitly, for the same reason. The incidents also surface as `diagnostics`-group findings in the verify report, since an agent that has to remember a second call will not make it. 6 tests ([ShAgentDiagnosticsTest](../shio-app/src/test/java/com/viglet/shio/api/agent/diagnostics/ShAgentDiagnosticsTest.java)). → was §IX.5
- **Block K wiring** — manifest: `contentLint` flips to `true` (backed by real rules, not a stub that always passes) alongside new `routeCheck`, `renderDigest`, `diagnostics` and the configured `renderFetch`; three endpoints join the curated index and `startHere` gains the verify step (the existing five-line cap held by folding the digest hint into the context line). CLI: `shio verify` (`--site`/`--checks`/`--limit`/`--strict`, **exit 1 on an error** so it sits in CI beside `shio push --check` and `shio apply --check`) and `shio digest <address|url>`, with 10 network-free tests ([verify.test.mjs](../cli/test/verify.test.mjs)). Terse renderings for all three payloads ([ShAgentVerifyTerse](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/agent/verify/ShAgentVerifyTerse.java)) — a report is the worst possible shape for JSON, and unlike a listing it is read in full by definition, so the saving is never wasted. The SH132 tool-list budget rises 1750 → 2110 for the two new tools (~355 est. tokens per turn), which is the trade the whole block exists to make: a fixed per-turn cost against a human round trip that costs orders of magnitude more.
- **SH560** — The corpus's second driver got a caller: cli/conformance/source-corpus.conformance.mjs serves each archetype over a real node:http socket with the platform's own fetch, asserting the three things an injected fetch structurally cannot - what the server was ASKED for (SH387), that both drivers of one route table agree, and that the browser-shaped archetype is refused with browser.mjs's install line rather than skipped (SH434). INERT_KEYS is now empty: scenarios.headless was never inert, it was misfiled - a claim about a browser capture held by a tier that declares it runs without one - and the first live run flipped spa's declaration to true because the check reads in both directions.

**Follow-ups — the third report state, and a run scoped to what changed**

- **SH142** — **Accepted findings** ([verify-baseline.mjs](../cli/src/verify-baseline.mjs), [commands/verify.mjs](../cli/src/commands/verify.mjs)). A report had two states and real content has three. `ok`/`not ok` cannot say *known and accepted* — a decorative image the markup cannot describe, a folder deliberately staged empty, a link into a route the front end owns — and the first legitimate warning nobody intends to fix is the moment the exit code stops being read. After that the errors go unread with it. A committed `shio/verify-baseline.json` of `(rule, address, field)` triples is subtracted before the gate decides.
  <br>**The half that keeps it from becoming a blanket suppression:** an accepted finding that the run *no longer produces* fails the run. Without it an entry outlives the defect it excused and silently swallows the next real one at the same address — which would make the file worse than not having it. That check is also why an entry is a triple and not a rule name. Matching is on rule + address + field, deliberately not on `message` (a copy-edit would look like a new defect) and not on `severity` (promoting a rule would quietly un-accept everything).
  <br>**A truncated report cannot prove staleness**, so it does not try: an unmatched entry is reported and the run does not fail on it, because a finding that did not fit is not a finding that is gone — the SH138 hazard read from the other side. `--accept` writes the baseline (naming every entry on stdout, `--reason` optional) and **merges** rather than replaces, since a run narrowed by `--site` sees only part of the project.
