- **SH161** — **Memory travels with the content** ([ShAgentMemoryService](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/agent/memory/ShAgentMemoryService.java), [ShExchangePackage](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/exchange/model/ShExchangePackage.java), [content-notes.mjs](../cli/src/content-notes.mjs), [ShSiteMemoryExchangeTest](../shio-app/src/test/java/com/viglet/shio/exchange/site/ShSiteMemoryExchangeTest.java)). A site's notes now leave the instance that learned them, both ways. **In the SH68 package**, as `ShAgentNote`s — the same shape, not a new serialization, the rule that file already follows for `ShPostTypeDef`. Only the **site-scoped** notes travel: an instance-wide note describes the *installation*, and importing another instance's house rules alongside somebody's blog is the surprise P7 exists to prevent (**SH231** revisits that for a whole-instance migration). A note names its site by **name** and an import renames the site, so notes are **re-scoped on import** — carried through verbatim they would be filed against a site that does not exist here, which is indistinguishable from losing them; the tenant-provisioning path renames them alongside its site suffixes for the same reason. Attribution is preserved and the timestamps are not: the author is the load-bearing half (SH114 keeps it so a human's instruction and an agent's inference stay distinguishable), while the dates describe this instance's copy, which really did arrive now. **In the file projection**, as `shio/content/<site>/.memory.yaml` — read on push, written on pull, with the same three-way merge the content tree already uses. `updated` is deliberately **not** written to the file: it would rewrite the bytes on every pull that touched a note for any reason. The base snapshot records notes for the reason SH149 needed it for folder markers: a key the server has and the file does not is *either* a new note *or* a deleted one, and existence alone cannot tell them apart — and **no file at all means "never projected", never "forget everything"**, so a first push from a fresh clone cannot wipe a site's memory. Notes are applied **outside** the desired-state document, because a note is not content and `--prune` must never be able to reach it. A note changed on both sides is a conflict that writes nothing, the rule the post merge already follows. 13 CLI tests, 3 backend.
- **SH174** — **The manifest can be asked for in pieces** ([ShAgentManifestSection](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/agent/ShAgentManifestSection.java), [ShAgentManifestTerse](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/agent/ShAgentManifestTerse.java), [ShAgentManifestProjectionTest](../shio-app/src/test/java/com/viglet/shio/api/agent/ShAgentManifestProjectionTest.java)). `?include=identity,features,limits,endpoints,start-here` and `?format=json|terse` on the document every session reads first. **The capability check is the read this exists for**: `include=features,limits` measures **298** against the full document's **2343**, a 7.9× saving on an agent re-reading the manifest to confirm one boolean — and no `304` can help there, because SH116 already covers the repeat case and this is the *first* call. The identity scalars survive every projection (a response a client cannot branch on turns a saving into a second call), and the tag mixes in `format` plus the section set in **declaration order**, so two spellings of one projection share a tag instead of revalidating forever. **The terse number is the finding, and it is recorded rather than quietly dropped**: 2088, an 11% saving where the same encoding is worth a third to a half everywhere else — because this document's weight is *prose*, a purpose sentence and a runnable example twenty-nine times, which the terse form keeps verbatim on purpose since an abbreviated example is a call the instance would reject (**SH230**). It ships anyway, for a reason about the 400 beside it: an unknown `format` is now a teaching error the way `/agent/context` has always answered, and an agent that asks for terse uniformly across the surface must not be the one who pays for that. Implementing it is what makes refusing the typo safe.
- **Block M wiring** — manifest: `instanceMemory`, `conditionalReads` and `agentsMd` flip to `true`, and `PUT /agent/memory` joins the curated endpoint index. The index is capped at 30 by [ShAgentManifestTest](../shio-app/src/test/java/com/viglet/shio/api/agent/ShAgentManifestTest.java), so it **displaced** an entry rather than raising the ceiling: `/cda/post/by-url`, whose own description ("the cheapest addressing available today") was a hedge written before addressing existed and which SH79 plus `/agent/resolve` and `/agent/read` now do better without a site id. The endpoint itself is unchanged and still served. Context pack: memory rides in `conventions` behind a `[memory:key@site by author]` marker, and one derived line tells the agent the store exists and how to write to it — a store nobody writes to never pays back the row it costs. CLI: `shio remember [<key> "<note>"]` with `--forget`, `--site` and `--limit`, plus `--as agents-md` on `shio context`; a truncated listing says so rather than reading as the whole set (SH138's rule).
- **SH435** — Each command exports its own help and prints it; a lint derives its flags from the source, and the global help fell from 357 lines to 58.
- 🗑 **SH519** — abandoned: Not a defect: the corruption was mine. subprocess.run(text=True) decodes with cp1252 on this machine, so the read-modify-write patches I applied to the VILT pages turned C3 A9 into the UTF-8 of A-tilde-copyright before posting it back. A fresh convert into a clean site stores correct UTF-8, and an apply round trip of an accented string returns it unchanged.
- **SH513** — A refusal whose body is valid JSON but not a teaching document now prints the fields it does carry - Spring's default names the endpoint in path and the CLI was discarding it - while a body holding any SH80 key prints exactly as before. One choke point, so it reaches every write the CLI makes.
- **SH597** — ShAgentDiscoveryCostTest scores the path rather than a surface: six intents with a known right first move, each walked from an empty context until a cold-start read names the move, then the move executed and required to succeed. Measured 10604 tokens across six independent cold starts, and it prints which rung answered each — two of the six are reachable only from the ~2400-token endpoint index, because `startHere` names neither /agent/diagnostics nor /agent/changes.
- **SH227** — shio_apply takes a verify argument, so a desired-state apply returns the lint of what it touched instead of costing a closing round trip.
- **SH228** — A write proof now covers the folders a run touched as well as its posts, and a run with nothing lintable gets an explicit empty report instead of no proof key.
- **SH229** — A lint walks every conditional endpoint's request params and fails when one is missing from the entity tag, with exemptions that have to say why.
- **SH394** — The CLI's help has three ceilings in the same file and shape as the MCP ones, and the per-session comparison between the two surfaces is printed on every run.
- **SH396** — The build-a-site benchmark now ends at a rendered page rather than at a lint, and both paths build the render model so the ratio compares the same job.
- **SH647** — The vocabulary's cost is decomposed into keys and prose and measured against the manifest alternative on every build, so the trade re-runs itself instead of waiting for the next op.
- **SH651** — The probe found create assigned no furl at all; it now derives one from the title through the shared ShFurlNaming, suffixing on collision, skipping FILE posts, and taking a declared furl as identity.
- **SH673** — The conformance constant follows the properties file at 2400, and cli/test/budget-restatement.test.mjs holds every restated budget against the key it restates - in pnpm test, where both sides are files and no instance is needed, so the drift is no longer only discoverable by the gate it breaks.
- **SH683** — Re-measured 10651 to 6387 tokens with all six intents now at rung 1, the ceilings lowered onto that, the false prose deleted, and the total given a floor so the next win cannot be absorbed in silence.
- **SH723** — The feed charges each row against a token ceiling before committing it: a delta stops at the last row that fit and the cursor carries the rest, a window narrows from its old end, and budget.truncated plus a note say which happened. Default 6000 (declared in token-budgets.properties), ?budget=0 opts out, and the terse header carries max-tokens= so the bound is visible before it cuts.
- **SH232** — Both modes revalidate now. Measuring found SH147's watermark had already made a non-empty window byte-stable and nobody noticed; the one case left was the empty window, whose cursor was the ceiling and so was now to the microsecond. It is the start of the trail instead — an empty window proves no row exists below the ceiling, so a floor skips nothing — with a note, since cursor=1970-01-01 otherwise reads as a bug.
- **SH231** — An instance's own notes now project to shio/.memory.yaml on a pull — beside content/, since they describe the installation and not any site. They are reported and never applied by a push unless --adopt-memory is passed, which keeps SH161's refusal while removing the hole it left: the least reproducible thing in the system had no export path at all.
- **SH736** — The help total is 9475 of a 9950 ceiling, and the gate now asserts 4% headroom under it, so raising the ceiling to meet the total fails instead of charging the next task for every verb.
- **SH230** — format=terse now cuts each endpoint purpose to its lead sentence and keeps the example verbatim, taking the manifest from 2395 to 1890 where the two candidates aimed at examples were worth 3.6%.
- **SH743** — Every response budget must keep 4% free or be declared in AT_THE_WALL with the reason it cannot be trimmed, and that list is the seventh row in the known-debt registry.

## Block N — Realignment of what already shipped (SH74)

> The reorientation was mostly additive, but it did invalidate some existing choices, and
> this block spent them. Two of the four tasks removed a *second* way of saying something
> the platform already said; one folded a second half-format into the real one; one closed a
> drift nothing was watching. The block's most useful output is not a feature — it is that
> **fixing the baseline cost the agent surface most of its measured token advantage**, which
> is recorded below rather than rounded off.

- **SH117** — **One name-keyed post-type surface** ([ShPostTypeAPI](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/post/type/ShPostTypeAPI.java), [ShPostTypeAdminService](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/post/type/ShPostTypeAdminService.java), [ShPostTypeApiTest](../shio-app/src/test/java/com/viglet/shio/api/post/type/ShPostTypeApiTest.java)). The id-keyed, entity-shaped `/api/v2/post/type` is **retired** and the React console reads and writes the same name-keyed, lossless `/api/v2/post-type` the CLI and the agent use. Two APIs for one concept was a tax paid on every agent session ("which one, and by id or by name?") and a straight violation of P5/P10.
  <br>**The load-bearing decision is what `managed` means on a write.** It became a `Boolean`, because absent and `false` have to differ: *absent* (the CLI's canonical serialization omits the key) is a code-owned write — mark it managed, and let the owner keep converging; *`false`* is a hand edit — mark it unmanaged, and refuse against a managed type with a 409 rather than silently winning a race with the repository. Get that backwards in either direction and unifying the APIs either locks the console out of every type it creates or lets it quietly overwrite the model a repo owns. It is a UX guard, not an ACL: any caller may claim either, and what it must never do is let one writer's convention overwrite the other's without saying so.
  <br>**Two verbs, not one.** `PUT /{name}` stays the idempotent upsert — converging a model that is already declared has to be a no-op or `shio push --check` means nothing — and `POST` creates and conflicts, because a name collision in the console's "new post-type" form is a mistake to report, not a content model to replace.
  <br>**`POST /api/v2/post-unified` now accepts `postType` by name** beside `postTypeId`. The console picks a post-type off a name-keyed surface and has no id to send; resolving the name server-side is one lookup where the id lives, instead of a round trip whose only purpose is translating a name the caller already knows. Unknown or absent is a teaching 400 carrying the installed catalogue.
  <br>**The security half is not incidental.** `/api/v2/post-type` was blanket CSRF-exempt so the stateless CLI could reach it; with a logged-in browser on the same path that exemption would have made "unify the two APIs" quietly mean "drop CSRF protection on the content model". [ShStatelessRequestMatcher](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/spring/security/ShStatelessRequestMatcher.java) narrows it to callers holding no session cookie — the right discriminator because the cookie is exactly the credential a cross-site request replays, and because it is readable *before* authentication, which a principal-based check would not be (`CsrfFilter` runs ahead of the authentication filters).
  <br>**Rename is not on this surface, deliberately.** The console's API-name field is read-only: a `PUT` to a new name would create a second post-type and leave the first one's content behind, which is SH134's lesson for posts. **SH163** is the task.
- **SH119** — **The Next.js starter is a blueprint** (`blueprints/nextjs-starter/`, [create-shio-app/src/emit.mjs](../create-shio-app/src/emit.mjs), `shio init --blueprint`). `create-shio-app`'s `template/` and the blueprint format were two half-formats for one idea — a tree of files with `{{placeholder}}` substitution — and neither was the other. The template is now also a first-party package: a `Page` model, two published pages, and the whole App Router project as carried `files`, with a `verify` promise like every other package.
  <br>**`template/` stays the single source of truth**, and the package is generated from it by `pnpm -C create-shio-app run emit` with `test/emit.test.mjs` failing the build on drift. A running instance reads packages off the classpath and cannot run a JS build, so the second copy is unavoidable — and an unavoidable second copy needs a guard, or `npm create shio-app` and `shio init --blueprint nextjs-starter` slowly stop producing the same project with nothing to say so. Same discipline as `shio-sections`' emit.
  <br>**Substitution is split by who knows the answer, and the rule is shared.** The server substitutes a package's *content*; the client substitutes its *carried files*, because the one parameter a starter needs is the project's own local identity and because the server never writes a project file anyway. The JS regex is now character-for-character `ShBlueprintParams`', so a package cannot have a parameter one half fills in and the other leaves standing — narrow enough that JSX (`style={{ color: "#666" }}`) is not a placeholder, which is what lets a starter tree carry both. `shio apply --blueprint` also substitutes now; it had been writing carried files verbatim, so a `{{param}}` landed on disk unsubstituted while the same run filled it in throughout the content.
  <br>**One production bug fell out of carrying a Next.js tree:** the registry's path-escape guard was `path.contains("..")`, which also rejects `app/[...slug]/page.tsx`. A dot run inside a segment is a filename; only a segment that *is* `..` traverses. Asserted directly in both directions — a security check that has been loosened is exactly the kind that must be shown still catching what it was written for (§XIV.4's lesson, applied to itself).
- **SH120** — **Console navigation reads adopt the CDA shapes** ([ShConsoleListing](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/object/dto/ShConsoleListing.java), [ShConsoleNavigationMapper](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/object/ShConsoleNavigationMapper.java), [ShConsoleShapeOverlapTest](../shio-app/src/test/java/com/viglet/shio/api/object/ShConsoleShapeOverlapTest.java)). `/object/{id}/path` and `/folder/{id}/path` return the CDA's own `ShCdaPath` — the shapes were already identical apart from `shSite` versus `site`. `/object/{id}/list` returns `ShCdaListing`'s `{folderId, folders, posts}` envelope with rows that are **strict supersets** of `ShCdaFolder` / `ShCdaPostSummary`: the CDA's components first, name for name and type for type, then the fields a console has and a delivery API cannot express (draft `state`/`published`/`publishStatus`, manual `position`, the post-type's human `title`).
  <br>**What it replaced was worse than a naming problem.** The listing serialized the `ShFolder`/`ShPostUnified` entities, so browsing a folder of five posts read each post's attributes, its folder, its folder's site and its post-type's whole field tree in order to render five rows. It also stopped repeating the site and the breadcrumb: `/path` is the one endpoint that answers "where am I", and the listing's copy was the one that would go stale, because it is the response people add fields to.
  <br>**A superset, not the record itself** — the CDA delivers published content and has no way to say "draft", and a console's job includes saying it. The guard is a shape test rather than a convention: a shared component that drifts in name, order or type fails the build (the SH162 mirror-test pattern, applied inside the backend). Paging is deliberately *not* copied: this listing returns a folder's children whole, so `page`/`size`/`totalPosts` would be three constants pretending to be a contract. That it is unpaged is a real limitation, filed as **SH165**.
  <br>One latent console bug surfaced on the way: the post-type picker read `/path` as a flat array, a shape the endpoint never returned, so its breadcrumb had always been just "Sites". One spelling everywhere is what stops that being an easy mistake to make.
- **SH162** — **The SDK type mirror is complete, and stays complete** ([ShCdaTypeScriptMirrorTest](../shio-app/src/test/java/com/viglet/shio/api/cda/ShCdaTypeScriptMirrorTest.java)). `ShCdaPost` had delivered `locale` + `availableLocales` since SH52 — the two fields a headless front end needs for a language switcher — and `@viglet/shio-client`'s `types.ts` declared neither, so the one feature the types exist to make usable was invisible to a typed consumer without a cast. The fields are added; the task is the **test**, because the drift was invisible precisely because nothing compared the two shapes and will happen again the next time a DTO grows. Names must match one-for-one **in both directions** (a component with no property is a feature the SDK cannot see; a property with no component is a field the CDA dropped and the SDK still promises), a new DTO must be listed as mirrored or as deliberately unmirrored *with a reason*, and primitives may not be declared optional because SH127 omits nulls and nothing else. Types are deliberately not compared — `Instant` is delivered as an ISO string and `JsonNode` as an arbitrary object, so a mapping table would be a second contract to keep in sync for far less than it costs. The parser self-tests against known content and against a synthetic drift, per §XIV.4: a lint that matches nothing passes forever.
- **SH166** — **A package's carried files say they are templates, and are reachable at all** ([ShBlueprintApplied.CarriedFile](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/blueprint/dto/ShBlueprintApplied.java), [ShBlueprintTerse](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/blueprint/ShBlueprintTerse.java), [ShMcpResources](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/agent/mcp/tools/ShMcpResources.java), [ShBlueprintCarriedFilesTest](../shio-app/src/test/java/com/viglet/shio/blueprint/ShBlueprintCarriedFilesTest.java)). SH119 split substitution by who knows the answer — the server fills a package's *content*, the client fills its *carried files*, because a project's npm name is local identity the server has no business being told — and an MCP-only caller was left holding source that still says `{{projectName}}`. The apply and plan responses now report each carried file with the placeholders standing in it, so `file package.json not-written placeholders=projectName` replaces a bare path. **The names are read from the bytes, not from the manifest's parameter list**: a package may declare a parameter its files never use, and reporting that one sends the caller hunting for a placeholder that is not there.
  <br>**Reading the task turned up a worse version of it.** The bodies were not merely unsubstituted for that caller — they were **unreachable**. They travel on `GET /agent/blueprints/{name}?include=files`, which a client with no HTTP of its own cannot call, so "your front end is thirteen files" named things that existed somewhere else. `shio://blueprint/{name}` now serves the parameter-by-parameter detail and `shio://blueprint/{name}/files` the bodies. A **resource**, not a tool argument, for two reasons that agree: it is reference material a session pins (this surface's own test for resource-versus-tool), and `shio_apply` measures 457 against a 460 per-tool ceiling with `tools/list` re-sent every turn (P3), so the argument that would have carried it does not fit. One bean serves both URIs because `ShMcpResource#matches` keys on the literal prefix before the first brace — two beans would both claim `shio://blueprint/…` and which answered would depend on sort order.
  <br>**Server-side substitution was the option refused, and the reason is not squeamishness.** The bodies do not travel on the apply response at all; they come from a **read** with no parameter values to substitute with, and giving that read some would put a write's arguments on a cacheable GET (SH116). Naming the placeholders is what lets a caller that fetched the bytes substitute for itself, from the `params` the same response echoes — defaults included, which is the half that makes it actionable.
- **SH167** — **The last blanket CSRF exemptions are narrowed** ([ShSecurityConfig](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/spring/security/ShSecurityConfig.java), [ShCsrfExemptionLintTest](../shio-app/src/test/java/com/viglet/shio/spring/security/ShCsrfExemptionLintTest.java), [ShAgentCsrfExemptionTest](../shio-app/src/test/java/com/viglet/shio/spring/security/ShAgentCsrfExemptionTest.java)). `/api/v2/cda/**`, `/api/v2/agent/**` and `/mcp` were exempt for every caller on the true premise that only stateless clients reach them. `ShStatelessRequestMatcher` — SH117's matcher, unchanged — now wraps all three, so the exemption covers exactly the callers that need it: a token client and the `shio` CLI hold no session cookie and are unaffected.
  <br>**The agent namespace is the one that mattered.** It is gated by `anyRequest().authenticated()` and nothing more, so a logged-in curator's session already reached `POST /api/v2/agent/batch` — the endpoint that deletes content — and a blanket exemption there is a cross-site write on the most destructive call in the product. The CDA is a pre-emption rather than a fix: a session-bearing CDA write already failed for want of `ROLE_CDA_WRITE`, so narrowing it changes nothing that works and means the check is in place the day something teaches the browser to reach it.
  <br>**The guard is a lint over the configuration, not a test of today's paths**, because SH117's lesson was that an exemption stops being safe when a *new* caller arrives and nothing in the arriving feature notices. Every entry in `ignoringRequestMatchers` is either session-narrowed or named in an allow-list with the reason a forged request there can do nothing an unauthenticated one could not. Beside it, four requests through the real filter chain assert the pair of status codes that distinguishes the two failure modes: **401** for a cookie-less agent write (passed CSRF, failed authentication — the agent path working) and **403** for a cookie-bearing one. Asserting only one would pass on a chain that rejects everything.
  <br>**`/graphql` is left blanket, deliberately and in writing** — no `Mutation` in the generated schema, and GraphiQL is a cookie-bearing browser the matcher would break for nothing. That premise is the same shape as the one that expired on the post-type API, so it is **SH234** rather than a comment. Reviewing the CDA also turned up **SH233**: the Universal Editor's `withCredentials: false` does not do what its comment says for a same-origin request.
- **SH233** — **The Universal Editor's save-back authenticates the way it always claimed to** ([ShApiTokenFilter](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/spring/security/auth/ShApiTokenFilter.java), [ShApiTokenFilterTest](../shio-app/src/test/java/com/viglet/shio/spring/security/auth/ShApiTokenFilterTest.java), [universal-editor.service.ts](../shio-react/src/services/universal-editor/universal-editor.service.ts)). An explicitly presented `Key` header now wins over an authentication already in the security context, on the delivery and agent namespaces where token auth lives. The filter used to return early whenever *anything* had authenticated — which reads as conservative and was the reason the editor could not save: the console is **same-origin** with the API, so the session cookie rides along whatever `withCredentials` says (that flag governs cross-origin requests only), `SecurityContextHolderFilter` restores the session before this filter runs, the `Key` header was never read, and the PATCH authenticated as a curator with no `ROLE_CDA_WRITE`.   <br>**It is not an escalation, and the reasoning is worth keeping.** Presenting a valid token *is* the authorization; its scope, site allow-list, expiry and rate limit bound the request exactly as they do for a cookie-less caller (a READ key that PATCHes is still the SH2 403, with the session not consulted as a fallback), the SH2 namespace confinement still means a `Key` cannot authenticate a console request at all, and a forged cross-site request cannot set a custom header without the target's CORS consent. A token that fails to resolve **leaves the context untouched** — a key is a request to be someone, not a request to stop being someone else — so the change is additive.
  <br>**The client half is the same fix from the other end.** The editor's private `axios.create()` was not just failing to dodge the cookie; it had silently opted out of every shared interceptor, including the CSRF one that SH167 made mandatory for a session-bearing caller on this path. It uses `@/lib/axios` now and passes `Key` per request.
  <br>**What is still uncovered, stated rather than implied:** nothing here proves the browser behaviour, because every test in this repository builds the request in Java or mocks the client. The five new filter tests pin *which credential wins*; the cookie-is-always-sent half is documented XHR behaviour, and the editor's own save path has no automated coverage at all — it needs a front end to embed, which is Block P.
- **SH234** — **The last blanket CSRF exemption's premise is enforced, not written down** ([ShCsrfExemptionLintTest](../shio-app/src/test/java/com/viglet/shio/spring/security/ShCsrfExemptionLintTest.java)). SH167 left `/graphql` exempt for every caller on two true premises — the delivery schema has no `Mutation`, so a forged POST cannot write, and GraphiQL is a cookie-bearing browser the narrowed matcher would break for no gain — and filed the question of what happens the day a mutation lands. The first premise is the same shape as "only the CLI reaches the post-type API": true, load-bearing, and expiring silently in whichever commit adds the mutation. So the lint now fails the build on a `Mutation` in `schema.graphqls` or a `.mutation(` in `ShGraphQLSchema`, and **its failure message is the decision, made in advance**: narrow `GRAPHQL_PATH` with `ShStatelessRequestMatcher`, move the constant from the blanket allow-list to the narrowed one, and set `spring.graphql.graphiql.enabled=false`. A mutation-capable delivery endpoint does not get a cookie-bearing playground in the console's browser; the alternatives are shipping a CSRF-aware GraphiQL replacement or accepting cross-site writes on the delivery API, and a query playground is not worth either. The finder self-tests against both spellings of a mutation and against the prose about mutations both files contain, per §XIV.4: a lint that matches nothing passes forever.

  <br>**It found the attribution's own numbers were order-dependent.** The batching pair wrote its five posts into the same folder the addressing and lint pairs measure, so whichever ran first changed the other's baseline: addressing read **26.2×** when batching had already run and **11.8×** when it had not. Batching writes to its own folder now, the class is method-name ordered so the scale comparison has its baseline, and every figure in the budgets file was re-measured.
  <br>**What the second size changes about the claim.** The **lint** is the only source that scales without bound: 15.5× → 139.6× on tokens and 5.0× → 45.0× on calls, one call against one read per candidate. **Addressing scales sublinearly** — 11.8× → 53.1× for nine times the content — because its baseline is a listing *plus* an id-keyed post read, the read is the larger and constant half (SH176 made it lean), and since SH165 the listing is paged, which caps the growth at one page however large the folder gets. - **SH237** — **"Select everything" means everything again** ([object.children.page.tsx](../shio-react/src/app/console/content/object.children.page.tsx)). - **SH240** — **The console's search box asks what the delivery API asks** ([ShPostUnifiedRepository](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/persistence/repository/post/ShPostUnifiedRepository.java), [ShConsoleListingPagingTest](../shio-app/src/test/java/com/viglet/shio/api/object/ShConsoleListingPagingTest.java)). SH165 moved the filter to the server as a title substring, faithfully reproducing what the browser's local filter did over the rows it held; the effect was that a curator who remembered a phrase from a page's *body* was told there was nothing there, by a system that could have found it. Five isolated pairs — addressing, projection, batching, discovery, lint — each with its own ratio floor, because the SH112 task ratios had fallen three blocks running against an *unchanged* agent path (SH117, SH120 and SH176 each made the baseline leaner) and one number per task could no longer distinguish "the protocol is cheaper" from "the old console was fat". A floor per source holds when the baseline improves and fails when that idea stops paying.
  <br>**What the measurement says, and it is not what the task ratios implied.** (Figures as corrected by SH239, which found this test's own first numbers were order-dependent.) **The lint carries the token claim and is the only source that scales without bound** — 15.5× on five posts, 139.6× on forty-five, 45.0× on calls — because it is one call against one read per candidate. **Addressing is second and scales sublinearly** (11.8× → 53.1×): its baseline is a listing *plus* a lean id-keyed read, and since SH165 the listing is paged, so the growth caps at one page. **Batching buys turns, not bytes** (5.0× / 6.1×; five posts' fields are sent either way). **Discovery is a round-trip claim and almost nothing else** (4.0× calls / **1.2×** tokens, the call ratio growing by one per folder) — P2 was always about turns. **Projection is the smallest source measured** (1.0× / 1.5×) and the easiest to point at, which is exactly why it needed separating: its baseline is the protocol itself, so it is the one number a wasteful console cannot inflate.

An aggregate mixes five independent savings, names none of them, and *falls* when the console gets leaner — so a team defending that number would be a team arguing against P1 and P5. What replaces it: per-source floors; ≈10× on tokens where it is real (addressing, the lint); and on calls a **session** — a canonical task is 3–4 calls after SH157, which is one agent session instead of three, which is what "≈6× fewer tool calls" was always a proxy for.
- **SH163** — **Renaming a post-type is a move, not an upsert** ([ShPostTypeAPI](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/post/type/ShPostTypeAPI.java), [ShPostTypeAdminService](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/post/type/ShPostTypeAdminService.java), [ShPostTypeRenamed](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/post/type/dto/ShPostTypeRenamed.java), [ShPostTypeRenameTest](../shio-app/src/test/java/com/viglet/shio/api/post/type/ShPostTypeRenameTest.java), [post-type.edit.page.tsx](../shio-react/src/app/console/content/post-type.edit.page.tsx)). `POST /api/v2/post-type/{name}/rename` with `{"to":"NewName"}`. The surface is keyed by name, which is right, and it meant the one thing a `PUT` could not express was a rename: `PUT /post-type/NewName` creates a **second** post-type, answers `200` with a definition that looks correct, and leaves the original holding its id, its attribute rows and every `sh_post_unified` row that points at it. SH134's defect one level up, with SH134's answer — one operation that moves, and a response that says what moved.
  <br>**What actually has to move is smaller than it looks, and that is the finding.** A post references its type by **id**, so renaming the row carries the content for free; what breaks silently is the one place the model stores a post-type *by name* — a `Multi Select`'s `multiselect.postType` (SH154). Those are rewritten and returned as `referencesUpdated`, because a field that quietly narrows to a type which no longer exists is exactly the breakage a rename is supposed not to cause. The response also counts the posts, since the workaround it replaces reported success and moved none of them.

Renaming to the current name is a **noop**, which is what makes a re-run safe (P5).

The CLI has no rename verb yet: a renamed `shio/post-types/*.json` still pushes as a create.
- **SH165** — **The console listing is paged** ([ShConsoleListing](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/object/dto/ShConsoleListing.java), [ShObjectAPI](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/object/ShObjectAPI.java), [ShObjectNavigationService](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/object/ShObjectNavigationService.java), [ShConsoleListingSort](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/object/ShConsoleListingSort.java), [ShConsoleListingPagingTest](../shio-app/src/test/java/com/viglet/shio/api/object/ShConsoleListingPagingTest.java), [object.children.page.tsx](../shio-react/src/app/console/content/object.children.page.tsx)). `GET /api/v2/object/{id}/list` takes `page`/`size`/`sort`/`q` and answers with the CDA's own `page`/`size`/`totalPosts`, so the console envelope is now `ShCdaListing`'s exactly — SH120 aligned the names and left the paging out rather than shipping three constants, and that absence is what this closes. The browser appends pages behind a "Showing N of M" + Load more footer.
  <br>**The order and the filter had to move with it, and that is the whole design.** A paged listing with a client-side sort silently sorts *one page*, and a client-side search searches one — the half-migration §XIV.7 warned about, which answers `200` and looks exactly like a correct answer. So `sort` and `q` are the server's now, and an unknown `sort` is a teaching **400** rather than a fallback to the default: once the listing is paged, answering in another order returns other **rows**. What the browser still sorts is the folders, because it still has all of them; the two halves render folders-then-posts rather than interleaved, since merging a complete set with a partial one into one sorted sequence is the thing that would read as a lie.
  <br>**The DRAFT-preference became a predicate, not an in-memory dedup.** The CDA pages draft-preferred rows by loading the folder whole and slicing the list, which makes the response smaller and the query no cheaper; `pageConsoleRows` qualifies a row if it is the DRAFT or is the PUBLISHED row of a post with no DRAFT, which is exactly one row per logical id — so `LIMIT`, `ORDER BY` and the count are the database's, and a post with both rows takes one slot and is counted once. It compares `p.shFolder` to an entity (the FK column, no join), which is what keeps it clear of the SH22 `@TenantId` JOINED-join hazard.

Block O's lesson one component late, found by asking who else reads this response.
- **What the block did to the measurement, stated plainly.** Block M measured **3.8×–23.3×** cheaper on tokens. Block N measures **2.6×–12.6×** against an *unchanged* agent path, and the entire difference is SH117 and SH120 fixing the baseline: post-type listings stopped shipping ids, widget objects, dates and owners, and folder listings stopped shipping entity graphs (`fix-broken-link`'s baseline 7145 → 3877, `translate-site`'s 10033 → 5539, both roughly halved). **Tokens now clear the spec's ≈10× on one task of four, down from three; tool calls clear ≈6× nowhere, best 3.2×.** So a large part of the advantage was never the protocol — it was the console reads being entity-shaped, and it is now on both sides. What remains is the part worth defending: addressing instead of id round trips, one batch instead of N writes, a context pack instead of a crawl, a lint that names the defective post instead of a read-everything sweep. The floors in [token-budgets.properties](../shio-app/src/test/resources/token-budgets.properties) drop with the measurement rather than being defended, and the file says all of this at length. **SH164** owns re-establishing the token claim on its actual sources.
- **SH541** — LICENSE and the README badge said Apache 2.0 while ten package.json files, the Claude Code plugin manifest and 182 source headers said GPL-3.0 - so every published npm package and every file a reader opens carried the copyleft claim, and only the file nobody fetches carried the real one. All 195 files now say Apache 2.0, including the two READMEs whose License section was the bare string; the POM, which declared nothing at all, gained a licenses block, because a consumer resolving Maven metadata got the same silence a wrong value would have been. The plugin manifest's own test asserted the old value and moved with it. cli/src/verify-baseline.mjs is rewritten byte-safe: it carries a deliberate NUL as a join separator, which is why git calls it binary, and a text-mode pass would have eaten it. 1471 backend tests and 1058 JS tests green after.
- **SH659** — The drive now publishes too, but only on the site provision.mjs created — matched on the description it writes, with candidates ordered so ours is tried first.
- **SH645** — `pnpm test` is now `scripts/test-with-log.mjs`: the same eight-package filter, spawned, with every byte streamed to stdout and to `shio-js-test.log`, exiting with the child's code. The deliverable is capture and not diagnosis, because the failure has never reproduced and the two sightings recorded a count - both runs were read through a grep for the summary line, which is the one thing a filter leaves behind. A script rather than a shell pipeline: this repository is driven from PowerShell and from Git Bash, `tee` and `Tee-Object` differ in buffering, encoding and what they do to the exit code, and a runner that swallowed a non-zero exit would trade the one reliable gate for the flake it is chasing. Verified in both directions - green, and against a deliberately failing test, where the exit is 1, the failing test's name is in the log and the closing line names the log. `pnpm test:raw` keeps the unlogged form and the existing `/*.log` already ignores the file. Both cheap causes the task named are ruled out, so the next sighting starts from the log rather than from them: every cli test uses `mkdtemp` and none a fixed temp path, `create-shio-app`'s emit test only reads and compares rather than running `emit` into the tree, and every test server binds `listen(0)`. What is left is contention under pnpm's concurrent workspace run, since the suite has never failed with `cli/` run on its own - and that is a hypothesis, not a finding.
- **SH649** — `roadkeep.toml` declares `reserved_ids`, and the gate goes from twelve findings to one. Nine of the ten remaining at HEAD were ids this project spoke for and deliberately never wrote as a line, in two families: epics that own a sub-range - SH62, SH67, SH74 and SH19, whose own ledger entry says "tracked as SH19 in ROADMAP" while every slice of it landed under another number - and ranges retired with their block, SH17/SH18 for the dropped GraalJS engine and SH23 with SH27-SH31 for the absorbed marketplace epic. Declared rather than reworded, because the fix the lint suggested - spell the example outside the prefix - would make the non-goals stop naming what they refuse, and a decision not to build something has to keep its address or the argument loses it. The declaration buys what the rule was right about: the deriver skips them because they ARE taken, the gate stops calling every mention a hazard, and a genuine typo still fails because it is not on the list. The capability is RK1031, filed against roadkeep from this repository three iterations earlier and shipped there, so this is the second half of one finding rather than a workaround. The tenth finding is not this defect at all and is filed separately: SH169 shipped inside a ledger entry led by SH154, and a per-id reader cannot see it - `roadkeep show` answers "never written or was retired" about a task that is in the file. Writing this entry walked into the very hazard it closes, which is worth recording: naming the follow-up's id in this sentence before the line existed spent that id, the deriver stepped past it, and `renumber` then refused to reuse it - so the sentence names no id at all.
- **SH655** — The docs instruments run in CI, split by the cost the task asked to decide. `docs-vocabulary` and `docs-stack` touch no instance - one reads source, the other build files - so `pnpm conformance:docs` is its own job beside `pnpm test`, on every push, answering in about a second: 12 assertions over 36 executable blocks across 13 pages. Only `docs-examples` calls requireInstance, so it stays in the conformance job behind the boot; putting the pair there too would make the cheapest question anyone asks about the published pages wait on the most expensive gate. Both jobs now check out vigletdocs/vigletdocs.github.io - public, so no token - and set SHIO_DOCS_DIR at it, which is the wiring that was missing: the default is one machine's drive letter, `suites.yml` cloned only this repository, and SH499 chose absent to be a hard failure rather than a skip so an unread checkout could not pass quietly. The consequence is the sharp part and it is why this was a task: the instrument SH628 landed was in that state from the day it shipped - not a check that passed, a check nobody was running, anywhere but one laptop. `ci-gates.test.mjs` holds three facts, because they break apart: the checkout exists, something points SHIO_DOCS_DIR at it (a clone nothing points at is the same absent directory with an extra step), and the docs script excludes docs-examples - a job without an instance running it would fail on requireInstance and read as the documentation being wrong. Verified locally in both directions: green against the real checkout, and two hard failures naming the clone command against a path that is not there.
- **SH656** — `ShBoundPropertiesReachabilityLintTest` lands first and the deletions follow it, which is the order that mattered: written for `shio.git` it immediately found a second, `ShMgmtProperties` binding `shio.mgmt.enabled`, documented as "Enable the management interface" and injected by nothing. The defect was never the dead class - `docs-vocabulary` derives the legitimate `shio.*` vocabulary from these very classes, so the published configuration reference documented `shio.git.url` and PASSED the gate, and an operator who sets it gets no error and no way to learn it was never read. A documentation check cannot see a defect in the vocabulary it checks against. A third needed the rule sharpened: prefix coverage alone is too weak for the catch-all `shio` prefix, so the first segment under a prefix must be a field the binding class declares, relaxed the way Spring binds - which found `shio.plugin.blogger`, naming a class this repository does not contain, with no false positive anywhere else in the file. Two classes, three properties lines and three published rows removed; the exemption map is empty, because a bound prefix nothing injects has no honest reason to exist and an entry would have to survive "then why is it bound?". Source-level rather than reflective: Spring injects by type, so a consumed class names itself at the injection site, and `ShSourceText.code` strips prose first so a javadoc mention cannot make a dead class read as live. Red at HEAD naming both classes, green after. The other half of why the page shipped is filed separately as SH663 - the property check reads fenced blocks, and the configuration reference is a table.
- **SH657** — `RAW_TEXT_FIELDS` is derived from the table that declares the fields, so the list and its own stated rule can no longer disagree. It spelled four pairs by hand while its sentence said "the fields the product declares as Ace Editor - CSS/JavaScript", and `ShRenderPostTypes` declares six: `Theme.TOKENS` and `SiteScripts.SCRIPTS` were each added there on their own task, correctly, and neither reached the list, because nothing joined them - the rule lived in prose and the list in code, and they drifted twice without a single thing able to notice. Both are JSON in a JavaScript editor, so what they were one template away from is `<script type="application/json">{{TOKENS}}</script>` emitting `&quot;` for every key: a document that does not parse, which is SH461's defect and SH555's a third and fourth time. The widget is the whole rule and `Ace Editor - HTML` stays out deliberately - a PageLayout's or Region's HTML is a template, rendered rather than interpolated, so it reaches no stash and marking it raw would say something true about a path that does not exist. `ShRawTextFieldParityTest` names all six pair by pair rather than recomputing them, because once two things cannot drift there is nothing left to tell a live rule from a vacuous one, and it also holds what is deliberately not raw. Two existing guards earned their keep on the first run: `ShByteStabilityLintTest` refused the draft's `Map.copyOf`, whose iteration order comes from a per-JVM salt (P5), and the suite is 1698 green with the derivation in place.
- **SH660** — `isObjectReference` guards both resolvers, so a field value that cannot be an id is never looked up. The widget renders two different things with one component and that is the whole finding: on another post's field the value is a reference the content browser wrote as `selection.id`, and on the File type's own FILE field it is the stored file name, because ShStaticFileService puts `fileName` there and keeps the bytes under the post's id. The resolver assumed the first, so opening any uploaded file issued GET /v2/post/xp/<name> and GET /v2/folder/<name>, both 404 - and nothing reported it, because each call ends `.catch(() => null)`, the widget rendered its null branch and the page returned 200. The only witness was the network tab, which is why it took a probe that reads FAILED REQUESTS to see it at all. The rule is the value's shape rather than the field's identity: a reference in this console is an object id and an object id is a UUID, so anything else is a value the field holds. The narrow alternative - skip when this is the File type's FILE field - couples a generic widget to one system post-type and would be wrong for the next field that stores a name. `content-select.widget.tsx` carries the same guard as a precaution rather than a fix: its values are always ids today and the failure mode is identical and equally silent. The assertion is the decision and not the regex - the two values this field really holds, plus the near-misses a looser rule would let through - and it also holds that both resolvers call the guard BEFORE the lookup, since a guard below the first fetch would let out the request it exists to prevent.
- **SH663** — The extractor reads Markdown tables, so the page the property check exists for is finally one it reads. It took fenced blocks tagged `properties` and `configuration-reference.md` has none - its whole content is a table, one row per key - so the page whose entire subject is the property vocabulary contributed nothing to the count that checks it. Independent of SH656 and that is why fixing that one did not close this: with the vocabulary correct, a page naming a key that was never bound at all would still pass, because the row is not read. The rule is narrow because a table cell is prose - only the first cell of a row, in a table whose header names a property column, and only a dotted key. Each bound was met rather than imagined: a backticked key in a Description column is the page citing itself while explaining another setting, and a bare `max-width` is a field named relative to a prefix `search-caching.md` spells in a fence three lines above, which this reader cannot join. Both are declined and COUNTED - `tables past` and `rows relative` in the printout - because a check that silently covered some tables would be worse than one covering none. Measured: 14 property blocks became 22 and 77 known keys became 121 assertable subjects, with 7 tables past and 4 rows relative. One more finding came with it: `shio.turing.sites.<ShioSite>` is the documentation's own placeholder notation, so a key carrying angle brackets is skipped rather than resolved - a wildcard would match anything after a dot, and demanding a literal binding would make the page less readable to satisfy a check. Proved by injecting `shio.invented.key` as a table row and watching the gate name it.
- **SH664** — The console-check fixture no longer declares the instance as its own front end, so the editor drive can select it; a test holds the fixture and the drive's exclusion together.
- **SH667** — console-check gained --strict, which CI passes and which turns any editor-drive skip into a failure; ci-gates asserts both halves, and the debt SH238/SH659 carried is paid.
- **SH662** — SH169 has its own ledger entry, so show answers and every per-id reader can see it; RK1051 had shipped and the blocker recorded here was stale.
- **SH665** — The config registers react-hooks itself, so the lint loads; it gates in CI against a 33-finding suppressions baseline, and the one real defect it hid is fixed.
- **SH666** — The export composes through ShAddress.post instead of adding strings, so both stored spellings name one address, and a lint fails the next bypass.
- **SH668** — **Every §X.Y in the rationale resolves, and a reader in `pnpm test` says so** ([improvements-debt.test.mjs](../cli/test/improvements-debt.test.mjs)). Sixteen citations pointed at headings that were not there while `roadkeep lint` called the file clean — the thirteen this was filed on, plus `§VIII`, which was cited in the preamble *and* offered in the table of contents because Block H's family heading went when the block shipped. The mechanism is `ship` doing its job: it drops the section of the task that shipped and cannot know who was pointing at it, so `section.stale` had the question one way round and nothing had it the other.
- **SH669** — **The licence is a claim about this repo, checked the way its versions are** ([docs-stack.conformance.mjs](../cli/conformance/docs-stack.conformance.mjs)). SH541 moved 195 files from GPL-3.0 to Apache-2.0 and the docs landing page kept a `GPL v3` pill after it — the most-read fact on that page, and the one subject a reader may not act on wrongly. The SPDX id in `package.json` is now cross-read against `LICENSE` so no single file can move alone, which is SH541's own defect turned into the pair that catches it. Found by Block N's completion sweep rather than by a task, which is the argument for having one. Fixing it exposed a second defect in the instrument: `at()` read `page.file` where `pages()` has only ever produced `label`, so **every** failure message in that suite died on `Cannot read properties of undefined` instead of naming the line it promises — invisible for as long as the suite was green, and the reason the licence check is asked to fail rather than trusted.
- **SH672** — A walk over the suites classifies each floor by what it counts and refuses an absolute one over a corpus meant to empty — the three named were at 6 citations against a floor of 5.
- **SH680** — The bootstrap passes its arguments to run, so --server.port=8099 now answers on 8099 where it silently came up on 2710 — and a lint refuses the argument-less form.
- **SH681** — The local login resolves authorities through the same resolver OAuth2 and OIDC use, so the seeded admin carries ROLE_ADMIN and the blueprint reload stops answering 403 to an administrator.
- **SH706** — SHIO_ADMIN_PASSWORD gives a container a usable admin login on first start, through one service the setup screen now delegates to, and it never overwrites nor fails startup.
- **SH735** — A failing run is copied to shio-js-test.red.log and a green one is not, so the re-run that checks whether a flake reproduces no longer destroys the only record of it.
- **SH737** — The vacuity check now asserts the heading scan found every anchor the roadmap points at, a yes/no derived from the roadmap instead of a floor pinned near the count it watches.
- **SH729** — ShLiquibaseEntityConstraintLintTest parses the changelogs for unique and not-null constraints and fails naming any the entity metadata does not also declare; it found the agent-memory upsert index, which the suite could not see.
- **SH731** — A reference is now spelled see SHnnn and the reader skips it, chosen over the first-id-is-subject rule by measurement: that one loses credit for 58 genuinely asserted ids, this one for none.
- **SH738** — The classifier now walks the Java suites too and knows AssertJ's spelling of a bound, so the half of the repository SH737 happened in is inside the population it reports.
- **SH739** — The sweep checklist now names readme-surface.test.mjs and marks which rows it derives, and that pointer is asserted, so renaming the guard fails the document that sends people to it.
- **SH740** — support/source-text.mjs is the one stripper and source-scan.test.mjs the lint: fourteen scans declare code, prose or both, and Markdown gets unquoted() so a quoted claim is not read as a claim.
- **SH741** — TOLERATED is the sixth row in LEDGERS and the count is asserted at six, with a staleness check asking whether the floor each exemption excuses still exists, over the scan the lint itself uses.
- **SH742** — The population is found by naming a path inside this repository rather than by a constant's spelling, which takes it from 15 to 23 and finally includes the three readers that scan the published docs.
- **SH745** — assertion-debt now prints the open tasks the suite already asserts, deliberately as a report rather than a failure, because red-first assertions put an open id in the suite legitimately.
- **SH752** — `cli/test/roadmap-blocks.test.mjs` fails the run when a block heading stands over no open task, which is proof its completion sweep did not finish — `block drop` is the sweep's last step and the only thing allowed to remove a heading. It asserts what is decidable (the heading is gone) and deliberately not that the sweep happened, which no file here can claim. Found by running `stats` during Block O's sweep and seeing three other zeros: I since 2026-08-04, Q since 2026-08-12, S since 2026-08-13. All three swept in the same commit — their COVERAGE rows were already green, so the repair was the site's backlog verdict and the three headings, and Block S's was not cosmetic: `shio-site/README.md` named SH540 as "all that is left" for a day after it was retired. The reader is guarded by its own second test, which requires it to count a task line, ignore the `- Block L` priority entry and a non-goal bullet, and report an empty block — the last one being the whole point.

## Block L — Agent safety & human-in-the-loop (SH74)

> The block that makes the rest adoptable. An agent-driven CMS is only usable if the answer to
> "what if it gets it wrong" is a mechanism rather than a promise, and the three guards here are
> deliberately different shapes because they fail differently: a credential that cannot publish,
> a delete that needs the plan it was shown, and a queue that can put things back.
>
> **The invariant held throughout:** the agent path is never a privilege escalation. Every guard
> is *narrower* than what an agent could reach before — nothing on this surface gained a
> capability, and the SH22 tenant isolation, the SH54 ACL and the SH2 site allow-list still
> decide everything they decided before.

- **SH106** — **`AGENT` token scope + session identity** ([ShApiTokenScope](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/persistence/model/token/ShApiTokenScope.java), [ShApiTokenFilter](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/spring/security/auth/ShApiTokenFilter.java), [ShAgentSessionContext](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/agent/ShAgentSessionContext.java), [ShAgentSessionFilter](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/agent/ShAgentSessionFilter.java), [v2026.3.11.yaml](../shio-app/src/main/resources/db/changelog/v2026.3.11.yaml)). Until now an agent ran on one of two credentials and both were wrong: a `WRITE` CDA token — the Universal Editor's key, which patches published content outside the agent protocol's guards — or a console username and password, which is every capability the human has and cannot expire. `AGENT` is the third: it writes on `/api/v2/agent/**` and `/mcp`, reads drafts like `PREVIEW`, carries `ROLE_AGENT`, and deliberately **not** `ROLE_CDA_WRITE`. On the CDA it stays read-only, which is the entire reason it is a scope of its own rather than an alias for `WRITE`. It extends the SH2/SH5/SH13 model (expiry, per-site allow-list, rate limit) instead of adding a parallel one (P10).
  <br>**The session id got the column SH75 deferred.** `ShHistory.agent_session_id` makes "show me everything that run changed" a `where` clause instead of a `LIKE` over an actor string, and `owner` went back to naming only the human whose credential was used — one fact per field. Rows written before this keep the old `alice (agent:7f3c…)` suffix; they predate the column and nothing can honestly backfill them.
  <br>**It is no longer MCP's session.** The REST agent surface writes too — `/agent/batch`, `/agent/apply`, everything the CLI drives — and a review queue that could only see MCP's changes would have a hole in it exactly where the most common client is. `ShAgentSessionFilter` accepts the same `Mcp-Session-Id` header on the agent namespace; it deliberately **does not mint one per request**, because a session is a *run*, and one session per call is the same as having none — the reviewer would face two hundred one-change sessions instead of one thing to approve.
- **SH107** — **Draft-by-default + publish gate** (`api_token.may_publish`, [ShAgentBatchService](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/agent/ShAgentBatchService.java)). Agent writes already landed in DRAFT and publishing was already a separate op; what was missing is that anything able to write was able to publish. `mayPublish` is now a per-credential capability, **off unless granted**, enforced on the batch path — which is also the apply path and the blueprint path, because a desired-state document compiles to `post.publish` ops before it reaches the writer. One check, not four.
  <br>**Two deliberate calls.** It is checked **before the first write**, so a refusal is "you cannot publish" rather than a half-built site with a 403 at the end; and it refuses a **`dryRun` too**, because an agent should learn it cannot publish while planning, not after building twelve pages around the assumption. A console-authenticated caller has no token and is unaffected — the SH54 ACL is what bounds a human — and the SH10 CDA write path is untouched, because there a person is the one clicking.
  <br>**It is a tightening, and the changelog says so:** an existing `WRITE` token that used to publish through the agent surface now needs `mayPublish`. That is the point of the task; the alternative default would have made the flag decorative.
- **SH108** — **Destructive-op confirm tokens** ([ShAgentConfirm](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/agent/ShAgentConfirm.java)). `post.delete`, `folder.delete` and any `prune` that would remove something take two calls: a `dryRun` hands back a `confirm` digest over the deletions, and the real run must send it back. The token makes two promises at once — an agent cannot destroy what it did not just render, and it cannot destroy something that **changed underneath it**, because a prune re-derives its deletions from current state and a page somebody else added since the plan moves the digest.
  <br>**What it covers is exactly the deletions**, sorted so the same intent always hashes the same (P5), and nothing else: re-confirming a document because a headline changed would train callers to paste the token back without reading, and a confirmation nobody reads is worse than none. A batch that destroys nothing needs no token and is handed none. Absent is a **428** with the token and the list; wrong is a **409** naming what would go now. Both are bounded at 20 addresses with a real count and a pointer to the plan — SH138's rule, applied to the one list where truncation is most dangerous.
  <br>**The CLI does the two-step for you** (`applyConfirmed` in [agent-client.mjs](../cli/src/agent-client.mjs)): a document that declares `prune` is planned first, the deletions are printed **before** the apply — the terminal is where the CLI's human sees them — and the token goes back with the write. Only pruning documents pay the extra round trip, and a prune that would delete nothing gets no token and needs none, so the flag alone is not the test.
- **SH109** — **Review queue** ([ShReviewService](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/review/ShReviewService.java), [ShReviewAPI](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/review/ShReviewAPI.java), [review.list.page.tsx](../shio-react/src/app/console/admin/review/review.list.page.tsx)). "The agent proposed N changes": the runs, what each one touched, and **approve** / **revert**. `GET /api/v2/review/sessions`, `/sessions/{id}`, `POST …/approve`, `POST …/revert` — an API, not a console-only feature (P1), console-authenticated and deliberately **not** on the agent namespace, because an agent's own credential should not be what approves its work.
  <br>**It is a view over the audit, not a proposal table.** A second copy of the content waiting to be accepted is the design the unified model already rejected: a post has a DRAFT row and a PUBLISHED row, and the draft *is* the proposal. So approve = publish the run's drafts (exactly the step SH107 keeps the agent from taking), and revert reuses SH14 restore and the SH55 trash. Nothing here is a third mechanism for saying what changed (P10).
  <br>**Revert is per entry and refuses to guess.** A `CREATE` is undone by trashing (recoverable, not purged), an `UPDATE` by restoring from the published snapshot, a `DELETE` by untrashing, a `PUBLISH` by unpublishing — and an entry with no honest undo, like an update to a post that was never published, is **reported with its reason** instead of approximated. The list walks newest-first so a create-then-publish pair ends as "unpublished, then trashed" rather than as a publish applied to a post that no longer exists. Every action is ACL-checked per post: reviewing is not a privilege.
  <br>The console page reuses the **SH14 diff dialog** unchanged, which only works because SH176 made the post read carry its post-type — before Block O the dialog had no schema to render.
- **SH200** — **A folder delete leaves a trace, and can be undone** ([ShFolderWriteService](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/folder/ShFolderWriteService.java), [ShFolder](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/persistence/model/folder/ShFolder.java), [ShFolderRepository](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/persistence/repository/folder/ShFolderRepository.java), [v2026.3.13.yaml](../shio-app/src/main/resources/db/changelog/v2026.3.13.yaml)). The cascade cleared its subtree with `shPostUnifiedRepository.deleteAll(...)` — the repository, not the post writer — and everything this block built hangs off that writer, so one line skipped all of it at once: the SH55 trash (rows simply gone), the SH51 audit (nothing recorded, so the deletion was invisible to the SH88 feed and there was nothing for the SH109 queue to revert) and the `DELETE` lifecycle event (no SH12 webhook, and SH38's cleanup listener never ran, so the file bytes leaked forever). **The inversion is what made it urgent rather than untidy:** the most destructive operation on the surface — the one SH108's confirm token exists to gate — was also the least recoverable and the least observable. A curator who deleted forty pages one at a time could restore them; the same curator using the folder's delete button could not.
  <br>**The fix is a delegation, not six re-implementations** (P10 inside the engine, and SH139's rule one level down): each post goes through `ShPostUnifiedWriteService#delete`, so a folder delete means exactly what forty post deletes mean. That forced the folder half of the soft-delete — `ShFolder.deleted_date` — because a trashed post keeps its `folder_id` and `sh_post_unified.folder_id → ShObject` is FK `onDelete NO ACTION`: the folder rows have to outlive the gesture. **The FK ordering that motivated the old direct `deleteAll` is satisfied at purge time instead**, exactly where §XII.6 predicted it would move. `restore` and `purge` join `listTrash` on the same service; `DELETE /v2/folder/{id}` is now reversible, with `GET /v2/folder/trash`, `POST /v2/folder/{id}/untrash` and `DELETE /v2/folder/{id}/purge` beside it, and the console's trash page lists sections and posts in one list.
  <br>**Four calls worth keeping.** (1) **No `@SQLRestriction` on `ShFolder`**, unlike `ShPostUnified`: a restriction fires when a `@ManyToOne` to a folder is initialized, so a trashed post's `getShFolder()` would throw — and that association is precisely what the trash listing reads. The exclusion lives in `ShFolderRepository`, whose derived finders are spelled out as JPQL with `deletedDate is null`, keeping their names so no call site had to change and no plain-named finder is left for the next reader to use by accident. (2) **A restore returns what *this* deletion trashed** — the delete stamps one instant down the subtree, and anything marked earlier stays in the trash, compared on loaded instants rather than in SQL, because timestamp equality is a fractional-second promise three engines do not make the same way. (3) **The trash lists sections, not folders**: one row per thing a human deleted, since eleven sub-folder rows would imply eleven decisions. (4) **Still no lifecycle event on the delete** — SH55's rule, not an omission: a reversible trash has no side effects, and the webhook plus the byte cleanup fire on the purge. The audit records the folder *and* every post, so reverting the folder's entry in the SH109 queue restores the whole subtree in one move, which is the gesture a human means. `/agent/changes` grew a folder-address fallback for the same reason a deletion needs one at all: an entry nobody can address is a change nobody can act on. 9 tests ([ShFolderTrashTest](../shio-app/src/test/java/com/viglet/shio/api/folder/ShFolderTrashTest.java), [ShAgentChangesTest](../shio-app/src/test/java/com/viglet/shio/api/agent/ShAgentChangesTest.java)). → was §XII.6
- **SH201** — **The console's move and copy authorize both ends** ([ShObjectAPI](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/object/ShObjectAPI.java)). `requireWrite(destId)` and nothing else, so write on any single folder was enough to relocate content *out of* a subtree the caller could not write — a removal, from the owner's point of view — and to copy content they had never been granted read on. A move now requires WRITE on every source, a copy requires READ, and the checks run over the whole request body **before** the write service starts, so a partially-authorized batch is refused whole rather than moving the ids that happened to be listed first.
  <br>**This is the block's invariant read from the other end.** SH106–SH109 were all argued as tightenings — every guard narrower than what an agent could reach before — and the agent path has checked both ends since SH134/SH137. After Block L it was in places *stricter than the console*, and where that happens the console is the hole. The rule to carry forward is symmetrical: **the two surfaces enforce the same ACL, and whichever is stricter is the correct one** — a curator's session is not a lower bar than an agent's credential, it is a different one. Explicitly *not* a reason to loosen the agent path to match. 4 tests ([ShObjectMoveAuthorizationTest](../shio-app/src/test/java/com/viglet/shio/api/object/ShObjectMoveAuthorizationTest.java)). → was §XII.7
> **SH110** (agent budget guards) **is not in this block**: per-session call/write/storage ceilings layer on SH45's per-tenant metering, and SH45 has not shipped. Building the ceiling first would mean a second metering mechanism to reconcile later.
- **SH430** — A mutating agent endpoint now refuses a query parameter it does not declare, teaching where `dryRun` belongs; the allow-list is read off each handler.
- **SH591** — `ShSite` carries a `scratch` column, `site.upsert` reads `data.scratch:true` on the create branch and nowhere else, and `shio site rm --scratch` sweeps every site carrying it in one confirmation instead of thirteen. The create-only rule is the whole safety argument rather than a limitation: a flag an existing site could gain would make the sweep a fast way to delete a site somebody chose to keep, while a flag set at creation was declared in a document a human could read before there was anything in it to lose. Nothing in SH108 changed — the token has always been per batch, and what was missing was something to compose the document from. The second half is the listing: `shio context` and `shio site` mark the disposable ones, because thirteen sites with no difference between the two a human curates and the eleven an agent left behind is a list the human cannot act on.
- **SH222** — Both design questions settled. The surface is a verb on the existing vocabulary rather than a new tool - post.restore and folder.restore, so a restore costs no MCP schema on a budget paid every turn - and the listing is find?trash=true, a shape over the read that already lists posts, which forces the id: form because a trashed post keeps a friendly URL that no longer resolves. No confirm token: a restore is not destructive and it is audited, and a token would put a round trip in front of the one call somebody makes in a hurry. Two defects found on the way: getTenantId() is null when unset, so the trash listing reported empty on a single-tenant instance, and a required key the vocabulary declares must be enforced the way every other op enforces it.
- **SH223** — The stated defect was mostly gone: delete already trashes each root folder before purging it, so the posts leave through the SH55 trash with their audit rows, the feed and the DELETE events - the section described a JPA cascade the service no longer relies on. What was still missing is the row for the SITE, so the largest deletion in the product was the only one that left nothing saying it happened, while its posts and folders were audited one and two levels down. ShContentSubject gains SITE and the delete records itself after the delete succeeds. Whether a deleted site is itself trashed is the design question left, and it is a schema change plus a name-collision teaching error rather than a service fix: SH648.
- **SH224** — purge fired the DELETE lifecycle event and wrote no audit row, so the reversible half of the trash was fully recorded and the irreversible half recorded nothing - and a caller walking the feed saw a post enter the trash and never learned it was gone for good. PURGE is its own action rather than a second DELETE, because those are the two states a reader most needs to tell apart. It takes the actor the endpoints already have, and a cascade passes null honestly rather than attributing to whoever was nearest. Threading it created an overload pair, and SH358's lint refused the shape rather than the annotation: its advice is to collapse, which is what shipped - the first attempt ran the native purge with no transaction because a delegation is a self-invocation.
- **SH225** — A permission decision no longer depends on how folders are fetched: the entry points carry their own transaction and the ancestor walk resolves parent ids by query.
- **SH226** — One resolver, ShLiveObject.of, is the only spelling for resolving an object id, and ShLiveObjectInvariantTest fails the build on any production read that skips it - which on its first run found two unguarded call sites, one of them a live defect: a section could be created inside a trashed folder and then appear in no listing.
- **SH727** — An absent system File type is an empty listing rather than a refusal, and find is not reached at all — while a type the caller did name still refuses.
- **SH648** — A site delete now trashes and `site.restore`/`/untrash` bring it back with its content; a trashed site keeps its unique name, and the create that meets it is told where the name went.
- **SH650** — ShAclAssociationWalkLintTest fails the build when a security-relevant read navigates an association, with the banned getters derived from the entity model rather than listed; the standing count is zero.
- **SH719** — A unique index over site, state, locale and furl makes a second live post at one address impossible; the racer that loses gets a duplicate-url 409 whose fix is retry, which an upsert can act on.
- **SH720** — verify's duplicate check counts distinct post ids across both states, so the draft pair its own refusal promised to report is reported; two rows of one post stay one claimant, which is what keeps it off every edit.
- **SH721** — A read can hand back a state digest and a write op can carry it as `expect`, refused as stale-expectation when it no longer holds; the default stays last-write-wins, so only an agent that cares pays.
- **SH722** — ShUnstableSortLintTest fails a sort whose only key is one that repeats, and the seven it found — CDA fields, the GraphQL schema, the console form, navigation and a write path — all break the tie by name.
- **SH728** — cli/test/instance-assumptions.test.mjs classifies every post-type a conformance suite names as seeded, provisioned by that suite, or a declared assumption, reading the seeded set from the import file so it cannot go stale.
- **SH730** — post.move, post.delete and post.publish take `expect` too, publish comparing the draft so it does not refuse every publish that changes something; the vocabulary paid for the four keys by trimming prose.
- **SH732** — The trash is classified reachable and dropped from the manifest's elsewhere map, and an exception now names the ops that would close it, so one shut by another road fails instead of persisting.
- **SH733** — post.delete and folder.delete take `data.purge:true`, so an agent can release a deleted asset's bytes and fire the DELETE webhook; the modifier is stated once in the grammar and the ceiling moved 680 to 720 with the argument.
- **SH734** — A credential's writes are counted across a configurable window and refused with a 429 naming the reset instant; dry runs are free, a refused run keeps its charge, and the ceiling is off until an operator sets one.
- **SH749** — `ShFileStorageService#copy` duplicates the source id's whole directory, so a copied `File` post answers 200 with its bytes instead of 404ing at delivery. Asked of the storage rather than of the post-type — "does this id have a directory" is the same question one syscall cheaper and cannot disagree with the layout, so an ordinary post is a no-op. Copied, not shared: pointing the copy at the source's directory is cheaper and wrong the first time either is purged, since `ShStaticFileCleanupListener` frees a directory on DELETE, so one asset's purge would blank every copy of it. Both surfaces get it, since both share `copyPost` — the console's clone has carried this since it existed and SH244 is what made it reachable at scale. `ShCopyKeepsAssetsTest` asserts the reader's own question rather than a file being on disk, and it was run with the fix disabled first: three of three fail. What the copy still does not do is move the SH45 storage meter, and neither does an upload — nothing calls `ShTenantStorageMeter.record` at all, which this task found and SH751 records.
- **SH751** — The storage meter is moved by ShFileStorageService itself — store, copy, delete and deleteTenant are where the bytes actually go, and upload, replace, the SH749 copy, the cleanup listener and tenant teardown are all callers of those four. Putting the call in each caller is what failed: three sites were meant to remember, none did, and a fourth arrived with SH749. Deltas are differences measured before and after, and are recorded exactly when bytesOnDiskFor would have counted them — under the tenant root, never the pre-SH47 flat layout — so a reconcile after a mixed run of stores, replaces, copies and deletes changes nothing, which is the assertion that now carries the id.
- **SH753** — The throwing resolver is deleted rather than documented: ShWidgetRepository.findByName threw on a second row, three of its four call sites had already been moved to findFirstByName with a comment each, and the fourth resolved the File post type on every upload — so a catalog holding five rows named Text took uploads down. One resolver now, enforced by the compiler instead of by a comment. Tolerant readers would have made the duplication invisible, so ShWidgetOnStartup.duplicateNames reports each duplicated name and its count at boot. Not a unique index: an instance already carrying duplicates would fail the migration, and de-duplicating means repointing the post-type attributes on the losing rows, which is a migration rather than a seed.
- **SH754** — The meter is on the surface it counts: shio://usage is an MCP resource whose HTTP twin is GET /agent/context?include=usage, both served by one ShAgentUsageService so identical bytes are a property of the construction. A resource and a projection rather than a twelfth tool and a new route — tools/list is paid every turn. Written and pending are stated separately per surface, because the meter flushes on an interval and a document reporting only durable counts answers zero for the first minute of every window. The section is opt-in for a reason the other two only share by accident: it changes on every call, so a digest covering it would make a conditional read never match.
