Manifest flag usageMeter, classified MCP_RESOURCE against the registered beans.
- **SH110** — The storage ceiling is enforced, because the blocker was lifted rather than waited on: viglet-core 2026.3.11 adds VigletQuotaService.check(resource, delta), so the question is now whether what is about to be written fits rather than whether the tenant is already full. The algebra is what makes it backward compatible and is asserted rather than trusted — count + 1 > max is the same predicate as count >= max, so the one-argument forms delegate instead of keeping a copy. ShTenantQuotaService.checkCanStore charges upload with file.getSize() before the post row and before the bytes, and charges replace with the DIFFERENCE, since replacing a 900 MB video with a 1 MB one frees 899 MB and charging the new size would refuse a write that makes the tenant smaller. The kernel compares delta > max - held rather than held + delta > max, because the latter wraps to negative near Long.MAX_VALUE and would admit the write it exists to refuse.
- **SH750** — folder.copy is charged for what it creates. It asked the per-one question because that was all the shared kernel offered, so a tenant one post below its ceiling could copy a section of fifty and land fifty over it, refused nowhere; the op now passes scope.posts(), the number it has already walked for its own detail line. The two shapes XII.28 ruled out while the SPI was missing are still the wrong answers now that it is not: looping the check reads a count the copy has not written yet, so N calls answer one question N times and refuse nothing, and refusing on size invents a second quota model whose failure — a legitimate section copy refused on a generous plan — is worse than the one it prevents. The delta is the third answer and the only exact one. Verified with Docker present, so the schema ran on H2, MariaDB and PostgreSQL rather than H2 alone.

## Block O — The human half (the console the curator uses, SH74)

> The product says the agent builds and the human curates. Block N made the console's *reads*
> agent-shaped; driving the finished surface end to end then showed the curating half did not
> work — a site an agent builds correctly could not be edited, previewed or opened. Every
> defect in this block answered `200`, which is why the block starts with an instrument
> (SH182) rather than a fix: without it these regress silently and a green probe on any route
> proves less than it appears to.

- **SH202** — **A copy takes names that are free** ([ShObjectWriteService](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/object/ShObjectWriteService.java), [ShObjectCopyNamingTest](../shio-app/src/test/java/com/viglet/shio/api/object/ShObjectCopyNamingTest.java)). "Clone" is copy-to-the-same-folder and `copyPost` re-slugged the copy's `furl` from the source's title — the same title, so the same slug. Two posts in one site then claimed one URL, and every downstream mechanism already called that broken: `shio verify` reports `duplicate-url` as an **error**, and `findPost` resolves the URL to whichever row it reaches first, so the clone was unaddressable and so, from that moment, was the original. The curator's most casual action produced it. SH134 spent its whole design budget refusing an occupied address on a *move*; create simply never asked.
  <br>**The title moves with the URL**, because a `-2` URL under an identical title still leaves two rows the curator cannot tell apart — and that is the symptom they actually see, the URL being the derived value. But the two counters are **independent**, which the first implementation got wrong: sharing one produced "Contact (2)" in a folder holding no other "Contact", renaming a page for a collision in a scope the curator cannot see from where the rename shows up. A title is unique per *folder* (a display concern — two "Overview" pages in different sections are not a defect), a URL per *site* (it is the address). So a clone is "Home (2)" / `home-2`, a copy into another folder of the same site keeps its title and moves only its URL, and a copy into an empty folder of another site keeps both verbatim. That the two can end up disagreeing is not a compromise: SH79 keeps them as separate namespaces and SH139's whole point is that moving a post does not re-derive its URL.
  <br>The suffix is **numeric, not `(copy)`**: the server writes this string into content the console renders in whichever language the curator picked, and "Home (copy)" would be English in a Portuguese listing forever.
  <br>**The folder branch had the same defect one level up.** A folder is addressed by its name chain (SH79), so cloning "docs" into its own parent made `folder:<site>/docs` resolve to whichever the walk reached first. Same numbering, applied to the name.
- **SH203** — **The move/copy picker no longer offers destinations the server refuses** ([object.children.page.tsx](../shio-react/src/app/console/content/object.children.page.tsx), [ShFolderWriteService](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/folder/ShFolderWriteService.java), [ShFolderCopyException](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/folder/ShFolderCopyException.java)). SH137's cycle guard is right and belongs on the server, but the dialog navigates *down* from the site root, so the folders inside the one being dragged are exactly the ones a curator scrolls into — and they now answer `409`. **A picker that lists choices the server will refuse teaches the user that the operation fails at random.** The folders in the run are shown **disabled** rather than hidden (someone hunting for "Docs" needs to see that it is the thing they are dragging, not conclude the picker lost it), with a "being moved" / "being copied" marker, and the confirm button is disabled with the reason spelled out. The refusals stay where they are: **the client prevents what it can see, the server refuses what it must** — the same division SH108's confirm flow uses, where the CLI prints the deletions and the server still demands the token.
  <br>It needs **nothing new from the server**. The dialog only ever walks downward, so a row is unreachable exactly when it is one of the ids in the run; disabling it means the walk can never get *inside* one, which is why there is no ancestor check and no subtree fetch.
  <br>**And it found that copy had no guard at all.** SH137 argued a copy needs none — "the new folder is not yet in the tree, so it cannot be its own ancestor" — which is true of the folder being created and false of the traversal that fills it: `copyFolder` saves the copy and *then* walks `findByParentFolder(source)`, so a destination inside the source makes the walk descend into the copies it is still making. It does not terminate. So the two operations refuse the same destinations for two different reasons — a move would detach the subtree from the site root, a copy would never finish — and both checks now live on `ShFolderWriteService` (`checkMovable`/`checkCopyable`), the one place that knows what a subtree is. A second copy of that walk is how the two would come to disagree, and the picker can only disable one subtree for both modes if they agree.
- **SH182** — **The console smoke check runs in CI** ([console-check.yml](../.github/workflows/console-check.yml), [e2e/provision.mjs](../shio-react/e2e/provision.mjs), [e2e/console-check.mjs](../shio-react/e2e/console-check.mjs)). The job packages the real jar (so the console under test is the one a release serves, no dev server involved), boots it, provisions a site from the SH94 `marketing-site` package — the one every Block O defect was reproduced against — and walks the routes in Chromium. Report and screenshots upload on pass and on fail, because "which page was blank" is the question a failure raises.
  <br>**Provisioning is a script, not shell in a YAML step**, because a clean instance is not walkable and neither reason is a console defect: the admin user is created with **no password** (first-access setup sets it) and there is no site at all. It does the three steps a human would — `POST /api/v2/setup`, `POST /api/v2/site`, then a blueprint apply — and it is idempotent, so it also works against a developer's running instance. The site-creation step does the full **CSRF dance** (fetch the token, keep the cookie, echo it back) rather than hiding it: that is exactly the friction **SH170** exists to remove, and writing it out keeps the cost visible instead of making it look free.
  <br>The check itself is unchanged and still discovers its targets from the agent surface, so it runs against any instance. Its two acknowledged debts stay open: it asserts *a* field renders, not the *right* field (a per-post-type expectation is the honest next step), and it has no accepted-findings baseline — **SH142**'s shape applies here unchanged.
- **SH176** — **The post read carries the post-type and parsed data** ([ShConsolePost](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/post/unified/dto/ShConsolePost.java), [ShConsolePostMapper](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/post/unified/ShConsolePostMapper.java), [ShConsolePostReadService](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/post/unified/ShConsolePostReadService.java), [ShPostUnifiedAPITest](../shio-app/src/test/java/com/viglet/shio/api/post/unified/ShPostUnifiedAPITest.java)). `GET /post-unified/{id}` serialized the JPA entity, and the storage shape emptied the form twice over: the LAZY `shPostType` was never fetched so it arrived as `null`, and `data` is a `String` column so it arrived as a JSON *string* while the console's model declares an object. Every post edit page rendered zero fields, for every post-type, and would have rendered no values even with a schema. SH120's treatment applied to the read it skipped: a console DTO that composes the existing services, with `data` parsed and the post-type as its SH16 `ShPostTypeDef` — the same bytes `/api/v2/post-type/{name}` returns, so there is no third serialization of the model (P10).
  <br>**The writes moved with the reads.** `create`/`update`/`publish`/`restore`/`schedule`/`translate` returned the same entity, and the edit page rebinds its form from what a save returns — so fixing only the reads would have left the form working until the first save. They re-read through the read service rather than mapping the entity their own transaction returned, because that transaction has closed by the time the controller sees it: one extra query on a console write beats a response the form cannot bind to. `versions`, `listByFolder`, `trash` and `translations` had the same defect and are converted too.
  <br>**A field the post-type does not declare is named, not dropped** (`undeclaredFields`, rendered as a warning above the form). A projected object must not become a place values vanish into — the form cannot render such a field, saving still preserves it, and the honest thing is to say so. It is the read side of **SH168**; hiding it is how content gets lost.
- **SH177** — **`schemaJson` is retired** ([v2026.3.10.yaml](../shio-app/src/main/resources/db/changelog/v2026.3.10.yaml), `ShPostType`). A denormalized copy of the field list whose only writer was the one-shot `POST /api/v2/migration/unified/run`: correct exactly once, empty for every post-type a blueprint, `shio push` or the console's own editor created afterwards, stale for every type edited afterwards — a denormalization with no invalidation. The column is dropped, the migration service and its endpoint (its only writer) are deleted, and the console's `ShPostUnifiedMigrationService` goes with them. The model already carries `fields`; one shape is cheaper to keep right than two, and nothing read the column.
  <br>**The empty state it produced was wrong in three ways at once** — it named an internal migration in a curator-facing UI, prescribed a fix that could not work for a type created after the migration, and blamed the data when the cause was SH176. It now says the post-type declares no fields and offers the post-type editor.
- **SH178** — **One schema entry point for the form** ([post-unified.ts](../shio-react/src/models/post-unified/post-unified.ts)). The module exported `parseSchema` (no fallback) and `buildSchemaFromPostType` (with one) at equal prominence; the create page called the second and worked, the edit page called the first and rendered nothing. That single difference was the whole distance between "creating a post is fine" and "editing the post I just created is impossible", and it read as a content problem rather than a missing line. There is now one exported `postFormSchema()`, `parseSchema` is gone with the column it parsed, and the projection is private.
- **SH179** — **"View Site" goes somewhere that exists** (`site.list.page.tsx`, since deleted in SH910; [object.children.page.tsx](../shio-react/src/app/console/content/object.children.page.tsx), [routes.const.ts](../shio-react/src/app/routes.const.ts)). `ROUTES.PREVIEW` was declared and registered by nothing, and three call sites navigated to it — including both **View Site** buttons — so they rendered a blank page. This was the literal answer to "I cannot see the site".
  <br>**The two questions inside it are separated rather than conflated.** Reaching a *published* site is the CDA's business and depends on a front end the CMS does not own, so View Site opens the site's configured URL and says plainly when there is none — a legitimate answer where a blank page was not. Reaching a *draft* is Shio's own and already worked, so the per-post **View Page** mints an SH13 preview token, exactly as the editor's Preview Draft does, and it now only renders for posts (it was offered on folders too). The dead constant is deleted, so nothing can navigate there again.
- **SH180** — **An unknown console route says so** ([not-found.page.tsx](../shio-react/src/app/console/not-found.page.tsx), [App.tsx](../shio-react/src/App.tsx)). The SPA rendered a normal-looking, error-free empty page for any unmatched path, which is what made SH179 invisible in the product and what let a probe of a nonexistent route report success — a blank page and a working page were the same observation. A catch-all inside the console shell (so the user can navigate out of it) and one outside it name the path they could not match. The SH182 check's `unknown-route` probe asserts it, which is what makes every other probe's "ok" mean something.
- **SH181** — **The site read answers the key it is given** ([ShSiteAPI](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/site/ShSiteAPI.java), [ShSiteResolveTest](../shio-app/src/test/java/com/viglet/shio/api/site/ShSiteResolveTest.java), [visual-editor.page.tsx](../shio-react/src/app/console/universal-editor/visual-editor.page.tsx)). Opening the Universal Editor issued `GET /api/v2/site/{furl}` against an id-keyed endpoint and 404'd twice before rendering. `GET /{id}` now resolves id → furl → name, in that order so the declared key wins a collision; **the writes deliberately do not** — a read that resolved a near-miss shows the curator the wrong site, a write that did would change it. The guard is a test rather than a patched call site, because this is the third instance of one confusion (SH117 settled id-versus-name for post-types) and §VIII.10's rule is a guard per invariant.
  <br>The editor also **reports a failed resolve** instead of spinning: a site with no front-end URL configured renders a sentence and a way back, which is the SH180 lesson at page level.
- **SH246** — **The Java suite is green on the default branch again** ([ShAgentRoundTripTest](../shio-app/src/test/java/com/viglet/shio/api/agent/ShAgentRoundTripTest.java)). `./mvnw -pl shio-app -am test` failed 1 of 824, and had since SH144 without anything reporting it (which is SH241's half of the story). Not a product defect: SH144 made the SH103 incident store **durable**, so `ShAgentDurableIncidentTest`'s deliberately-recorded `/skip-guard` 500 outlives its own class in `sh_agent_incident` on the shared test datasource, and `ShAgentRoundTripTest.aWriteCanReturnItsOwnProof` — which asserts a *clean* `?verify=true` proof carries no attribution prose — then read a `diagnostics` finding it did not cause.
  <br>Both behaviours are right and neither moves: SH143 keeps the cross-cutting checks whole on purpose, and the proof's own `notes` already say the findings are not necessarily the run's. So the fix is the test's, and it is **isolation rather than a weaker assertion** — the point of that assertion is that a clean proof is cheap, and it can only be made against an instance that is actually clean. The class boots its own in-memory database, the precedent the SH164/SH239 benchmarks set for exactly this reason: a response that describes the whole instance cannot be asserted on a datasource every other test writes to.
- **SH454** — DELETE /v2/site/{id} trashes and purges the site's root folder through ShFolderWriteService - the verb that already gets the FK ordering right - before the site row goes, so a site holding content deletes instead of answering a body-less 500, and it takes an actor because the walk down audits per post and per folder. SH448's teardown, which did those three calls by hand, is one call again and therefore the assertion.
- **SH459** — The locale segment is checked against the locales the site's published content is actually in (plus the route's own default), so /sites/<site>/default/xx-yy/ is a teaching 404 instead of the home page with a 200 — and the authentication entry point answers 404 for a URI no controller claims, so a missing font is absent rather than behind a door.
- **SH242** — monaco-editor is pinned to 0.52.2, strictPeerDependencies makes an unmet range refuse the install, and a test resolves every Monaco specifier the GraphiQL tree imports.
- **SH542** — All nine use import.meta.dirname and a repo walk keeps them there, so Vite's native config loader becoming the default cannot fail the console build.
- **SH574** — The four replaced packages are gone from every Java source, and ShJacksonVersionLintTest holds the rule: imports, pom declarations, and the annotations exemption's own vacuity.
- **SH241** — Half of the defect had been fixed by SH579's suites.yml, which runs the JS workspace and conformance on push; what was still dispatch-only is the Java suite and the console walk, so two of the three gates agents.md names never ran unasked. The Java job is clean test from a clone, which is the only place SH282's stale-but-valid class can be caught - the local lint protects the person committing and cannot protect the branch. It publishes surefire's own Results line as the run's headline and tees the log, because every alternative is a number somebody derived by hand. The console walk goes on pull request rather than push: it boots a jar and drives Chromium, and a gate that expensive on every push is the one people cancel.
- **SH654** — Publish and Unpublish sit beside Save on the post edit screen; publish saves the form first, and Unpublish reads whether a live row exists rather than the edited row's state.
- **SH243** — The naming loop now sees the trash, so a copy skips a sleeping URL, and a restore onto an occupied one is refused naming the occupant instead of duplicating silently.
- **SH690** — A folder.restore plan now reads the trash, names a trashed parent as its own reason, and raises SH243's refusal — so plan and apply give one answer.
- **SH696** — folder.restore now asks the ACL, and a lint classifies every op: 12 of 13 check authorisation, render.provision exempt. Two ops it first read as unguarded carry a stronger check.
- **SH699** — The mount effect now starts the fetch without raising state and loading begins true, so pnpm lint is green; the fifteen the SH665 baseline still absorbs are held by SH701.
- **SH701** — eslint-suppressions.json is now a named list that prints its counts and fails on drift, with four of the fifteen paid off and the other eleven held by SH702-SH704.
- **SH702** — Four dialogs mount their body inside DialogContent keyed on its subject, so a reopen renders nothing from the previous read - proved by a probe red before and green after.
- **SH703** — Six hand-maintained flags become derived - the spinner is a comparison, the selection and the bridge handshake carry what they belong to, and the widgets tag their resolved path, closing a race.
- **SH704** — The cache became a subscription, so there is no second copy to republish and no alive flag to remember - and it moved somewhere a Node test can drive it, which is where the five assertions live.
- **SH716** — A crumb is keyed on where it goes rather than on what it says, so a site and its root folder stop colliding - and console:check reads 19 of 19 for the first time.
- **SH691** — A restore now refuses a title a live post took while it slept, with a teaching 409 naming the folder, so the trash-blind counter stays and the collision is refused where a curator would meet it.
- **SH245** — ShContentWriterOwnershipLintTest fails on a write mapping reaching a content repository, with a named-comment hatch; keyed on the content repositories because any Repository finds 23 admin writes.
- **SH744** — ShSiteFurlNaming owns a site's address for all three writers, refusing a declared furl that is taken and numbering a derived one, with the check ahead of the bootstrap branch.
- **SH244** — `folder.copy` — an address pair on the batch surface, so duplicating a section is one call instead of a walk plus an upsert per post. `to` is the copy's own name chain, occupied is refused rather than numbered (the console clones by numbering, which hands an agent an address it did not ask for), and it may cross sites where `folder.move` refuses to — whose own teaching error used to send the caller round a per-post loop and now names this op. No `post.copy`: a read plus an upsert duplicates a page losslessly, and a second name is paid by every `tools/list` forever (SH733's rule). Not destructive, so no confirm token. §XVI.4's reason for "the copy is a draft" was wrong and the first assertion said so: `copyPost` sets `published(false)` and also reproduced each state row as it found it, so a copy of a live page came out PUBLISHED with the flag off — on the console a pinned decision, here a hole in SH107's publish gate that a credential without `mayPublish` could walk through (SH201), so `copyFolderAs` takes an `asDrafts` flag and the console keeps what it had. A post that exists only as PUBLISHED is copied as a draft rather than skipped. One writer for both surfaces (SH245), so SH202's naming and SH203's cycle guard cannot disagree. The vocabulary ceiling went 720 → 770 (measured 740) after a trim, and the decomposition says why that is allowed: per-op prose held at 36.3, so the growth is an op rather than drift.

## Block P — The visible site (what the human actually looks at, SH74)

> The block that closes the gap between *correct content* and *a page a person sees*.
>
> **What it turned out to be about.** The old engine is remembered as "Nashorn, therefore
> unsafe, therefore never again", and reading `origin/FSP` — an ancestor of HEAD, not a
> divergent branch — reversed that: the template language *was Handlebars* (loaded from a CDN
> at render time), the capability set *was* a closed list of seven functions, and the liability
> was one line, `scriptEngine.eval`. So the block restores a model rather than inventing one,
> and what it deletes is the host.

- **SH183** — **Page → layout → region renders on the server, with no script engine** ([render/](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/render/), [ShRenderNoScriptEngineTest](../shio-app/src/test/java/com/viglet/shio/render/ShRenderNoScriptEngineTest.java), [ShPageRenderTest](../shio-app/src/test/java/com/viglet/shio/render/ShPageRenderTest.java)). Applying `marketing-site` produced thirteen correct pages and no way to look at one: preview minted a URL against `site.url` and 400'd without it, the Universal Editor is an `<iframe src={site.url}>`, and nothing in this repository rendered a page. `GET /preview/{site}/{url}` now composes a layout and its regions from content the instance already holds — no client setup, no front end, which is also the only path an MCP-only caller has (SH186).
  <br>**The non-goal is honoured by construction, not by configuration.** Handlebars.java declares `nashorn-core` at *compile scope* for its JavaScript-helper integration, so adding it while deleting the orphaned direct declaration would have swapped an unused script engine for a used one and read as a cleanup. It is **excluded**: the classes that would evaluate a script are not on the classpath, which is a stronger statement than FSP could make — its failure was calling `getScriptEngine(String[])` when the `ClassFilter` overload existed the whole time. Two smaller defaults are closed the same way: the context resolves with `MapValueResolver` **only** (the default chain includes `JavaBeanValueResolver`, under which a template handed an entity walks the persistence model), and the `TemplateLoader` refuses everything (the default reads the classpath, so `{{> application}}` in a layout — which is content — is a file read). All three are asserted, because each is one dependency bump or one shorter call away from being undone and none of them changes the rendered output when it breaks.
  <br>**Layouts, regions and themes are posts**, of three system post-types created on demand (`POST /api/v2/render/post-types`, idempotent, never touching an existing type — SH38's precedent for `File`, SH152's provision-never-upsert rule). That is the decision the block turns on: an agent writes them with `post.upsert`, they travel in the SH68 package, they project to files and `shio verify` lints them, all for free. A closed Java projection of the SH95 section types would have been none of those and would need a release to extend. It also needs **no schema work** — the 2018 `openviglet/bootstrap-site` export imports byte-identically, `sh-region="NAME"` and all.
  <br>**The seams survive the render.** `sh-region` is kept and joined by `data-shio-region` + `data-shio-region-post`, because the rendered DOM is the only place the Universal Editor can learn which node maps to which post — SH185's whole problem, answered by an attribute that has been in the content since 2018. A slot with no Region post is *marked*, not silently empty: a missing region and an empty one are different mistakes, the rule SH169 set for the digest.
  <br>**Three of the seven `shObject.js` capabilities land as helpers** — `{{#query}}`, `{{#navigation}}`, `{{file_url}}` — which is what the shipped sample used, and they replace 767–1098 characters of hand-written JavaScript *per region* that was almost entirely a loop remapping fields. `search`, `form` and `getRelation` are **not stubbed**: each needs a backing component the nuclear refactor removed, and a helper that silently renders nothing is worse than the unknown-helper error Handlebars raises with a line and column. They are **SH247**.
  <br>**Preview-grade on purpose.** A preview URL that renders production content *becomes* a delivery path the moment somebody points DNS at it, and then Shio owns HTML rendering, caching and SEO — a position §0.3 declined. If that is ever reopened it has to be a decision, not the consequence of a route getting popular: hence a distinct path, `no-store` with `X-Robots-Tag: noindex` (a `max-age` here is how a preview quietly becomes infrastructure), authentication, and a banner the page's own stylesheet cannot hide.
  <br>**Two findings from writing it.** Echoing a region name into the HTML comment that marks an unfilled slot is not provably safe — a name containing `-->` closes the comment and the rest becomes markup — so the marker is a constant and the name goes only where jsoup escapes it. And `ShRenderPostTypes` mapped its defs *outside* the transaction at first, which passes on a fresh instance and throws `LazyInitializationException` on every instance after, because a type the call created still holds its fields in memory while one it merely found does not. That is SH176's defect exactly, and its own test caught it.

- **SH192** — **A template fails when it is written, not when somebody looks at the page** ([ShTemplateValidator](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/render/ShTemplateValidator.java), [ShAgentBatchService](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/agent/ShAgentBatchService.java), [ShTemplateValidatorTest](../shio-app/src/test/java/com/viglet/shio/render/ShTemplateValidatorTest.java)). `post.upsert` refuses a field the post-type does not declare (SH168) and had no opinion about the 1330 characters of markup inside one, so an unclosed `{{#each}}` was accepted, stored, published — and discovered as a blank page. **Every iteration then cost a guess**, which is the loop this block exists to make cheap. A `PageLayout`'s or `Region`'s `HTML` is now compiled on write: a real run **refuses** with a 400 carrying the line, the column and a caret under the offending character — FSP's `regionError` output, which this product had in 2019 and lost — while a plan **reports**, following SH168 exactly, because a plan that died on the first broken template would hide the rest of the report and the report is the reason to plan.
  <br>**Writing it found that Handlebars already does half the job.** A block called with parameters (`{{#search q="x"}}`) cannot be anything but a helper, so the compiler raises `could not find helper` on its own; a paramless `{{#search}}` is a valid section over a context value and compiles silently. The split falls out of that: the compiler covers the unambiguous half, a targeted scan covers the three helpers that are *known* missing (`search`, `form`, `getRelation` — SH247), and **nothing guesses**. Handlebars' own wording is re-worded rather than passed through: "could not find helper: 'search'" leaves the author hunting for a typo when the truth is that the helper was one of the seven the 2019 engine had and has not been reimplemented.
  <br>**Two rules that keep it from becoming noise.** Unknown *sections* in general are not flagged — `{{#items}}` is a legitimate iteration and there is no way to tell it from a mistyped helper without the parameter list, which the AST does not expose; a rule that fires on both is a rule authors learn to ignore. And an ordinary post's markup is **not** compiled: an `Article`'s `TEXT` can legitimately contain braces, and rejecting it would refuse perfectly good content.
  <br>**What §XV.10 asked for and could not have**: unknown *field* references as errors "when the post-type is known". At write time it is not — a Region's post-type declares `HTML` and `JAVASCRIPT`, while the fields its template interpolates belong to whatever page is later bound to the layout that slots it. That check needs a resolved page, so it belongs to a lint over rendered pages; it is **SH251**.
  <br>The test is a Spring test against the *wired* engine on purpose: a bare `new ShTemplateEngine()` has no helpers registered, so every legitimate `{{#query}}` would be reported as unknown and the validator would look stricter than the renderer. That the two agree about which helpers exist is exactly the property worth asserting, and only the real engine can prove it.
- **SH185** — **The Universal Editor has a counterpart, and the protocol is written down** ([SH185-universal-editor-protocol.md](specs/SH185-universal-editor-protocol.md), [ShEditorBridge](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/render/ShEditorBridge.java), [shio-editor.js](../shio-app/src/main/resources/render/shio-editor.js), [ShRegionComposer](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/render/ShRegionComposer.java), [visual-editor.page.tsx](../shio-react/src/app/console/universal-editor/visual-editor.page.tsx)). `visual-editor.page.tsx` has posted `{type, data}` into an iframe and listened for replies since SH10, and its own comment said the replies came from `shio-editor.js` — **which did not exist anywhere in this repository**, not in `create-shio-app`, `shio-react-sdk`, `shio-sections` or `shio-client`, not one `postMessage` among them. The console was one end of a conversation nobody was on the other side of. Writing the format down only now is deliberate: specifying a wire format with nothing on the other end is how the shell got here, and SH183 is the first implementation to target.
  <br>**The annotation contract is 2018's, extended by one level.** `sh-region` already survived the render (SH183) as `data-shio-region` + `data-shio-region-post`; SH185 adds the field level — `sh-field="TEXT"` → `data-shio-prop`, `sh-post="{{id}}"` → `data-shio-post` — and stamps the page's own post on `<body>`, so the common case needs no `sh-post` at all. **Ownership is the template's job, not the engine's**, and that is the load-bearing decision: a region renders against the *page's* model, so `{{TEXT}}` inside it is the page's, while inside a `{{#query}}` block `{{title}}` is the listed post's. Nothing in the rendered HTML records which interpolation came from where, and inferring it would mean tracking provenance through every helper. Resolution is nearest-ancestor, so a row's declaration wins over the page's without either knowing about the other. A field whose owner cannot be resolved is rendered **read-only and outlined**, not dropped — SH169's rule again.
  <br>**Both attribute forms survive on purpose.** The `sh-*` pair is a contract the *content* declares, so SH193 can extract it into the reference graph and SH192 can lint it; the `data-*` pair is what the browser consumes. One attribute doing both jobs could not change on either side without breaking the other.
  <br>**Neither direction uses `"*"` any more.** The console posts to the iframe's origin and ignores inbound messages from anywhere else; the page posts to an origin **passed in on the script tag**, because `document.referrer` is empty on some navigations and `window.parent.location` throws cross-origin — the server that rendered the page is the only party that reliably knows who asked. The script is also **inert when not framed**: a page that starts making elements `contenteditable` outside the editor is a page that corrupts content.
  <br>**The bridge is opt-in per request** (`?editor=true`), so an ordinary preview ships no editor code, and it is injected *after* the render rather than inside `ShPageRenderService` — which keeps the renderer returning exactly what a front end would serve, the separation SH101's digest and SH102's snapshot depend on and the one `ShPreviewBanner` already keeps. A front end that never heard of the flag ignores it and degrades to a plain iframe.
  <br>`universalEditor: true` in the manifest is now true. It was the first flag to break the rule that an unshipped capability reports `false` and never overstates, and the fix was to ship the counterpart rather than demote it. `serverRender: true` joins it — the flag an MCP-only caller needs most (SH186), since without it "build a site" ends with content nobody can look at and no way to know `/preview` exists.
- **SH248** — **A region's browser JavaScript actually reaches the browser** ([ShRegionComposer](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/render/ShRegionComposer.java), [ShRegionComposerTest](../shio-app/src/test/java/com/viglet/shio/render/ShRegionComposerTest.java)). SH183's whole resolution of the Block D non-goal is a split — HTML composes on the server, declaratively; JavaScript runs in the browser as a region's static asset — and it shipped the first half only. `Region.JAVASCRIPT` existed, the console gave it a code editor, and the composed page carried no `<script>` for it, so the field accepted working code and silently discarded its effect. **That is worse than not having the field**: a missing capability is discoverable, while one that takes input and drops it teaches the author they wrote the code wrong. Same shape as SH178's two schema entry points, where one worked and one did not and the difference read as a content problem.
  <br>**Inline, not a route.** The page is served `no-store` (SH183's guard against a preview quietly becoming infrastructure), so caching a fragment of an uncacheable page buys nothing, and a route is a second thing that can 404. It also keeps the render self-contained, which is what SH102's snapshot and SH187 want. If preview ever becomes delivery, this is one of the decisions revisited alongside the headers.
  <br>**Once per region, keyed by name.** A layout may slot the same region twice — a nav in the header and the footer — and the markup is wanted in both places while the initialisation is not; running it twice is a bug that only appears on the layouts that do it. Each tag carries `data-shio-region` and the post id, so a script is traceable to its post exactly as its markup is. And the body is a jsoup `DataNode` rather than text: as text, `if (a && b)` is escaped to `&amp;&amp;` and the script becomes a syntax error.
- **SH184** — **A site's front-end URL is reachable from the agent path, and a site without one is no longer invisible** ([ShSiteFrontEnd](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/render/ShSiteFrontEnd.java), [ShSiteWriteService](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/site/ShSiteWriteService.java), [ShAgentBatchService](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/agent/ShAgentBatchService.java), [site-front-end.ts](../shio-react/src/lib/site-front-end.ts)). `site.url` gates every way of looking at a page, and nothing an agent could call set it: SH170's `site.upsert` deliberately never updated a site, on the reasoning that a URL is a console concern with a human looking at it. That holds for a decision about a domain and not for a blank — the agent is the thing that just deployed the front end and knows the address.
  <br>**The P7 line runs between filling in what was empty and redirecting what somebody chose**, and only the second is a surprise. So `site.upsert` fills an empty `url`, `description` or `furl` and reports `update` naming the fields; a value that is already there is **kept**, and the change note says which and points at the console — a bare `noop` reads as the request having been ignored rather than as a value having been protected. It stays idempotent, so a document is still re-runnable, and a **dry run answers from the same code that performs the write** (`planFill`), which is what lets a plan say in advance that a URL will not be applied. The rule lives on `ShSiteWriteService` rather than in the batch service, because what an upsert may overwrite is write semantics and SH245 is the standing lesson about second copies of a verb; `update` could not be reused, since it is the console's full replace and would null out `postTypeLayout` on the way past.
  <br>**And a site with no front end stopped being a dead end.** `ShPreviewTokenAPI` answered `400 site has no url` and the Universal Editor rendered `universalEditor.siteNoUrl` — for the *normal* state of a site an agent just built, so both visual surfaces were unavailable at exactly the moment there was something new to see. SH183 removed the reason, and `ShSiteFrontEnd` is the one place that answers "where can a person look at this site": the configured front end, or Shio's own `/preview/**`.
  <br>The two destinations are **a record, not a string**, because they differ by a token: an external front end needs one to turn its own draft mode on at `/api/preview`, while `/preview/**` is already console-authenticated and already draft-preferred. Minting for the second would issue a credential that unlocks nothing, so the preview response's `token` is now **nullable** and `previewUrl` is the field that is always there. The fallback is **resolved, never stored** — writing `/preview/<site>` into the column would make every later reader unable to tell a placeholder from a real deployment, and would destroy the fill rule by leaving no empty to fill.
  <br>The console had the same question in three places (both **View Site** buttons and the editor's iframe) each answering it inline; they now share `siteDestination`, mirroring the server so the two cannot come to disagree about where a site is visible. Both `siteNoUrl` strings are deleted from all four locale files.
- **SH191** — **A template is code, and it projects as a file** ([content-files.mjs](../cli/src/content-files.mjs), [content-store.mjs](../cli/src/content-store.mjs), [content-pull.mjs](../cli/src/commands/content-pull.mjs), [content-files.test.mjs](../cli/test/content-files.test.mjs), [content-commands.test.mjs](../cli/test/content-commands.test.mjs)). `bodyFieldFor` treats only an `HTML Editor` as a document body, so SH183's render model — whose fields are `Ace Editor - HTML` and `Ace Editor - Javascript` — collapsed into `fields:` as escaped one-liners inside YAML frontmatter: an HTML document and a JavaScript program with no line numbers, no highlighting, nothing `Grep` reaches, and a re-escape for every tweak. Law P4 says files beat APIs for authoring, and it was failing on the one artifact an iterative loop touches constantly. A `PageLayout`'s `HTML`, a `Region`'s `HTML`/`JAVASCRIPT` and a `Theme`'s `CSS` now project as sidecars beside the `.md`, named by a `files:` block — `body:` generalized past one field and one widget, so reading a file back still never consults the model.
  <br>**The widget decides, never the post-type.** A rule keyed on `PageLayout`/`Region`/`Theme` would work for exactly the three types SH183 ships and stop working the moment somebody models a layout type of their own — which is the *expected* case, since the whole reason a layout is a post is that it is content. The widget is already the thing that says "this value is a program": the console gives it a code editor for that reason. `HTML Editor` deliberately stays the body (moving it would rewrite every existing file) and `Text Area` stays prose.
  <br>**The file name always carries the field** — `content-list.HTML.html`, not `content-list.html`. The pretty form collides the day a post-type declares two `Ace Editor - HTML` fields, silently, because the second write overwrites the first and the file still parses. Making the field segment conditional on a collision would be worse: it is the same defect `bodyFieldFor`'s own comment refuses, a file name that moves when somebody adds a field, which is a content change wearing a formatting diff.
  <br>**The bytes are verbatim — the one place this format normalizes nothing**, and deliberately unlike the body's CRLF → LF. A sidecar is read back as the whole file with no framing to strip, so byte-for-byte is achievable here, and it has to be: the base fingerprint is taken from the *server's* document, so a writer that normalized would produce a file that reads back different from the base, and every later pull would report a "local change" nobody made until somebody pushed. Writing this found that live on the body field — **SH253**.
  <br>**Three refusals, all the `url:`-versus-path rule applied to a second pair of places one value can live.** A field in both `files:` and `fields:` (or named as both a sidecar and the body) is refused, because whichever side won would discard the other silently. A `files:` entry naming a path rather than a file name is refused — a sidecar sits beside its `.md`, so a separator there is never a location. And a named file that is **not on disk** stops the command: the two silent readings are both destructive, since "empty" publishes a blank layout and "absent" makes `post.upsert` — which declares whole state — clear the server's copy.
  <br>**A sidecar the post no longer needs is removed**, read off the file already on disk rather than inferred, because only the file knows what the last write produced. An empty value gets no file at all: an empty program cannot be told apart from one somebody emptied. And a `.remote` conflict copy stays **whole**, values in `fields:` — a conflict is an artifact a human diffs, and three files nobody named would not be cleaned up by the write that resolves it.
  <br>A `Theme`'s `CSS` field is declared `Ace Editor - HTML` because no CSS widget is seeded, so its sidecar is `.html` — wrong for highlighting, right for lines, `Grep` and a reviewable diff, which is the whole of the claim. `SIDECAR_WIDGETS` is the one line **SH252** changes.
- **SH253** — **The merge happens in the projection's domain, so a normalization stops causing the drift it prevents** ([content-files.mjs](../cli/src/content-files.mjs), [content-store.mjs](../cli/src/content-store.mjs), [content-pull.mjs](../cli/src/commands/content-pull.mjs), [content-push.mjs](../cli/src/commands/content-push.mjs), [content-commands.test.mjs](../cli/test/content-commands.test.mjs)). `serializePost` rewrites a body's CRLF to LF, and its comment says why: *"without it a server value holding CRLF would serialize one way and parse back another, and every pull would report a change nobody made."* Sound about the file, wrong about the comparison — the base snapshot was fingerprinted from the **merge result**, which for a post the server changed *is the server's document*, CRLF intact. So a pull wrote LF to disk and recorded CRLF in the base, the next pull found them different, and `reconcile` answered `local-changed`: a change nobody made, reported on every run, forever, until somebody pushed — and `push --content --check`, the CI drift gate, red on content nobody edited. The normalization produced exactly the failure it was added to prevent.
  <br>**Fingerprinting the projected document is only half, and that was measured rather than assumed.** It is the obvious repair and the design filed it as "the real answer"; building it showed it converts a permanent `local-changed` into a permanent `remote-changed` — the file settles and the pull still reports a write every run, because the *server's* value is still outside the domain everything else is compared in. So the rule is one step earlier and one step wider: **a remote document is projected on the way in, and the merge only ever compares documents that have been.** Then an unrepresentable value is *unchanged* instead of eternally in flight.
  <br>**Not a new idea here — SH145's, generalized.** `idsToPaths` already rewrites a `File` field from an id to a path as it is read, "so the base, the server side and the file side all speak paths and a File field does not read as changed on every sync". That is this argument for one field type; `projectRemote` is it for every normalization the format has, and it runs *after* the asset rewrite because a path is what the file will hold.
  <br>**`projectedPost` round-trips through the format instead of restating its rules** — serialize, parse, reattach the SH191 sidecars (verbatim, so they survive untouched). Exact by construction: a normalization added later cannot escape it, and there is no second list of "things the projection changes" to keep in step with the first, which is precisely what this defect came from lacking. `publish` and `movedFrom` are carried rather than round-tripped, since neither is state the merge compares.
  <br>**Both commands, because both ask the server's copy a question.** `push --content` uses it to decide whether a post changed on both sides (a body differing only in line endings is not a conflict) and what to record as agreed for a post the tree does not declare — recording the unprojected form *there* is how a clean push left the next pull reporting a change nobody made. It also stopped fetching the post-type defs twice.
  <br>**Nothing caught it because no fixture in the suite had a CRLF in it.** The round-trip tests assert `parse(serialize(doc)) === doc.data` on LF content, where the normalization is the identity function — a rule stated in a comment, contradicted by a caller two files away, and invisible to every assertion because the fixtures all happened to satisfy it. The three regression tests were each checked against the old code: two fail without the pull half, the third without the push half, and one pulls a **third** time on purpose, because a fix that merely swapped which side looked changed would pass a second pull and fail there.
- **SH254 + SH255** — **A note with a trailing space stops being a permanent conflict, and the round trip becomes a property** ([content-notes.mjs](../cli/src/content-notes.mjs), [content-round-trip.test.mjs](../cli/test/content-round-trip.test.mjs), [content-notes.test.mjs](../cli/test/content-notes.test.mjs)). `content-notes.mjs`' `scalar()` said it was *"the same rule `content-files` uses"* and was missing one of that rule's seven clauses — `encodeScalar` quotes when `value !== value.trim()`, this charset allowed a trailing space, and `parseNotes` strips trailing whitespace off every line. So the file could not hold the value, and the symptom was not cosmetic: with an empty base — a fresh clone, the case a projection exists to serve — `reconcileNotes` saw the server's `"terse "` and the file's `"terse"` as two different edits and reported a **conflict** on every pull, forever, while advising the operator to edit the file or run `shio remember`, neither of which can settle a value the format drops on the way in. SH253 produced a phantom *write*; this produced a phantom *stalemate*.
  <br>**Exactly one clause and exactly one value shape**, measured rather than assumed: leading spaces, `: `, ` #`, tabs, newlines, YAML keywords and numeric-looking strings all round-tripped already, because the charset's first-character rule and its exclusions cover the rest of `encodeScalar`'s list by accident. The two rules stay **two** — these are deliberately separate readers (SH161 chose a small dedicated one over a YAML dependency for four keys) and their charsets differ because their parsers do. What has to agree is not the output but the *property*.
  <br>**Which is SH255, and it is the half that matters.** `parse(serialize(x)) === x` is universally quantified and every existing test was an example, with fixtures that all happened to be values their format represents exactly — the post round-trip test uses LF bodies, where the CRLF normalization is the identity function. So there is now one adversarial value list (trailing/leading whitespace, CRLF, lone `\r`, YAML keywords, numeric strings, `: `, ` #`, empty, `-`, `[`, `{`, BOM, a bare `---`, a tab, an emoji) run as a table against **all four** round trips: a post field, a post body, a memory note and an SH191 sidecar — 131 assertions where there were none.
  <br>**The exemption list is as load-bearing as the assertion**, because a format is allowed not to represent something, and a declaration turns "we lost it" into a decision somebody made. It carries the SH142 rule too: a declared loss the format *no longer* has fails the build, so the list cannot rot into a suppression that hides the next defect at the same spot. A refusal counts as a legitimate non-holding — it is the only one that cannot lose work silently — so the check takes a thunk and catches.
  <br>**Writing the list corrected the first draft from nine declared losses to three**, which is the finding worth keeping: the reflex is that stripping the body's framing must cost every whitespace-ish value, and `bodySafe` already keeps those in `fields:`, so they survive the *document* exactly and merely stop being the body. Only three are real — CRLF and a lone `\r` (converted on purpose), and an empty note (refused, because SH160's "forgetting is an empty note" is an API gesture that deletes the row, so a read never returns one and a forgotten note is an absent key). The guard caught its own author's wrong declarations on the first run.
  <br>A second table asserts **projection is a fixed point** — `projectedPost(projectedPost(x)) === projectedPost(x)` for every adversarial value. That is SH253's guarantee stated as a property: whatever the format does to a value it must do *once*, or the base chases it, which is the permanent `remote-changed` the half-fix produced.
- **SH256 + SH257** — **An asset path can no longer navigate the filesystem, and the guard covers all six round trips** ([content-assets.mjs](../cli/src/content-assets.mjs), [content-files.mjs](../cli/src/content-files.mjs), [content-store.mjs](../cli/src/content-store.mjs), [content-round-trip.test.mjs](../cli/test/content-round-trip.test.mjs), [content-assets.test.mjs](../cli/test/content-assets.test.mjs)). `assetPathFor` concatenated `siteName + chain + fileName` with no validation and `assetLocationOf` read the last segment as the file name, so the pair was neither injective nor bounded. Measured: a `File` field reading `Blog/../../../../etc/passwd` resolved through `readAssetBytes` to **`/etc/passwd`**, outside the project entirely — `push --content` would have read those bytes and uploaded them as an asset, while `folder.upsert` was handed the chain `/../../../../etc`. Separately, a file name containing `/` projected to a path that read back as a *different folder and a different name*, colliding with any real asset there. This was the only path in the tree that did not already refuse it: `siteDir` refuses a slash, SH191's `sidecarNameFor` refuses a separator, and `ShBlueprintRegistry` checks a package's refs per segment for `..`.
  <br>**The two ends refuse differently, and the asymmetry is the design.** `assetLocationOf` **throws**, because its input is a value from the tree — hand-editable, and writable by a blueprint or a generated document — and both silent readings are wrong: `null` means "this is an id, leave it alone" (SH145), which would send the traversal to the server as a dangling reference and never mention that the tree contains one, while treating it as a location reads outside the tree. `assetPathFor` returns **null**, because its input is the server's own media listing, and taking a whole pull down over one unprojectable asset is SH173's mistake; the caller skips it and *names* it, since the `File` field then stays an id and a silent skip reads as "this site has no such asset".
  <br>**SH257 finished the SH255 table**: the asset-path pair and a post's own `type` and `site`, plus four values the earlier list did not need (`a/b`, `a\b`, `..`, `.`) — 241 assertions over six round trips. Every post-type name round-trips; the sixteen new `DECLARED` entries are all *refusals*, which is what a format whose output is a filesystem path should mostly do.
  <br>**And it found a third defect, in the frontmatter.** `siteDir` trimmed a site's name for the directory while `serializePost` wrote the untrimmed name into the frontmatter, so a site called `"Blog "` made `shio pull --content` emit a file whose `site:` disagreed with its own path — a tree the pull wrote and every later command refused, with a message blaming the disagreement rather than the trim that caused it. It is now refused, naming the site, which is the answer the slash already got. Trimming into the frontmatter as well was the other candidate and is worse: the file would declare a site name that is not the server's, so a push would target or create the wrong site.
  <br>**Worth recording how that one was found, because it says what the guard cannot do.** The table did *not* fail on it. It asserts "exact, or declared", and this case was already a refusal — just the wrong one — so it satisfied the property; it came out of reading the refusal's message during the probe. A declared refusal is not checked for being the *right* refusal, which is **SH258**.

  <br>**`getRelation` takes the field's value, not its name**, which is why it needs no access to the post-type and why it covers all three shapes a reference actually takes here: a `Content Select`'s post id, an SH95 `Multi Select` of friendly URLs, and a single URL. Each entry resolves **by id, then by friendly URL** — SH181's order, so the declared key wins a collision and a template's idea of what a reference points at cannot depend on what else is in the site. The URL half is scoped to the **current site**, like `query`'s `folder`: a relation that could reach another site's content would make a shared region's output depend on which page slotted it.
  <br>**A dangling reference is skipped, not marked** — deliberately unlike SH183's missing *region*, and the difference is who else can see it. A region slot is named inside a layout's HTML, so before SH193 nothing but the renderer could report an unfilled one; a dangling `Content Select` or `references: "post"` entry is already an SH154 `dangling-reference` finding with an address and a `fix`. Marking it in the page too would put one defect in two reports that can disagree, and every template would have to branch on a `missing` flag the row shape does not need. `{{else}}` still renders when *nothing* resolved, so "the references are all broken" is not silently an empty `<main>`.
  <br>**`search` is the CDA's own predicate, reached through the repository's `search*` defaults** so the term is normalized exactly once (SH131: normalizing twice searches for `%%term%%` and matches nothing, which reads as an empty index rather than a bug). Title, summary *and* stored field data — the same predicate the delivery search and the SH240 console listing use, so three surfaces cannot come to disagree about what "matches" means. A type filter is resolved to an **id** before the query rather than filtered after, because `p.shPostType.name` in JPQL joins `ShPostType` and the tenant predicate then hits a subclass alias with no `tenant_id` — the SH22 join hazard, which fails at prepare time. An unknown type name yields **nothing** rather than everything: a filter that silently stopped filtering would render the whole site.

The model holds no request parameters, because SH183 kept the raw request out of template scope on purpose, so putting a query string back in is a decision of its own rather than a consequence of registering a helper — **SH259**. What it *is*: a term the template supplies, literal or read from the page's own field, which is a tag page, a curated collection, a "more about this" listing. A blank `q` renders `{{else}}` rather than the whole site, because a search box nobody has typed in yet must not read as "everything matched".
  <br>**Three things were unified rather than copied.** All five listing helpers now yield the same row shape, so a card body written for `{{#query}}` works for a relation or a search result — a helper with its own row shape would make one capability set into five vocabularies. The DRAFT-preference dedup and the date-then-id total order are extracted and shared: a second copy of the preference is a second chance to get it backwards, and the failure mode there is a preview showing the live page while the curator hunts for their unpublished change.
  <br>**And the validator shrank with the implementation.** `KNOWN_MISSING_HELPERS` is down to `form`, and the test asserts both directions — `{{#form}}` is still named, `{{#getRelation}}`/`{{#search}}` are now accepted. - **SH251** — **A template interpolating a field nothing declares is a finding, not a blank space** ([ShTemplateFieldScanner](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/render/ShTemplateFieldScanner.java), [ShTemplateFieldLint](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/agent/verify/ShTemplateFieldLint.java), [ShPageRenderService](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/render/ShPageRenderService.java), [ShTemplateFieldScannerTest](../shio-app/src/test/java/com/viglet/shio/render/ShTemplateFieldScannerTest.java), [ShTemplateFieldLintTest](../shio-app/src/test/java/com/viglet/shio/api/agent/verify/ShTemplateFieldLintTest.java)). The half SH192 could not deliver: `{{headline}}` against a post-type that renamed the field to `title` compiles, renders empty, and is indistinguishable from content nobody wrote — SH168's defect wearing a template. At write time the owner is genuinely unknown, since a `Region`'s post-type declares `HTML`/`JAVASCRIPT` while the fields its template interpolates belong to whatever page is bound to the layout that slots it. So it is a lint, and `template-unknown-field` joins `checks=content`.
  <br>**It iterates bindings, not pages — and that was a finding, not an optimisation.** §XV.17 called for "a lint over resolved pages"; building it established that the resolution does not depend on the page at all. `site.postTypeLayout` is keyed by **post-type**, and a layout's slots are static `sh-region` attributes, so every page of a type resolves to the same layout and the same regions. A thousand articles resolve once, and the finding is addressed at the **layout or region post** — the artefact somebody edits — rather than at a page of which there could be a thousand. Being subject-addressed also makes SH143's scoping work for free: a finding is emitted only when the post holding the template is one of the run's subjects.
  <br>**Two severities, because there are two kinds of interpolation.** A top-level `{{TEXT}}` resolves against the page's model and the page's post-type is known, so an undeclared name is an **error**: it renders empty on every page of that type, always. Inside `{{#query}}` the rows are whatever posts the helper found, so the strongest honest claim is that **no post-type in the instance** declares the name — a **warning**, which is exactly SH99's line that `ok` is false only for what the CMS can prove from inside itself. Row values (`title`, `link`, `summary`, …) are never reported, or every legitimate listing body would be a finding.
  <br>**The scope is the whole difference, which is why the scanner is not `Template#collect`.** Handlebars.java does offer `collect(TagType.VAR)` and it returns every variable flat, with no indication of which block it sits in — so it cannot tell the page's `{{TEXT}}` from a listed post's. A brace scanner tracking block depth is small, depends on no internal API, and gets the one thing right that matters. It follows `ShTemplateValidator`'s precedent for the same stated reason: the public AST does not distinguish a helper call from a section over a context value.
  <br>**The negative cases got most of the attention**, because a rule with false positives is one authors learn to ignore (SH192's finding, applied again). Not reported: the reserved frames (`post.`/`site.`/`theme.`/`render.`), `this` and its `./` and `../` forms, data variables, subexpressions, literals, partials, comments, a block's own name, and an inline helper's name — `{{file_url HERO}}` reports **HERO** and not `file_url`, which would otherwise be a false positive on the one helper the 2018 navigation region used. A block's first positional argument is reported in the **enclosing** scope, since `{{#if TEXT}}` and `{{#getRelation SECTIONS}}` ask about the current scope — and that last one is the reference that matters most for an SH95 `Page`, where a wrong field name renders the whole composition empty.

  <br>In `content` rather than a group of its own, deliberately: a template *is* content (the decision SH183 turns on), it costs nothing on a site with no `postTypeLayout` because there are no bindings to walk, and a new group would mean every existing `checks=content` caller silently not getting it while adding churn to the manifest and the MCP golden for no semantic gain.
- **SH193** — **A shared region has a blast radius, and an unreachable template says so** ([ShTemplateGraph](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/render/ShTemplateGraph.java), [ShAgentChanges](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/agent/dto/ShAgentChanges.java), [ShAgentChangesService](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/agent/ShAgentChangesService.java), [ShAgentVerifyService](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/agent/verify/ShAgentVerifyService.java), [ShTemplateGraphTest](../shio-app/src/test/java/com/viglet/shio/render/ShTemplateGraphTest.java)). Composition is an attribute inside an HTML string — `<div sh-region="NAV">` — so "which layouts slot this region, which pages use those layouts, how many are published" was unanswerable. Editing a shared region was an unbounded change nobody could scope beforehand and `verify` could not prove afterwards, which is the difference between a CMS region and a component in one application where the blast radius is the file.
  <br>**Computed, not extracted — and that corrects the design.** §XV.11 proposed extracting slot references at write time into `ShReference`, "which already exists and already survives a move". It does not: `ShReference` joins `object_from`/`object_to` to `ShObject`, and **a post is not an `ShObject`** — the unified model is its own table — so a post-to-post edge would need a new table. It is not needed, and SH251 is why: that task established a page's presentation resolves from its **post-type**, so a site's whole forward index is one resolution per binding regardless of how many pages exist, and inverting it is a map built in memory. Two properties come free that a persisted index would have had to earn — **it cannot go stale** (an extracted edge would need maintaining when a layout drops a slot, when a region is renamed, and when `site.postTypeLayout` changes, which is an `ShSite` write no post-level extraction would ever see), and **it needs no migration**, so it answers correctly for the 2018 `bootstrap-site` package the moment it is imported. What a persisted graph would buy is a cheap reverse query at scale; that trade is real and is not this one.
  <br>**Two surfaces from one graph, and no new contract.** On `/agent/changes`, a row whose object is a `PageLayout` or `Region` carries `affects` — the layouts, the post-types, the draft count and the published count. That is §XV.11's own suggestion and it buys two things: it arrives at the moment the question is asked (an agent has just edited a shared region and the next question is always "what did I just touch"), and it needs **no twelfth MCP tool**, so `shio_changes` carries it for free — which matters because the tool count is capped at 12 and `tools/list` is paid every turn (SH132). `published` is separate rather than a total, because "how many are published" is the number that decides whether the edit was safe to make now.

  <br>**And `verify` gained the inverse, which is the half that is a defect**: `unused-region` (no layout slots it) and `unused-layout` (no post-type binds it) — content nobody can reach, previously indistinguishable from content merely not visited. **Warnings**, deliberately: a region waiting for the layout that will slot it is work in progress, and SH99's rule is that `ok` is false only for what the CMS can prove is wrong. A gate that failed on work in progress is a gate people bypass. The messages name the exact `sh-region="…"` and the bound layouts, because a title differing in case or spacing is the usual cause and the fix is then a comparison.
  <br>**SH136's lint caught a real defect in this code**: `Set.copyOf(layoutsByRegion.keySet())`, whose iteration order comes from a per-JVM salt. It is only a membership test today — which is exactly the reasoning that would have justified the `byte-stable-exempt` hatch, and the reason not to take one is that the next caller to iterate or serialize it would inherit an unstable order silently, with nothing to fail. A `TreeSet` over the `TreeMap`'s keys is sorted for free.
  <br>The **pre-edit** form of the question shipped in turn as **SH262**, below.
- **SH298** — **An unused-template finding says what happened, not just that something is wrong** ([ShTemplateGraph](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/render/ShTemplateGraph.java), [ShAgentVerifyService](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/agent/verify/ShAgentVerifyService.java), [ShTemplateGraphTest](../shio-app/src/test/java/com/viglet/shio/render/ShTemplateGraphTest.java)). `unused-region`, `unused-layout` and `unused-theme` all walked one site's graph and reported the same sentence — nothing here uses this — which is true and is not what the reader needs, because the two cases that actually happen looked identical.
  <br>**A template in the wrong site got a fix line naming a layout it cannot find.** "Add `sh-region="X"` to the layout that should show it" is unactionable when that layout is next door. The graph already held every site's bindings, so the finding now names the site where that title *is* used and points at `post.move` — a stray template is a move, not a re-creation. Scoped to the run's own sites and never the instance: a finding naming a site the caller cannot read would be a disclosure, and an unhelpful one.
  <br>**A site that binds nothing reported one finding per template** when the defect is a single missing `postTypeLayout` entry. Each finding now says so, so a reader who acts on one is not sent to fix the same root cause N times. The sentence is appended, so a finding with nothing extra to say is byte-identical to what it was.
  <br>This is message quality rather than detection, and it is worth a task for a reason SH142 makes concrete: a warning a reader cannot act on is a warning that ends up in the baseline file, where it stops reporting anything at all.
- **SH268 (with SH189 complete)** — **`shio import` accepts a package, and the MCP half is CLI-shaped by construction** ([import.mjs](../cli/src/commands/import.mjs), [admin-client.mjs](../cli/src/admin-client.mjs), [index.mjs](../cli/src/index.mjs), [commands.test.mjs](../cli/test/commands.test.mjs), [ShAgentP1ConformanceTest](../shio-app/src/test/java/com/viglet/shio/api/agent/ShAgentP1ConformanceTest.java)). An SH68 package is a **zip**: a client with no filesystem can neither read one nor put one in a JSON-RPC message, and both ways of pretending otherwise are worse than saying so — a URL the server fetches is SH101's request-forgery surface argued a second time, and a base64 body is a megabyte of tokens for what this command does in a line. So the P1 inventory moves `exchange` from `REST_ONLY` ("an agent cannot accept a package") to **`CLI_ONLY` with the reason** — the manifest telling an MCP client which tool to reach for, instead of letting it find out by failing. Export stays declared: a zip *out* is a byte stream a caller can already ask for.

SH183 made a site visible with no front end and no project, and SH327 declared and CSRF-narrowed the endpoint that provisions the render model. What neither could fix: **a client that speaks only JSON-RPC has no HTTP of its own**, and `PUT /api/v2/post-type/{name}` refuses a system type — which is exactly why `POST /api/v2/render/post-types` exists.   <br>**Five checks, and the fifth is the one with teeth.** "Every pointer resolves" would have passed while eight lines pointed at one section about three other tasks; the rule that catches it is **if a section names a task, that task's line must point at it** — and it needs no exemption list, because an epic section that names none of its follow-ups (§VI.1's four lines, §VIII.11's one) has no section of its own to be pointed at. The other four: every section is numbered, no number or body is repeated, every pointer resolves, and a section whose task is no longer in the backlog must say why it is still there (✅/shipped/superseded) — which is the check that would have caught SH300's leftover on the commit that shipped it.
  <br>Verified by planting one defect per claim: five planted, five red.

A name the page's schema lacks falls back to the field name, which is indistinguishable from a type that declares no labels: silent, and wrong in the direction that looks fine.
  <br>**Both candidates measured, and §XVI.52's premise about the winner was wrong.** Emitting the row's type per row costs **~31 bytes on every listing row of every page** — ~620 on a twenty-row listing — paid by every visitor forever for a case only the editor uses, which is SH121's trade about per-row ids and it went the other way. Resolving it in the console was filed as "one fetch it is going to make anyway"; in fact the console **never called `getEditable`** — it patches by id at save time, and that method had sat in the service with no caller. But it is still the right answer, because the fetch it needs *is* the one that answers the question: `GET /api/v2/cda/post/{id}` returns `{ post, fields }`, and those fields are the declared fields **of that post's own type**. One call when a curator clicks — already a human round trip — and **zero bytes** for every visitor who never opens the editor.
  <br>**The fallback is the old behaviour, not a blank panel.** The CDA read needs the WRITE token the editor already requires to save, so with no token chosen the labels come from the page's type exactly as they did after SH303 — an editor that cannot save is not made worse by labels that are only right about the page.

Five tests: a blank label is *absent* rather than empty (an empty string renders as a missing label), the post wins when it can be read, the page's type is the fallback, nothing-to-load is a state rather than a fetch, and **the cache key distinguishes the two sources** — keyed by name alone, selecting a row right after a page field would have skipped the fetch, which is the defect with a cache in front of it. And the two vocabularies are not one contract forked: the renderer writes `data-shio-*`, an external front end's author writes `data-sh-*`; two *producers*, two vocabularies. Two copies of one script is the actual duplication, and that is what went.

So there are two ceilings, and `naive.max-silent-drops` is the one SH331 and SH332 exist to lower. The classifier is mechanical: the call carried a key the tool's own `inputSchema` does not declare, and it succeeded anyway — checkable without knowing what the key *meant*, which is what lets the sweep cover tools nobody has made a mistake on yet.
  <br>**The sweep is the finding.** `shio_context`, `shio_find`, `shio_verify` and `shio_changes` all accept an unrecognised key and answer 200, so SH331's one case is a **class**: four of six read tools ignore arguments silently, which is a direct violation of the rule SH320 settled. (`shio_read` and `shio_digest` refuse first for a missing required argument, not because they validate — worth knowing before reading their rows as compliance.) The ceilings are set to the measured values, and the sweep grows with the tool count, so a new tool that ignores unknown arguments fails here instead of arriving quietly.
  <br>**Its own database** (SH315): `shio_context` with no site describes the whole instance and `shio_remember` writes to it, so on the shared datasource both would depend on what every other test created.
  <br>**One number in the first run was measuring the fixture, and SH331 found it.** The drop count was right — 2 naive rows plus 4 sweep rows, all genuinely 200-with-a-key-ignored — but the *teaching* count included four rows that failed because the fixture named a site the isolated database did not contain. A benchmark about argument names must fail only for an argument name, so it now seeds the site it names. Recorded rather than quietly corrected, because it is the same class as SH324: a fixture describing something the run is not actually about.
- **SH345** — **A read-only transaction must not eat the refusal it just wrote** ([ShAgentSiteAccess](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/agent/ShAgentSiteAccess.java), [ShTeachingRollbackLintTest](../shio-app/src/test/java/com/viglet/shio/api/agent/ShTeachingRollbackLintTest.java), [ShAgentUnknownSiteRefusalTest](../shio-app/src/test/java/com/viglet/shio/api/agent/ShAgentUnknownSiteRefusalTest.java)). Found by SH340's own first run, which crashed instead of measuring. **`GET /api/v2/agent/find?site=nope` answered a 500**, not SH80's teaching 404: `ShAgentSiteAccess` is `@Transactional(readOnly = true)` and throws `UnknownSiteException`, so as a *participating* transaction its interceptor called `setRollbackOnly()` — and `ShAgentReadService.find`, which declares `noRollbackFor` precisely to avoid this, then failed at **commit** with `UnexpectedRollbackException`. The refusal, its `fix` and its list of readable sites were all destroyed by a transaction attribute one bean away, and the failure surfaced nowhere near its cause.
  <br>**SH171 diagnosed this exact shape for `ShAddressResolver` and SH249 for `ShPageRenderService.render`. Nobody asked which other beans had it** — so the deliverable is the lint (SH322's habit, and this is its third application in this block). The rule is safe as an absolute: on a read-only transaction there is nothing to roll back, so rollback-only can only take away a caller's ability to report the failure. A **writing** transaction is deliberately out of scope, because a refused batch must roll back and that is what makes `ShAgentBatchService` atomic.
  <br>**Two corrections the lint needed before it was right, both found by running it.** Keyed on any read-only annotation in the file, it flagged `ShPostTypeAdminService` and `ShRenderPostTypes`, whose read methods are read-only and whose *writing* methods throw — requiring `noRollbackFor` there would be asking a refusal not to roll back a write. A lint that does not catch its own motivating case is the under-reporting failure in its purest form, and it was only visible because the answer was already known. It now keys on a **class-level** annotation (column 0 — a method annotation is indented) and matches any qualifier; the known limit, a method-level `readOnly` that throws, is declared rather than silently uncovered.
  <br>**The set of teaching exceptions is derived, never listed** — 83 of them, from `class X extends ShTeachingException` — because a hand-kept list is what SH260 removed for helpers and SH300 for DOM attributes, and it fails the same way: a new refusal type nobody adds is a bean the lint stops covering, with nothing failing. Five beans were fixed; the behaviour is asserted separately from the shape, since the attribute could be present and the refusal still lost.
- **SH339** — **The inverse of the CSRF lint: which mutating paths can an agent write to at all** ([ShStatelessReachabilityLintTest](../shio-app/src/test/java/com/viglet/shio/spring/security/ShStatelessReachabilityLintTest.java), [ShCsrfAccessDeniedHandler](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/spring/security/ShCsrfAccessDeniedHandler.java), [ShCsrfRefusalBodyTest](../shio-app/src/test/java/com/viglet/shio/spring/security/ShCsrfRefusalBodyTest.java)). `ShCsrfExemptionLintTest` asks whether a blanket exemption is a *decision* — the right question from the security side, and it leaves the operator side entirely unasked. The cost was a recurring class: SH170 (creating a site needs session + CSRF, worked around by hand in `e2e/provision.mjs`), then SH327 (`/api/v2/render/**`) and SH335 — the same defect three times, each found by a human doing a build rather than by a build failing.
  <br>**25 mutating controller roots, 8 stateless-writable.** Of the 17 that require a browser session, 5 are `AGENT_EQUIVALENT` (the capability has an address-native form — SH170's own resolution was to grow `site.upsert`, not to open `POST /api/v2/site` to a token), 9 are `CONSOLE_ADMIN` (an agent minting or widening its own credential is the escalation Block L exists to prevent — the one entry that must never move), and **3 are real gaps**: `/api/v2/render/post-types` (SH327), `/api/v2/site-webhook` (SH343) and `/api/v2/preview-token` (SH344).
