The scanner reads source like `ShCsrfExemptionLintTest` does, resolves all three spellings of `@RequestMapping` this codebase uses, and **fails rather than skips** a mutating controller whose root it cannot resolve — silent under-reporting is the one way a lint like this goes wrong. `covers()` is asserted against `/api/v2/site` vs `/api/v2/site-webhook`, the case where a sloppy prefix match would have hidden SH343.

Both are asserted, because one alone would pass on a handler that gives everybody the browser's answer. The **status stays 403** (the console's axios interceptor re-fetches and retries on exactly that, so the body is purely additive); it is wired onto **`CsrfFilter` alone** through an `ObjectPostProcessor` rather than as the chain-wide `accessDeniedHandler`, since a CSRF rejection and an authorization denial have different remedies and one handler for both would have to guess which it is sending; and the body is an ordered map rather than a serialized `ProblemDetail`, because an order that reaches the wire is a decision (P5).
- **SH325** — **The widget catalogue is seeded per widget, so the render model is creatable on an instance that already exists** ([ShWidgetOnStartup](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/onstartup/widget/ShWidgetOnStartup.java), [ShOnStartup](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/onstartup/ShOnStartup.java), [ShRenderPostTypes](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/render/ShRenderPostTypes.java), [ShWidgetSeedTest](../shio-app/src/test/java/com/viglet/shio/onstartup/widget/ShWidgetSeedTest.java)). The whole catalogue was guarded by `if (findAll().isEmpty())`, so SH252's `Ace Editor - CSS` existed only on a brand-new database and `POST /api/v2/render/post-types` answered **500** on every install older than the feature — SH183's render model uncreatable exactly where real users are. The sharpest part: **SH289's `reconcile` failed identically**, the verb written to repair an older instance's render model broken by the defect it exists to repair, because both go through `specsFor`. One reader, one bug, both doors.
  <br>**There were two guards and the task named one.** Fixing the `isEmpty()` check alone would have changed nothing: `ShOnStartup` calls the seed **inside** its own first-time gate (`ShConfigVarOnStartup.FIRST_TIME_NAME`), so on an existing instance the method was never invoked at all. - **SH338** — **P1 has an instrument, and its exception list is the first honest inventory of how far the law is honoured** ([ShAgentP1ConformanceTest](../shio-app/src/test/java/com/viglet/shio/api/agent/ShAgentP1ConformanceTest.java)). Eleven lints in this repository guarded *internal consistency* — the code agrees with itself, with its own documentation, or a decision was taken rather than inherited — and **none** guarded *reachability*, so a consistency defect became a permanent guard while a reachability defect became a task that is fixed once and guards nothing. That is why the same classes kept coming back: SH160's `instanceMemory: true` half-truth returned as SH326's `serverRender: true`, and SH170's session+CSRF friction returned as SH327 and SH335 — each found by a human doing a build rather than by a build failing. **P1, the law the product is named after, was the only one of the ten with no instrument.**
  <br>**Every `features` key is classified, and a `true` must be delivered by something that exists.** A registered `ShMcpTool` (the strictest bar — what an MCP-only client can invoke) or a path in the manifest's own endpoint index (an agent with HTTP, and *discoverable*, which is P2). Both sides were already machine-readable, so this needed no new metadata. **A feature is not 1:1 with a tool**, and forcing it to be would make the table lie in the direction hardest to notice: `teachingErrors`, `terseResponses`, `conditionalReads`, `fieldProjection`, `contentAcl`, `publishGate` and `agentTokenScope` are properties of *every* route (`CROSS_CUTTING`), and `multiTenant`, `oidc`, `rateLimit`, `signedImageUrls` and `mcp` describe the installation rather than offering a capability (`INSTANCE_FACT`).

Four are deliberate and are recorded so the trade stays visible: `reviewQueue` (SH109 keeps the human's veto off the agent namespace — the one entry that is a decision rather than a gap), `graphql` (the front end's surface, not the agent's), `contentAsFiles` (CLI-shaped by P4's own argument) and `postTypeMerge` (adding it to `shio_apply` puts that tool over the SH132 ceiling it sits 3 tokens under). **And four had no task at all** — `locales` and `scheduledPublish` (**SH342**: `POST /post-unified/{id}/translate` and `/{id}/schedule` are id-keyed, undeclared, and have no address-native form, so an agent cannot make a translation or schedule a publish), `webhooks` (**SH343**: the agent reads its own delivery failures in diagnostics and cannot touch the subscription that produced them) and `previewTokens` (**SH344**: SH184's answer ends at a call the agent has no route to).   <br>**The list is asserted over the classification, not over what the instance advertises.** A config-driven flag (`webhooks`, `previewTokens`, `scheduledPublish`) drops out when an operator disables the subsystem, so an inventory keyed on the live map would shrink on a perfectly conformant instance — measuring the environment instead of the code, which is SH315's lesson one surface along. The run **prints** the whole classification, like the SH264 sweep benchmark. What it deliberately does **not** ask is whether a declared route works without a cookie: that is **SH339**, and keeping the two apart is the point — this one asks whether a capability has an agent route at all.
- **SH323** — **The locale-keyed URL finder answers an ordered list, and the lint catches the next one** ([ShPostUnifiedRepository](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/persistence/repository/post/ShPostUnifiedRepository.java), [ShFurlReaderLintTest](../shio-app/src/test/java/com/viglet/shio/persistence/ShFurlReaderLintTest.java), [ShContentLocaleTest](../shio-app/src/test/java/com/viglet/shio/api/cda/ShContentLocaleTest.java)). SH321 fixed the state-keyed finder and eight call sites and missed `findByShSite_IdAndFurlAndStateAndLocale` — the same declaration one parameter along, on the CDA's localized read — so two posts sharing a URL *within one locale* still reached the caller as `IncorrectResultSizeDataAccessException`. - **SH321** — **Two posts on one URL is a teaching 409, not a 500** ([ShPostUnifiedRepository](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/persistence/repository/post/ShPostUnifiedRepository.java), [ShAddressResolver](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/agent/ShAddressResolver.java)). Textual, like `ShFolderSiteInvariantTest` and `ShByteStabilityLintTest`, because SH278 established that this defect class is **invisible on H2 and appears on somebody else's engine** — no behavioural test in this suite can reach it.
- **SH320 / SH287** — **One rule for what an unrecognised parameter value means** ([ShAgentFlag](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/agent/ShAgentFlag.java), [ShAgentAPI](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/agent/ShAgentAPI.java), [ShAgentParameterRuleTest](../shio-app/src/test/java/com/viglet/shio/api/agent/ShAgentParameterRuleTest.java)). - **SH315** — **A test that measures the whole instance may not share it, and now that is enforced** ([ShBenchmarkIsolationLintTest](../shio-app/src/test/java/com/viglet/shio/api/agent/benchmark/ShBenchmarkIsolationLintTest.java)). Neither had ever failed, because nothing else happened to record an incident — which is a coincidence, not a property, and exactly the latent order-dependence the lint exists for. The `-it` suffix is also an allowed *shared* name, because those ITs are one scenario across several files rather than independent measurements.
- **SH314** — **"Bounded by bindings, not pages" is a measurement now, not an argument** ([ShTemplateGraphScaleBenchmarkTest](../shio-app/src/test/java/com/viglet/shio/api/agent/benchmark/ShTemplateGraphScaleBenchmarkTest.java)). SH311 sharpened the doubt: a change aimed at the digest sweep made a `verify` pass 2.3× cheaper by removing re-resolution, which is a strong hint that re-resolution rather than the walk was the cost.
  <br>**Two dials, because one can only answer "it grew."** A site with 2 bindings and 60 pages costs **12 queries** to graph; one with 20 bindings and 6 pages costs **84**. Thirty times the pages and a tenth of the bindings is seven times cheaper — so the walk really is per binding, and the three designs' shared premise holds.
  <br>**Both regimes measured, and the uncached one is the honest answer.** Inside a read-only transaction SH311's cache collapses the per-binding walk as well (84 → **8**), because every binding of one site resolves the same layout, region and theme lists. That number is what production pays; it is not what the *claim* is about, and measuring only it would have answered "the cache works" — SH311's question, not this one.
  <br>**It also caught the confound it was about to create.** The first version lived inside `ShRenderSweepBenchmarkTest`, and its two large fixture sites pushed that class's three-site `verify` number from 59 to **159** — a benchmark silently reporting another benchmark's fixture, passing or failing on method order. Its own class with its own database fixes it, which is the fourth sighting of the same lesson (SH239, SH272, SH289): **a shared fixture makes every measurement an input to the others**, and the instance-wide ones are where it hides.
- **SH311** — **A sweep resolves the presentation chain once, and a writing transaction gets no cache at all** ([ShPageRenderService](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/render/ShPageRenderService.java), [ShRenderSweepBenchmarkTest](../shio-app/src/test/java/com/viglet/shio/api/agent/benchmark/ShRenderSweepBenchmarkTest.java)). SH264 measured the case for this rather than arguing it: every page of a site re-read its layout, both its regions and its theme, so a ten-page proof was ten full presentation chains — per-page work carrying per-**type** information, since a binding resolves to the same templates for every page of its type (SH251's finding, which is what made the graph affordable in the first place).
  <br>**The lifetime was the whole design question, and the answer is a read-only transaction.** A longer-lived cache must be invalidated when a layout, a region or a theme is written *and* when `site.postTypeLayout` changes — that last one an `ShSite` write no post-level listener would see, which is the trap SH193 avoided by computing its graph instead of storing it. Scoped to one transaction, staleness cannot outlive the call: a `?digest=true` proof over ten affected pages, a preview render, an `/agent/render` request.
  <br>**A writing transaction gets no cache, and that is a condition rather than a convention** — `isCurrentTransactionReadOnly()` is on the line above the lookup, so a future writer that renders mid-write cannot silently read what it has just replaced. SH275's lesson about premises that quietly stop being true, applied while writing the premise.
  <br>**Measured, both shapes.** A sweep of ten pages in one read-only transaction: **6 queries per page**, down from 19. A `verify` pass over three sites: **59 queries, down from 137** — the graph resolves through the same path, so SH307's suspected multiplication mostly went with it. And the standalone number is *unchanged at 19*, which is correct and is now asserted with its reason: **independent calls share nothing**, because a cache that made them diverge would be one living longer than a transaction. If that number ever drops to meet the sweep's, something is caching across calls and the invalidation question has been reopened without anyone saying so.
  <br>The benchmark's ceilings were tightened as the numbers came in (30 marginal, 12 per swept page, 120 for the three-site pass) rather than left at the comfortable values first written — a ceiling with 6× headroom catches nothing.
- **SH264** — **A whole-site structural proof is measured, and it does not reuse anything** ([ShRenderSweepBenchmarkTest](../shio-app/src/test/java/com/viglet/shio/api/agent/benchmark/ShRenderSweepBenchmarkTest.java), [token-budgets.properties](../shio-app/src/test/resources/token-budgets.properties)). Since SH249 a digest composes the page for real, so a per-page proof pays a render each, and three tasks had piled up against the same unknown number — this one, SH307 (`usedElsewhere` building every site's graph per finding) and SH310 (message length on a many-template site). Block M's discipline is that a cost is measured rather than asserted; "bounded by construction" was an argument, not a number.
  <br>**Queries, not wall-clock.** A timing assertion on a shared machine is a flake, and SH250's lesson is that a flake is worse than a break because it teaches people that red might mean nothing. Hibernate's statement count is deterministic and is the cost that actually scales here — and it answers the question in the form the tasks ask it: *does this grow with pages, or with bindings?*
  <br>**The measurement: 21 queries for the first page of a site, and 21 for every page after it.** So the answer is **bindings are not reused at all** — every page re-resolves its layout, both its regions and its theme. A ten-page site is ten full presentation chains. That is asserted rather than remembered, in SH274's shape: the test asserts the marginal cost *equals* the first-page cost, so the day somebody adds a cache the assertion fails and sends them to reopen the question rather than leaving the story stale.
  <br>**It also answers the other two.** A `verify` pass over three sites is **137 queries** and carries **1,119 characters** of finding prose — so SH307's suspected multiplication is real but small at this size, and SH310's worry about SH298/SH308's longer messages has a number to watch. Both retired into this benchmark's ceilings, which are set close (250 / 2,000) rather than at the comfortable numbers first written, because a ceiling with 6× headroom catches nothing.
  <br>**Printed on every run, not only on failure** — SH264's deliverable is the number, and a benchmark that speaks only when it breaks leaves the next person to re-derive what normal is.
  <br>It opened **SH311**: a whole-site sweep re-resolving the presentation chain per page is exactly what a cache keyed on `(site, post-type)` would remove, and now the case for one is a measurement rather than a guess.
- **SH308** — **The finding names the layout post, not just the site** ([ShTemplateGraph](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/render/ShTemplateGraph.java), [ShAgentVerifyService](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/agent/verify/ShAgentVerifyService.java)). SH298's new sentence said *"a region of that name is used in Blog"* — what happened, and then the reader had to go and find it. A site name is not an address, and a layout title is not one either; the **layout post** is (SH79), and it is the thing to open. `usedElsewhere` now carries the post rather than the site name, and the message reads *"That name is used by 'SH193_ARTICLE_LAYOUT' in 'blog' (post:blog/l-article)"*.
  <br>**A one-line message change that was a signature change**, which is the point: the graph had the post all along — `templatesFor` resolves it — and returning a title threw it away at the boundary. SH80's promise is that a finding carries what to do next, and this was the one instruction in the rule that ended at the reader's judgement.
  <br>**The same-site "Bound: A, B" list stays titles, deliberately.** Those layouts are in the site the reader is already looking at, and the finding's own address is in it too — an address there would be noise for a lookup that is one listing away. The distinction worth keeping is that a **cross-site** pointer needs an address because nothing else in the message can find it.
- **SH303** — **A field's label comes from the model, and the dead read is gone** ([shio-editor.js](../shio-app/src/main/resources/render/shio-editor.js), [visual-editor.page.tsx](../shio-react/src/app/console/universal-editor/visual-editor.page.tsx), [universal-editor.model.ts](../shio-react/src/models/universal-editor/universal-editor.model.ts)). The bridge labelled every field with `el.getAttribute("data-shio-label") || prop`, and **nothing has ever emitted `data-shio-label`** — `annotateEditable` translates `sh-field` and `sh-post` and has no `sh-label` case — so the fallback was the only branch that ever ran and every field in the Universal Editor was labelled `TEXT`, `HTML` or `DESCRIPTION` rather than "Headline". Found by SH300's table, which is the argument for tables of that kind: the defect is invisible from either side alone, because the script looks right (it has a fallback) and the composer looks right (it translates everything it knows about).
  <br>**The read was removed rather than the write added.** A field's label is declared once, by the post-type, where the console already shows it and `shio pull` round-trips it; a copy in the markup is a second place for it to be wrong and a thing an author has to keep in sync. So the page sends its post-type with each selection — from `data-shio-post-type`, which SH185 put on `<body>` *for exactly this* and which nothing had ever read — and the console resolves labels from `GET /api/v2/post-type/{name}`, the SH16 name-keyed surface it already uses. Two dead ends closed with one edge.
  <br>**The lookup fails silently, on purpose.** No labels means the panel shows the field name, which is what it showed before this existed — a labelling nicety must not be able to break the editor. It is fetched once per post-type and cached in a ref, so selecting a second field re-renders nothing.
  <br>**And it taught the SH300 test something.** Emptying `READ_BUT_NEVER_EMITTED` left the test failing, because the document still *discusses* `data-shio-label` in a paragraph explaining why the read went away — and a whole-file scan read that prose as a claim that the attribute exists. **The contract is the table**: the scan now reads rows only, and prose is free to talk about names that no longer exist, which is most of what makes a document worth reading.
- **SH300** — **The rendered DOM is a contract, and it is written down and checked** ([SH185-universal-editor-protocol.md](specs/SH185-universal-editor-protocol.md), [ShRenderedDomContractTest](../shio-app/src/test/java/com/viglet/shio/render/ShRenderedDomContractTest.java)). Fourteen `data-shio-*` attributes had accumulated across four blocks — defined in three classes, explained in as many changelog entries, read by the editor bridge, by anyone debugging a preview and (SH299) by the digest — with no single statement of what they mean. SH185's protocol document covered the editor's four and predated the rest, so the only way to learn the other ten was `git log`. The same gap SH272 closed for helpers, on the other side of the renderer.
  <br>**Asserted, not maintained by hope** — SH273's instrument, because the failure direction here is *silent under-documentation*: an attribute gains a meaning nobody wrote down and the page still renders, so no functional test can see it. `ShRenderedDomContractTest` fails the build when the code emits an attribute with no row, or a row names one nothing writes. It reads **source** rather than reflecting over constants, for `ShCsrfExemptionLintTest`'s reason: an inline literal is exactly what a constant scan would miss, and is the likeliest way a fifteenth attribute arrives. Proved by mutation — adding an undocumented attribute to the composer fails it.
  <br>**Three producers, one contract, three tables.** The renderer emits eleven; the bridge script sets three more *in the browser* (`data-shio-editing` on `<html>`, `data-shio-editable` per field, `data-shio-editor` on its own stylesheet), which exist only while `?editor=true` is on. A reader of the DOM cannot tell which side wrote an attribute, so the test treats them as one set while the document keeps them apart — the lifetime is what differs.
  <br>**Writing the table found two defects, which is what the table is for.** `data-shio-label` is **read by the bridge and emitted by nothing**: `annotateEditable` never translates an author's `sh-label`, so the editor silently falls back to the property name and a human-readable label has never worked (**SH303**). And there are **two editor scripts with two vocabularies** — SH185's injected `render/shio-editor.js` (`data-shio-*`) and the older `universal-editor/shio-editor.js` (`data-sh-*`, 550 lines, still served, written for a front end that includes it itself), which is **SH304**. The read-but-never-written name is a *row in the table* rather than an omission, because from the reading side it looks like a working feature.
- **SH299** — **A structural proof cannot come back green on a page that says it is broken** ([ShAgentDigest](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/agent/verify/dto/ShAgentDigest.java), [ShAgentRenderService](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/agent/verify/ShAgentRenderService.java), [ShRegionComposer](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/render/ShRegionComposer.java), [ShAgentRenderedDigestTest](../shio-app/src/test/java/com/viglet/shio/api/agent/verify/ShAgentRenderedDigestTest.java)). `/agent/render` hashes a page's structure — headings, landmarks, links, images, words — and the three defect markers (`data-shio-region-missing`, `-region-unpublished`, `-theme-missing`) are attributes on elements that outline does not describe. So an agent could write, render, compare the digest and report green on a page carrying all three: the same false green SH141 was filed for one level out, where a route resolved in the CMS and the front end did not serve it.
  <br>**A count beside the digest, and in neither hash.** Folding the markers into `digest` would be *worse* than leaving them out: the hash would then move when a region is **published**, which changes what the page contains and not its structure — and SH187's whole point is that two hashes exist so "I restyled it" and "I broke the outline" stay different answers. A third meaning smuggled into the first hash undoes that. A count is also what a caller branches on anyway.
  <br>**Present on every rendered page, all zeroes when clean** — unlike `appearance`, which is absent when it has nothing to say. The question here is "is this page broken", and a caller that had to tell *no markers* from *this build does not report markers* would be back at the ambiguity the field removes. The `source: content` fallback still carries none, because there is no page.
  <br>**The names come from the composer** (`ShRegionComposer.DEFECT_MARKERS`, now public), not from a second list in the verify package — SH260's rule about a capability set with five hand-kept copies, applied to the rendered side. A marker the renderer stops emitting or starts emitting cannot silently go uncounted.
  <br>**Deliberately not a new `verify` finding.** The lint already reports every one of these through its own queries, and one defect in two reports is two reports that can disagree — the rule `dangling-reference` set and the renderer follows.
- **SH297** — **A layout naming a theme that is not there says so, twice** ([ShTemplateGraph](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/render/ShTemplateGraph.java), [ShRegionComposer](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/render/ShRegionComposer.java), [ShPageRenderService](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/render/ShPageRenderService.java), [ShAgentVerifyService](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/agent/verify/ShAgentVerifyService.java)). The three presentation edges failed in three different ways and only two of them had been decided: an absent layout is a **409** (SH280), an absent region is a **marker in the HTML** (SH169/SH281), and an absent **theme was silence** — `themeOf` returned null, the page rendered with no stylesheet, and nothing anywhere said why. That is the worst of the three to debug, because *unstyled but serving* reads as a CSS fault rather than a missing post, so the search starts in the wrong place.
  <br>**Both halves of SH281's answer, because a theme degrades rather than fails.** The page carries `data-shio-theme` + `data-shio-theme-missing` on `<body>` with a constant comment, and `verify` reports `missing-theme` as an **error** against the layout. Marked and not refused: an unstyled page still serves, which is right for a preview — refusing is the layout level's job, because a page with no layout is not a page.
  <br>**An error, unlike the unused-* warnings beside it.** The layout *names* a theme and no post of that title exists in either state: a claim that turned out false, not a guess about whether somebody is still working, which is SH99's line for what makes `ok` false. Reported against the **layout**, because that is the post to edit — the theme does not exist, so it has no address.
  <br>**Checked in both states deliberately**, so a theme that exists only as a draft stays SH281's `unpublished-template` — a different finding with a different fix. One defect in two reports is two reports that can disagree.
  <br>**On `<body>` and not on a slot**, because a theme is not slotted: a layout names it in a field and decides itself where `{{theme.css}}` goes, so no element stands for it. The title travels as an **attribute**, where jsoup escapes it, and the comment is a constant — SH183's rule, third application, because a title is content and `-->` inside one would close the comment and put the rest of the page into the document as markup. "No theme named" and "a theme named that is not there" stay different facts, and only the second is marked.

So the blast radius of a theme edit, which is the *largest* in the model (one theme is typically named by every layout in a site), was the one question that answered nothing at all: SH262's `include=impact` returned no section for a `Theme`, indistinguishable from the same answer for an `Article`.

A `PER_CLASS` fixture makes every mutating test an input to the others (SH239's confound, third sighting); the fixture now **forces** the pre-SH277 state instead of creating it once, and the mutation fails as it should. - **SH272** — **What a template may call is discoverable** ([ShTemplateEngine](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/render/ShTemplateEngine.java), [ShRenderHelpers](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/render/ShRenderHelpers.java), [ShAgentContextService](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/agent/ShAgentContextService.java), [ShTemplateHelperDiscoveryTest](../shio-app/src/test/java/com/viglet/shio/render/ShTemplateHelperDiscoveryTest.java)). SH260 made the engine the one source of the capability set and every reader of it was internal — the write-time refusal, the SH251 scanner, the SH251 lint.   <br>**A signature, not a list, and it travels with the registration.** `register` gained a third argument — `{{#query folder= type= limit=}}` — because the shape is the part an author gets wrong and a hash parameter's name **exists nowhere but inside the helper's own body**: no downstream reader could have derived `folder=` from a `BLOCK` shape. It also asserts that `form`, deliberately unregistered since SH247, is never advertised — a list naming it would have the author write exactly what SH192 refuses.
- **SH277** — **A template written through the documented flow has a title, and no two share one** ([ShTemplateTitles](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/render/ShTemplateTitles.java), [ShRenderPostTypes](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/render/ShRenderPostTypes.java), [ShPostUnifiedWriteService](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/migration/unified/ShPostUnifiedWriteService.java), [ShAgentBatchService](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/agent/ShAgentBatchService.java), [ShTemplateTitleWriteTest](../shio-app/src/test/java/com/viglet/shio/render/ShTemplateTitleWriteTest.java)). SH263 made a duplicate template title an error in `checks=content` and nothing stopped one being created — the identity was enforced by a lint somebody had to run rather than by the write that broke it.
  <br>**Writing the first test found a larger defect underneath it: the SH183 flow could not produce an addressable template at all.** `ShRenderPostTypes` declared no `isTitle` field on `PageLayout`, `Region` or `Theme`, on a stated premise — "the title is the post's own column, not a field ... the thing the curator types into the title box" — and there is no title box: a unified post's title column is *derived by the writer* from whichever field carries `isTitle`, and `post.upsert` sends nothing but `data`. So every template written through the documented flow landed with an **empty title**, which no `sh-region` slot and no `postTypeLayout` binding can resolve to; and because the type did not declare `TITLE`, SH168 refused the key as undeclared, so there was no way to set it either. Measured, not reasoned: the first run of the new test returned `A post.upsert declares whole state, so writing a field the post-type has no place for…` for a `Region` carrying `TITLE`.
  <br>**Every render test built its fixture with `entityManager.persist` and `setTitle`, which is exactly why nothing caught it.** The flow SH183 documents — `POST /api/v2/render/post-types`, then `post.upsert` — was the one path with no end-to-end test, and the class comment on the new test says so, because the next fixture written that way will hide the next one. The fix restores what the 2018 package it was copied from already had: `TITLE` first, `Text`, required, `isTitle` — the part that got dropped when the field list was transcribed.
  <br>**The refusal lives on the post writer, so every surface refuses identically** — the console, the CDA, `/agent/batch`, a desired-state apply and a blueprint apply all go through `ShPostUnifiedWriteService` (SH201's rule that the two surfaces enforce the same thing). And the interactive-versus-bulk distinction §XVI.29 said "the write path does not draw anywhere and would need one" turned out to need **no new mechanism**: SH68's exchange import writes rows through the repository directly, so putting the check on the writer refuses the interactive write and leaves the bulk one alone, which is the outcome that task asked for. The bulk half's "report" is SH263's lint, already shipped — said out loud in the class comment, because the *absence* of a call there otherwise reads as something nobody got round to.
  <br>**A plan reports what a real run refuses** (SH168's rule), and asks the *same* component with the *same* derivation: `titleOf` was extracted from `applyTitleAndSummary` and shared rather than restated, because a second derivation would disagree with the writer the first time a type gains a title field — and the disagreement would read as the plan being right.
  <br>Two false positives it must not have, both asserted: **a template's own row is not its duplicate** (a DRAFT row and a PUBLISHED row share id *and* title, so comparing rows instead of ids would fail every edit and every publish of every template — the trap SH263's lint had to avoid one surface along), and **a trashed template's title is free**, which needs no clause because `ShPostUnified` carries `@SQLRestriction("deleted_date is null")` — the finder sees exactly what the renderer sees, and the two agreeing is what stops this refusing a title nothing could resolve to.
  <br>**The limit worth knowing:** `ensure` never touches an existing post-type (SH152's provision-never-upsert), so an instance that already created its render types keeps them without `TITLE` until the field is added by hand — the same trade SH252 made for the `Theme`'s CSS widget, and for the same reason: the alternative is a startup that rewrites somebody's model. It opened **SH289** (existing instances need a way to reconcile a system post-type) and **SH290** (nothing asserts that a system model matches the package it claims to be copied from).
- **SH262** — **A read answers what editing this template would affect** ([ShAgentDoc](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/agent/dto/ShAgentDoc.java), [ShAgentReadService](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/agent/ShAgentReadService.java), [ShAgentReadTerse](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/agent/ShAgentReadTerse.java), [ShReadTool](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/agent/mcp/tools/ShReadTool.java), [ShTemplateGraphTest](../shio-app/src/test/java/com/viglet/shio/render/ShTemplateGraphTest.java)). SH193 put `affects` on the change feed and SH194 put digests on a write, so *"what did I just touch"* and *"what did it do"* both have answers. The question an agent asks **first** — before rewriting a shared region, what does it reach — had none, and it is the one that decides whether to edit at all. `ShTemplateGraph.impactOf` already computed it; the whole task was a surface.
  <br>**`?include=impact` on `/agent/read`, which was the third of §XV.20's three candidates and the only one that could ship.** A field attached unconditionally would have made every reader pay tokens for a question some are not asking (P3). A `GET /agent/impact?address=` reads clearest and is a fourth contract restating a graph two surfaces already expose (P10) — and, decisively, it would have been **REST-only**: the MCP tool count is capped at 12 with 11 used, so a new endpoint with no tool is a capability law P1 forbids. Riding the read means `shio_read` carries it, and the subject of a read is already an address.
  <br>**It cost no budget.** One boolean of schema put `tools/list` at 2379 against its 2360 ceiling, so `shio_read`'s description was trimmed *first* — the rule this repository follows, and the one that took `shio_remember` from 167 to 128 before its ceiling moved. Wording went ("the current content of one or more posts" → "post content"; "One or more post addresses" → "Post addresses", since the schema type is an array and says that in a place a client cannot misread), teaching stayed: the draft-preference, the reason to project, and the address example are all still there. The tool came out at 165 against 182 before, and the list fits **under the unchanged ceiling** — a capability added for free.

Two lookups is exactly the arrangement that comes to disagree about which row it describes, and the DRAFT-preference is the thing they would disagree about — so the impact and the fields are guaranteed to be about the same row.

  <br>**In terse, its own `impact` line** rather than attributes on `doc`: the header describes the post, this describes everything *else* the post reaches, and a reader that does not know the line skips it instead of being handed a `doc` line with a wider meaning than it had.

- **SH249** — **The digest and the previewer compose the same page the same way** ([SH249-sections-and-regions.md](specs/SH249-sections-and-regions.md), [ShAgentRenderService](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/agent/verify/ShAgentRenderService.java), [ShPageRenderService](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/render/ShPageRenderService.java), [ShAgentRenderedDigestTest](../shio-app/src/test/java/com/viglet/shio/api/agent/verify/ShAgentRenderedDigestTest.java)). `/agent/render` composed a page's **sections** (SH169) and `/preview` composed its **regions** (SH183), and neither knew the other existed — so an agent proving structure and a human looking at the page could be reading two different compositions of the same post, with nothing reporting the disagreement. That is law P9 failing in the one place it is supposed to work, since the whole value of a cheap textual proof is that it stands in for looking.
  <br>**The prior question is settled in writing first**, because pointing the digest at the rendered HTML — obviously the better input — silently picks a winner otherwise. The decision: **sections and regions are two mechanisms, they compose, and the renderer has exactly one composition path.** A region is named by a *layout* by title and varies with the post-**type**; a section is named by a *page* by URL, in order, and varies with the **page**. Neither can absorb the other without losing something real. What joins them is SH247's `getRelation`: a section-composed page is rendered by the ordinary path, because its layout slots a region whose template iterates the field. So **sections are content a template reads, not a level of the render model** — which is what stops this from becoming a third path, and is SH185's "the engine never infers ownership" one level out.
  <br>**The digest therefore reads the rendered page** (`source: rendered`) whenever the post-type has a layout binding. SH169's synthetic composition **stays as the labelled fallback** (`source: content`) for a post that cannot be rendered — no binding yet, or no friendly URL to render at, which is SH172's `id:` case. Keeping it is not sentiment: an unbound type is the normal state of a site mid-build and answering "the hash of nothing" for it was the SH169 defect. A fallback that is *labelled* is strictly better than one that is guessed at, which is why `source` is in the response rather than implied.
  <br>**Every render failure is a fallback, never an error.** The renderer throws teaching 4xx for an unbound type, an absent layout and an unknown page — all correct for somebody who asked to *see* a page, all wrong for a digest, because a proof that started failing where it used to answer would break the SH99 loop for every unfinished site. The catch is narrow: `ShTeachingException` only, so a genuine failure is not swallowed.
  <br>**And it re-taught SH171's lesson one service along.** Catching a teaching exception thrown by an inner `@Transactional` marks the *caller's* transaction rollback-only, so eleven unrelated tests died at commit with `UnexpectedRollbackException` — nowhere near the catch that caused it. `ShPageRenderService.render` is now `noRollbackFor = ShTeachingException.class`, which is what SH171 already did for the agent read path. Worth naming twice precisely because the symptom appears at commit.
  <br>**SH187 becomes nearly free**, which was the stated reason to settle this: the artefact to snapshot is the rendered HTML, produced in-process with no browser and no outbound fetch, and it is now the same artefact the digest reads — so a structural proof and a visual one cannot disagree about which page they describe. The spec records the one-time consequence: a stored SH102 baseline or an accepted SH142 finding taken against the old composition has to be re-accepted once.
- **SH187** — **The agent gets an appearance payload, not a picture** ([ShHtmlAppearance](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/agent/verify/ShHtmlAppearance.java), [ShAgentRenderService](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/agent/verify/ShAgentRenderService.java), [ShAgentDigest](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/agent/verify/dto/ShAgentDigest.java), [ShAgentRenderedDigestTest](../shio-app/src/test/java/com/viglet/shio/api/agent/verify/ShAgentRenderedDigestTest.java)). SH101 proves structure; nothing proved a page *looks* right, so an agent asked to change appearance had to hand the question to a human — the expensive unit Block K exists to remove. SH102 shipped the right instrument for a human (`shio snapshot`: a PNG, a baseline, a diff) and said so explicitly, "for the human handoff rather than for the agent". Visual autonomy needs the agent to be the reader, which means a payload rather than an image, and SH249 had just made the artefact free: the rendered page, in-process, no browser and no outbound fetch.
  <br>**It is not a rendering and says so.** Computed style, box geometry and "does the hero overlap the nav" need a layout engine. What is extracted is the part of appearance that is *in the document*: the class inventory, which of those classes no stylesheet the page carries defines, inline `style="…"` counts, images with no declared size (the "page jumps on load" defect, and one of the few a parser can be certain about), and the external stylesheets that explain the rest. Small, honest, and it happens to cover the failure an **agent** actually creates — markup written against class names the theme does not have, which nothing else in the system reports.
  <br>**The undefined-class list is advisory, not a lint finding**, because a page may load a stylesheet this instance has never seen. The 2018 `openviglet/bootstrap-site` package is exactly that: its markup is full of Bootstrap classes from a CDN, so a rule reporting every class the `Theme` lacks would fire dozens of times on the one real example in the repository. A rule with false positives is one authors learn to ignore (SH192's finding, third application), so the set is reported with `externalStylesheets` beside it — which turns a confusing number into an explanation. An agent comparing two runs of its own page still gets the useful half: a class that was defined before its edit and is not now.

Both sort their own inputs before hashing, SH136's rule.

  <br>**The manifest gains `appearanceDigest: true` and `visualSnapshot` stays `false`**, which is the only honest pair: there is still no raster on this surface, and an agent that read `visualSnapshot: true` would go looking for a PNG and find none. That flag's own comment already argued this; SH187 adds the capability beside it rather than overstating the existing one.
  <br>**Its own test caught a silent bug in it.** `Pattern.compile("(?is)<style\b…")` — in a Java string literal `\b` is the **backspace character**, not the regex word boundary, so the pattern matched nothing, no stylesheet was found, and the comparison was skipped entirely. The failure direction that does not announce itself: an empty list reads as "nothing wrong". Rewritten as `<style(\s[^>]*)?>` so the intent survives without an escape whose meaning differs between the language and the regex.
- **SH194** — **A write returns the digests of the pages it affected** ([ShAgentProofService](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/agent/ShAgentProofService.java), [ShAgentChangeSet](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/agent/dto/ShAgentChangeSet.java), [ShAgentAPI](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/agent/ShAgentAPI.java), [ShTemplateGraphTest](../shio-app/src/test/java/com/viglet/shio/render/ShTemplateGraphTest.java)). - **SH189 (partial)** — **An import failure says which of four things went wrong, and a stateless caller can reach it** ([ShImportFailedException](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/imports/ShImportFailedException.java), [ShExchangeImportAPI](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/imports/ShExchangeImportAPI.java), [ShSecurityConfig](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/spring/security/ShSecurityConfig.java), [ShImportFailedExceptionTest](../shio-app/src/test/java/com/viglet/shio/api/imports/ShImportFailedExceptionTest.java)). `ShExchangeImportAPI` ended every failure with `ResponseEntity.badRequest().build()` — a bodiless 400 — while `ShExchangeException` knew exactly what was wrong. - **SH190** — **A diagnostics finding carries the frame it threw from** ([ShAgentIncidentFrames](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/agent/diagnostics/ShAgentIncidentFrames.java), [ShAgentErrorRecordingFilter](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/agent/diagnostics/ShAgentErrorRecordingFilter.java), [ShAgentIncidentStore](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/agent/diagnostics/ShAgentIncidentStore.java), [v2026.3.15.yaml](../shio-app/src/main/resources/db/changelog/v2026.3.15.yaml), [ShAgentIncidentFramesTest](../shio-app/src/test/java/com/viglet/shio/api/agent/diagnostics/ShAgentIncidentFramesTest.java)). An `api-error` finding reported the exception message and then advised: *"Retry it; if it fails again the instance log has the stack trace (the body never will)."* Accurate, and a protocol that stops one step short — it directs the agent to a file it has no access to, and in the session that found this the running instance was not writing to the log the repository contains. The message alone identified SH188 only because that exception named its own field; a `NullPointerException` inside a service method produced a finding that said a call failed and nothing about where, which is exactly as useful as the bare 500 it replaced.
  <br>**Frames, not a log tail** — the alternative, and worse on the three counts SH103 already argued: a tail hands over every request's data to answer a question that is always about one request, it is a per-deployment path an agent should not have to know, and it cannot be scoped by the SH2 allow-list or the SH54 ACL that bounds everything else here. Bounded, attributed evidence attached to the incident is smaller and safer than a file.
  <br>**Only Shio's own frames, at most three.** A full trace is mostly Spring, Tomcat and reflection — dozens of frames identical for every failure in the process, telling a reader nothing about this one. Trimming to `com.viglet.shio` is what makes the evidence a line rather than a page, and it is the same judgement a human makes reading a trace: find the first frame you own. Three because that is what gets read — where it threw, who called it, who called that; more is a stack trace by instalments, and the argument against carrying one does not weaken at four. **No arguments and no locals**: a frame is a *location*, and content in a diagnostics feed is how a log leaks what the ACL exists to protect. A Spring proxy frame (`…$$SpringCGLIB$$0`) is skipped, since it is the same method one indirection out and names a generated class.
  <br>**Absent, not empty, when there is nothing of ours in the trace** — a malformed request rejected by Tomcat has no frame of Shio's to name, and `""` would read as "we looked and there was no code here".   <br>**Persisted** (`v2026.3.15`, nullable `VARCHAR(500)` — short by construction, so a column and not a CLOB), because SH144's whole point is that "was anything failing while I was away" is answerable after a restart. Evidence living only in the process would have made the *durable* answer the weaker one. And a repeat that arrives without a frame **cannot erase** the frame the first occurrence carried — the same rule `fix` already followed, and the failure it prevents is a second occurrence caught somewhere shallower deleting the location that identified the problem.
  <br>The `fix` text changed with it: it used to end by pointing at a log file, and now names `frames` — something the reader can act on.
- **SH269** — **Every incident kind that has a throwable now carries its frame** ([ShWebhookDispatcher](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/webhook/ShWebhookDispatcher.java), [ShPostScheduler](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/schedule/ShPostScheduler.java), [ShThumbnailatorImageTransformPipeline](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/staticfile/transform/ShThumbnailatorImageTransformPipeline.java), [ShAgentIncidentFramesTest](../shio-app/src/test/java/com/viglet/shio/api/agent/diagnostics/ShAgentIncidentFramesTest.java)). SH190 attached the throwing location where an exception is *caught*, and that was one place — `api-error`. The three kinds whose failures are hardest to diagnose from a message had none, and they are the asynchronous ones nobody watches: a **scheduled publish** that threw at 03:00 recorded the symptom without the writer it threw inside; an **image transform** recorded "transform failed" identically for a corrupt source, a missing ImageIO writer and a re-encode fault, across a pipeline with four stages; a **webhook** dispatch error recorded the message with no sign of whether the fault was Shio's or the subscriber's.
  <br>**Four of the five recorders now pass a frame, and the fifth deliberately does not.** The webhook's *give-up* branch — delivery completed and the subscriber rejected it — has no exception of ours and nothing in Shio's code to point at, so it records without one. That is SH190's rule held rather than an omission, and this task is where it earned its keep: the distinction between "we failed" and "they refused" is now visible in the presence of the field.
  <br>**Guarded by a source lint rather than three integration fixtures**, which is the judgement worth recording. Reproducing a failing webhook dispatch, a corrupt image and a scheduled publish that throws is three fixtures asserting one line each — expensive, slow, and not testing the thing that actually goes wrong. What goes wrong is a `catch` that records the message and drops the throwable it is standing on, which is precisely what SH190 shipped with and is invisible until somebody reads a diagnostics row and finds no `frames`. So the test walks the source for `incidentLog.record(...)` inside a `catch` that passes no frame — and it was checked by reverting one call site, which named the file.
  <br>The lint over-reports by construction (a `catch (` anywhere in the preceding lines counts), which is the safe direction for a guard whose whole job is to notice an omission.
- **SH250** — **Mockito is a real agent, so the suite stops teaching people to disbelieve red** ([shio-app/pom.xml](../shio-app/pom.xml)). The suite printed this on every single run: *"Mockito is currently self-attaching to enable the inline-mock-maker. This will no longer work in future releases of the JDK."* Two problems stacked. Instrumentation installed by attaching an agent to the **running** JVM succeeds or fails depending on what has already been loaded — which is why `ShTenantSuspendedAccessTest` failed six of six once during Block P and passed on every re-run, in isolation and in the full suite, with no change to it or to anything it touches. And the JDK is removing dynamic agent loading, so the intermittent failure was on a timer to become permanent.
  <br>**Why this was worth doing before more features.** A flaky suite is more expensive than a broken one: it teaches everybody that a red run might mean nothing, which is how a real regression gets a re-run instead of an investigation. It is the same failure as a gate people have learned to bypass — SH99's argument for why warnings must not fail a build, pointed the other way.
  <br>**The wiring is the whole task, and the hypothetical turned out to be real.** SH250 was filed as an idea rather than designed work because "getting two agents onto one `argLine` is the part that actually takes care" and the note wondered about JaCoCo "if that is ever added". It is already there — the build prints `argLine set to -javaagent:…org.jacoco.agent…`. So `@{argLine}` (surefire's **late** replacement) rather than `${argLine}` was load-bearing rather than defensive: the Mockito agent appends to JaCoCo's value instead of overwriting it. The property is also declared **empty** in `<properties>`, because `@{argLine}` must resolve even on a profile where nothing has set it.
  <br>`maven-dependency-plugin`'s `properties` goal supplies `${org.mockito:mockito-core:jar}`; hard-coding the path would bind the build to one machine's local-repository layout. Failsafe gets the same treatment — the SH26 cross-database ITs boot the full context and mock alongside it — merged into its existing `configuration` block, since two of those on one plugin is a non-parseable POM.
  <br>Verified by the absence of both warnings across a full run (self-attach and "Dynamic loading of agents will be disallowed"), with 948 tests still green.
- **SH260** — **The helper catalogue has one source, and readers ask it** ([ShTemplateEngine](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/render/ShTemplateEngine.java), [ShRenderHelpers](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/render/ShRenderHelpers.java), [ShTemplateFieldScanner](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/render/ShTemplateFieldScanner.java), [ShTemplateValidator](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/render/ShTemplateValidator.java), [ShTemplateFieldLint](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/agent/verify/ShTemplateFieldLint.java)). Five places restated what `ShRenderHelpers.register()` knows: the validator's list of choices, the scanner's two exclusion sets, and the lint's copy of a row's keys. SH247 had to edit three in step to add two helpers and SH251 added the last two, so the cost was already visible — and **every failure mode was silent**: a registered helper missing from the scanner's list is reported as an unknown *field*, so the rule that exists to catch typos invents one; a row key missing from the lint's list is a warning on a correct template.
  <br>**The engine records what it is told, including the call shape.** `register(name, ShHelperShape, helper)` — `BLOCK`, `BLOCK_PATH_ARG`, `INLINE_PATH_ARG` — because the shape is precisely what the SH251 scanner needs and the registration is the only thing that knows it. Only distinctions that change how a *call is parsed* are in the enum: whether a helper reads the database is its own business, whether its first token is a field name is the scanner's, and getting that wrong is the difference between reporting `HERO` and reporting `file_url` as an undeclared field.
  <br>**The scanner takes the shapes as a parameter, not as an injected dependency**, so it stays pure — text in, references out — which is what keeps its own test cheap enough to assert every false-positive case. And there is deliberately **no overload that omits them**: a convenience form defaulting to "nothing is registered" would make a forgotten argument report every helper's name as undeclared, which is the worst failure this rule could have. A caller with no engine passes `ShHelperShapes.none()` and says so.
  <br>**SH136's lint caught two copies in the new code** — `Map.copyOf(registered)` and `Set.copyOf(...)`, whose iteration order comes from a per-JVM salt. Both are membership-only today, which is exactly the reasoning that would justify the `byte-stable-exempt` hatch, and neither took it: the validator already renders the *names* into a refusal message, so the map is one caller away from being observable output. `ShStableMap` and `TreeSet`-backed sets instead.
  <br>**Two of the new tests corrected my own expectations**, which is the argument for writing them: the refusal now lists helpers **alphabetically** rather than in registration order (a total order, per SH136 — and registration order was the hand-written list's accident of history, not a fact a reader needs), and asserting it needs a *parameterised unknown* helper rather than `{{#form}}`, since that name is in `KNOWN_MISSING_HELPERS` and takes the SH247 branch instead.
  <br>`KNOWN_MISSING_HELPERS` stays a list on purpose: it is a statement about what an author might reasonably expect, not about what exists, and it becomes empty when `form` lands. Handlebars' own `if`/`unless`/`each`/`with` also stay in the scanner, since they are not Shio's to register.
- **SH261** — **A hash argument that is a field is checked too** ([ShTemplateFieldScanner](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/render/ShTemplateFieldScanner.java), [ShTemplateFieldScannerTest](../shio-app/src/test/java/com/viglet/shio/render/ShTemplateFieldScannerTest.java)). SH251 read a block's first *positional* argument and treated a `name=value` pair as not-positional — right for `folder="/blog"`, since a quoted literal is not a field, and wrong for the **model-driven** form. So `{{#search q=TOPIC}}` and `{{#query folder=SECTION}}` produced no reference at all, which left the rule blind exactly where its subject is most likely to be wrong: SH247 shipped `search` explicitly as "a term the template supplies, literal **or read from the model**", a page whose `TOPIC` field drives its own related-content listing is the case that makes the helper worth having, and a typo there renders an empty listing — the very failure SH251 exists to catch.
  <br>**Only the unambiguous case, each exclusion for its own reason.** A quoted value is a literal; a numeric one is a number; a value starting with `(` is a subexpression, which is a parse this scanner deliberately does not do and is therefore skipped **whole** rather than descended into. What is left — an unquoted token made entirely of path characters — is a path and nothing else looks like one. Same "weak claim, always true" bar the in-block warning already uses.
  <br>**The tokenizer tracks quotes and parens**, which is six lines and removes a class of defect rather than an instance. Splitting on whitespace alone would cut `q="two words"` into `q="two` — not a path, so dropped, which is the right answer reached for the wrong reason and stops being right the day somebody writes `q=(concat A B)`.
  <br>Hash arguments resolve in the scope the **call** is written in, so they nest exactly as positional ones do: `{{#query folder=OUTER}}{{#search q=INNER}}` puts `INNER` in the outer block's scope. Inline helpers get the same treatment, so `{{file_url HERO alt=CAPTION}}` reports both fields and still not the helper's name.
- **SH273** — **The scanner's grammar coverage is a table, and writing it found a dropped field** ([ShTemplateGrammarCoverageTest](../shio-app/src/test/java/com/viglet/shio/render/ShTemplateGrammarCoverageTest.java), [ShTemplateFieldScanner](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/render/ShTemplateFieldScanner.java)). SH251's scanner reads Handlebars' syntax by hand and SH261 added a third construct to it, so the total is a small parser of somebody else's grammar maintained against no specification. **The risk is silent under-reporting**: a construct it does not recognise yields no reference, the lint quietly stops covering it, and nothing goes red. That is what `{{~TEXT~}}` did until SH251's own test noticed an asymmetry — found by looking, not by failing.
  <br>**So the coverage is the assertion.** Thirty constructs, each with a declared disposition: `REPORTED` (the field is found), `SKIPPED` (not a field reference at all), or `UNREACHABLE` (could hold a field, but something else already prevents it mattering). A second test requires every `UNREACHABLE` row to carry its reason, because that disposition is a claim about *another part of the system* — three of them rest on SH183's refusing `TemplateLoader` making partials fail to compile — and a claim like that rots when the other part changes. A third checks that every marker the scanner branches on appears somewhere in the table, which cannot prove completeness against the grammar but does fail when somebody adds a branch and no row. This is SH255's "exact, or declared" applied to a parser instead of a format.
  <br>**Writing it found `{{& TEXT}}` being dropped** — Handlebars' unescaped-output form, the same reference as a triple stash, skipped as though it were a directive. A real field silently uncovered by the lint, exactly the class this task predicted, found by enumerating rather than by any test failing.
  <br>**And verifying the fix corrected the fix.** The change was made in two places — removing `&` from the directive skip-list and adding it to `strip` — and reverting the first proved it had never mattered: `strip` runs *before* the kind check, so the skip-list branch was already unreachable. The comment now says that instead of claiming a deletion did the work. Worth recording as method rather than trivia: this session has now had three changes whose halves were not both load-bearing, and each was caught by reverting one and watching the test, not by reading.
- **SH274** — **The AST premise is asserted against the library instead of remembered** ([ShHandlebarsAstPremiseTest](../shio-app/src/test/java/com/viglet/shio/render/ShHandlebarsAstPremiseTest.java)). "Use Handlebars.java's AST rather than a hand-written scanner" had been rejected twice on a premise stated once and inherited since — internal API, and `Template#collect` carries no scope. An inherited premise that happens to be right is indistinguishable from one that expired, right up to the moment it costs something, so it is now measured against the version on the classpath (4.5.3) and **asserted**, which is the only mechanism that makes a design decision one somebody will actually reconsider.
  <br>**The premise holds, and the reality is worse than the premise claimed.** `collect(VAR, TRIPLE_VAR, AMP_VAR, STAR_VAR)` on a template holding `TEXT` four times — top level, inside `{{#query}}`, as `{{&TEXT}}`, as `{{{TEXT}}}` — returns exactly **`[TEXT]`**. It is *deduplicated*, so it cannot say how many references exist or where any of them is: strictly weaker than the flat list the premise assumed, and far weaker than the scope SH251 needs. `collect(SECTION)` returns the helper's name and nothing about its contents. The structural nodes (`internal.Block`, `internal.Variable`) are in `internal`, asserted by class name so a move out of that package fails the build and reopens the question.
  <br>**One finding is a genuine cross-check rather than a limitation.** `collectReferenceParameters()` returns `[SECTION]` for `{{#query type="Article" folder=SECTION}}` — the hash **path** and not the literal. The library draws SH261's line between a hash path and a hash literal in exactly the same place, arrived at independently. It is still unscoped so it cannot replace the scanner, but it is the strongest available evidence that SH261's classification is right.
  <br>**And `TagType` has `AMP_VAR`**, which is the library confirming SH273's finding from the other direction: `{{&x}}` is a variable form, so treating it as a directive dropped a real reference.
  <br>**Verdict: the scanner stays, and a hybrid buys nothing** — `collect` would supply names, and having the nesting already gives you the names. What changed is that this is now recorded with a version number and enforced by four assertions, rather than being a habit anyone would have to re-derive.
- **SH371 (SH275, the first two premises)** — **The load-bearing dependency premises are asserted, starting with the dangerous defaults** ([ShRenderNoScriptEngineTest](../shio-app/src/test/java/com/viglet/shio/render/ShRenderNoScriptEngineTest.java)). SH274 turned one inherited belief about somebody else's code into a tripwire; six more were load-bearing and enforced nowhere. This does the two that pass SH275's own bar — *does the premise expiring change behaviour, or only tidiness?* — which are the two Handlebars defaults SH183's guards exist to override.
  <br>**What was missing was not our behaviour but the premise.** The suite already asserted that *our* engine resolves no bean property and refuses every partial. It never asserted that an **unconfigured** Handlebars does the dangerous thing — so if the library became safe by default, the guards would silently become dead weight and their comments would become false, with nothing failing. Now a bare `new Handlebars()` is measured: `{{secret.value}}` returns `classified`, and `{{> application}}` fails with a message naming **`/application.hbs`** — it is not refusing to look, it is failing to find, which is the evidence that the default loader resolves a partial to a *path*.
  <br>**And it corrected a natural misreading of the existing guard.** `beanPropertiesAreNotResolved` asserts `[{{secret.value}}][{{secret.class.name}}]` renders `[][]`, which reads as proof that both routes are closed by `MapValueResolver`. Measured, `{{secret.class.name}}` is empty on a **default** engine too — the library already blocks the reflection route. So only the first half is evidence for our configuration, and that is now pinned separately rather than left to be inferred.
  <br>Two premises are deliberately not asserted, with reasons: `Map.copyOf`'s salted iteration cannot be caught behaviourally at all (SH136 says so — twice-in-one-process comparison passes over broken code, which is why that guard is a lint), and "the MCP SDK is Jackson-2/Boot-3" is a fact about a dependency this project does not have. The remaining rows are in §XVI.27.
- **SH263** — **A duplicate template title is an error, because a title is an identity** ([ShTemplateGraph](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/render/ShTemplateGraph.java), [ShAgentVerifyService](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/agent/verify/ShAgentVerifyService.java), [ShTemplateGraphTest](../shio-app/src/test/java/com/viglet/shio/render/ShTemplateGraphTest.java)). `ShPageRenderService.postOfSystemType` resolves a layout or region **by title** and takes the first match, so two `Region` posts called `NAV` in one site rendered whichever row the query happened to return — intermittently, with no error anywhere, and SH193's graph counted the slot once. SH202's duplicate-URL defect one namespace over: `sh-region="NAME"` and a `postTypeLayout` binding both address a template by title, which makes a title an identity in fact, and nothing enforced uniqueness because nothing had noticed.
  <br>**An error, unlike the unused-template warnings beside it.** An unused region may be work in progress; two templates competing for one name is provably wrong whatever anybody intended, and which page renders correctly is undefined. So this one fails the gate and those deliberately do not.
  <br>**Detection is instance-wide within the site, reporting is subject-scoped** — SH143's rule, and the reason it matters here is sharper than usual: a scoped run that saw only one of the two would answer that the name is *unique*, which is the worst false green available. One finding per template involved, addressed at each, the shape `duplicate-url` already uses.
  <br>**The false positive that would have made it useless** is a post's own PUBLISHED row: a template has a DRAFT and a PUBLISHED row sharing both id and title, so counting *rows* would report every published template in every instance as a duplicate of itself. Keyed by id, with a test for exactly that.
  <br>**And the first version of its test broke two others** — it added the second `NAV` to the class's `PER_CLASS` fixture, so `unusedIsNotAGateFailure` (which asserts `ok()` is true) started failing. That is SH239's confound one class along: in a shared fixture every mutating test is an input to the others. Both new cases build their own site now, which is what SH239 did for the benchmark pairs.
- **SH278** — **Which row of a template renders is now decided, not discovered** ([ShRenderState](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/render/ShRenderState.java), [ShPageRenderService](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/render/ShPageRenderService.java), [ShRenderHelpers](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/render/ShRenderHelpers.java), [ShPageRenderTest](../shio-app/src/test/java/com/viglet/shio/render/ShPageRenderTest.java)). Filed as "one `order by`" and it was two defects, the second worse than the one on the ticket.
  <br>**The one on the ticket:** `postOfSystemType` took the first row a derived finder returned, with no order, so a duplicate title (SH263) rendered whichever template the database chose — differently on H2, MariaDB and PostgreSQL, moving SH101's digest for a change nobody made. A duplicate cannot render *correctly*, but it can render **consistently wrongly**, which is a defect somebody recognises rather than one that looks like flakiness in the renderer.
  <br>**The one that was not:** it read **both states with no DRAFT preference**. So a curator editing a layout and opening a preview could be shown the *published* layout — the exact failure SH247 extracted `preferDraft` to prevent for listings, in the one place nobody applied it, and the whole reason somebody opens a preview is to see the change they have not published. The render's state now reaches every level: a DRAFT preview resolves the draft layout, the draft region and the draft theme; a PUBLISHED render never picks up an unpublished template edit, which is the direction that would have been a live incident.
  <br>**One writer for both, which is SH245's rule applied where it had been missed.** SH247 extracted `statesFor`/`preferDraft` out of the listing helpers *with a stated reason* — "a second copy of the preference is a second chance to get it backwards" — and `ShPageRenderService` did not have a second copy, it had **none**. Both now delegate to `ShRenderState`, and the fold gained a total order in the move (title, then id) — invisible in a listing that sorts afterwards anyway, and decisive where `findFirst` was the answer.
  <br>**Worth recording how the verification went, because it makes the case for the fix better than the fix does.** Reverting the change failed the published-render test and left the draft-preview one **passing** — on H2, `findFirst` happened to return the draft. So the more serious half of this defect is *unobservable on the engine the suite runs against* and would have appeared on somebody's PostgreSQL. That is the argument for deciding an order rather than discovering one, stated by the code itself.
- **SH370 (SH279, the renderer half)** — **The unordered finders in the renderer are ordered, and the bar is written down** ([ShRenderHelpers](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/render/ShRenderHelpers.java), [ShPageRenderTest](../shio-app/src/test/java/com/viglet/shio/render/ShPageRenderTest.java)). SH278 showed that `findFirst()` over a derived finder returns the row the *database* chose, and that the worse half of the resulting defect was invisible on H2. The sweep applies its two-question bar — **does anything guarantee uniqueness, and is the guarantee enforced?** — to the render package, which is where the neighbouring evidence was.
  <br>**`{{file_url}}` read whichever row came first**, with no state preference. The bytes of a `File` post are immutable (SH145) but `data.FILE` is the *name* in the path, so the two rows can disagree and a draft rename could produce either path. It now follows the render's state, with a test: a preview resolves `drafted.png`, a published render resolves `live.png` and never the other.
  <br>**`currentFolder` had the same shape.** SH134 moves both rows of a post together so they agree about the folder today — which is a property of the *move verb*, not of this read, and relying on it silently is exactly what the sweep is for.
  <br>**`rootFolder` is the "guaranteed" case, and got both halves of the bar.** A site gets exactly one root from `ShSiteWriteService`: guaranteed by construction and enforced by no constraint and no lint. So the comment now names the rule *and* the read is ordered — because "one by construction" is precisely the reasoning that held for a template's title until SH263 proved it did not.
  <br>**One call site needed nothing, and that is the argument for where SH278 put the order.** `resolveReference`'s friendly-URL branch can genuinely match two posts — a URL's uniqueness is *reported* by SH99's `duplicate-url` rather than enforced, and SH243 is open about a trashed post still holding one — but it is already deterministic, because `preferDraft` gained a total order in the shared writer. Fixing the rule in one place fixed a call site nobody looked at.
  <br>**And the sweep surfaced a behaviour change SH278 introduced that its own tests did not reveal (SH280).** Writing this fixture failed twice, both times correctly: a PUBLISHED render now needs a **published** page *and* a published layout, because it reads only published rows at every level. Before SH278 a draft-only layout was silently used for a published render. The new behaviour is right — what a visitor gets must not depend on an unpublished edit — and it is a change for any instance whose templates were never published, which is filed rather than glossed.
- **SH280** — **An unpublished layout says so, and `verify` finds it before a visitor does** ([ShPageRenderService](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/render/ShPageRenderService.java), [ShTemplateGraph](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/render/ShTemplateGraph.java), [ShAgentVerifyService](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/agent/verify/ShAgentVerifyService.java), [ShPageRenderTest](../shio-app/src/test/java/com/viglet/shio/render/ShPageRenderTest.java), [ShTemplateGraphTest](../shio-app/src/test/java/com/viglet/shio/render/ShTemplateGraphTest.java)). SH278 made a PUBLISHED render read only published rows at every level — correct, since a visitor must not get an unpublished edit — and that turned "the layout exists but nobody published it" from silently working into a failure reported as **"no such layout"**. Which is the normal state of a site built through the SH183 flow: `post.upsert` writes a DRAFT and publishing is a separate act (P7), so telling that operator the layout does not exist sends them to create a second one.
  <br>**The urgency check came back negative, which is worth recording as much as a fix.** The task flagged that if the SH68 import or SH92 blueprints wrote templates without publishing them, every imported site would arrive broken. Import is **faithful** — it preserves each post's own state from the package — and no first-party blueprint ships a `PageLayout` at all (they compose SH95 sections). So the exposure is an agent-built site, not an imported one, and the task shrank to the two halves that help.
  <br>**A distinct exception, not a reworded one.** `UnpublishedLayoutException` is a **409** rather than a 404 — the thing exists, the request conflicts with its state — and it carries its own `fix` naming `post.publish`, which the 404's could not have. A caller that branches on the problem type can now tell "you have not written this" from "you have not published it".
  <br>**And a warning, because a refusal only reaches whoever asked for the page.** `unpublished-layout` in `checks=content` reports a bound layout with no published row **where the site has published pages of that type**, naming those types. That second condition is what keeps it off every site mid-build: a draft layout with nothing published behind it is somebody working, the same layout with published pages behind it is a page that 404s in production. Same shape as SH193's unused-template warnings — *the difference between work in progress and something wrong is almost always another condition, not a stricter first one.* A warning rather than an error, since SH99's line is that `ok` is false only for what the CMS can prove is wrong and the remedy is one publish away.
  <br>One test note: the assertion had to read the `ProblemDetail`'s **title**, because `ShTeachingException.getMessage()` returns the *detail* — so `hasMessageContaining` was checking the wrong half of the problem.
- **SH281** — **An unpublished region says so, and an unpublished theme stops being silent** ([ShRegionComposer](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/render/ShRegionComposer.java), [ShPageRenderService](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/render/ShPageRenderService.java), [ShTemplateGraph](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/render/ShTemplateGraph.java), [ShAgentVerifyService](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/agent/verify/ShAgentVerifyService.java)). SH278 changed all three render levels and SH280 diagnosed one. The other two failed worse: an unpublished **region** produced SH183's *"no Region post"* marker — **a wrong diagnosis, not a missing one**, since the author is looking at the region in the console while the page says it does not exist — and an unpublished **theme** yielded no CSS at all, silently, with nothing in the markup, the digest or the lint.
  <br>**The fix is a marker and a finding, not a second exception**, because these two levels *deliberately degrade* rather than refusing: a slot is skipped so the rest of the page still renders, which is right for a preview. So `data-shio-region-unpublished` joins `data-shio-region-missing` — **a separate attribute rather than a value on the existing one**, because SH169's rule is that different mistakes must not look alike, and this is a **third** state beside missing and empty.   <br>`themeTitleOf` is exposed on the renderer so the lint reads the theme binding from the same place the renderer does; a second parser of that field would be a second thing that can disagree about which theme a page uses.
  <br>One process note worth recording: that accessor was **silently missing** for a full test run, and `mvn compile` reported success. The cause was investigated rather than assumed and is **not** what it first looked like — see SH282: the IDE compiles into `target/classes`, so Maven's staleness check skips the module and reports "Nothing to compile". The tell is a `ServletException` wrapping `java.lang.Error: Unresolved compilation problem`.
- **SH283** — **The suite is measured from the run, and the inflated counts are corrected** ([agents.md](../agents.md)). Filed one iteration earlier as "the reports directory accumulates", which was true and was the second link in a chain rather than the cause. Traced: **`-q` suppresses surefire's `Results:` summary** — it is a Maven INFO line, so quiet mode removes the only authoritative total — which is why the count was being summed from `target/surefire-reports/*.txt` at all, and *that* directory keeps reports from targeted `-Dtest=X` runs beside the full run's, so the sum double-counts those classes.
  <br>**The numbers quoted through Block P were inflated**, drifting to 977 against **974** on a clean run. Nothing was failing and nothing was hidden — but a test count is offered as evidence, and this one was arithmetic over a directory rather than a reading of a result. Corrected here rather than quietly dropped, because the earlier commits carry the wrong figure.
  <br>The fix is a command, verified both ways: no `-q` when the number matters, `clean` for SH282's reason, and the total read from surefire's own summary line. Recorded in `agents.md` beside SH282, since they are the same shape — *an artefact of an earlier command changing what a later one appears to say* — and `target/` holds several.
- **SH252** — **A stylesheet is not an HTML document** ([ShSystemWidget](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/widget/ShSystemWidget.java), [ShWidgetOnStartup](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/onstartup/widget/ShWidgetOnStartup.java), [ShRenderPostTypes](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/render/ShRenderPostTypes.java), [widgets/index.ts](../shio-react/src/components/widgets/index.ts), [widget-colors.ts](../shio-react/src/lib/widget-colors.ts), [builders.ts](../shio-model/src/builders.ts), [content-files.mjs](../cli/src/content-files.mjs)).
