  <br>Noted while seeding: `ShWidget.implementationCode` points every widget at `template/widget/*.html`, and **that directory does not exist** — it is dead metadata left by Block E's retirement of the Thymeleaf UI, still writable through `ShWidgetAPI`. The new widget matches the existing (inert) pattern rather than inventing a convention; the column is **SH285**.
- **SH188** — **`may_publish` reads as not-granted instead of throwing** ([ShApiToken](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/persistence/model/token/ShApiToken.java), [v2026.3.14.yaml](../shio-app/src/main/resources/db/changelog/v2026.3.14.yaml), [ShApiTokenMayPublishNullTest](../shio-app/src/test/java/com/viglet/shio/api/token/ShApiTokenMayPublishNullTest.java), [ShH2SchemaIT](../shio-app/src/test/java/com/viglet/shio/tenant/ShH2SchemaIT.java)). SH107's `v2026.3.11` added the column nullable with no default and no backfill, recording the intent that it "read as `false` when absent" — and `ShApiToken` mapped it as a primitive `boolean`, which cannot express absent. Hibernate throws on NULL → primitive, so **every install holding an api_token row from before SH107 failed on `GET /api/v2/api-token` and on `POST /api/v2/preview-token`**: preview was dead for a reason entirely its own, independent of the missing `site.url` this block's SH184 is about. The precedent for getting it right was one table over and two changesets earlier — SH13's `ephemeral`, added with `defaultValueBoolean: false`.
  <br>**Both halves ship, because they answer different failure modes.** The entity maps `Boolean` and reads it through `isMayPublish()` (`Getter(AccessLevel.NONE)` keeps a nullable `getMayPublish()` off the API, so no caller can hold the null), which means a row arriving NULL from anywhere at all is only *not granted* rather than a 500. `v2026.3.14` is the disk half: an `update` for the rows that already exist — `addDefaultValue` alone never touches them — plus the default, so nothing writes NULL again.
  <br>**Nothing caught it because every test in the package was a Mockito unit test** that constructs the entity in Java and never hydrates one, so the value read was always the field initialiser and never the column. The regression test therefore goes the only way that reproduces it: write the NULL with native SQL, clear the persistence context, read it back the way the endpoints do. It was checked against the old mapping and fails there with `Null value was assigned to a property of primitive type`.
- **SH330** — A durable incident is a verify *warning*, not an error, so a past 5xx no longer keeps the CI gate red after its cause is fixed: SH99's rule says ok is false only for what the CMS can prove from inside itself now, and an incident is by construction something that already happened. All five kinds, asserted together so the next kind cannot inherit error by default.
- **SH337** — A template can ask for the site's origin: the render model carries post.canonical and site.baseUrl beside the raw post.url and site.url, resolved through ShSiteFrontEnd so they are never blank (the external front end when there is one, /preview/<site> when there is not). Makes a canonical tag, an og:url and a sitemap entry buildable; the raw fields keep meaning what they meant, so 'has this been deployed?' stays answerable.
- **SH329** — A dry run resolves against the sites the same batch creates: Declared.withSitesFrom reads them off the run's own ops in runOps, so the bootstrap case plans instead of failing at ops[1]. The refusal when the site is really absent names a site.upsert op rather than a ?site= this endpoint does not have, and drops the allow-list branch that read as 'check your token' on a brand new instance.
- **SH328** — site.upsert binds a post-type to a PageLayout through data.postTypeLayout, per key: an unbound type is filled, a bound one is kept and reported, and nothing is ever a whole-map replace. Closes the one edge that makes a site render and that no agent op could write, while two surfaces already instructed the write.
- **SH326** — data.reconcile:true on the addressless render.provision op reaches SH289's repair verb, which had stayed HTTP-only — so an MCP-only client could diagnose an old instance and not fix it, while untitled-template's own fix named the route. Opt-in and never implied by ensure, and one op rather than a tenth name. Half of this line was already stale: SH186 had made ensure reachable.
- **SH333** — The Universal Editor's iframe gains onLoad and onError and the SH185 handshake gains a deadline, so one BridgeState of waiting/ready/absent replaces a badge that read Connecting forever, with a timeout rather than an inspection of the framed document, an amber banner that never claims the site is broken, and i18n key parity as a lint.
- **SH334** — A routes warning names a site that publishes pages and has none at / — the convention nothing enforced, defaulted or reported — skipped when the site publishes nothing and on a scoped run, since every other routes rule is about a subject the run looked at and this one is about the site.
- **SH336** — Two mechanisms with two jobs make a previewed site walkable: a server DOM pass beside the banner rewrites a root-relative href only when the path is a URL this site publishes, and click interception in shio-editor.js catches the nav a region's JAVASCRIPT builds at runtime, handed the same index so a page can be told from a file.
- **SH335** — The editor saves through PATCH /api/v2/post-unified/{id} on the curator's session, so no WRITE token is minted, pasted or parked in localStorage — the merge verb rather than a client read-modify-write, because the cheap option reintroduces a lost update, and ShPostDraftMergeService is that merge once with the CDA allow-list and the console ACL as two guards over it.
- **SH258** — A DECLARED entry names the refusal it expects — {why, refuses: /pattern/} for a throw whose message must match and {why} for a lossy carry that must not throw — so refused stops being one outcome and becomes N, which is what lets the intended refusal be told apart from one three layers down blaming a symptom.
- **SH259** — A param frame carries the reader's query string as strings — read-only, never headers or cookies, sorted so the SH101 digest cannot vary by parameter order, with the renderer's own state and editor excluded — and {{{param.q}}} is refused at write time as param-unescaped, since it is the only value in the model written by anybody with the URL.
- **SH309** — A lint walks a full verify report and resolves every SH79 address it finds in address, message and fix, so a teaching message can no longer name an object that 404s — with placeholders skipped as shapes rather than names, and a rule that names something absent on purpose declared in NAMES_SOMETHING_ABSENT with its reason.
- **SH318** — The instance-wide read list is derived from the service surface rather than hand-kept — a method taking String site first is instance-wide when that argument is null — which found find and the SH160 memory reads the three written names never mentioned, and caught ShAgentMemoryTest and ShRememberToolTest asserting on notes(null) from the shared context.
- **SH352** — ShPageRenderService carries noRollbackFor on the class rather than on one of two render overloads, and ShTeachingRollbackLintTest scopes its escape to the annotation's own parentheses instead of searching the whole file.
- **SH313** — A lint fails the build when anything holding a ShPageRenderService renders from a writing transaction, which is the only way to lose SH311's cache and costs 19 queries a page instead of 6 with no error and no log line — the half asserting the cache works was already the sweep benchmark's marginal-cost number.
- **SH296** — The convention a mutating test must force its precondition rather than assume the @BeforeAll one is written down with the three defects it has already hidden, and the two instruments that were weighed are recorded as rejected: random ordering trades a silent dependence for a flake (SH250), and a lint cannot tell a normal write from a vacuous assertion.
- **SH319** — A digest request above the instance ceiling is reported as one row naming both numbers, so a caller that asked for 200 and got three can tell the instance disagreed from three being all there was — in the branch where the cut row is absent, since that one fires when the pages run out rather than when the request was reduced.
- **SH346** — The write vocabulary is readable without an MCP client: `GET /agent/context?include=ops` serves the same bytes as `shio://ops`, on a section nobody pays for unless they name it and which does not move the SH116 digest. Chosen by measurement — 447 tokens against a 2343-token manifest is a 19% regression on the first read of every session, so the manifest section was the option to reject; the endpoint index stopped enumerating op names in prose and points at the vocabulary instead, so the manifest got smaller in the same change. The deliverable before the fix was the instrument (SH322/SH338): `ShMcpResource.httpTwin()` plus `ShMcpResourceHttpTwinLintTest`, which asserts every resource's declared REST twin against the live handler mappings — one MCP-only document was the finding, six resources was the question.
- **SH316** — The measurement moved the subject: assembling the graph again inside one read-only transaction already cost no queries (1.13 ms of CPU), while the queries were the site's ROWS, re-read per rule. Both are memoized now through one extracted mechanism, ShReadOnlyTransactionCache — impactOf 2 -> 0 queries per call, a one-site verify pass 95 -> 60, a repeat assembly 1129445 -> 9065 ns, measured by ShTemplateGraphMemoBenchmarkTest before and after.
- **SH312** — The two claims held and a third appeared. ShRenderHelperSweepBenchmarkTest measures four page shapes on a fixture of its own: plain 5 queries a page, a {{#query limit=10}} listing region 7, five sections stored as ids 10 (one lookup an entry, as filed) and the same five stored as friendly URLs 15 — two an entry, which nobody had predicted and which opened SH353. SH311's 6 is confirmed as a floor for the simplest page there is, and helper reads are per page by construction because their input is the page's own field values.
- **SH353** — The site-wide read behind a URL-keyed relation is a resolution, not a listing's rows, so SH316's ShReadOnlyTransactionCache reaches it: one read per read-only transaction instead of one per entry. Five sections stored as friendly URLs went from 15 queries a page to 10 — the same as the identical page stored as ids, so the storage shape an author happens to use no longer decides what the page costs. SH312's finding-recording assertion became the guard on it.
- **SH322** — The habit is written into agents.md beside the measure-first rule: when a task's body says 'and whatever a grep turns up', the grep is the deliverable and it lands as a lint before the fixes do. It shipped in the SH321 commit that found it (6e9ba956, agents.md:150) and the line stayed open; SH338 has since extended the same rule from a call site to a design law. The three lints its reasoning cites are all in the tree, and SH323's ShFurlReaderLintTest is the habit already applied.
- **SH317** — About 1.5 s per isolated context, measured with a probe class that declared its own datasource and did nothing but boot: 1.585 s and 1.390 s on two full runs against 0.002 s for a class with no context. At 33 isolated databases that is roughly 50 s of a 124 s suite, so the next one costs a second and a half rather than twenty and SH315's rule stays as it is. Three findings came with it: the suite's wall clock cannot see the delta (2:09 vs 2:30 on an identical tree), the probe must be deleted rather than kept because it would permanently consume the cache headroom SH347 guards, and 'share a context but not a database' stays closed since the URL is part of the cache key. The count and the dated cost now print on every run from ShContextCacheHeadroomTest.
- **SH293** — The audit produced a deletion for eight and a comparison for one. Photo, Video, Quote, Link, TextArea, Article, FolderIndex and Alias were referenced nowhere but in ShSystemPostType — nothing created them, nothing looked them up, and Link had been misspelled against the 2018 model's Links since it was written. File is compared with import/post-types.json the way SH290 compares the render three, down to the FILE field's isTitle and widget, because ShStaticFileService really does create it and a drift there breaks uploads rather than rendering. Text stays as the one declared exception: read by ShUserOnStartup, created by nothing. ShSystemPostTypeInventoryTest keeps it honest — a constant with no creator fails the build, and it distinguishes a creator from a reference, which is what a naive grep would have got wrong.
- **SH354** — The documented command now tees the run before filtering it, so reading the total no longer discards which test failed: shio-test.log lives outside target/ (gitignored) because the clean SH282 makes mandatory deletes surefire-reports on the next run. Chosen over a Maven profile and a CI step because the loss happens at the terminal where the command is typed. ShTestCommandDocLintTest asserts the property rather than the spelling — a documented command may not pipe a run into a filter without keeping it — and it earned itself twice on the way in: it caught the second copy of the command in build.md, then caught its own author hiding a command from it behind a backslash continuation. The original failure stays undiagnosed; what changed is that the next one will not.
- **SH285** — The audit answered for all six columns and dropped three: class_name pointed at com.viglet.shio.widget.Sh*Widget, a package that holds only a constants class, and implementation_code and setting_path pointed into template/widget/**, a directory that left with the AngularJS console. Nothing read them and two were writable through PUT /api/v2/widget/{id}, which is what makes a dead column worse than clutter — a caller sets a template path, gets a 200, and concludes widgets are extensible by pointing them at a file. - **SH295** — Settled as a GET beside the call that already answers 'can this instance render': GET /api/v2/render/post-types/drift names each render type missing a field the shipped model declares. The comparison existed only as POST /reconcile?dryRun=true, so learning whether an instance needed repairing meant issuing a write verb and trusting a flag not to write — a read-only caller could not ask at all. Rejected on their stated trades: not a verify finding (a post-type has no SH79 address, the constraint that shaped SH289) and not the context pack (every session pays for a line most instances do not need, P3); the teaching message and the manifest row point at it instead, which costs no new row. reconcile now formats the read rather than repeating the comparison, so plan and repair cannot describe different things.
- **SH288** — Decided first: shio impact <address>, and shio read deliberately not built. A post's content is on disk after pull --content where grep is cheaper than a request (P4), so read would be a worse version of a file; the blast radius is computed from the site's bindings rather than stored in the post, so no projected file holds it and include=impact (SH262) had no terminal path at all. The command prints kind, title, layouts, post-types and the draft/published counts, says 'is not a template' for an ordinary post instead of failing, and --json prints the section or null so a pipeline can branch. The client's read gained an include option, absent by default so no pull --content slice pays for a section nobody asked for.
- **SH284** — Its deliverable was a justification and it has landed in SH241's rationale, not in code: a clean-room build is the only thing that can tell a real green from a local one, since SH282 and SH283 were both artefacts of a local working tree and neither can happen in a job that starts from a clone. XVI.1 now carries that framing plus the two consequences it implies — publish surefire's summary as the run's headline so no count is re-derived by hand, and choose deliberately which jobs run on push versus pull request. The CI work itself remains SH241; retire was unavailable because this ledger declares no marker, so the honest record is this entry saying what was written and what was not.
- **SH275** — Of six dependency premises two were already asserted, two are declared unassertable with their reason, and the stale Mockito row's live successor is now guarded by ShBuildWarningLintTest.
- **SH341** — Every task line is one sentence now and the gate is at zero: 38 were cut after reading the section at the other end of the pointer, SH140 and SH265 had their rationale written into VIII.13 and XV.22 first because they had no pointer at all, and SH213 and SH220 pointed at sections thin enough to need reading rather than counting.
- **SH195** — A Theme carries TOKENS in the W3C Design Tokens shape — adopted, not invented, so a Style Dictionary or Figma export pastes in — and ShThemeTokens compiles it to CSS custom properties prepended to the theme's own stylesheet, with the same values also readable as a dotted map for where var() cannot go.
- **SH324** — The instrument is a runtime guard rather than the cheaper source lint, decided by build.md's own test — what would a broken fixture do differently inside one JVM? It inserts a second row, so the fact is observable and a textual scan would be reading the wrong document. ShFixtureShapeGuard is auto-detected, runs one query per test class and judges only what that class created, because the first version accused two classes of one row on the shared datasource. It found two unknown instances immediately, one of them in the class XVI.31 recorded as having got this right, and four classes that build duplicates deliberately now say so with a reason.
- **SH358** — Three services declared a proxy-reachable overload with no annotation beside an annotated one it self-invoked, so every incident write ran with no transaction of its own, /preview/** with a query string lost its noRollbackFor and the proof service walked SH193's LAZY graph with no session; ShAgentTransactionalOverloadLintTest makes the mixed pair a build failure and ShAgentIncidentStore is one method now.
- **SH294** — A package whose templates are keyed the 2018 way now imports and renders in a test, with every name in the fixture read out of /import/post-types.json so it cannot assert against a shape the 2018 exporter never produced.
- **SH357** — The counts were summed over the page while the payload promised a cap narrows detail and not diagnosis, so the 26th-newest kind vanished and which ones survived moved with test order; and the diagnostics read no longer carries the feed's ceiling, which protected no cursor there.
- **SH359** — /preview/** sat in permitAll() from before the renderer existed, so SH183's GET /preview/{site}/{url} — which defaults to DRAFT — never reached the anyRequest().authenticated() its own class note claims, and an anonymous GET answered 404 for an unknown site and 200 for the editor script; ShPreviewIsNotPublicTest asserts the refusal from outside.
- **SH265** — The answer is that an instance does not run a browser: raster stays in the CLI, where the agent has a shell and the human opens a local PNG, and shio snapshot now photographs a front-endless site through the instance's own preview instead of refusing.
- **SH360** — SH247 declared FORM_FIELD_KEYS, documented it as read by SH251's lint, and wired it to nothing, so the lint checked a form's rows against a listing's keys; ShRenderHelpers.rowKeysFor asks the helper which shape applies, and the false-positive guard that already existed caught it the moment its fixture grew a form.
- **SH276** — The premise defending ~1500 lines of hand-rolled MCP cannot be asserted, because checking it means adding the dependency being evaluated, so the instrument is a date: ShMcpServer carries SDK-PREMISE-CHECKED and SDK-PREMISE-VERSION, ShMcpSdkPremiseTest fails the build eighteen months after the last look, and looking once already found the sentence stale — the SDK is 2.0.0 and publishes mcp-json-jackson3 against the same Jackson 3 this application runs.
- **SH355** — RK121 shipped and the plugin here was 100 commits behind it, so the parenthetical parses now, SH96 resolves for SH217 and SH219, and what is left under it is SH361's duplicates and RK122's two-files.
- **SH361** — Decided as one id per step rather than one entry rewritten, so SH366-SH371 now carry the six and each qualifier names its parent; the two id.two-files left are RK122's.
- **SH372** — The store hands out a strictly increasing instant now, so the order has a total tail with no new column, and a frozen-clock test pins it — it failed three runs in three before.
- **SH362** — The fixture now calls all six registered helpers and asserts it does, failing by name when a seventh arrives; widening it found SH372, a defect the old fixture's timing had been hiding.
- **SH414** — Four surefire forks cut the test phase from 91.8s to 68.4s and, more usefully, its spread from 9s to 0.5s; eight forks is slower, and lazy-init cost 26 failures for nothing.
- **SH415** — The ITs are opt-in now: `skipITs` defaults true and `-DskipITs=false` runs them, on the finding that no workflow ran the Java suite at all and failsafe ignored its own failures.
- **SH416** — A `@Container` read from `@DynamicPropertySource` starts eagerly now, so 26 ITs pass with none skipped; a lint names the next one and failsafe stops ignoring its own failures.
- **SH365** — the page is --page and --url is the instance in snapshot and digest both, with --url still naming the page when nothing else does and saying which flag to use; the grep landed first as flag-meaning.test.mjs, which found digest carrying the identical collision the task had not named and keeps the colliding set empty
- **SH451** — ShSitesAPI maps GET /sites/<site>/<format>/<locale>/<path> and splits it by position exactly as 0.3.8's ShSitesContextURLProcess did, with x-sh-site naming the site as a header and sh-format replacing the format segment; the path stays plural and the format segment is vestigial - read, kept in every rewritten link, and carrying no behaviour, since a layout comes from postTypeLayout. Six guards are inverted rather than dropped: anonymous on a permitAll path that was already there, PUBLISHED with no way to ask for a draft, no banner, no editor bridge, public max-age=300, indexable, and links rewritten into the public space by the same pass the preview uses.
- **SH457** — The format segment accepts `default` and nothing else, from the path or from sh-format, so the three-segment form stops serving the home page with a 200 to a request a browser made for an image; a value that is not `default` is a teaching 404 whose fix names where the path should have gone. Its two siblings — the locale segment's identical shape and the 401 an unmapped path outside /sites answers — are filed as SH459 rather than folded in.
- **SH558** — ShTemplateGraph.relatedThemeTitles reads the literal address in every {{#getRelation}} across a layout and its regions, resolving it by friendly URL the way the renderer does, so a theme reached only by relation carries its layout in the graph — unused-theme, include=impact and the reachability question all read the one edge set, and a path expression stays unmatched because no static read can say what it points at
- **SH559** — ShRenderedPage carries a composition of verbatim, authorable or mixed, computed from the page's own content and sections — the same two fields the generated layout branches on — so the preview banner states how the page was made instead of letting a layout title that has named one mode since SH464 stand as the only claim; the title stays, quoted, because renaming a postTypeLayout key is a migration
- **SH593** — `pageLayout` emits `<meta name="description" content="{{post.summary}}">` and `<link rel="canonical" href="{{post.canonical}}">`, so the two warnings that headed every replication report for twelve rounds — including the round whose whole output was `0 error(s), 2 warning(s)` — are gone at the source and the lint stays sharp for a layout somebody wrote by hand. `{{post.summary}}` rather than `{{description}}` because it is a key of the render frame and cannot fail on a `Page` built by hand, and on the type this chain writes against it *is* that field. The other half is what makes the tag carry something: `composePages` writes the description the capture already scanned off the source's head and dropped, because a tag that can only ever be blank is lint-satisfying theatre and one level up that is the same defect as the warning. `HEAD_CONVENTIONS_HTML` is a no-interpolation export and `ShHeadConventionsTest` runs the real JVM lint over those bytes.
- **SH356** — Measured again at this commit by roadkeep's own counters: 0 sections over budget, 0 stale, lint clean, and the four line-level corruptions gone with SH361. What ships is the ratchet the task said was missing - cli/test/improvements-debt.test.mjs holds stale at zero, holds every roadmap pointer resolvable, and holds SH361's outcome that one id never names two entries.
- **SH363** — Both instruments the task named now exist: ShAnonymousRouteAccessTest asserts every controller route from outside with no credentials against a classification table, and ShAllowListIsGroundedTest reads the permitAll literals and fails on one that denotes nothing - the state /preview/** was in for years before SH183 mounted the renderer on it. Proved by injecting a ghost entry, which the build refused.
- **SH364** — The door is scoped: submissions are token-scoped and never anonymous, the eligible types are a site allow-list intersected with not-a-system-type because a submitted PageLayout is server-side template execution, the folder is site configuration rather than a template setting, and the owner is the token. SH631, SH632 and SH633 build it; ShRenderFormTest holds the half that is decidable now - the renderer names no destination.
- **SH392** — shio audit compiles every script[data-shio-region] on the page and reports one that does not parse as an error naming the region - the case that renders, hashes, lints and verifies clean because the browser runs none of it. Compiled with new Function so no region is initialised twice, judged once rather than once per viewport, and a runtime throw stays console-error so one defect is not two findings. Forwarding it found SH526's shape line had never reached the reader.
- **SH419** — The listing decides its window over sort keys - id, state, date, title, post-type id - and loads only the rows it will draw, so 213 entity rows per 10 rendered became 2 and the ceiling went 25 to 4. No predicate, comparator or fold moved: the ORDER BY deliberately stayed in Java because date is nullable and MariaDB has no NULLS LAST, so a pushed-down sort would give different page boundaries per engine. SH634 carries the scan that is left.
- **SH420** — query saves the ten data variables it owns before its block and puts them back after, so an inner listing no longer overwrites the outer's position - the pager went from 2 of 2 to 1 of 2 on a nested layout. Save-and-restore of the three candidates because it is the only one that costs a template nothing; namespacing is a rename and moving them onto the row gives up drawing a pager once. Absent is restored as absent, not as false.
- **SH421** — PageLayout gains NO_SITE_SCRIPTS, a Check Box the lint honours, so an email template or a print sheet can declare that it omits the site's scripts on purpose. A field rather than a baseline acceptance for SH385's reason - the decision belongs beside the HTML that omits them, not in a suppression file - and the finding's fix now names both ways out. Unticked by default, so the rule keeps checking every layout that exists.
- **SH572** — dangling-relation reports a getRelation literal that resolves to no post in the site, as an error - the same severity as SH297's THEME field twin, because both are a template making a false claim about one address. Resolved against any post rather than Themes only, so relating a Region is not a finding; a path expression stays unchecked because what it points at is data. One row per id before reporting, so a published template is one finding rather than two.
- **SH573** — The generated layout is <site> (layout): the mode claim is gone from a template that has served all three since SH464. Renaming is safe because the binding key and the post's TITLE come from one call in one document and the post is addressed by url, so a new conversion is consistent, an old site never re-run stays consistent, and a re-run migrates both together with no window where the binding names a title no post has - asserted, not trusted.
- **SH631** — ShApiTokenScope.FORM exists and is bounded by data: it carries ROLE_FORM alone - neither ROLE_CDA nor ROLE_USER, which every other scope grants - so a credential that rides in a public page cannot read the site it posts to, and it may use a non-GET method only under /api/v2/cda/form. ShFormEligibility is the floor the endpoint's severity turns on, refusing a renderer type on its name and on its system flag independently.
- **SH632** — sh_site_form holds one site's destination folder, its invited post-types and whether it accepts at all - a table keyed by site following site_webhook, never columns on ShSite and never a template setting, because a folder chosen in a template is a folder an attacker chooses. Creating a row does not enable it and an empty type list invites nothing. Classified CONSOLE_ADMIN: enabling converts an authenticated capability into a public write path.
- **SH633** — POST /api/v2/cda/form/{site} writes one DRAFT post into the site's configured folder or refuses. DRAFT is never a parameter, the rate limit is the CDA bucket the token already spends, and the honeypot answers exactly as a success does because an error naming the field describes how to evade it. A system post-type is refused at the boundary even when the site's list names it. Its own AUTHENTICATED row, ahead of the cda wildcard that would have covered it.
- **SH634** — The window is in the query: fold, type filter, order and offset. Measured first - 228 rows returned to render 10, ratio 22, invisible to the entity counter that proved SH419 because a projection is not an entity - then 3 after. The fold is one predicate correct for both renders, and coalesce(date, floor) gives every engine the null placement the Java comparator has, which the Postgres and MariaDB ITs now prove. title keeps the scan: no collation is CASE_INSENSITIVE_ORDER.
- **SH636** — site.formAction and site.formHoneypot: a template writes <form action="{{site.formAction}}"> and the honeypot input by name, with neither literal in content. On the SITE and not as block data variables from the helper - the first shape, which a test disproved in an hour, because the form element wraps the block and a block's data variables do not exist outside it. The honeypot name is read from the controller that checks it, so the rendered and checked names cannot drift.
- **SH637** — One CorsConfigurationSource, registering only the form path, so the preflight that made SH633 unreachable now succeeds and every other path keeps exactly the behaviour it had. CORS is not the control: sh_site_form.allowed_origins is, checked against Origin in the endpoint where the tenant is resolved and every caller is subject to it - per site, matched exactly, empty meaning none. And security.md documented an addCorsMappings the code never had.

## Block Q — Replication (an existing site becomes an authorable Shio site)

- **SH377** — shio clone walks one origin and writes an inventory plus a report and no content: pages with titles, assets, locales with the URL shape each uses, forms with fields, the navigation in source order and the third-party scripts, bounded by depth, a page ceiling and the site's own robots rules
- **SH378** — shio clone --assets downloads the referenced images, stylesheets, fonts, icons and media into shio/assets/<site>/<the source's folder chain>/<name> and records the URL-to-path map back into the inventory: same-origin only with the hosts left behind named, deduped by sha-256 keeping the most-referenced name, and a name no path can hold refused rather than trimmed
- **SH381** — the navigation row carries the url its docstring promised since SH183: the folder's index post — the post inside it whose friendly URL is the folder's own chain, matched case-insensitively because a label and a slug are different namespaces — absent where there is none so a template branches on it for a group heading, and never fabricated
- **SH379** — shio propose reports each captured block's section type, fields and the markup it would lose; --accept records one, unaccepted stays verbatim.
- **SH380** — A captured stylesheet arrives as DTCG tokens plus CSS, url() rewritten to tree paths, and a token that fails the name round trip is reported not written.

The source spelled rerank ampersand-entity media models, the replica stored those five characters, and the renderer escaped the ampersand again — correctly, it emits text into HTML — so the page showed the doubled entity. Neither half was wrong; the missing one was the decode at the boundary. It compounds, because every re-capture escapes what the last one stored, and it is worse than a display bug: the editor field holds the entity too, so a curator who types the correction stores the character and the next capture overwrites it. Fidelity mode never had it, which is why it survived until the authorable path was tested. The decoder is one pass left to right, so an author's own escaped entity survives as text rather than becoming a tag; the named table is the marks a page actually spells rather than HTML5's 2500 and an unknown name is left verbatim, since a surviving name is a report a reader can file and a dropped one is content that vanished; numeric forms are decoded in full, with surrogates and the C0 range refused. URLs are untouched — unescaping a query string belongs where the URL is parsed. The assertion is the round trip on both sides of the seam: the CLI test re-escapes the stored field and requires the source's own bytes back, and ShConvertedLayoutRenderTest renders a field holding a literal ampersand and requires one entity, because one language could only check a copy of itself.

- **SH507** — The decision is recorded where the design lives: an authorable conversion yields structured, editable content presented by a Shio theme, and stops promising the source's appearance. docs/agents/cli.md now states the measurement that settled it — the editor showed unstyled text over 1,066,436 bytes of which 99% was the inlined captured theme, ~2,894 rules meeting 19 class attributes on 8 shio-* names, no source class surviving — and the two cheaper repairs that were measured and rejected: emitting the source's classes per field recovers 7 of the ~22 that style one heading, the other 15 sitting on wrapper divs the generated layout does not have, so it buys typography and no layout; translating them onto a shio-* contract is not a repair but a design system, one per replicated site. So the promise changes rather than the implementation being patched. The source's appearance is what fidelity is for, and fidelity reaches 0.00%, which makes the reviewer's choice their look or curate this — two good answers instead of one mode half-doing both. The propose paragraph's parenthetical stops saying the pixels have moved and says the fields become editable and the presentation becomes Shio's. Four things follow and are filed as SH508 to SH511: a structural layout contract for the vocabulary, the theme written against it, the captured theme no longer inlined on an authorable page, and a proposal that reports the replaced presentation as the mode's contract rather than as a loss.
- **SH508** — The generated layout now carries a structural layer a theme can lay out with, named by role and never by section type. It emitted section, heading, list and item with eight shio-* names, where the source needed five nested wrappers to place one heading, so there was no container to bound a measure, no stack to space siblings and no grid to put cards beside each other. LAYOUT_ROLES is the contract: shio-page on body, which is the rhythm between sections and needs no wrapper at all because the sections are body's own children, shio-container as the outer bound so a section can still go full bleed, shio-stack for the rhythm inside one, then grid, card, media, actions and button. Roles rather than types, so a theme written against them survives the eighth section type that ships; shio-section-Type stays as the per-type hook. The column count is deliberately not a role, because SectionFeatureGrid.columns is already on the section as data-shio-columns, so a theme reads the attribute from the ancestor and the template writes the number once. The two properties SH185 imposes are held by convert.test.mjs over the three pure wrapper roles: no sh-post, because ownership resolves to the nearest annotated ancestor and a wrapper that declared one would silently reassign every field under it to the wrong post, and no sh-field, because a wrapper is presentation and a curator has nothing to edit in it. The rule is scoped to three of the eight names and the test asserts the premise of that scoping rather than leaving it unexamined: a feature row is a card and draws its icon into an attribute, so a rule written over all eight would be false rather than strict. CLI suite 1035 green, backend 1460 green.
- **SH509** — vocabulary-theme.mjs is the stylesheet SH507's decision promised, written into the conversion document as a Theme post at /theme/shio titled <site> (Shio). Small on purpose: type scale, measure, vertical rhythm, a card, a button, and two colour roles, surface and ink, each with the one companion a card and a caption need, plus the accent a button is and the line a card is bounded by. Content and not a file, exactly the way the captured theme already ships, so a curator changes a colour without touching the CLI and a site with its own theme overrides it by naming that one on the layout; a stylesheet compiled into the jar would be the one part of a converted site nobody can change. The rationale named a blueprint as the vehicle and this is a post instead, for a reason worth stating rather than working around quietly: convert writes a desired-state document and has no way to apply a blueprint, so a converted site would render themeless until somebody applied one by hand, and a package plus the constant convert needs would be two copies of one stylesheet. It is written only when the conversion produces both sections and a layout to name it, because the roles are SH508's and a verbatim page has none of them. The tokens ride it as DTCG, so changing a colour is a field edit: ShThemeTokens compiles color.ink into --color-ink and prepends the :root block. Three closures are asserted, each of which fails silently the way an unstyled page does: every role LAYOUT_ROLES declares is styled, every var() the stylesheet reads is a token the theme declares, and every token it declares is read, because a token nothing uses is a field a curator can edit to no effect. Nothing in it names a section type; the only per-section selectors read data-shio-align, data-shio-variant and data-shio-columns, which are fields of the vocabulary rather than types. Two stylesheets on one page is still the open half and is SH510. CLI suite 1038 green, backend 1460 green.
- **SH510** — The authorable layout no longer resolves the captured theme: layoutTheme names <site> (Shio) for an authorable conversion and <site> (captured) for a fidelity one, and the layout still emits exactly one {{theme.css}}. The mechanism is the name rather than a second style element, so there is no template branch, no second handle, and the vocabulary theme keeps its token compilation, which a literal copy of the CSS in the layout would lose along with being a second copy of one stylesheet. What was being sent was 1,062,141 of an authorable page's 1,066,436 bytes, a stylesheet whose 2,894 rules met 8 shio-* names, on every page of a converted site with max-age=300, and with SH509's theme in the document it would have become two stylesheets on one page whose order decides the outcome, which is the accident SH424 spent a task removing reintroduced by inclusion rather than by cascade. Authorable is verbatim equals zero and not has any section: a conversion that left a page verbatim still names the captured theme, because fidelity's claim is a pixel comparison and cannot be made without those bytes, so a mixed site's composed pages stay exactly where they are today and no page is made worse to make another better. The capture is written byte for byte as before. The test measures rather than asserting a name: against a 1.04 MB captured stylesheet the theme the layout names is under one percent of it, there is exactly one theme handle in the layout, and a document with no theme at all names none. convert's report now names the theme, because under SH507 which presentation a reviewer is getting is the mode's contract and not an implementation detail. CLI suite 1041 green, backend 1460 green.
- **SH511** — The proposal stops reporting the mode's own contract as a loss. One list became two: discards names the elements and the behaviour a conversion genuinely drops, which a reviewer should weigh because an icon set is not presentation, and replaces names the class count as what the site's own theme takes over. The count stays, because a reviewer is entitled to know how much of the source's styling is being set aside; what goes is the framing. loses: 311 class name(s) all styling read as an argument for fidelity on every candidate, since 311 dropped classes always sounds worse than none, and that is how a session accepted candidates and then went looking for the styling as though it should have survived. The header now states the choice as two good answers rather than one with a penalty: fidelity keeps the source's appearance and offers no fields, authorable gives these fields presented by the site's own theme. That placement is P2 and P3 rather than style, and the cost test settled it. propose-cost.test.mjs reads 99 tokens per candidate against a baseline of 74 and its ceiling moved from 120 to 105 with it, because a budget sitting 60 percent above the measurement is not a budget. Two intermediate drafts were measured and rejected on the way: repeating the sentence per candidate cost 120 and landed exactly on the old ceiling, and printing an empty half as nothing cost 109 to say twice that there was nothing to say, so an empty half now prints no line and a candidate that loses nothing at all still says so on one. The proposal data is unchanged, because loss always held elements, behaviour and classes as separate keys and only the presentation conflated them, so no version moves and no plan file is invalidated. The two other documents that carried the old promise change with it: propose.mjs's header no longer says the pixels have moved, and the shio-replication-test skill no longer calls an authorable page's appearance a known limit but the contract, with finding the captured theme on the page as the defect to look for. CLI suite 1043 green, backend 1460 green.

- **SH870** — An annotated element shows the post's own field, substituted into the value before a template sees it — and markup with nothing to substitute is returned byte-for-byte rather than parsed.
- **SH868** — convert --annotate stamps the mapping onto a wholly verbatim page's own markup and declares the fields it addresses, so the page keeps the source's bytes and gains editable ones.
- 🗑 **SH875** — abandoned: AEM integration is not being pursued: filed and withdrawn on instruction the same day, 2026-08-20, so no authenticated capture was ever attempted.
- 🗑 **SH874** — abandoned: AEM integration is not being pursued: filed and withdrawn on instruction the same day, 2026-08-20, so the measurement it proposed was never run.
- **SH871** — --annotate declares its own fields: the document's postTypeFields compile to render.provision's data.fields, listed once per name, and no longer as requires lines nobody could satisfy.
- **SH872** — The annotated text stays in the markup that carries it, so Page keeps its four fields on a site of any size and a key its own markup annotates is declared by that markup.
- **SH873** — Both section packages ship a curated Primary menu and render it, so the nav carries short labels in editorial order instead of every page's SEO title alphabetically.
- **SH878** — A replica's nav is a Menu built from the source's own navigation, in its order, admitting the entries that appear on every page; the page listing survives as the fallback.

## Block 0 — Headless groundwork already in the tree (pre-roadmap)

These shipped before this roadmap was written and are the foundation the
backlog builds on. Listed so the roadmap doesn't re-propose them.

- **SH-0a** — **`@viglet/shio-react-sdk`** — React SDK consuming the Content Delivery API, with hooks `useShioPost`, `useShioChildren`, `useShioQuery`, `useShioSites`, a `ShioProvider`, and shared `types.ts`. ([shio-react-sdk/src](../shio-react-sdk/src))
- **SH-0b** — **`@viglet/shio-editor-cors`** — Universal Editor bridge enabling inline visual editing for any externally-rendered page. ([shio-js-sdk/src/shio-editor-cors.ts](../shio-js-sdk/src/shio-editor-cors.ts))
- **SH-0c** — **API-token auth** — `ShApiToken` model + `ShApiTokenFilter` allow headless, non-session content consumption. ([ShApiTokenFilter](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/spring/security/auth/ShApiTokenFilter.java))
- **SH-0d** — **Unified Post API** — `/api/v2/post-unified` with create/update, `publish`/`unpublish`, `versions`, and folder listing — the seed of a delivery + lifecycle contract. ([ShPostUnifiedAPI](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/post/unified/ShPostUnifiedAPI.java))
- **SH-0e** — **Discovery endpoint** — `/api/v2/discovery` exposes instance/API metadata for clients. ([ShDiscoveryAPI](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/discovery/ShDiscoveryAPI.java))
- **SH-0f** — **GraphQL scaffold** — Spring for GraphQL wired with a programmatic schema (`ShGraphQLSchema`); placeholder `schema.graphqls` in place (real delivery schema is SH4).
- **SH-0g** — **CSRF + Basic/OAuth2 security** — `CookieCsrfTokenRepository` + `ShCsrfHeaderFilter` + OAuth2 client, matching the Turing security pattern.
- **SH-0h** — **Modern backend baseline** — Spring Boot 4 + Java 21, JPA + Liquibase (Postgres/MySQL/H2), Hazelcast cache, Tika extraction, Actuator/OpenAPI.

## Block A — Headless foundation (Content Delivery API)

- **SH5** — **Per-environment keys (prod/preview).** `ShApiToken` gains an `env` ([ShApiTokenEnv](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/persistence/model/token/ShApiTokenEnv.java): `PROD`/`PREVIEW`; `environment` column, `ddl-auto=update`, no migration; `null` = `PROD`). The axis is orthogonal to the SH2 `scope`: scope = *what operations*, env = *which content state*. [ShApiTokenFilter](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/spring/security/auth/ShApiTokenFilter.java) reads it, grants `ROLE_CDA_PREVIEW` for `PREVIEW` keys, and carries it in [ShApiTokenContext](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/spring/security/auth/ShApiTokenContext.java) (new `env` component + `preview()`; back-compat 3-arg constructor defaults `PROD`). [ShCdaService](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/cda/ShCdaService.java) replaces the hard-coded `PUBLISHED` with a per-request resolution — **`PROD` keeps the existing efficient single-state `Page` queries byte-for-byte**; **`PREVIEW` reads draft-preferred** (point lookups try `DRAFT` then `PUBLISHED` via `resolvePost`/`readStates`; listings/query/GraphQL fetch `{DRAFT,PUBLISHED}` via new `…StateIn` finders, dedup by post id keeping the `DRAFT` row, and page in memory). Driven **solely by `env`** (the SH2 `PREVIEW` *scope* stays an authz marker SH13 builds on), so there's one draft-visibility driver and REST + GraphQL (SH4) inherit it identically; the SH2 per-site allow-list still applies on every branch. `ShApiTokenAPI` persists `env`; React token editor adds an **Environment** select + description, list shows a preview badge, en/pt i18n. No-token / pre-SH5 access stays `PROD` = the SH1 behaviour. 17 tests green (`ShApiTokenFilterTest` 10 (+2), `ShCdaEnvTest` 4 (new), `ShCdaScopeTest` 3) + SH1's `ShCdaAPITest` 11 still green. **SH13** (short-lived preview tokens + in-console "preview this draft" UX) layers on this draft-visibility machinery. Spec: `docs/specs/SH5-per-environment-keys.md`.
- **SH4** — **Real GraphQL delivery schema.** [ShGraphQLSchema](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/cda/graphql/ShGraphQLSchema.java) now builds the GraphQL schema programmatically from the content post-types (replacing the placeholder `schema.graphqls`): a `ShContent` interface carries the common post fields, each `system=0` post-type becomes an object type implementing it with a `String` field per `ShPostTypeAttr` (keyed by attr `name`), and a `ShGenericPost` fallback backs system / unmapped types (also guaranteeing the schema builds with zero content types). Names are coerced to the GraphQL grammar (invalid chars → `_`, dedup on collision). The `Query` root — `post(id)`, `postByUrl(siteId, url)`, `posts(siteId, folderId, postType, page, size)` — delegates to [ShCdaService](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/cda/ShCdaService.java) (new `queryPosts` returns full posts with attrs; shared `queryPage`), so GraphQL **inherits SH2 per-site scoping + `PUBLISHED`-only** rather than re-implementing them — a second *shape* over the same contract, not a second contract. Served via a [ShGraphQLConfig](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/cda/graphql/ShGraphQLConfig.java) `GraphQlSourceBuilderCustomizer.schemaFactory`. `/graphql` is now a CDA delivery surface: [ShApiTokenFilter](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/spring/security/auth/ShApiTokenFilter.java) authenticates + rate-limits it like `/api/v2/cda/**` (the SH2 GET-only gate skipped — GraphQL reads via `POST`, and the schema exposes **no `Mutation`**), and [ShSecurityConfig](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/spring/security/ShSecurityConfig.java) requires `ROLE_CDA` on `POST /graphql` (was `permitAll`). Build-at-startup caveat: a new/edited post-type needs a restart to appear in the schema. Attr fields are `String` for now (strong per-widget typing awaits SH11). 8 tests green (`ShGraphQLSchemaTest` 7 incl. query-execution, `ShApiTokenFilterTest` +1 = 8) + SH1/SH2/SH3 still green. Spec: `docs/specs/SH4-cda-graphql-schema.md`.
- **SH3** — **CDA rate limiting + caching headers.** [ShCdaCacheConfig](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/cda/ShCdaCacheConfig.java) registers two servlet filters scoped to `/api/v2/cda/*`: Spring's `ShallowEtagHeaderFilter` (body-hash `ETag` + `304` on `If-None-Match`) and [ShCdaCacheControlFilter](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/cda/ShCdaCacheControlFilter.java) (`Cache-Control: public, max-age=N`, or `no-cache` when `N=0`) — both ordered after the security chain so a `401`/`403`/`429` never gets cached. [ShCdaRateLimiter](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/cda/ShCdaRateLimiter.java) is an in-memory, per-token token bucket (keyed by `ShApiToken.id`, lazy refill off a monotonic clock); [ShApiTokenFilter](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/spring/security/auth/ShApiTokenFilter.java) enforces it after auth → `429` + `Retry-After` + `X-Rate-Limit-Remaining`. All tunable via `shio.cda.*` ([ShCdaProperties](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/cda/ShCdaProperties.java): `cache.max-age-seconds` default 60; `rate-limit.{enabled,capacity,refill-tokens,refill-period-seconds}` default 120 burst / 120-per-min). **Single-instance** limiter (per-JVM budget; a Hazelcast-backed bucket is the later multi-node hardening, out of scope). 13 tests green (`ShCdaRateLimiterTest` 4, `ShApiTokenFilterTest` +1 = 7, `ShCdaCacheControlFilterTest` 2) + SH1/SH2 still green. Spec: `docs/specs/SH3-cda-rate-limit-cache.md`.
- **SH2** — **API-token scopes + per-site keys.** `ShApiToken` gains a `scope` ([ShApiTokenScope](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/persistence/model/token/ShApiTokenScope.java): `READ`/`PREVIEW`/`WRITE`) and an optional `siteIds` allow-list (`@ElementCollection` → `api_token_site`; empty = all sites). [ShApiTokenFilter](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/spring/security/auth/ShApiTokenFilter.java) now **confines token auth to `/api/v2/cda/**`** (a `Key` on any other path is ignored — closes the prior any-path authentication), gates methods by scope (`READ`/`PREVIEW` GET-only, `WRITE` any), grants `ROLE_CDA_PREVIEW`/`ROLE_CDA_WRITE` accordingly, and carries scope + allow-list to the service via [ShApiTokenContext](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/spring/security/auth/ShApiTokenContext.java) (the auth `details`). [ShCdaService](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/cda/ShCdaService.java) enforces the allow-list at every read boundary — a disallowed site collapses to the existing 404/empty, so a per-site key can't distinguish "wrong site" from "missing". No-token / null-scope paths stay unrestricted = the SH1 behaviour (`ddl-auto=update`, no migration). React token editor adds a **Scope** select + **Site access** (all-sites switch + per-site checkboxes); list shows a scope badge; en/pt i18n. 9 tests green (`ShApiTokenFilterTest` 6, `ShCdaScopeTest` 3) + SH1's 11 still green. Spec: `docs/specs/SH2-token-scopes.md`.
- **SH1** — **Versioned, read-only CDA contract.** New `/api/v2/cda/**` namespace ([ShCdaAPI](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/cda/ShCdaAPI.java)) with 7 GET endpoints (sites, site-by-id, folder children listing, breadcrumb path, post-by-id, **post-by-url** for `[...slug]` routing, query) backed by `ShPostUnified` pinned to `PUBLISHED`. Returns frozen DTO records ([api/cda/dto](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/cda/dto)) via [ShCdaMapper](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/cda/ShCdaMapper.java) — never the JPA entity; authoring fields (`owner`/`publisher`/`publishStatus`/`modifier`) excluded; malformed `data` → `attrs:{}`. Furl resolution rides the existing `idx_post_unified_furl` index. Secured by `hasRole("CDA")` (GET-only via the existing `ShApiTokenFilter`). 17 tests green (`ShCdaAPITest` 11, `ShCdaMapperTest` 6). Spec: `docs/specs/SH1-cda-read-contract.md`.

## Infra — JS monorepo (pnpm workspace)

- **pnpm workspace** — root `package.json` + `pnpm-workspace.yaml` cover `shio-react` (console), `shio-client`, `shio-react-sdk`, `create-shio-app`. `shio-react-sdk` now depends on the core via `workspace:*` (was `file:`). `frontend-maven-plugin` migrated npm → pnpm (`install-node-and-pnpm` + `pnpm install` + `pnpm run compile:build`); Maven console build verified producing `shio-app/.../public/`. Native builds allowlisted (`esbuild`, `@tailwindcss/oxide`). Publish workflow rewritten to `pnpm publish` (auto-resolves `workspace:*`). npm lockfiles removed in favor of a single root `pnpm-lock.yaml`.

## Block B — JavaScript-for-pages DX

- **SH66** — **Console "managed by code" lock.** Closes the SH62 epic: makes the DSL↔GUI boundary explicit instead of a silent last-writer-wins race. A new `managed` flag on the post-type ([ShPostType](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/persistence/model/post/type/ShPostType.java), `boolean`; Liquibase [v2026.3.4.yaml](../shio-app/src/main/resources/db/changelog/v2026.3.4.yaml) `addColumn` — nullable + backfill `false`, DB-agnostic) is set **true by every SH16 admin-API `upsert`** ([ShPostTypeAdminService](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/post/type/ShPostTypeAdminService.java)) — i.e. any `shio push` — so a code-owned type is marked the moment it lands. The flag is **delivered, not authored**: carried on `ShPostTypeDef` (and exposed by `GET /api/v2/post-type` + the console entity API), but **excluded from the CLI's canonical `normalizeDef`** so a hand-written `*.json` that omits it never registers as drift; `upsert` always stamps it regardless of the value sent (mirroring `system`). The React post-type editor ([post-type.edit.page.tsx](../shio-react/src/app/console/content/post-type.edit.page.tsx)) renders a "Managed by code" badge + banner, disables Save/Save&Close, and wraps the model in a native `disabled` `<fieldset>` (read-only cascades to every input/switch/dnd handle). Server-side backstop: console `PUT` of a managed type → 409 [ShManagedPostTypeException](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/post/type/ShManagedPostTypeException.java). `provisionFromDef` preserves the flag for SH22 per-tenant copies; system types stay separately read-only. **Jackson 3 gotcha:** adding a *primitive* `boolean` component broke `ShExchangePackageCodec` parse of pre-SH66 manifests (the bootstrap `export.json` omits it) — Jackson 3 defaults `FAIL_ON_NULL_FOR_PRIMITIVES` to true, so the absent primitive threw `MismatchedInputException`; fixed by disabling that feature on the exchange mapper (absent primitive → type default), keeping the SH68 format version-tolerant. **Tests:** `ShPostTypeAdminServiceTest` (upsert marks managed + pull reports it, orthogonal to `system`), `ShPostTypeConsoleAPITest` (GET exposes `managed`, PUT → 409), CLI [post-types-io.test.mjs](../cli/test/post-types-io.test.mjs) (managed never registers as drift); full backend suite 236 green, CLI 25, shio-react `tsc -b` clean. Spec: `docs/specs/SH62-post-types-dsl.md` §7.
- **SH65** — **CI drift guard (`shio push --check`).** A read-only assertion that "git == server" for the code-owned post-type subset, for use in CI. New `--check` boolean ([index.mjs](../cli/src/index.mjs) `BOOLEANS` + HELP) runs the unchanged SH16/SH64 compile + `diffDefs`/`planPush`, prints the plan, **writes nothing**, and exits non-zero when the plan is non-empty so a pipeline fails on drift. Drift is the *actionable* plan — `toPut.length + toDelete.length` (added + changed, plus prunable non-system removals only when `--prune` is also passed) — so remote-only system types (always absent locally) never trip the guard, mirroring exactly what a real `push` would change. Distinct from `--dry-run` (informational, always exit 0). Exit-code plumbing is generic: [push.mjs](../cli/src/commands/push.mjs) `run` returns `{ check, drift, exitCode }`, and [index.mjs](../cli/src/index.mjs) `main` honors any command result's numeric `exitCode` (`exit(result.exitCode)` when non-zero), keeping the command testable without touching `process`. **Tests:** 3 new `node:test` ([commands.test.mjs](../cli/test/commands.test.mjs)) — drift → `exitCode 1` + "drift detected" + zero non-GET calls; in-sync → `exitCode 0` + "in sync"; `--check --prune` counts the prunable delete as drift while excluding a `system` type from `toDelete`. Full CLI suite 24 green. Console "managed by code" lock (SH66) still builds on SH63. Spec: `docs/specs/SH62-post-types-dsl.md` §6.
- **SH64** — **CLI compile step (`shio push`/`build` recognize DSL sources).** Closes the SH63→CLI gap: `shio/post-types/` may now hold `*.ts`/`*.mjs` DSL modules (authored with `@viglet/shio-model`) **alongside** `*.json`, and the CLI compiles them to canonical JSON before the unchanged SH16 diff/serialize/PUT pipeline runs — the admin API and wire format are untouched. New shared loader [post-types-compile.mjs](../cli/src/post-types-compile.mjs): `readLocalDefs(ctx, dir)` reads the directory in sorted order, `JSON.parse`s `*.json`, and for `*.ts`/`*.mjs` dynamically `import()`s the module (via an **injectable** `ctx.import`, defaulting to native dynamic import — a `.ts` rides the project's own TS toolchain / Node type-stripping, *no new bundler in the CLI*) and `collectDefsFromModule` gathers every `ShPostTypeDef` it exports — default, named, or an exported array, flattened; non-def exports (helpers, `WIDGET`) ignored. A name defined by more than one source is a hard error (ambiguous source); a DSL module exporting no post-type is an error. [push.mjs](../cli/src/commands/push.mjs) drops its JSON-only reader and delegates to the shared loader, so `.ts`-authored and `.json` models push identically. New [`shio build`](../cli/src/commands/build.mjs) command compiles DSL+JSON → canonical JSON artifacts under `shio/.out/` (`--out` override) **without** touching the server — byte-identical to what `pull` writes, for inspection/CI. CLI help + `--dir`/`--out` docs updated. **Tests:** 7 new `node:test` ([compile.test.mjs](../cli/test/compile.test.mjs)) — `collectDefsFromModule` over default/named/array exports, `readLocalDefs` over a mixed `.ts`/`.json` dir (fake module loader + in-memory fs), duplicate-name + empty-module errors, `build` canonical output, and a `.ts`-authored `push` PUTting like JSON; full CLI suite 21 green. End-to-end verified against the built `@viglet/shio-model` via the real native importer. **Still deferred:** `pull --as ts` lossy scaffolding (the SH63 decoders exist for it but it's a best-effort convenience, not in the acceptance set). Drift guard (`push --check`, SH65) and console lock (SH66) build on this. Spec: `docs/specs/SH62-post-types-dsl.md` §5.
- **SH63** — **Post-types DSL core (`@viglet/shio-model`).** The authoring inverse of SH11's model→types codegen: a pure, zero-dependency ESM workspace package (sibling to `@viglet/shio-client`) that lets a JS dev write the content model as **typed TypeScript** and compile it to the canonical SH16 `ShPostTypeDef` JSON the admin API already consumes. **Builders** ([builders.ts](../shio-model/src/builders.ts)): `postType(name, opts)` + one factory per the 14 widgets (`text`/`textArea`/`htmlEditor`/`checkBox`/`comboBox`/`date`/`hidden`/`multiSelect`/`aceJs`/`aceHtml`/`contentSelect`/`file`/`relator`/`tab`), each returning a `ShPostTypeAttrDef`; ordinals auto-assigned 1-based by array position (override via `ordinal`), `system` always `false` (system types stay backend-owned). Settings-bearing factories take **typed** options (`comboBox` *requires* `choices` — a missing one is a `tsc` error, not a `push` 400), so `tsserver` gives autocomplete + compile-time validation with no custom VSCode extension. **widgetSettings codec** ([widget-settings.ts](../shio-model/src/widget-settings.ts), the heart of the package): encodes the ergonomic typed settings to the *exact* legacy wire string — `choices: {tech:"Technology"}` → `"{\"choices\":\"tech: Technology\\nbiz: Business\",\"allowNull\":1}"`, `file`/`contentSelect`/`multiselect`/`relator` single-key wrappers, empty settings → `null` (never the string `"null"`) — with a **symmetric decoder** for every encoder (`decodeChoices`/`decodeFile`/`decodeContentSelect`/`decodeMultiSelect`/`decodeRelator`) so SH64 can scaffold a starter `.ts` from `pull`ed JSON. **Serialization** ([serialize.ts](../shio-model/src/serialize.ts)): `normalizeDef`/`serializeDef`/`toDef` reimplement SH16's canonical normalization (fixed key order, fields sorted by ordinal-then-name, stable defaults, trailing newline) so the compiled JSON is **byte-identical** to a hand-written `shio/post-types/*.json` — one serialization contract, the DSL can never disagree with the bytes that drive `push`'s diff. **Tests:** 15 `node:test` green ([builders.test.mjs](../shio-model/test/builders.test.mjs)) — widget-by-widget codec round-trips, ordinal assignment (auto + explicit-preserved), relator/tab nesting, null/garbage-tolerant decoders, and the §8.1 acceptance anchor: byte-identical serialization vs a hand-checked golden fixture ([news.golden.json](../shio-model/test/news.golden.json)). Wired into the root `pnpm test`. SH64 (CLI compile step) / SH65 (drift guard) / SH66 (console lock) build on this. Spec: `docs/specs/SH62-post-types-dsl.md` §4.
- **SH11** — **TypeScript type generation from post-types (`shio-types`).** Closes the loop between the runtime-configured content model and the statically-typed JS front: `post.attrs.*` now gets real autocomplete. **Backend:** a read-only CDA post-type schema surface — [ShCdaAPI](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/cda/ShCdaAPI.java) `GET /api/v2/cda/post-type` (all) + `/post-type/{name}` (one, 404 if unknown), returning [ShCdaPostTypeSchema](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/cda/dto/ShCdaPostTypeSchema.java) / recursive [ShCdaSchemaField](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/cda/dto/ShCdaSchemaField.java) via new `ShCdaMapper.toPostTypeSchema`/`toSchemaField`. The mapper drops layout-only `Tab` widgets, marks `Multi Select`/`Check Box` and Relator fields `multiple`, and nests a Relator's sub-fields under `fields`. [ShCdaService](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/cda/ShCdaService.java) gains `listPostTypes`/`getPostType` over a new `ShPostTypeRepository` injection — **not** SH2 site-scoped (post-types are global; the schema carries field shape only, never content). No security change (GET under the existing `ROLE_CDA` rule, inheriting SH3 cache/rate-limit). **JS:** [@viglet/shio-client](../shio-client) gains `getPostTypes`/`getPostType` ([client.ts](../shio-client/src/client.ts)) + `ShioPostTypeSchema`/`ShioFieldSchema` types, and a **pure, dependency-free** `generateShioTypes(schemas, {importFrom?, banner?})` ([codegen.ts](../shio-client/src/codegen.ts)) that emits one `…Attrs` interface + a `…Post = ShioPost & {…}` intersection type (not `interface extends` — an interface isn't assignable to `ShioPost.attrs`'s `Record<string, unknown>`) per post-type plus a `ShioPostTypes` name→type map (Relator → `Array<{…}>`, `multiple` → `string[]`, else `string`; non-required → `?`; non-identifier names PascalCased/quoted; deterministic; output tsc-strict clean). A `shio-types` Node CLI ([bin/shio-types.mjs](../shio-client/bin/shio-types.mjs), `--url`/`--token`/`--out [-]`/`--import-from`, env fallbacks `SHIO_URL`/`SHIO_CDA_TOKEN`) wires fetch → generate → write; `bin`+`files` declared in [package.json](../shio-client/package.json). **Starter:** `create-shio-app` gains `npm run shio:types` ([template/package.json](../create-shio-app/template/package.json)) + a "Typed content" README section. Tests: backend `com.viglet.shio.api.cda` package **38 green** (new [ShCdaPostTypeSchemaTest](../shio-app/src/test/java/com/viglet/shio/api/cda/ShCdaPostTypeSchemaTest.java), 3) + shio-client **19 `node:test` green** ([codegen.test.mjs](../shio-client/test/codegen.test.mjs) + `getPostTypes`/`getPostType` cases) + create-shio-app scaffold **10 green**. This also unblocks the SH7/§II.2 `ShioField` follow-up (the real widget type is now deliverable). Spec: `docs/specs/SH11-type-generation.md`.
- **SH10** — **Matured the Universal Editor bridge (CDA write surface + console editor shell).** The save-back half of the inline editor now exists, riding the SH2 `WRITE` scope. **Backend:** a CDA write surface in the `/api/v2/cda` namespace — [ShCdaWriteAPI](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/cda/ShCdaWriteAPI.java) (`GET /post/{id}/editable`, `PATCH /post/{id}`, `POST /post/{id}/publish`) over [ShCdaWriteService](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/cda/ShCdaWriteService.java). Edits **merge into the post's `DRAFT` row** (seeding a draft from `PUBLISHED` when a published-only post is first edited, so the live snapshot is untouched until an explicit publish — and a `PREVIEW`-env client (SH5) renders that draft for live preview); writes delegate to the existing `ShPostUnifiedWriteService.update/publish`, and the SH2 per-site allow-list is re-enforced on the write path (disallowed → 404/empty). `getEditable` returns the post + its post-type **field schema** ([ShCdaField](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/cda/dto/ShCdaField.java) via new `ShCdaMapper.toFields`) so the editor panel can render every field, not only DOM-instrumented ones. [ShSecurityConfig](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/spring/security/ShSecurityConfig.java) gates `PATCH`/`POST /api/v2/cda/**` to `ROLE_CDA_WRITE` (GET stays `ROLE_CDA`) and CSRF-exempts the namespace (token writes are stateless); `ShApiTokenFilter` already grants `ROLE_CDA_WRITE` + lifts the GET-only gate for WRITE tokens (SH2). **Frontend:** the React console editor shell (the iframe *parent*) at `/console/universal-editor` — an [editor-sites page](../shio-react/src/app/console/universal-editor/editor-sites.page.tsx) (site list + external-URL entry + a WRITE-token selector persisted to `localStorage`) and a [visual-editor page](../shio-react/src/app/console/universal-editor/visual-editor.page.tsx) that loads the page in an iframe, exchanges the `sh:*` `postMessage` events with the existing `shio-editor.js` bridge, accumulates inline edits, and saves/publishes via [ShUniversalEditorService](../shio-react/src/services/universal-editor/universal-editor.service.ts) — which uses a **credential-less** axios instance so the `Key` token (not the console session) authenticates the CDA write. Route group registered in `App.tsx`; en/pt i18n completed. 7 tests green (`ShCdaWriteTest` 5 new, `ShApiTokenFilterTest` +2 = 12) + SH1–SH5 CDA suites still green. Live draft-preview UX in the console is **SH13**; the publish *webhook emitter* is **SH12**. Spec: `docs/specs/SH10-universal-editor-bridge.md`.
- **SH9** — **SSG/ISR/SSR recipes + on-demand revalidation (Next.js side).** The `create-shio-app` template now ships all three rendering modes against the CDA and the on-demand revalidation receiver. New [`app/api/revalidate/route.ts`](../create-shio-app/template/app/api/revalidate/route.ts) (Node runtime): verifies an HMAC-SHA256 `x-shio-signature` over the raw body against `SHIO_WEBHOOK_SECRET` (constant-time `timingSafeEqual`), then `revalidatePath(url)` + `revalidatePath("/")` + optional `revalidateTag` — staleness drops from the ISR window to seconds on publish. New [`app/api/preview/route.ts`](../create-shio-app/template/app/api/preview/route.ts) toggles Next.js Draft Mode (gated by `SHIO_PREVIEW_SECRET`, relative-URL redirect only); [`lib/shio.ts`](../create-shio-app/template/lib/shio.ts) gains a PREVIEW-env client + `getShioClient()` that returns it when Draft Mode is on (SSR draft preview, riding on SH5 per-env keys). Catch-all + home pages branch on `draftMode()` and show an "Exit preview" banner. `.env.example`/scaffolded `.env.local` carry the three new (empty) keys. Recipe + the webhook contract SH12 must emit: [docs/recipes/nextjs-rendering.md](recipes/nextjs-rendering.md). 10 `node:test` tests green (2 new). (The webhook **emitter** is SH12; this is the consumer side, ready to be driven.)
- **SH8** — **`create-shio-app` — Next.js starter.** Zero-dependency Node scaffolder ([create-shio-app/](../create-shio-app)) — `npx create-shio-app my-site --url … --site … --token … --yes` (interactive prompts otherwise). Generates a Next.js 15 App-Router project: shared `@viglet/shio-client` instance from env ([lib/shio.ts](../create-shio-app/template/lib/shio.ts)), home page listing published posts (`shio.query`), and a catch-all [`app/[...slug]/page.tsx`](../create-shio-app/template/app/%5B...slug%5D/page.tsx) that resolves CDA friendly-URLs via `shio.getPostByUrl` with `generateStaticParams` (SSG) + `revalidate` (ISR). Pure file-ops core split out for testing; ships `gitignore` (renamed on scaffold per the npm dotfile gotcha); writes `.env.local` from flags. 8 `node:test` tests + CLI smoke green. The flagship "JS dev, zero Java" deliverable. (Note: the generated app depends on `@viglet/shio-client`, which must be published/linked.)
- **SH7** — **`shio-react-sdk` rebased onto the core + completed surface.** The React SDK no longer ships its own HTTP client — `provider.tsx` builds a core `ShioClient` (or accepts a pre-built one for SSR sharing), and `client.ts`/`types.ts` re-export from `@viglet/shio-client` (declared as a dependency, kept external in the bundle). New shared `useAsync` (abortable loading/data/error). Hooks now return `{ data, loading, error }` over CDA types: `useShioSites`/`useShioSite`/`useShioChildren`/`useShioBreadcrumb` (new)/`useShioPost`/`useShioPostByUrl` (new)/`useShioQuery`. New render components: `ShioRichText`, `ShioImage` (relative-path resolution), `ShioRelator` (render-prop list), `ShioField` (value-shape resolver with `as` override). tsc clean + vite build green (~4.5 kB). **Breaking** (pre-release): legacy `ShPost`/`ShObjectItem` shapes and `queryBySite`/`getPostsByType` removed — hooks return CDA types now. Note: full widget-map fidelity in `ShioField` awaits post-type schema in the CDA (SH11) — current inference is heuristic.
- **SH6** — **`@viglet/shio-client` — framework-agnostic TS core.** New zero-runtime-dependency package ([shio-client/](../shio-client)) consuming the SH1 CDA contract (`/api/v2/cda/**`). `ShioClient` with `getSites`/`getSite`/`listChildren`/`getPath`/`getPost`/`getPostByUrl`/`query`; injectable `fetch` (Node/browser/edge/SSR), `Key`-header auth, 404→`null` on single-resource getters, typed `ShioHttpError` otherwise, `AbortSignal` support. TS types mirror the CDA DTOs. vite lib build (ESM + UMD + `.d.ts`, ~3.5 kB). 11 `node:test` tests green (network-free, injected fetch). Targets the CDA — **not** the legacy console endpoints the old `shio-react-sdk/src/client.ts` used.

## Block C — Composable platform primitives

- **SH55** — **Trash / soft-delete + restore (posts).** Deletes were permanent; a mis-click lost content. SH55 turns the post DELETE into a reversible trash. **Model:** a nullable `deletedDate` on [ShPostUnified](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/persistence/model/post/unified/ShPostUnified.java) + a Hibernate **`@SQLRestriction("deleted_date is null")`** on the entity, so **every** Hibernate-generated read (CDA delivery, console navigation, search, listings, `findByIdAndState`, …) auto-excludes trashed rows with **zero finder changes** — the key design choice over threading a flag through ~15 queries. Liquibase [v2026.3.8.yaml](../shio-app/src/main/resources/db/changelog/v2026.3.8.yaml) (`addColumn deleted_date TIMESTAMP`, nullable, no backfill). **Service** ([ShPostUnifiedWriteService](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/migration/unified/ShPostUnifiedWriteService.java)): `delete` now **soft-deletes** (stamps `deletedDate` on the DRAFT+PUBLISHED rows, records the SH51 `DELETE` audit) and deliberately fires **no lifecycle event** — a reversible trash has zero side effects (no SH12 webhook, no SH38 file-byte cleanup). `restoreFromTrash` clears the marker (+ `RESTORE` audit); `purge` permanently removes the rows and fires the `DELETE` lifecycle event **then** (so byte-cleanup + webhook run only on irreversible deletion); `listTrash` returns one row per id (DRAFT-preferred). The trash queries are **native** (`findTrash`/`findTrashedById`/`restoreFromTrash`/`purge` on [ShPostUnifiedRepository](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/persistence/repository/post/ShPostUnifiedRepository.java)) since native SQL bypasses both `@SQLRestriction` and `@TenantId` — so they explicitly tenant-scope via `ShTenantContext`. **API:** `GET /api/v2/post-unified/trash`, `POST /{id}/untrash`, `DELETE /{id}/purge` ([ShPostUnifiedAPI](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/post/unified/ShPostUnifiedAPI.java), SH54 WRITE-gated). **Console:** a [Trash page](../shio-react/src/app/console/content/trash.page.tsx) (`/console/content/trash`) listing trashed posts with Restore + Delete-permanently, wired into routes + the Content sidebar (Trash icon) over the extended [post-unified.service.ts](../shio-react/src/services/post-unified/post-unified.service.ts) (`trash`/`untrash`/`purge`); en/pt i18n. **Scope:** posts only — folder soft-delete (subtree-hide semantics) is a deliberate follow-up; folder deletion still hard-removes its live posts. Test: [ShPostTrashTest](../shio-app/src/test/java/com/viglet/shio/api/post/unified/ShPostTrashTest.java) (soft-delete hides from reads but lists in trash; restore brings it back; purge removes permanently + is idempotent). Green on full backend suite + console `tsc -b`. → ROADMAP §III.10
- **SH54** — **Content-level ACL / permissions (folder/post grants, inherited, default-allow).** `ShUser`/`ShGroup`/`ShRole` had full CRUD but **nothing tied them to content** — any authenticated console user reached all content. SH54 adds a per-object ACL. **Model:** new [ShContentAcl](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/persistence/model/acl/ShContentAcl.java) (`sh_content_acl`, `@TenantId`) — one grant = "{principal} may {permission} {objectId}", with [ShAclPrincipalType](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/persistence/model/acl/ShAclPrincipalType.java) (USER/GROUP/ROLE) + [ShAclPermission](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/persistence/model/acl/ShAclPermission.java) (READ/WRITE, WRITE⊇READ). `object_id` has no FK (folders/sites live in `ShObject`, posts in `sh_post_unified` — two tables). Liquibase [v2026.3.7.yaml](../shio-app/src/main/resources/db/changelog/v2026.3.7.yaml) (`createTable`, enums as VARCHAR per the agnostic lint, `QUOTE_ALL_OBJECTS`). **Resolution** ([ShContentAclService](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/acl/ShContentAclService.java)`.canRead/canWrite/requireRead/requireWrite`): walks the object → its folder → ancestor folders; the **nearest level carrying any ACL decides** (levels above are not consulted); **default-allow** when no ACL exists anywhere up the chain (so existing installs are unaffected until an ACL is set); **admin bypass** (`ROLE_ADMIN` always passes — an ACL can't lock the admin out); **no security context** (internal/system calls) passes. The current user's principals are resolved username + group names + role names (same `findByShUsersIn`→`findByShGroupsIn` chain as `ShCustomUserDetailsService`). **Enforcement at the console boundary** (CDA delivery is already token-scoped by SH2, so user-ACLs target authoring): [ShObjectAPI](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/object/ShObjectAPI.java) (list/path/copyto/moveto), [ShFolderAPI](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/folder/ShFolderAPI.java) (get=READ, create/update/delete=WRITE), [ShPostUnifiedAPI](../shio-app/src/main/java/com/viglet/shio/api/post/unified/ShPostUnifiedAPI.java) (get/listByFolder=READ; create/update/publish/unpublish/delete/translate/restore/schedule=WRITE) — a denied check throws `AccessDeniedException` → 403. **ACL management API:** `GET/PUT /api/v2/object/{id}/acl` on `ShObjectAPI` (editing requires WRITE-or-admin; PUT replaces the object's grants, empty = reopen). **Console:** a [PermissionsDialog](../shio-react/src/components/permissions.dialog.tsx) (grant rows: principal-type select + name + READ/WRITE) wired into the content list hover actions ([object.children.page.tsx](../shio-react/src/app/console/content/object.children.page.tsx)) over a new [acl.service.ts](../shio-react/src/services/acl/acl.service.ts) + en/pt `acl` i18n.
