- **SH487** — docs-shio/cli.md documents every verb of the shio command grouped by what a reader is trying to do - start something, discover, the content model, content, prove it works, replicate - with the connection flags and their environment variables, the fact that each command prints its own help, and a CI section giving the three gates in the order their failures make sense: push --check, push --content --check, verify. It carries the traps that cost time: verify prints its notes because an unreported cut reads as a clean pass, --delivery appends rather than replaces --checks, playwright is optional with a teaching error, and a changed snapshot exits 0 on purpose.
- **SH488** — docs-shio/blueprints.md opens on the distinction the law is about - a recipe tells you what to do, a blueprint does it - lists the six first-party packages and which three carry front-end files and why the other three do not, shows the plan-then-apply flow with every flag, and gives the five refusals that make applying somebody else's package safe: a package may not name its own site or prune, the model is provisioned never overwritten with the missing fields named, substitution is {{name}} only, a malformed package is a 409 because nothing the caller sent caused it, and the server never writes a project file. Ends with the package layout and the point that none of it is a new serialization.
- **SH489** — docs-shio/universal-editor.md explains the surface a curator uses to fix a page in place: why a form is the wrong tool for a headline, the three annotations with what the browser receives, the two rules that make ownership predictable (the page's post is stamped on body, resolution is nearest-ancestor and never inferred), opening a page in the console with ?editor=true injecting the bridge only there, the external front-end path with @viglet/shio-editor-cors and the editor-origin meta tag that the package is inert without, the fact that neither side posts to a wildcard, and what saving does - a merge into the DRAFT, seeded from PUBLISHED, through three delivery-API calls where editable returns the whole field schema.
- **SH492** — docs-shio/replication.md puts the mode choice before the pipeline, as the table that decides a run: fidelity is pixel-achievable and not editable, authorable is annotated and arrives unstyled, and you choose by what you accept at propose. Then clone with every flag, propose as the step where you approve a lossy transformation and see the loss, convert writing drafts at the source's own URLs, and judging on the public route rather than the preview with the two reasons that have burned a run. Four checks in the order that finds things, snapshot with open-the-PNG rather than trust-the-number, and the collection-row prop count that a glance cannot make. Four boundaries stated up front, including that the instance never renders JavaScript.
- **SH490** — intro.md now answers what Shio is with the premise it has: an agent builds, a human curates, the CDA delivers, plus the problem that shape solves and the no-model-no-prompts line. core-concepts.md is the vocabulary one level deeper, corrected against the tree: a folder is not a URL segment, two states and not four (DRAFT and PUBLISHED, both at once), post types as the one name-keyed surface with the real widget catalogue, the actual system types, the SH79 grammar with post:site/ for a home page, the render model in the renderer's own words, and what headless means for a CMS that also serves pages. Neither page teaches shObject and both end at the four hubs.
- **SH491** — architecture-overview.md is now the system that exists: one Spring Boot 4 application holding one content model behind four surfaces, with the argument that each is a shape over the same services and never a third contract. It carries six figures where the page had none, five of them pre-rendered SVGs per the repo convention (SH498), and states plainly what is not a dependency: no script engine on the classpath and Elasticsearch is not one at all, since search runs in the database and Turing is an optional client. Deployment topologies are corrected for what must be co-located, and the multi-node section names the two facts that bite: the rate limiter is per JVM and the change feed is commit-ordered per node.
- **SH493** — docs-shio/multi-tenancy.md documents SH22 for an operator: off by default, discriminator-column isolation applied by the persistence layer rather than by services remembering to filter, and the three consequences of that choice. It gives the resolution table with the fact that matters most, a token carries its own tenant so delivery is scoped to the content owner, then provisioning that copies the default model, membership, the free plan's 2 sites and 200 posts enforced with a 402 at creation, suspension and teardown, per-tenant file storage, and a four-item checklist before enabling it.
- **SH494** — search-caching.md separates the two things it conflated and retracts the false promise in the open: full-text search runs in the database with no extra infrastructure, and Turing ES indexing is opt-in, off by default, and reached on publish rather than on save. The retraction is explicit because the failure mode is a site that appears to have search and does not. It gives the three independent conditions and says none of them failing is an error, the event table with save-a-draft indexing nothing, the after-commit seam, why routing is configuration rather than content, and a four-layer cache table that answers the stale-content question by naming which layer a reader is looking at.
- **SH495** — The three reference pages were rebuilt from the tree rather than softened. rest-api.md opens by naming all four HTTP surfaces and says the agent surface is usually the better target, then documents post-unified with its trash, versions, schedule and translate verbs, the object listing/copy/move/ACL controller, folders, sites with export, the name-keyed post types with rename, static files with both URL forms, and the fifteen remaining roots, ending with the three endpoints that do not exist. configuration-reference.md is regenerated from the properties classes: every shio.cda, shio.agent, image, schedule, blueprint and turing key with its real default, ddl-auto=none with the reason, and the load-bearing H2 URL parameters. security.md is rewritten around the browser-versus-program split, with the four independent limits a key carries, where a key is accepted, what an AGENT key may not do, and the CSRF exemptions explained by the mechanism that makes them safe: they apply only to a caller with no session cookie.
- **SH496** — content-modeling.md is now the model as it is: one name-keyed surface with rename as a move and a teaching 409 for a type content points at, the real widget catalogue with what each widget decides, widgetSettings and why the references key is what makes a composition verifiable, the relationship table, the model as code in JSON and in TypeScript with the compile-time argument for the DSL, managed-by-code as an explicit boundary rather than a race, generated types for a front end, and the addressing grammar because a model that cannot be named cannot be queried. The delivery pages keep their shape and gain the corrections they needed; the JS-dev audience is kept and strengthened.
- **SH497** — docs-shio/token-economy.md publishes what a call costs: the budget table read from token-budgets.properties, the four levers (terse, ask for less, conditional reads, fold the proof into the write), the attribution ratios per source rather than one aggregate, and the four benchmark tasks with build-a-site at four calls and 2700 tokens. It publishes both unflattering numbers with their reasons rather than the flattering one: terse mode saves about a tenth on the manifest and not a third, because the per-endpoint prose is kept verbatim on purpose, and the build-a-site number ends at verify rather than at a page a person can open.
- **SH498** — Six shio-*.mmd sources now sit beside the turing and dumont sets, rendered to SVG and committed: shio-architecture (graph TB, callers, surfaces, core, persistence), shio-agent-loop (discover, plan, write, verify, hand over), shio-render-pipeline, shio-content-files (the round trip with the fingerprint base), shio-replication-flow (with the accept-or-not branch that decides the mode) and shio-curation-flow. They use the repo's four-colour palette, and the architecture page's oversized inline mermaid is replaced by them, which was the convention breach the task named. The one figure left inline is the delivery-read sequence, which is small. All 20 diagrams render green.
- **SH504** — docs-shio/design-tokens.md explains the protocol and the job it does in Shio: why a declared vocabulary turns the commonest change from a stylesheet rewrite into a reviewable field edit and leaves raw CSS as the escape hatch, what DTCG is (groups, $value, $type, $description) and that it was adopted because Style Dictionary, Figma and Tokens Studio already export it, the compilation to :root custom properties prepended to the theme CSS and why prepending rather than a separate handle, the dotted map for where var() cannot reach, the five authoring paths including post.upsert, the six degradation rules as a table with the reason for each, the replication half with the declared-versus-recurring distinction and the eight groups a capture reads, and when not to use a token at all.
- **SH499** — Two instruments in cli/conformance/: docs-vocabulary reads the product's own declarations and holds every documented verb, route, tool name and shio.* key against them with no instance, and docs-examples.conformance issues the 15 read-only documented requests against a live one; the execution half found three P6 gaps on its first run, now held by SH621 and SH622 in a fifth debt ledger.

## Block S — The public site (shio.viglet.org)

- **SH530** — shio-site/ is the public site: Vite, React 19, Tailwind v4 and shadcn/ui in the pnpm workspace, built in four steps (typecheck, client, SSR entry, prerender + OG raster) with no router - a pathname maps to a page by one regular expression the prerender and the client both read, and the head patch throws rather than shipping a page carrying another route's title. All copy lives in src/lib/site-content.ts and every claim on it is a real surface: the ten laws verbatim, the eleven MCP tools and six resources, ten CLI verbs, four measured token figures with the tests that produce them, the six P7 mechanisms, the address grammar and a teaching 400. The landing page is ordered as an argument rather than a feature list - hook, three roles, the laws, then one section per law in the order an agent meets them - and the hero's centrepiece is a scripted Claude Code session that says it is scripted, complete in the prerendered HTML and reduced to the finished transcript under prefers-reduced-motion. Brand is tomato on warm near-black against Turing's blue on cold navy, with the light-mode primary darkened because #FF6347 under white text is 2.9:1. Measured at 375 and 768: zero horizontal overflow, zero console errors - and getting there found that TableScroll's wrapper leaks 176px of a nested scroll container's overflow into the document unless it clips, which is not the sticky column and is now recorded where the fix is.
- **SH532** — /claude-code is the product's first five minutes, and it is also the site's first second route - so `ROUTES` in App.tsx replaced the single-branch resolver, `routesAreDeclared()` asserts that table and the prerender's agree in both directions at import time, and the trailing-slash trim is done by index rather than by an anchored `/\/+$/`, which backtracks super-linearly over a string the URL bar supplies. The page carries both install paths (the marketplace plugin, and `claude mcp add shio -- npx -y @viglet/shio mcp` for any MCP client), what the plugin adds as three skills, three commands and the AGENTS.md fragment, the three calls a session actually opens with and what each buys, and the four ShApiTokenScope rows with AGENT marked - reads like PREVIEW, writes on /api/v2/agent/** and /mcp only, deliberately not a superset of WRITE. It closes on the two boundaries a reader of an agent-native CMS is holding the whole way down: no model, no prompts, no provider key in the CMS; and MCP is not the only door. The route guard was proved by injecting a mismatch and watching the prerender die at the import. Zero overflow and zero console errors at 1440 and 375.
- **SH534** — /compare is seventeen questions against Contentful, Sanity, Strapi and WordPress, grouped by the design law each one comes from rather than by feature area - so the tick column reads as one design position applied repeatedly instead of a long feature list. The competitor cells answer whether the product documents the property as a guarantee, not whether a path to it exists, because an export command is not a file projection with a three-way merge and an MCP server in front of an API designed for a browser is not a protocol designed for an agent; where the honest answer is "you can build it" the cell says so, the page dates itself to 2026.3 and asks for corrections. The second half is what makes the first readable: each rival gets what it is genuinely better at and the case for picking it instead, plus the case against Shio stated plainly - if nobody is going to drive it with an agent, this is a self-hosted CMS with a smaller ecosystem and a JVM to run. Five objections answered, the landing page's teaser matrix now links here, and the site is three prerendered routes with zero overflow and zero console errors at 1440 and 375.
- **SH535** — /replicate walks the four verbs with the promise each one makes that the next depends on - clone writes an inventory and no content, propose applies nothing, convert lands every post in DRAFT with publish absent rather than false so a re-run cannot unpublish, and diff is arithmetic over declared against produced with a gained fact never a failure. Its centre is the decision the pipeline exists to put in front of a reviewer, and the page states why there are two modes rather than one: an authorable replica of a real site rendered 1,066,436 bytes with 99% of it the captured stylesheet and no source class surviving, carrying the classes through recovers 7 of the 22 that style one heading, and translating them is a design system per replicated site - so the promise changed instead of the implementation being patched. The bounds are a section rather than a caveat, because a crawler nobody can bound is one nobody should point at a stranger. Two defects the page found in shared components and fixed there: the highlighter read the apostrophe in "the source's appearance" as an opening quote and rendered a paragraph as one string literal, and JetBrains Mono ligated `--site` into an em dash on every command a reader is meant to copy. Four prerendered routes, zero overflow and zero console errors at 1440 and 375.
- **SH536** — /curator is written for the person who will be asked to approve the agent's work rather than for the engineer who wires it up: a Tuesday first - the agent worked overnight and published nothing, a queue with approve and revert, an expiring single-post preview link, a fix made inline on the rendered page, then publish or schedule - then the five lifecycle states with only one of them public, then the six gates. Each gate carries its reason rather than just its rule, because a rule with no argument behind it is one somebody turns off the first time it is inconvenient, and the sharpest of the six is that the review queue is console-authenticated and deliberately absent from the agent namespace: a credential that can both make a change and sign it off is not a review step, it is a log line. It closes on the three-role shape in plain words for a non-engineer, and the landing page's P7 section now links here. Five prerendered routes, zero overflow and zero console errors at 1440 and 375.
- **SH538** — .github/workflows/publish-github-pages.yml is the whole publish path: install the workspace on the pinned pnpm and Node, run build:site, assemble _site from dist and push it to the github-pages branch of openviglet/shio-ce with the CNAME written on every publish - because each publish overwrites the branch, and a root without one drops the custom domain silently. workflow_dispatch only, on publish-js-sdk.yml's reasoning: a deploy that fires on every push to a long-lived branch is one nobody can hold still while reviewing it, and the site is the artefact where a defect is public immediately. The gates are the build's own rather than repeated steps - tsc -b is the first thing build:site runs, and the prerender throws on a drifted template or on a route declared in only one of App.tsx and entry-server.tsx - plus two assertions for the failures that are silent rather than loud: no index.html publishes a directory listing, and no CNAME publishes every canonical URL against the wrong host. dist-ssr is a build input and stays out of the tree. Verified the one thing that would fail the first run: shio-site is in the committed lockfile and pnpm install --frozen-lockfile passes.
- **SH539** — Five depth pages at /features/<slug> - the agent gateway, content as files, blueprints, rendering and themes, and delivery - each from one record in shio-site/src/lib/feature-content.ts that carries the route, the title, the description and the blocks alike, so a new pillar is an entry there plus a row in entry-server.tsx and the route guard refuses if only one is written. What they carry is the mechanism at the level a reader deciding needs it: the actual call, the actual file on disk, the actual refusal - because docs/agents is the authoritative version and is written for somebody about to change the code, which makes it the wrong link to hand somebody who has not chosen the product yet. The landing page's six pillar cards stop being anchors into their own page and become the entrance to these. The rendering page is where design tokens land on instruction: the W3C DTCG shape adopted rather than invented, the compilation to :root prepended to the theme CSS, why the commonest change to a site stops being a stylesheet rewrite, the eight groups a capture lifts with declared custom properties honestly separated from recurring literals, and the substitution that is deliberately refused because a search-and-replace over a stranger's bytes breaks a replica in a way no digest catches. /replicate gains the short version with a link here. Ten prerendered routes, all clean at 1440 and 375.
- **SH537** — Every route now emits <path>.md beside its HTML - 64 KB of Markdown against 465 KB across the ten, printed on every build - plus a manifest.json listing the routes, their twins and their sizes in the shape /api/v2/agent/manifest uses, so the discovery pattern the product teaches is the one the site is discovered by. The twin is converted from the same render rather than written separately, and that direction is the whole design: the copy is data in src/lib but the composition is JSX, so generating from the data alone would re-declare the composition and the two would drift into the version nobody reads. scripts/markdown.mjs is the one piece of real logic on this site and therefore the one with a test - 20 cases, including the two failures that are silent when wrong: chrome leaking into every twin, and content vanishing because a tag was not recognised, which is why an unknown tag degrades to its text rather than throwing. The nav and footer never reach a twin, and data-md-skip lets a page declare a region chrome - the call to action carries it, because it converts a reader and costs an agent forty identical words ten times. Four defects the first output found and fixed: a law chip glued to its heading, two buttons rendered as adjacent links, list items and table rows separated by blank lines that broke them into separate lists, and an anchored newline trim that backtracks super-linearly on the one input where a long run of newlines is ordinary. llms.txt now carries the twin convention and the endpoint index.
- **SH531** — The hero's transcript is a player: transport controls, six progress dots that are also buttons, arrow-key stepping, and an artefact pane that shows what each call actually produced - the context pack with its digest, the pulled tree, the edit as a coloured diff, the push landing a DRAFT with nothing published, the verify with its one warning, and the handoff as Markdown. Every step stays in the DOM at every moment and is dimmed rather than unmounted, which is what keeps three things true at once: a screen reader gets the whole session, the prerendered HTML carries all six calls, and so does the Markdown twin. prefers-reduced-motion means no autoplay at all rather than a frozen animation - it opens on the finished session with the controls still working - and playback arms once on intersection so a visitor who scrolls back finds the session where they left it. Two defects the first render found: Markdown list items in the handoff were painted as diff deletions, so the diff colouring is now an explicit flag on the artefact rather than a prefix sniff, and an artefact label that is a path was being uppercased. The arrow-key handler sits on the controls themselves rather than on a container, so no div is given a role it does not have.
- **SH533** — The four token figures are generated on every build instead of typed: scripts/token-budgets.mjs reads shio-app/src/test/resources/token-budgets.properties - the one file the Java suite already asserts every response against - and writes the JSON the site imports, so the site and the build cannot disagree. The cross-package coupling is the point rather than a compromise; the alternative is a copy, and a second place to keep a number is a place that goes stale. A renamed or non-numeric key throws before the typecheck runs, proved by renaming one and watching the build refuse. Two corrections the pipeline forced and a hand-copied list would have shipped. The values are ceilings, not measurements, so the chart says ceiling and prints the property key under each bar - the honest half is also the machine-readable half. And ShAgentTaskBenchmarkTest.ratio() returns integer tenths, so min-call-ratio=30 is 3.0x: read as a whole number the page would have claimed an advantage an order of magnitude larger than anything measured. The P2 frame is now a table of all four benchmarked tasks with calls, tokens and both floors against the id-keyed REST path, stated as at-least rather than as a best case.
- **SH566** — The transcript player now keeps its lit step in view by scrolling its own list: the `block: "nearest"` rule is computed from two rects and applied with `Element.scrollBy`, which moves that element and no ancestor. `scrollIntoView` moved every scrollable ancestor up to the document, so a reader who scrolled past the hero was pulled back to it on each of the six 2.6s ticks - the home page read as a scroll trap, and nothing in the build said so. Two assertions close it: a source lint holding that only reader-initiated hash navigation in App.tsx may call scrollIntoView, which runs on every CI build and is the one that would have caught this, and an opt-in playwright test that scrolls a running site to 2000px, waits out two player steps and asserts the window did not move (SHIO_SITE_URL; it skips without the browser, the same refusal rule cli/src/browser.mjs applies to clone --render). The buggy version was re-run against both: the page drifted and both assertions went red.
- **SH571** — Each step in the hero transcript is now its own control: clicking call four selects call four and its artefact, and the transport arrows and progress dots become the fallback rather than the only way in. The affordance is an empty overlay button carrying the label and nothing else, because the obvious markup - a button around the step's three lines - would have deleted the whole session from every .md twin: markdown.mjs drops a button whole, children included, which is right for the CTA and fatal here. The build proves it kept its content: six calls in dist/index.md, zero labels leaked, twin unchanged at 22 KB. z-10 on that overlay is load-bearing and the browser test is what found it - the dimmed wrapper carries opacity, an opacity under 1 makes a stacking context, and the dimmed items therefore painted over their own click target, so every step was clickable exactly when it was already selected. Two assertions close it: a markdown case holding that an empty overlay costs the twin nothing, and a playwright case that clicks the fourth step, waits out a full player tick to prove selection is also taking over, and round-trips the artefact pane away and back rather than repeating copy that lives in site-content.ts.
- **SH705** — A person is now named by the role — curator, editor, reviewer — or in second person, across the site, docs/agents, the specs, README, agents.md, the plugin and docs-shio; P7 reads "never surprise the curator" and `actor-vocabulary.test.mjs` holds published prose at zero, exempting only `human-readable` and `human-in-the-loop` and printing the 225 source-comment occurrences it deliberately leaves alone.
- 🗑 **SH540** — abandoned: Provar as afirmacoes do site com uma instancia Shio viva e trabalho de infraestrutura e de demo publica, nao do produto, entao sai do backlog e o site segue com o conteudo roteirizado.
- **SH861** — README and shio-site carry judge, the declared bar and the exclusion authorable mode rests on — and a reader now asks every recently finished block whether its sweep was owed and paid.
- **SH925** — The site's prose is linted against the AI-writing checklist, and five counts it published are now read back from the surface each describes.
- **SH929** — 262 em dashes left the site in four spellings, and the lint that had exempted them now refuses every one a reader could be handed.
- **SH930** — Reading the sixteen split them: six are sample content that becomes a page the user publishes and were rewritten, ten are field help a curator reads in the console and stay with the 38 of the same kind in its own bundles — the rule follows the prose to its reader rather than to a module, and a lint holds the content tree so a seventh cannot arrive (design §LVIII.2 recorded in `docs/agents/blueprints.md`).

## Block T — End-user documentation, round two (the curator's half)

- **SH625** — The console now has an end-user page: the browser and its 50-post paging against a folder count that is not it, the post form generated from the post type, copy and move with free names and both ends authorized and a picker that greys out what the server would refuse, what each Select choice actually selects and the 1000-item cap, and the trash as a reversible delete whose restore is scoped to one deletion and whose purge is the only permanent act. COVERAGE Block O goes from red to green.
- **SH623** — The administration guide is rewritten against the React console: the three sidebar groups, the dashboard, users, groups and roles, the two permission layers with the content ACL's default-allow spelled out, API tokens with all four scopes and the may-publish switch, tenants, the two provider screens with the one vendor each actually ships, email, webhooks, activity and agent review. Four sections describing surfaces that do not exist are gone - the search-provider screen, spreadsheet export, Git version control and workflows-as-approval-steps - and the Media Library, which is one screen with the static-file manager rather than two, is documented where a curator meets it, on the content console page under Content. COVERAGE Block E goes from red to green.
- **SH624** — The five lifecycle surfaces have a page of their own: preview links and the two destinations they resolve to, why they expire in fifteen minutes and never more than an hour, the draft-versus-published field diff with its three statuses and the two-click restore, scheduled publish and unpublish against a sweep that fires within a minute, and pointers to the audit trail and the trash where each is already written. Writing it surfaced that the console's post edit screen has no Publish button at all - the only console publish paths are the Universal Editor and approving an agent run - so the page says where publishing actually happens rather than describing a button that is not there. COVERAGE Block C goes from red to green.
- **SH626** — Outbound webhooks are documented from the side that sends them: the subscription form with its site and event scoping and the secret that is auto-generated and write-only on the wire, the exact five-field payload with which fields can be absent, and HMAC-SHA256 verification over the raw bytes with a constant-time compare and a working Next.js receiver. The delivery guarantees are written as answers rather than left unsaid - after commit, off the request thread, three attempts with linear back-off, no dead-letter queue, no ordering, not exactly-once, so a consumer must be idempotent - and the page names the commit-ordered agent changes feed as the alternative for callers who need what a webhook cannot promise. COVERAGE SH12 goes from red to green.
- **SH627** — Content i18n has a page: every post carries a locale that defaults to en and is never blank, a translation is a linked sibling post rather than a field, and because an address carries no locale two translations cannot share a friendly URL - the one decision that is expensive after the content is written, so the page leads with it. It also answers what the CDA returns for a locale with no translation, which is nothing rather than a fallback, and what availableLocales is for; the translations helper and post.locale cover the switcher and hreflang. The URL half is pointed at from website-development's public-delivery grammar and the modelling half from content-modeling, which is where each reader meets the segment first. COVERAGE SH53 goes from red to green.
- **SH628** — The instrument landed before the correction, because a version in prose is a claim nothing derives: cli/conformance/docs-stack.conformance.mjs reads Java, Spring Boot, Node and pnpm out of this repo's own pom.xml and package.json and fails on any page - docs-shio or the root README - that states a different one, and refuses a retired dependency presented as part of the stack while leaving architecture-overview's correct "Elasticsearch is not a dependency" sentence alone. It failed on exactly three real defects, and the developer guide is then rewritten: the six agent-drivable surfaces it never named, the real stack with search as optional Turing indexing, the mvnw and pnpm commands including why clean is not optional and why the ITs skip without Docker, and the ten design laws a contribution is judged by. Writing the docs also exposed a defect in SH499's own reader - it flattened nested @ConfigurationProperties groups, so it invented shio.cda.ttl-seconds and could not see shio.cda.preview.ttl-seconds, calling a correct page wrong - fixed with both directions asserted. COVERAGE's last warn row goes green.
- **SH629** — The image epic's operator half is documented as operations, in a section under Search & Caching that opens by saying the defaults already protect against the things it then explains. The result cache is written key-first, because the key is the invalidation: it hashes tenant, filename, lastModified, length and the four parameters and doubles as the ETag, so replacing an image lands every transform of it on a fresh key and there is nothing to purge - and the consequence an operator has to plan for is the orphaned entries, not a stale image. The three ceilings are given with the response each produces, including the deliberate asymmetry that an oversized request is a 400 and an oversized source serves the original rather than failing, and signed transform URLs are written with what the signature binds, that plain downloads are unaffected, and that it fails closed on a blank secret. COVERAGE's SH25 row goes from partial to green.

## Block V — The vocabulary proved live (integration tests against a running instance)

- **SH707** — The live tier calls 2 of 12 tools, 4 of 13 ops and 7 of 31 verbs - counted at the call site, held as a named list, and the section's own thirteen and thirty-three were both wrong.
- **SH708** — One suite drives all eight read tools over the wire against a site it seeds, taking live tool coverage from 2 of 12 to 8 of 12 - and the ledger's reader had to widen to see them.
- **SH709** — Every write scenario is call-then-look against the published projection, so dry-run, draft-default and a refused plan are proved by what is absent - live tool coverage is 12 of 12.
- **SH710** — Seven wrong-call shapes and an unknown tool name are refused over the wire carrying one of P6's instruments, with the store unchanged - and the sweep found SH717.

FileAlreadyExistsException and AtomicMoveNotSupportedException print identically through getMessage and are different diagnoses. ShIoCauseLintTest holds every catch (IOException) block in the tree to it and found two sites the hand grep missed, one of them feeding the agent's own diagnostics window. Its first draft matched whole files, reported nine findings of which six were false, and carried a comment arguing that was acceptable; it brace-matches the block now, because a lint wrong two thirds of the time is one somebody relaxes. SH719 was the one real defect and the ledger named it: the loser gets a duplicate-url 409, and measured live no MCP refusal carried its slug at all — only title, detail, fix and at — so a plugin user, whose only surface is MCP, could tell one refusal from another only by matching English. renderProblem now emits the bare slug as Type, which the wire golden could never have caught since it redacts the text. It PRINTS and does not fail, which §XXIV.5 asked for by name: a gate going red on every ship until a second repository is edited would turn one commit into two on pain of a red suite, and the silent failure is already prevented. A second copy of a fact is what SH673 says drifts, so docs-coverage.conformance.mjs asserts the mirror still equals what the real matrix names — checked against the authority, never trusted beside it.

The old shape set the window to 1ns and spent twice, on the argument that an already-elapsed window needs no sleep — but Instant.now() returns the same instant twice whenever the clock's granularity is coarser than the gap, so the reset was observed only when a tick landed between two adjacent reads. It also asserts the refusal BEFORE advancing, without which the test would pass against a guard that never charged anything. Nudging the duration was rejected: a longer window makes the failure rarer without making it impossible, which turns a diagnosable flake into an undiagnosable one. No lint, and the survey is why — the tree holds exactly one sub-millisecond Duration standing in for elapsed time, this one, so an instrument over a population about to be zero would be a guess at a future mistake rather than a finder of a present one.

SH596's lesson one level down — a classification can only be as honest as its categories allow, and this one had no way to ASK. Three of the eight exist specifically for the reader with no other route (shio://ops the write vocabulary, shio://diagnostics the failure report, shio://usage the spend), each argued into being in prose without once being read over the wire. mcpResources reads the URIs from the beans, mcp.readResource is the one greppable call shape, and a template is held by the prefix ShMcpResource#matches keys on. The vacuity guard matters more here than for the other three, because a population opening at zero looks identical whether the reader works or has stopped matching.

ShTenantContext.currentOrDefault is now the one place that decides, used by the filter and by the usage service, and getTenantId keeps answering null when unset because a reader must tell nobody from the default. metering.conformance.mjs reads the document, sends calls and requires the number to move — and is also the first live read of any MCP resource, taking SH760's population from zero of eight to one. SH751's shape one subsystem over: complete everywhere except the line that connects it, with every surface reporting success.
- **SH762** — The helper was discarding the race it found. It looped until it saw a DUPLICATE — the defect SH719 was demonstrating before SH719 made it unreachable — so the exit condition could never fire, the loop ran all five attempts every time, and the caller asserted a refusal against whatever the last attempt happened to be. Measured after the fix: contention on attempt 1, three runs of three. Racing was never the rare part; stopping when it happened was the missing part, and the obvious reading of a slow machine was wrong. The condition is now the one the caller needs, one of the pair refused, and the helper says so in its name. Two consequences kept: SH719's own guarantee is asserted on every attempt rather than only the returned one, which was throwing away four observations a run, and an uncontended run reports instead of failing — whether two requests overlap is a fact about the machine, and a suite that calls a slow box a broken product is one somebody switches off.

## Block AS — What Turing's index never receives (typed fields, a retry, a binary's text)

- **SH912** — A failed push is retried shio.turing.max-attempts times (3) with a doubling shio.turing.retry-backoff (1s), so a Turing restart no longer leaves a published page unfindable. The wait happens on the single index worker rather than by re-queueing, which keeps publish-then-unpublish ordering by construction, and the incident is recorded once at exhaustion — so a succeeded retry leaves nothing stale in the diagnostics window and an exhausted one leaves one incident rather than three. Pending retries do not survive a restart, deliberately: persisting them would add durability to the one subsystem that makes none, and reconciling a drained queue against changed posts is a reindex, which is SH413.
- **SH913** — A published attachment's text now reaches the index, read by Turing's own OCR API rather than by a parser here: ShTuringTextExtractor posts the bytes to /api/ocr/file through TurOcr, already in the SDK Shio indexes with, so a scanned PDF a local Tika parse would read as blank comes back with text. enrich() is the one call the AFTER_COMMIT listener and SH413's reindex share. The path is resolved on the committing thread because ShFileStorageService reads the tenant; the OCR runs on a worker of its own under a Shio-owned timeout, because TurOcr hardcodes five minutes and the single index worker keeps publish ordering. Every failure — too large, missing, refused, timed out — still indexes the metadata and reports why.
- **SH914** — A post-type field declares the Turing field it indexes into — indexed/turingField/turingType on ShPostTypeAttr, so a number or boolean leaves in a field of its own with the type Turing needs, and ShTuringDocumentMapper.specs sends a TurSNJobAttributeSpec with the job rather than the schema being configured by hand. The declaration lives on the attribute rather than in a list naming fields by string, which makes 'names a field the post-type lacks' unrepresentable instead of validated; what remains is refused at save by ShTuringFieldDeclaration — no type, an unknown type, two fields claiming one Turing name, a collision with a standard field, and a type set with indexed unset. A value that cannot be its declared type is omitted, never coerced to 0, so absent-is-not-empty still holds. Nothing changes for a post-type that declares nothing: no spec, same wire shape, and the CLI omits all three keys so no post-type file churns. Verified on H2, MariaDB and PostgreSQL with the ITs actually running.

## Block AT — What the Turing round left in the build and in a guard

- **SH916** — The six org.apache.tika declarations are gone, taking 23 compile-scope artifacts off the classpath — tika's six, pdfbox's seven and the four BouncyCastle jars pdfbox pulls for encrypted PDFs, which dependency:tree confirmed came from tika-parser-pdf-module and nothing else. Nothing in src/main ever imported one; they anticipated the local parse SH913 did not take. ShDeclaredDependencyUseLintTest now fails the next such declaration on the day it is added, and it is opt-in per group rather than a whole-POM sweep, because three shapes here are load-bearing with no import at all — an ImageIO SPI, a JDBC driver named in a URL string, and a Spring starter. jai-imageio is one of those and stays: it is a direct declaration rather than a Tika transitive, and a JPEG2000 upload cannot be read without its SPI readers.
- **SH917** — ShSilentCatchInventoryTest counts decisions, not catch blocks: a method whose comment carries `one-decision:` contributes one entry however many catches implement it, and the marker must name who records instead. It prints both figures every run — 103 silent catches in 101 decisions — and the turing column reads 7 rather than 9 with nothing removed, because ShTuringTextExtractor.ask's timeout, interrupt and SDK-throw are three ways for one question to come back unanswered. Both failure directions are asserted: a marker that folds nothing leaves the figure counting blocks with every number still adding up, and a signature walk that overshoots its method would collapse a whole file into one entry while the declared table gets adjusted down to meet it.
- **SH939** — The uncalled method is gone, the declaration is the pin it always was, and `ShDuplicateClasspathClassLintTest` fails on a class two jars supply instead of Spring Boot advising it every boot.

## Block AZ — What the content said before

- **SH985** — GET /api/v2/post-unified/{id} answers with an ETag and PUT, PATCH, publish and DELETE honour If-Match, refusing a stale write with the same stale-expectation problem the agent's expect throws — one digest, ShAgentPostDigest, so both writers ask one question about one row. The console holds the tag from its load, sends it on every write and answers a 409 by re-reading and opening a field-by-field comparison that defaults to what is stored. ShVersionGuardLintTest landed first and classifies all 22 content writes as guarded or unguarded-with-a-reason; its first draft read parameter lists with a regex and saw one write in ShStaticFileAPI where there are three, so it counts parentheses instead (design §LXV.1 recorded in `docs/agents/content-api.md`).
- **SH986** — sh_post_revision holds what a page was after the row that held it is gone: a post is (id, state) with exactly two states, so publishing deleted the live row and the bytes a visitor had been reading were not archived but destroyed. A separate table rather than a third state, since a third state is something every state-filtering query, the indexer, the CDA and the quota would each have to learn to exclude. The capture runs inside the publishing transaction on the row that just became visible, so a revision exists for every state a visitor ever saw; a draft save is captured behind shio.versions.capture-on-save, off by default, and retention is shio.versions.keep, fifty per post, pruned in the same write. A restore lands on the draft and is itself captured as a ROLLBACK. Validated with -DskipITs=false and Docker up: the PostgreSQL and MariaDB schema ITs ran rather than skipped (design §LXV.2 recorded in `docs/agents/database.md`).
- **SH987** — Revisions are readable from the surfaces an agent already has: include=revisions attaches the list to a read (numbers, dates, actors and changed field names, never bodies), state=rev:n reads one in place of a row, post.rollback joins the op vocabulary with address, revision and expect, REST carries a listing, one revision and a restore, and the CLI gains shio versions and shio rollback plus shio diff --against revision, which reuses the comparison --against published already has. A rollback restores into the draft, publishes nothing and writes a new revision rather than deleting one, so it is not destructive; a missing revision is refused before the address is resolved, through the shared missing-op-field shape. The op vocabulary's ceiling moved 770 to 800 with SH244's ritual — trim first (819 to 795), the decomposition saying the growth is one more op rather than fatter prose, and the surface choice re-run at the same 28% (design §LXV.3 recorded in `docs/agents/agent-surface.md`).
- **SH989** — Updates, publishes and restores record the names of the fields they changed, so an approved run stays describable on REST include=fields, shio_changes, shio changes --fields and the console (design §LXV.5 recorded in `docs/agents/agent-surface.md`).
- **SH1080** — GET /api/v2/events takes include=fields, so a followed stream names the fields each write changed and shio changes --follow --fields prints them instead of refusing (design §LXV.6 recorded in `docs/agents/agent-surface.md`).
- **SH988** — A created page's diff now opens with its render digest (words, headings, links, images and the outline) and a preview link, in the dialog and inline in the review queue, and each changed field restores alone by patching its older value into the draft behind a second press. shio diff keeps composing over the agent read surface, and diff/agreement.json holds it and the server to one answer; its first run caught the CLI reading an object whose keys only moved as a change, which it now compares canonically. A browser probe restored one field and left the other standing (design §LXV.4 superseded: shio diff calling the endpoint; a shared fixture holds both to one answer, since SH619 keeps the CLI a composition over the read surface).

## Block BC — The authoring surface, field by field

- **SH1009** — ShRequiredFields is the one evaluator of "is this page complete", and a publish is refused when it is not: the write service every publish passes through (the console's press, REST's, the batch's post.publish, the scheduler's sweep), plus the create that goes straight to PUBLISHED, which is the one publish that does not. A draft is never refused — drafts are where work happens, and refusing a half-written one would be worse than the defect — so the line is the publish, and the refusal is a teaching 400 whose at is data.field, which SH955's console reader already maps onto the input. The plans report it instead of refusing, in SH997's shape, so a plan of ten ops still reports ten: the console's publish preview and the batch's dry run both say which fields would stop it. Verify's own required-field-empty rule now calls the same evaluator, because two definitions of empty would mean a page verify calls complete and a publish refuses. Two defects the suites found in the first version: a post-type's attribute set is flat, so an unfiltered walk asked the document for a Relator child's field and every first-party section post refused to publish; and refusing regardless of SH998's waiver put a second lock on the one door that task built, so a recorded waiver — refused to an agent, written to the audit row and the revision — publishes.
- **SH1010** — The two rules that are not about one value, and the console's half. unique reads other posts, so it lives in ShFieldUniqueness with a repository rather than in the pure evaluator: the scope is the post-type, the comparison is trimmed and case-folded because ACME-1 and acme-1 being two posts is the failure it prevents, a page is excluded from its own comparison by id, and it costs one query per publish of a post whose type declares one — none at all for every other publish. It runs last in the gate, so a page already refused for its own shape does not pay for a scan of its siblings. defaultValue is not a check: it fills a missing field on create only, because a default re-applied on update would overwrite a value somebody cleared, and the document comes back unchanged when nothing was filled so a post that needs no default keeps its digest. In the console the post-type editor gains a constraints section under each field's flags, deleting a cleared key rather than writing null and dropping a block with nothing left in it, so no post-type reads as drift on the next pull; and the post form shows the rules as one sentence under the input, with the patternMessage and never the expression, which is the point of the vocabulary reaching the form at all — a rule stops being a discovery on save.
- **SH1011** — The editor stops losing work. Autosave writes the draft three seconds after the typing stops, debounced on the changed fields' value rather than their key list, which would fire after the first keystroke and call that the same thing. It sends only the changed keys, because the merge verb's rule that an unnamed field keeps its value is worth something only if the caller names as little as it can; it writes the draft alone, autosaving being a write nobody asked for; and the first refusal ends it, since retrying a conditional write refused for concurrency is the overwrite the guard exists to prevent, and doing it silently on a timer is that overwrite with nobody watching. The save bar says stopped out loud. Behind it a recovery buffer in IndexedDB covers what autosave cannot — the seconds before the next write and every case where the write cannot happen at all — offered and never restored, since a buffer that restores itself makes the page a second writer with no name on it. The CLI half the design also asked for was written and withdrawn: all three routes to a partial stateless write are blocked in a different place, and choosing between them is a security decision, so SH1091 holds it with each costed.
- **SH1012** — The one repeatable field writes again. RelatorWidget is an array editor — add, remove with undo, duplicate, collapse under a headline taken from the child marked isTitle, and reorder by drag or arrow keys, since drag alone is a feature some curators do not have. The half that made this more than wiring a callback: the round-trip wrote _id, _ordinal and _title/_summary back into the stored row, and a row of an SH95 collection is a plain map of its declared child fields, which is what lets the merge verb address features.1.body. Those four were undeclared keys waiting to be written into content, harmless only because the widget could not save, so wiring onChange without removing them is how the fix becomes the defect. Identity is now minted on read, held for React and dnd-kit, and stripped on write; position is the ordinal with no second copy to disagree. An emptied repeatable answers with an empty array rather than falling through to null, which had made removing the last row indistinguishable from a field never filled in. The instrument is the deliverable: a scan reads the widget table and fails any row it calls editable whose widget never calls onChange, anchored to that one table after a first version matched thirty-two names across four and passed by skipping nineteen.
- **SH1013** — The editor asks the instance what it already knows about the page being edited. An Insights panel reads the lint and the structural digest, addressed by id and scoped to the draft, and groups them as Blockers, Suggestions and Page shape — the third deliberately not a judgement, since folding a word count in with the findings would make it look like something to fix. A finding carrying a field offers a button that scrolls to the input and focuses it, through an anchor id both sides import rather than spell twice. It reads on demand and on the curator's own save, never on autosave's: both calls render the page server-side, and doing that every three seconds of typing is the cost P3 refuses one layer out from tokens. Two backend changes the design asked for turned out already shipped, checked against a running instance rather than read: verify has taken state since SH990 and a finding already carries its field. The third could not come from the linter at all — markup rules scan published rows only, deliberately, so the missing-alt count comes from the digest, whose scope already matches the question, and SH1092 is filed for the silence that leaves in a draft lint an agent runs over a whole site.
- **SH1014** — Unsaved edits can be seen before they are saved, on both tiers. shio_digest takes a data override, turning a dry run into an answer about how the page will look — a parameter and not a thirteenth tool, since the answer's shape is a digest either way and only the document it is taken of changes, while the authority does, so that path is gated by write. It was paid for rather than added: tools/list had seven tokens against its ceiling, the sentence saying why a digest is useful went, and the parameter cost three net. In the console a live preview posts the form's current values and puts the markup in an iframe by srcDoc, there being no URL that serves a page which exists nowhere. It runs scripts, because a page whose scripts do not run is not what a visitor gets, and deliberately withholds same-origin, so the frame is a unique origin that cannot read the session of the console showing it. Re-rendering as you type is a switch that starts off, each render composing a whole page on the server, so it refreshes on demand and on every save instead. SH1094 holds the split view, which changes the editor's shape rather than adding to it, and SH1095 the files tier's own verb.
- **SH1015** — A blocks body is a Markdown file that reads back as itself. A Blocks field is the body ahead of an HTML Editor, because it is the document, and it is projected rather than stringified — the value is an array, and stringifying one writes [object Object] into somebody's content file. The identities ride beside the body as an ordered blockKeys list, Markdown having nowhere to put a key: a comment per block litters the file P4 exists to make pleasant, and deriving a key from content changes identity whenever a paragraph is edited, which is the opposite of what a key is for. That is exact for an unedited file, which is the property a pull depends on, and its cost is named rather than hidden — insert a paragraph by hand and the keys after it shift, re-identifying those blocks while losing and reordering nothing. The parse keys off the list and never off the post-type, since reading a file back has not depended on the model since SH86. Blocks are canonicalized on the way in on both write paths, P5 being worth something only where content enters. The rule is implemented twice and made safe rather than argued about: both sides read one fixture corpus, the Java expectations are written by hand, and the parity test asserts that corpus covers every registered type.
- **SH1016** — Blocks reach a front end as blocks. The CDA's attrs already carried the array, checked against a running instance rather than read, so what was missing was rendered — field name to HTML, beside attrs and never instead of it, absent for a post with no block field so nothing written before the widget changes shape. It is rendered per request rather than stored at write, which departs from the design because storing derived HTML has no right home: a sibling key in data is an undeclared field the next write refuses, and a column is a schema change for a pure function of a value already there. The cost is measured and printed rather than assumed — blocks plus HTML is 2.55 times the HTML alone, bounded at three, which is the risk that actually existed since the body goes out twice. The HTML escapes the author's characters and emits its own tags, per run between mark boundaries: escaping first moves every offset the marks are expressed in and escaping last cannot tell an inserted tag from a typed angle bracket, which a test caught. GraphQL types a blocks field as a union over the eight kinds, declared whatever content exists, since a schema that changes shape with what happens to be stored is not a contract. The client gains a discriminated union and a reader that answers null for a field that is not blocks.
- 🗑 **SH1096** — abandoned: Filed on a premise I got wrong: shio-react-sdk exists and is a workspace package, and my directory listing truncated before it — so the helper it asked for was built as part of SH1016 instead, as ShioBlocks.
- **SH1017** — A block body has an editor. It is ordinary form controls rather than a contentEditable, because SH1015 made inline emphasis a range over the block's own text and a range is exactly what a textarea already reports — so a mark is applied by reading two numbers instead of asking the browser to mutate a DOM and then parsing what it did. That also makes every gesture keyboard-reachable without arranging for it. The cost is named rather than hidden: emphasis is not bold while typing, it is a removable chip carrying the text it covers, and the live preview renders the real thing. A trap was fixed on the way — the form routed by the value's shape, and a blocks document and a relator's rows are both arrays of objects, so a body would have been handed to the relator editor. Every block is a labelled region, and inserts, removals and moves speak through a polite live region, since a move has no visual anchor for a screen reader and the keyboard path is the one such a reader takes. Paste is treated as a document: only the shapes the model names survive, a script element yields no block, and text is taken as text so a paste can never introduce a tag. The console vocabulary mirrors the server's, so the editor cannot compose a document the instance would refuse.
- **SH1018** — A model change can be applied to the content it governs. Three mappings and no fourth — rename moves a value to the key the model now declares, drop removes one it no longer has, default fills a field added as required — because those are exactly the three shapes the check reports, so the migration answers the measurement rather than being a general-purpose rewriter. A rename onto an occupied key refuses the whole run and names the rows, both values being somebody's content and the two rules that would resolve it each silent data loss half the time. A default only fills what is empty. Nothing is written until everything is checked, since a run that failed part way leaves a type half in one shape and half in another. It plans unless told otherwise, so the flag a caller forgets leaves the content alone, and every row the plan names is checked against the content ACL before anything is written. It is not on the batch surface: the design put it there and three lints took it apart, the last of which measures the ops vocabulary at its ceiling and says growing past it is a reason to re-open the surface choice rather than raise the number. So it sits beside the check, which is where a model operation belonged — what batch would have given free is a dry run, and that is a query parameter.
- **SH1019** — A text-like field now offers Ask the agent while a run is recent: a short prompt prefilled from its label goes out as a request note anchored to the post and that field, shio://requests lists it with field=, and the agent replies with the value as the note's body. The dock's report then offers Apply to the field, which navigates to the post and writes the value into the form as an unsaved edit once the post has loaded, so dirty state, validation and save treat it as typed and nothing reaches the server. ShNoteRelayTest holds the field on the resource; console tests hold the ask, the report and the apply (design §LXVIII.11 superseded: a suggestion field on the reply note; for a field request the reply body is the value, so no schema change).
- **SH1090** — The console runs on a data router, so useUnsavedGuard now also blocks an in-app route change away from unsaved work in the post editor and the Universal Editor, asking once and never on a URL-only change (design §LXVIII.12 recorded in `docs/agents/console-ui.md`).
- **SH1092** — A state=draft verify of routes now names the eight rules that read published rows only and never ran on the drafts, so a clean draft report no longer reads as a verdict on links, images and markup (design §LXVIII.14 recorded in `docs/agents/agent-surface.md`).
- **SH1093** — A refused package rename now completes as a copy, and the keep-alive exit test asserts the disarm from the child's own trace apart from a looser clock, so each flake either passes or says which half broke (design §LXVIII.15 recorded in `docs/agents/troubleshooting.md`).
- **SH1095** — shio preview <file> renders a content file's fields and sidecars at its own page through the proposed render, prints the outline and writes the markup, storing nothing.
- **SH1143** — `shio preview` reads an unpushed image's bytes and sends them as a `data:` URI, and `ShRenderHelpers` treats a `data:image/` field value as the URL it already is rather than as a File post id — so a page whose image is only in the tree renders the image instead of nothing, which is what an author was previously shown. Bytes rather than a staged upload because a write needs sweeping and P7 says a preview stores nothing; only what the instance lacks, so an uploaded asset still goes as its id and renders the page a push will produce; the post-type def decides which fields, never the shape of a value; and a ceiling on both sides, past which the value falls through to the id lookup and answers as an unknown id does (design §LXVIII.20 recorded in `docs/agents/content-files.md`).
- **SH1132** — `POST /api/v2/post-unified/{id}/move` gives the console its first writer of a friendly URL, composed onto the agent's `post.move` through `ShAgentBatchService` rather than defined a second time, with SH1064's redirect offered after it. `dryRun` defaults to true and `PostRenameDialog`'s confirm button does not exist until a plan does, because both state rows move together — so a rename of a published page changes the live URL at once, and the plan says that, which address stops answering and how many pages link to it. §LXVIII.19's open question is answered by the writer's own note: moving the draft alone would make a post's identity depend on who was asking. Three guards caught the first drafts — a write may not use a bare `id:`, the destination is `to` as an address, and SH985 wanted the real run conditional, which it now is (design §LXVIII.19 recorded in `docs/agents/console-ui.md`).
- **SH1094** — The post editor and the translation workspace share the design system's split: both panes side by side at a width the curator sets and the console keeps, one pane and a switch on a phone (design §LXVIII.16 recorded in `docs/agents/console-ui.md`).
  checked **The editor and the workspace share a design-system split** Once the package ships a two-pane page shape, the post editor shows form and preview side by side with a ratio kept per curator, the translation workspace moves onto it, and a phone-width page stacks with a toggle rather than dropping a pane.
- **SH1180** — The console's load ceilings carry SH1094's measured cost, react-resizable-panels at 34855 bytes raw in the shared chunk, with room left for the next change (design §LXVIII.21 recorded in `shio-react/console-size-budget.json`).
- **SH1091** — shio post set changes some fields of a post through the CDA's merge, which now answers an ETag and refuses a stale If-Match with 409, using a WRITE token as the maintainer chose (design §LXVIII.13 recorded in `docs/agents/content-api.md`).

## Block BD — Finding, selecting and acting on content

- **SH1020** — The content browser can be operated without a mouse. Its rows carried no role, tabindex, selected state or key handler, and its eight row actions lived inside a block hidden until a pointer hovered — so a keyboard user could open a post and do nothing else to it, and a screen reader was never told the actions existed. It is a listbox now, multi-selectable because the checkbox column always was, each row an option carrying its selected state, with a roving tabindex so Tab moves past the list rather than through a hundred rows: a list that claims the role and does not move on arrows is worse than one claiming nothing. Arrows and Home/End move the ring, Space toggles, Shift with an arrow or a click extends from the anchor — where the selection last started, the rule every file manager uses, and what makes a bulk verb a gesture instead of a hundred clicks — Enter opens, Delete goes through the confirm flow, and slash focuses search, opening the field as well since it sits behind a toggle, and ignoring the key while a field has focus so a slash typed into a name does not jump the cursor out. The actions became data handed to the design system's menu, labelled per row rather than eight identical Actions buttons.
- **SH1021** — A curator can publish, unpublish or delete a selection in one call, through the writer the agent's batch runs through. The MCP publish tool has taken an array and promised atomicity since it shipped while the console offered copy, move and delete — and the obvious fix, a publish loop in a console service, is what lets two surfaces drift about what publishing means, so this builds ops and delegates instead. The test asserts the delegation rather than the behaviour, since a forked loop that happened to publish correctly would pass a behavioural one. The answer is the change set the agent already returned, an outcome and a problem per item: a selection where one post is refused publishes the rest and names which did not, with the fix its refusal carried, where one outcome for the batch would either hide the refusal or discard what worked. Dry run defaults to true, a bulk verb being the one shape where a mistake is multiplied by the selection, and the real run carries the token its plan returned. Permission is asked for the whole selection before anything is built, so a curator who may not publish gets one refusal rather than a plan they could not carry out.
- **SH1022** — One vocabulary filters every listing — site, folder, subtree, type, state, locale, dates, author, modifier — as a database predicate on all four surfaces (design §LXIX.3 recorded in `docs/agents/agent-surface.md`).
- **SH1023** — Every console list holds its search, sort, filters and view in its URL, in the server's own words, so an address reproduces the view and a link is a request (design §LXIX.4 recorded in `docs/agents/console-ui.md`).
- **SH1025** — The browser asks for a page of folders, and the select-all walk, the move dialog's blocked set and the folder sort were all paid for in the same change (design §LXIX.6 recorded in `docs/agents/console-ui.md`).
- **SH1027** — Console search composes the agent's find — drafts included, the folder scope recursive, each row checked against the reader's ACL and what was hidden counted (design §LXIX.8 recorded in `docs/agents/content-api.md`).
- **SH1028** — The palette answers with content and verbs compiled from the surface declaration, ranked by context, match and recency — and every write routes to the flow that asks (design §LXIX.9 recorded in `docs/agents/console-ui.md`).
- **SH1024** — Four lists — browser, search, trash, review — carry the bar with facet counts and saved views, and the agent option is the vocabulary word `agent` on every surface.
- **SH1026** — The list, grid and table each draw the rows their own way: an editable, virtualised data table, grid cards with thumbnails, and a list and grid windowed past 150 rows, all verified in a browser over 200 posts.
- **SH1097** — The shell binds its keys through useBentoShellShortcuts, the set the shortcuts sheet lists, so `?` opens the sheet and `/` is listed; a test refuses a second keydown keymap.
- **SH1142** — the toolbar's Select menu and the selection bar's Clear are absent in the table view rather than inert, so the table's own header checkbox and Escape are the one control for the one selection: both wrote `selectedItems` without `BentoDataTable` hearing it — it reports a selection through `onSelectionChange` and takes none in, where its column `layout` is controlled beside `onLayoutChange` — so picking Select all and then Delete deleted whatever the table last had ticked while the confirm dialog counted the page's set. `SH1142: no control outside the table writes the selection in the table view` walks the braces of each view guard and holds every JSX writer inside one, which is a rule rather than two spot-checks because the recurrence is a third control; SH1148 is the package's half and brings the two back everywhere (design §LXIX.11 recorded in `docs/agents/console-ui.md`).
- **SH1145** — the browser page is 592 lines rather than 1,593, and each concern is a module a reviewer can read whole: `use-browser-listing` owns every read, `use-browser-keyboard` the listbox, `use-bulk-verbs` and `use-browser-open` the verbs, with the toolbar, both dialogs, the row actions and the request constants beside them. The fourteen suites that match regexes against the page read the browser through `test/support/browser-source.mjs` — the page plus the directory, walked rather than listed — because a scan left on a file that no longer holds its subject keeps passing, which is SH1118's shape reached by relocation; the split also found the picker's read not cancelling, an unnamed icon that stopped being a page's tolerated debt when it became a shared component's, and SH1142's own lint blind to five of six controls until its count floor said so (design §LXIX.12 recorded in `docs/agents/console-ui.md`).
- **SH1148** — The content browser's table is controlled by the page's selection, so Select everything and Invert are back in the table view and tick exactly the rows the table shows (design §LXIX.13 recorded in `docs/agents/console-ui.md`).
- **SH1178** — The bulk plan marks each item added, removed, changed or unchanged with the design system's mark, names a change in the curator's language, and keeps a refusal's badge (design §LXIX.14 recorded in `docs/agents/console-ui.md`).
- **SH1184** — The content browser names a blank site once (sh8844001/menu), and "search this folder" builds a `folder:` address without the root folder, which now resolves (design §LXXV.1 recorded in `docs/agents/console-ui.md`).
- **SH1185** — A facet option the listing has none of leaves the menu unless it is the chosen one, and a choice facet with nothing to offer leaves the bar, on all four lists.
- **SH1186** — The note rail's Comment/Request pick is a segmented radio group with arrow-key switching, so the submit is the only filled button on the row (recorded in `docs/agents/console-ui.md`) (design §XCI.1 recorded in `docs/agents/console-ui.md`).
- **SH1187** — "Search in this folder" opens /bento/content/search scoped to the folder: the route is a required argument and the browser passes ROUTES.SEARCH (design §LXXV.1 recorded in `docs/agents/console-ui.md`).
- **SH1189** — Every hero back link now names its real parent: rail pages go home, editors go to their list, a folder to its parent listing, translation and languages to their post or site (design §LXXV.2 recorded in `shio-react/test/hero-back-links.test.mjs`).
- **SH1188** — Back from a folder search returns to the folder that opened it: the toolbar passes its location as router state and the search page reads it once, falling back to the site list (design §LXXV.1 recorded in `docs/agents/console-ui.md`).

## Block BE — Media: what the bytes mean

- **SH1029** — The media listing parses each asset's data once instead of once per key — 2400 parses down to 400 for 400 assets, with the response byte-identical (design §LXX.1 superseded: taking the file size from the stamp instead of the disk, which SH398 had already argued against and SH399 had already decided the stamp is for validating the digest rather than for reporting the size) (design §LXX.1 recorded in `docs/agents/content-api.md`).
- **SH1030** — The media library is paged on every surface, with server-side facets, a stamped content type and predicates that narrow the read — 400 rows down to 111 on a filtered listing (design §LXX.2 superseded: virtualising the grid, which the paging removed the need for: the page is fifty cards and a virtualiser over fifty is a second unused dependency beside the react-table one this task found already declared and imported nowhere) (design §LXX.2 recorded in `docs/agents/content-api.md`).
- **SH1031** — An image asset with no alt text is a finding the content check can actually raise, the helper stops fabricating an empty attribute, and the library narrows to what needs describing (design §LXX.3 recorded in `docs/agents/agent-surface.md`).
- **SH1098** — shio_assets answers a listing that holds assets: SANITIZED is declared on the File type, and the lint that guards this now reads the service's data.put call sites instead of trusting a DATA_ naming convention, so a key written through any constant fails on its own commit (design §LXX.8 recorded in `docs/agents/agent-surface.md`).
- **SH1032** — an asset's alt, caption and tags are part of the tree: they project to shio/asset-meta/<site>/<chain>/<name>.json, merge per key against content-base.json so an agent describing an image and a curator captioning it never collide, and push sends them through the same file-service writer the console and asset.meta use (design §LXX.4 superseded: the op was to take a focal point beside alt, caption and tags, and the product has no such field anywhere — not on the File type, not in the SH40 transform pipeline, not in the Media Library dialog. That is a new capability rather than reach, and an op key carrying it would have been a published contract for a field nothing reads or renders.) (design §LXX.4 recorded in `docs/agents/content-files.md`).
- **SH1033** — Where-is-this-used is measured rather than argued: at 1,000 / 10,000 / 50,000 posts the scan examines 1,002 / 10,002 / 50,002 rows and runs twice per dialog, while a prototype reverse index answers the same question by examining 4 and costs a flat 3 statements per write at every size — two curves rather than two numbers, so SH1034 builds the index and §LXX.5's cached-count branch did not fire. The cross-database half found more than a cost: MariaDB agrees with H2, PostgreSQL can serve the predicate with a pg_trgm GIN index (measured and declined — one cheap engine of three is not a design), and on PostgreSQL the query returns nothing at all, because @Lob stores data as a large object (filed as SH1099) (design §LXX.5 recorded in `docs/agents/database.md`).
- **SH1034** — The four reads the index made affordable. The media listing stamps `usageCount` on the rows of a page in one indexed query — never per row, never over the library to draw ten of it — and `null` (nobody asked) stays distinct from `0` (nothing references this), which is the value a deletion acts on. On that: the media card shows a badge, spelling zero as "unused" rather than "used 0"; `verify` warns `asset-unused`, instance-wide by construction so a site-scoped run cannot offer a shared logo for deletion; `shio assets prune` sums the reclaimable bytes, deletes nothing, and refuses an instance that sends no counts rather than reading absent as zero and inviting a mass deletion; and `shio_assets --usage` batches a page's counts so an unused asset costs no further query. Writing the tests found a real defect in the part that shipped: `restoreFromTrash` is a native bulk UPDATE, so the rows it re-read still looked trashed and the restore silently left every asset unreferenced.
- **SH1035** — Replace reached the console, with the safety net that makes it worth offering. The dialog's control calls the endpoint SH210 shipped and only the CLI ever used, and shows what a curator needs to press it: how many pages change before the picker, and the superseded bytes as numbered versions with a Restore after. A replace now captures what it overwrites, and a revert captures on the way past — so going back is itself undoable, which the first draft was not. Those copies live outside `/file_source/**`, asserted rather than remembered: that path is mapped at the root of the asset tree, so the obvious home for a rendition would leave a superseded document downloadable to anyone who guessed the path. Bounded at three per asset, which is what licenses keeping them out of the tenant meter — SH110 charges a replace the difference, so counting them would make replacing a 900 MB video with a 1 MB one increase usage. The File widget no longer dead-ends either: an upload into a field with no configured folder holds the file, opens the browser in a folders-only mode, and remembers the answer per attribute for the session rather than writing a guess into the configuration.
- **SH1099** — Long-text fields bind as LONGVARCHAR, not @Lob, so PostgreSQL stores the document inline and search matches body text; a changeset inlines and unlinks old objects, and a lint bars @Lob.
- **SH1100** — ShReference and ShReferenceDraft are dropped with their entity and repository and left the tenant backfill; the exchange format never carried them, so nothing moved.

## Block BF — The visual editor becomes a composer

- **SH1036** — Edit mode survives a click, and the badge stops lying when it does not. Both rewriters now thread the request's `editor` and `state` onto every navigation and onto no asset — the SH515 asset split is what keeps `?editor=true` off a stylesheet, which is the `href` that looks like a link — with the link's own query winning and the fragment split off first. The console re-keys on what the bridge reports instead of on an iframe `src` that in-frame navigation cannot change: a different `url` on `sh:ready` clears the selection, the pending changes and the loaded labels, and a navigation with no new `sh:ready` before the iframe's `load` is a page with no bridge, which the badge now says. Two things the design asked for were deliberately not built, because each would have been a second mechanism for something that already works: a `navigated` message, since `sh:ready` is posted from attach on every load and already carries the page, and a `navigate` message, since reassigning `src` already drives the frame and re-keys correctly. What was added instead is `sh:navigating` — departure, which nothing covered — so the panel stops describing a page that is unloading rather than during the load. The postMessage suite has a destination assertion for the first time; asserting only that the click was prevented is how this survived a green suite.
- **SH1037** — Protocol v2 is announced and the console offers only what the page claims. `sh:ready` carries a version, a capability list, the post id, the post type and the URL, and the capabilities are derived from what is true of that page rather than hard-coded — `navigate` appears only when the server shipped the URL index, because without it the click interception is off and claiming it would stop the console offering its own. A bridge that sends no list at all is read as supporting everything, the same compatibility rule as a missing field kind: two producers implement this protocol, the published one implements less, and treating silence as "supports nothing" would remove editing that works. The switch the page cannot honour is disabled with the reason on hover rather than removed, because a control that vanishes reads as a console bug.
