The rich-text toolbar is restricted to bold, italic, link and remove-formatting — what SH956's allow-list keeps — since a toolbar with headings and colours would offer writes the write boundary then strips, so the curator sees the change, saves, and loses it. It appears for a rich field only, uses `mousedown` because a click moves focus off the selection, and its CSS is scoped under the editing flag so preview is byte-for-byte a visitor's page. And the panel draws each field through the console's own widget map, synthesising the declared field rather than reading the post a third time.
- **SH1038** — A curator moves, duplicates and removes a section on the page itself: `sh:section-op` applies the change optimistically in the frame while the console replaces the owning Page's `sections` array in one write, and a console-drawn overlay carries the controls over the section they act on. Duplicate places the same section twice and says so in the control's own title; a page whose sections live in another field gets the header with no buttons rather than one that would write the wrong thing. The spec's message tables are now checked against the bridge, so a verb both halves speak and the document does not fails the build (design §LXXI.3 recorded in `docs/agents/renderer.md`).
- **SH1039** — A curator adds a section from the page: the console reads the catalogue on the session, shows each accepted type by its own title and description rather than as a post-type name, and places one as two writes in the order that matters — create the section as a draft, then replace the Page's array, so a failure leaves a post nobody names rather than a page naming a post that does not exist. The reference is spelled the way the array already spells its entries, and the frame reloads because a new section's markup comes from the template and `/preview` is draft-preferred. `above`/`below` instead of a drag caret, and the rail appears with nothing selected too — a page composing no sections has nothing to click, and is the page most in need of being told what fits (design §LXXI.4 recorded in `docs/agents/renderer.md`).
- **SH1040** — A block that works is captured and reused: the capability the symptom asked for exists end to end, through the CLI and the tree. The console's own half is not here and is now SH1108, because it turned out to rest on a question this task had to answer first — the console cannot read a project file, so a Patterns tab needs the pattern to reach the instance, which is the marketplace's upload path rather than a second store.
- **SH1041** — An edit can be taken back, and a refresh stops lying about what is pending. Only the page could say what a field held before the typing — `sh:content-changed` fires after the change — so the bridge takes a baseline on focus and sends `was` on every message, and the console keeps the first, which is what makes an undo mean *before I started on this field*. `sh:field-set` now reaches a **text** field as well as an attribute one, because clearing an entry without writing the page back is a worse lie than having no revert; a refresh replays the pending edits into the reloaded frame instead of counting what is no longer on screen; Discard is confirmed, and both exits ask. No Ctrl+Z: a `contenteditable` already has the browser's undo, which reports itself like any other edit (design §LXXI.6 recorded in `docs/agents/renderer.md`).
- **SH1042** — A stakeholder can be sent an expiring link to a draft Shio renders itself. A new `SHARE` scope grants one role no rule outside the renderer accepts — `FORM`'s reasoning, because reusing `PREVIEW` would have handed the recipient that site's whole delivery API through a `Key` header — and the confinement runs both ways: only `SHARE` authenticates the preview, and `SHARE` authenticates nowhere else. The link is exchanged once at a public sibling of the mint for an `HttpOnly`, `SameSite=Lax`, `Path=/preview` cookie, so the credential leaves the URL before it can reach a `Referer` or a paste; the site is enforced at the renderer where the site is already resolved, the editor bridge is forced off whatever the query says, and the banner stays. `/preview/**` did not join the allow-list and `ShPreviewIsNotPublicTest` is unchanged: no cookie is still no preview (design §LXXI.7 recorded in `docs/agents/security.md`).
- **SH1101** — copyto answers with the posts it made, id and address included, and the visual editor's Duplicate copies the section and places the copy, so the two no longer share one heading.
- **SH1105** — A rail card drags onto a caret between sections, placed through the one index arithmetic the Above and Below buttons use.
- **SH1106** — shio verify warns section-not-accepted once per type when a page composes a section its layout's sh-accepts does not name, with the accepted list.
- **SH1108** — shio patterns push copies a pattern file to the instance, and the visual editor's rail places it through the document and apply the CLI uses (design §LXXI.11 superseded: the marketplace installer it would reuse downloads by catalogue id and takes no upload) (design §LXXI.11 recorded in `docs/agents/blueprints.md`).
- **SH1109** — A visual editor save reports in the dock which fields it wrote and whether the structure and appearance digests moved, flagging a text-only edit that moved the appearance.
- **SH1110** — A share link renders only the page it was minted for: a path prefix on the token, checked in the preview route, with the site's assets still served so the page renders whole.
- **SH1111** — Live share links are listed and revoked on the mint's authenticated route, by row id, and shio share prints a link, lists them and revokes one (design §LXXI.14 superseded: the listing's own route, GET /api/v2/preview-share, is permitAll for the anonymous exchange) (design §LXXI.14 recorded in `docs/agents/security.md`).

## Block BG — The console as an application: cost, resilience and access

- **SH1043** — The console's load is measured and bounded: **7,473,483 bytes raw / 2,200,187 gzip** before the first row of content, of which `vendor-graphiql` is 4.8 MB preloaded on every route for one page whose own chunk is 3 KB — the number SH1044 now has to argue against. The reader composes on the bundler's own analysis (the entry plus every `modulepreload` Vite emits for a statically imported chunk) rather than re-deriving the import graph, and refuses a build that declares none rather than measuring the entry alone and passing forever. Ceilings are keyed by each chunk's stem, so an edit does not make them stale, and a chunk that is no longer eager fails as loudly as one that grew. The comparison runs wherever a build exists and says so when there is none; a planted `dist` drives the whole gate on every run, so it has been shown to fail (design §LXXII.1 recorded in `docs/agents/build.md`).
- **SH1044** — The console's eager load falls from 7,473,483 raw / 2,200,187 gzip to **1,542,579 / 413,169** — 79% and 81% — and the cause turned out to be the opposite of the config's own claim. `manualChunks` existed to keep GraphiQL out of the eager bundle and was what put it there: a named vendor chunk becomes a static dependency of the entry under rolldown, so every route preloaded 4.8 MB for a page whose own chunk is 3 KB. The reordering this design proposed was tried first and moved 4 KB, which is how the real cause was found; deleting the function lets the bundler put Monaco and GraphiQL behind the lazy route, and making the Ace widget lazy keeps CodeMirror's 573 KB out of the entry, since the widget map is drawn by every screen showing a post's fields. The `@radix-ui` rule named a chunk that never existed and went with the rest (design §LXXII.2 recorded in `docs/agents/build.md`).
- **SH1045** — Eighteen of the console's sixty declared dependencies were reached by nothing, and they are gone: the shadcn layer under `components/ui` became a re-export of the design system, so twelve `@radix-ui/react-*` packages, `radix-ui`, `clsx`, `tailwind-merge`, `class-variance-authority`, `@tanstack/react-table` and `@tailwindcss/typography` are the previous implementation's declarations outliving it. What makes a walk safe to delete on is the three ways of being reachable that are **not** an import — a grep for the name would have taken `sonner` and `next-themes` (peers of the design system, imported nowhere here), `typescript` (reached as `tsc` by a script) and `tailwindcss` itself (reached from CSS by `@import`, which a JavaScript-only scan does not read). The peer pass runs to a fixed point over the *reachable* set, never over everything declared, or one dead entry keeps the next one alive and the list can never shrink; `@tailwindcss/typography` was deleted precisely because no `@plugin` line registered it, which means it was never loaded either. The exemption map is empty — everything unreachable was deleted rather than excused — and a stale exemption fails as loudly as a new unreachable package, for the reason SH1043's budget fails on a ceiling that outlives its chunk. That budget is also the record that this changed nothing that ships: **1506.4 KB raw / 403.5 KB gzip before and after** (design §LXXII.3 recorded in `docs/agents/build.md`).
- **SH1046** — The console has one query layer and a cache key is an address. `lib/query-keys.ts` turns SH79's grammar into the key — `postType:` is the catalogue, `postType:Page` is one type — with the scheme as its own segment, which is what makes invalidating `postType:` reach the catalogue *and* every type under it rather than needing a second list of what-else-to-drop. An unknown scheme throws where it is written: a key built from a typo would cache and never be invalidated, because every invalidation names a scheme, and that is a screen showing yesterday's content with no error anywhere. Seventeen catalogue reads went through it, and the content browser's was the one that mattered — it read every post type inside an effect keyed on the folder id, so walking a tree cost one whole catalogue per folder. `ShioServiceProvider` was the story in miniature and is gone: a service-injection context built for exactly this, wrapped around the whole route tree, with no call sites, because sharing a stateless axios wrapper saves nothing and what every page was re-doing was the request. `AdminListPage` takes an `address` and caches inside itself, which reached eight configuration lists rather than the two on the list. The quieter half is the error: `catch(() => setState([]))` made "the server did not answer" and "there is nothing here" one screen, and `useQuery` answers the three states apart by default. Three instruments, because only one of the claims is checkable in one place — the client's defaults driven in-process (two reads, one request), a sweep of `src/app` that fails a page going back to the old shape, and a browser probe counting the API requests of a second folder navigation. Cost, measured by SH1043's gate before and after and recorded in its budget: 32,894 bytes raw / 10,054 gzip, nothing else in the eager load moved (design §LXXII.4 recorded in `docs/agents/console-ui.md`).
- **SH1047** — The console can hang up on a read. `ShRead` in `lib/read-options.ts` is the one option every read takes, so sixty-two reads across twenty-seven service classes cannot each invent a spelling and the lint can ask one question; writes do not take it, because aborting a POST does not undo it and a cancelled write is one whose *answer* was thrown away. The other half is `isCancelled`, and without it this would have been a regression: an aborted request **rejects**, so every `catch(() => setItems([]))` would read a navigation as a failed load and empty the list the curator is walking into — the trash needed a rethrow past its own per-read fallback, or leaving mid-load emptied the page it was drawing. Five screens migrated, the ones the symptom names: the content browser, search, trash, the media library and the activity trail, each aborting on effect cleanup. They deliberately did not move onto SH1046's query layer — their state is a cursor or an accumulating page, so caching them is a behaviour change that belongs to `useInfiniteQuery`. Search gained most: its `let current = true` flag ignored the superseded answer where the signal stops the server being asked for it. The guard is a **declared list, not a ceiling** — forty screens fetch inside an effect, five pass a signal, thirty-five are named, and the list's job is that a thirty-sixth cannot arrive quietly. It strips comments first, which found a real file rather than a planted one: `bento.root.page.tsx` says "an ambient signal" in its own prose and a raw scan passed it for talking about the thing. And because source can say an `AbortController` is there while only a browser can say the superseded answer loses, `console-check.mjs` holds the first folder's listing open, navigates past it, releases it and reads the rows — with a route that stops matching reported as a skip rather than a pass (design §LXXII.5 recorded in `docs/agents/console-ui.md`).
- **SH1048** — An unchanged console read answers 304 with no body, and what a console read costs is now a number the build guards. `ShConsoleCacheFilter` is one `ShallowEtagHeaderFilter` over `/api/v2/*` — one class and not two, because the `Cache-Control` has to be stamped before the body is written to survive the 304 the same filter produces, and two registrations with two patterns is two chances to exclude the streaming endpoint from one of them. `no-cache` rather than `no-store`: it means revalidate, so the second read is a conditional request that comes back empty rather than a request nobody makes, and `private`, because a console read depends on the caller's rights and their tenant. Four exclusions, and the first two are correctness: the filter buffers the whole response to hash it, so `/api/v2/events` would become Server-Sent Events that never reach the browser and `…/export` would hold a zip on the heap for a validator nobody asks about twice; the CDA and the agent surface are excluded because they already have their own, and a *shallow* body hash landing over the agent's *semantic* one is the defect rather than the cost. Registered at `LOWEST_PRECEDENCE - 20`, which is two claims an assertion holds rather than a comment: after the security chain, so a 401, 403 or 429 never receives a validator — a validator on a refusal is a client that caches the refusal — and inside the cost header, which has to see a 304 as the zero-byte response it is. The measurement landed beside the fix rather than after it, and it is the half worth keeping: a 304 saves whatever the body costs and nothing here knew what a console body costs, so `console-response-budgets.properties` prices eight reads against a fixed fixture, with the headroom check that stops a ceiling refusing the next field instead of pricing it. The widget catalogue is the largest at 2,165 bytes and the only one a new widget legitimately grows (design §LXXII.6 recorded in `docs/agents/content-api.md`).
- **SH1049** — A failure stays in the screen it happened in, and the post editor's spinner has an end. `RouteBoundary` wraps the shell's outlet so one screen's throw leaves the rail, the header and the palette alive; it is keyed on the pathname, which is not decoration — a class boundary holds `hasError` until something resets it, so without the key a curator who navigated away from a broken screen would carry its error to every screen after, and the fix would look exactly like the defect. `PanelBoundary` is the smaller one. **Try again re-runs the reads**: resetting the boundary alone re-renders against the same cached, failed queries and throws again, so the button reads as broken — SH1046's `resetQueries` is what makes it mean anything, which is why this task came after that one. The post editor loads with `Promise.allSettled` on purpose (SH654 needs to know which rows exist), so a 500 left its value null and `if (!post)` rendered a spinner with no end — a slow server, a deleted post and a broken instance were one screen. It records the rejection and hands it to the package's three-state gate. Three instruments. A lint refuses the **absence** of a loading state — forty-two pages read from the server, thirty-eight model one, four are a declared list that shrinks by deletion — following a page that imports another *page* one hop, and only page to page, because the first draft credited a list for importing a header with a `loading` prop. The browser probe answers every `/api/v2/` GET with a 500 on three routes and reads what is on the screen. And the shape test now anchors on the script's last statement, which is worth more than either: `stripComments` treats a slash and two stars as a comment opener wherever it appears, so a Playwright wildcard silently truncated its view of the script and every assertion below began matching an empty string and passing for it — twice in an hour, once in the pattern and once in the comment explaining the pattern (design §LXXII.7 recorded in `docs/agents/console-ui.md`).
- **SH1050** — The rest of it. `include=status` puts the same numbers in the context pack, opt-in for `usage`'s reason rather than `releases`': the section changes constantly, so letting it into the default pack would put a number that moves on every publish inside the document SH116's conditional read exists to keep matching. That is also the honest answer to the design's own escape clause — *dropped if it regresses the cheapest read* — because a caller who does not ask pays nothing and `context.terse` did not move. The pack's site count is the **readable** one where the endpoint's is the instance total: a pack is always the caller's view, since a credential is a site allow-list and a console session is a person with an ACL. `SOON` moved onto the record so both readers share one window — two definitions of "soon" is a tile and a pack disagreeing about what is due, which is the kind of thing nobody notices and nobody can explain. Home gained the two tiles it lacked. **What the agent did** is a list and not a count, because the count is already on the review tile and what a curator needs before opening a diff is the *intent* — a session id says an agent was here, the sentence it declared says what it was trying to do — with each row linking into the review queue. Runs with nothing pending are drawn too: *the agent ran and you have dealt with it* is a different fact from *the agent has not run*, and showing only the first would make a quiet instance and a busy one look the same. **Incidents** are a window and the sentence says so, in both readers: the log is in-memory and starts empty at boot, so a bare count would read as a total, and `unpersisted` is reported beside it because if the database was the thing failing then the record of the failure is exactly what could not be written down (design §LXXII.8 recorded in `docs/agents/content-api.md`).
- **SH1052** — Every field of every post type has a name, says what it requires, and can be reached from a keyboard. The form drew a `<Label>` with no `htmlFor` over a widget whose props were `attr`, `onChange` and `postId` — nothing in that contract could carry an id — so clicking a label focused nothing and a screen reader met each field as an unlabelled edit box, on every post, because this is the component every post is edited through. `WidgetProps` gained `fieldId`, `describedBy`, `required`, `invalid` and `labelledBy`, because a widget cannot invent an id the label already used: the form mints them and hands them down. `fieldIds` is **deterministic**, and that is not a nicety — `useId()` differs between renders of different trees, so two renders of one post would differ in their markup and a render digest compares markup; the field name is already unique, so the scheme is one function of it in `lib/field-ids.ts`, where the panel that scrolls to a field already looked. Two shapes, and the second is the contract's other half: a widget with one control takes the id, and one that renders several — a checkbox group, a code editor with its own focusable surface, relator rows — has no element for `htmlFor` to point at, so it names itself by the label on a `role="group"`. The required marker is hidden and the word said beside it, since an asterisk is punctuation and is announced as nothing. The File widget's drop zone is a button: it was a `div` with an `onClick` over an input hidden with `display: none`, which removes an element from the accessibility tree *and* the focus order, so there was no keyboard path to attach a file at all. The finding this turned up rather than the one it was filed for: `blocks` and `relator` declared their own `Props` restating the contract, so widening it widened everything except the two most complex widgets in the console. The lint walks the map — every widget threads the id or names itself, every one with a control points at its description, no form control is hidden with `display: none` — and each rule is driven against a planted widget written the old way, because all of them passed on their first run, which is exactly when a check has not been shown to check anything (design §LXXII.10 recorded in `docs/agents/console-ui.md`).
- **SH1055** — checks=a11y reports heading order, language, link names, landmarks and form labels over rendered pages; the blueprint it caught no longer fails two (design §LXXII.13 recorded in `docs/agents/agent-surface.md`).
  checked **One page with one violation of each rule reports all five** ShHtmlAccessibilityTest drives a fixture carrying exactly one heading-skip, lang-missing, link-no-text, landmark-missing and form-label-missing, and asserts the set is all five — a subset means a rule that is declared and does not run. Each finding carries a detail naming the place and a fix.
  checked **The correct form of each of those same shapes is silent** The second fixture is the first one written properly, in the ways that most look like the defects: an icon link named by its image's alt, a control wrapped in its own label, role="main" instead of main, an anchor with no href, a fragment with no html element. It reports nothing.
  checked **The headline benchmark stays under its unchanged ceiling** buildMarketingSite went 4432 tokens against a 4000 ceiling once verify reported accessibility, because the marketing-site blueprint had no main and no h1. Repairing the layout brings it to 3972 under the same ceiling, which is the fix rather than a budget raised over our own template.
- **SH1075** — pnpm test now runs the console lint and fails on any unsuppressed error; three of the twenty were fixed, the seventeen left are declared by name against SH1136, and CI's lint step is green (design §LXXII.14 recorded in `docs/agents/console-ui.md`).
- **SH1077** — An open change stream reads each ACL input once per pass and tenant, so the fan-out fell from 7.05 to 2.11 statements per entry per stream, with the ceiling lowered to 3 (design §LXXII.15 recorded in `docs/agents/agent-surface.md`).
- **SH1078** — A console move answers with the published addresses it retired and created, read before and after the write, so a caller learns what visitors lost without a verify run (design §LXXII.16 superseded: a URL is site plus furl, not the folder chain, so only a cross-site move or a first furl changes one) (design §LXXII.16 recorded in `docs/agents/content-api.md`).
- **SH1079** — An import answers with the site, what arrived by kind and what it could not do (skipped posts, unresolved types, files it never brings), and the console and shio import show it (design §LXXII.17 recorded in `docs/agents/content-api.md`).
- **SH1112** — GET /agent/manifest?include=console answers the console's eager load from the build the instance serves, with the ceiling the build now ships beside it; raw matches the script exactly.
- **SH1137** — a cross-site folder move is refused on the shared writer, where the console reaches it too, with a teaching 409 naming both sites and `shio export`/`shio import` (design §LXXII.25 superseded: the supposition that the agent's folder.move shared the hole — it already refused it, and the refusal belonged on the shared writer instead)
- **SH1113** — `console:check` records requests, bytes and time-to-first-row per route family against `console-route-budget.json`, held as 43 measured ceilings with a sentence each — and the first run's own findings: a 404 route still makes 7 API calls, the post editor makes 23, and the GraphQL explorer reads 1.13 MB of schema before a keystroke (design §LXXII.19 superseded: its own first implementation, twice: counting every same-origin request re-measured the 1.73 MB eager bundle on every route, and probe.ok as the costing predicate moved the costed set across three runs)
- **SH1114** — the reachability walk is lifted to the repository root and reads all eleven manifests from one `PACKAGES` declaration checked against `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, with the two breaches only a consumer sees — a `dependencies` entry nothing npm packs imports, and a `devDependency` shipped code imports — asserted for each of the seven published packages (design §LXXII.20 superseded: its count of four published packages — private: true is what decides, and seven of the eleven lack it)
- **SH1116** — UNCANCELLED is empty: the history panel, the live preview and the content picker each abort the read they supersede and on unmount, and the history panel names a failed read instead of saying nothing was recorded (design §LXXII.21 recorded in `docs/agents/console-ui.md`).
- **SH1149** — all three read through `useQuery` with the signal it hands them, `isCancelled` guards each failure path, and the two effects keyed on an identity rather than a subject — `form.reset` and `service` — are gone, as is the email read's `catch(() => setConfig(EMPTY))` that made an unanswered server and an unconfigured tenant the same screen
- **SH1150** — the folder, site and post-type editors read through `useQuery` with the signal it hands them and report a failure they previously had no path for, the site editor's one effect became three queries because its site, locale policy and locale catalogue have three lifetimes, and the fourth entry was deleted rather than migrated — its effect was empty and the scan had counted it by seeing a write elsewhere in the file
- **SH1151** — the scan reads the effects and what they call one hop out rather than asking whether a file holds a `useEffect` and a service call anywhere — so a write in a click handler is no longer counted as an uncancelled read, a read hoisted into a `useCallback` still is, and eight declared entries that were never debts left the list — and the two tenant components share one pair of cached reads instead of each making both, which was four requests for two answers on every visit to the bento root
- **SH1152** — the note rail, the insights panel and the translations menu read through `useQuery` with the signal it hands them, the locale catalogue and one site's locale policy became shared hooks the site editor uses too, and each write now invalidates the scheme it changed rather than the key it was called from — the staleness a cache brings and an effect-shaped read could not have
- **SH1153** — the Content Select and File widgets resolve through `useQuery` with the signal it hands them, threaded into both requests each resolve makes, so a curator leaving a field no longer sees the missing-reference state the `alive` flag could not tell a cancellation from
- **SH1154** — both dialogs read through `useQuery` with the signal it hands them, the publish preview reads only while it is open so closing it is the reset its effect used to do, and splitting that effect's read from its reset retired the `set-state-in-effect` suppression it was holding — plus a second one on the insights panel that a prune found stale from SH1152, taken off both books
- **SH1155** — the agenda, the working line, the GraphQL explorer and the setup check read through `useQuery` with the signal it hands them — the agenda's fifty-page walk of `/agent/find` now stops at the page it is on — a second empty effect went the way of SH1150's, and the setup page's redirect stayed in an effect because navigating is a side effect and `react-compiler` refuses one during render
- **SH1156** — the post create form reads its post-type through `useQuery` keyed on the name rather than on a translation function, and reports the failure that used to leave a form with no fields; the visual editor's site read became the first in this task derived from a query rather than mirrored into state, and its entry stays on the declared list because seven of its reads did not move with it
- **SH1157** — the command palette's `queryToken` guard is gone — a query key ignores a superseded answer for free and the signal stops the server being asked for it — its debounce is a committed term so "searching" means the request rather than the keystroke, and the review queue's session list, the costliest read the task touched, takes the signal and stops rendering a failed read as an empty queue
- **SH1158** — the post editor's two rows are one `useQuery` with `Promise.allSettled` so `state` and the PUBLISHED row's existence stay one answer while the permission read stays a second query whose failure leaves the buttons as the server left them, the review queue's four `service.detail` call sites became one query owned by the row that renders the detail — cancelled when the row closes, re-read by invalidation, with a failure state the old `Record<string, detail | null>` could not carry — and the finding that SH1157 shipped its report rather than its behaviour: it deleted the `catch` that made an unreadable queue and an empty one the same screen and left `read.data ?? []` rendering the same `[]`, because its assertion matched the mechanism rather than what the page draws
- **SH1159** — the visual editor's last three fetching effects are queries — a `loadedLabelsRef`, a `catalogue.key` and a `loadedSections.key` were each a cache key written out by hand that ignored a superseded answer while the server was still asked for it — the field labels and declared fields stopped being state because nothing edits them, the catalogue became two queries since what a page accepts belongs to the page while the patterns pushed to an instance are the same answer for every page, the reorder still seeds the array it just sent with `setQueryData` under the key the echoed selection will carry, and the finding a level below the pages: `insertable`, `patterns` and `editable` each swallow a failure on purpose, so without rethrowing a cancellation past those fallbacks a curator navigating the frame gets an empty rail that never fills and an aborted DRAFT read fires a second request for the PUBLISHED row nobody is waiting for
- **SH1117** — `shio` sends `If-None-Match` to Shio's own API now, so a second identical read costs a 304 and no body — `src/read-cache.mjs` is a response cache **validated by an ETag** rather than a validator store, because `clone`'s 304 means "the file on disk is still right" and an API read has nowhere to keep the bytes, so validators alone would answer a cheap request with nothing to return and have to ask again — there is no TTL and nothing to invalidate since every hit is confirmed by the instance before it is used, which is also why a body that is not the body its digest names throws `ShReadCacheCorrupt` naming the file and `--no-read-cache` rather than quietly re-fetching, while an absent or out-of-format store is simply nothing known — the saving is counted rather than claimed (a store that stopped matching otherwise reads exactly like a server that never answers 304), the store is keyed by instance and address with a sorted query and bounded per instance oldest-first, and it is enabled once in `index.mjs` and flushed once on the way out whatever happened, because twenty commands build the client with the same four arguments and a fifth threaded through all of them is a flag half of them would spell differently; MCP is deliberately a separate answer
- **SH1126** — a Vite plugin emits `build-info.json` beside `index.html` — the commit, the build time and a digest of the sources the bundle was built from — and the size gate compares that digest with the tree it runs in, which is SH460's instance identity given to a console build; the digest is the comparison and the commit is for a person, because a commit cannot be compared against a working tree that is dirty most of the time anybody runs this while a digest over file contents matches a dirty tree exactly when the build came from it; `SOURCE_INPUTS` is `src` plus the entry, the chunking and the dependency names, with the limit stated rather than left to be discovered — an install that changes a vendor chunk without touching any of them leaves the digest matching, which is the right trade since the failure this closes was seen twice and both times it was a source edit; three ways to be "not measured" — no build, a build from before this existed, one from another tree — produce no total and differ only in the sentence, each naming what to do, because a number from a different tree is worse than no number; and since a stale build must not fail the suite locally, the other half is CI's `js` job building the console and setting `SHIO_REQUIRE_CONSOLE_BUILD=1` so "not measured" fails there, with `ci-gates.test.mjs` asserting both halves and their order — a build after the suite measures nothing and the two lines look equally correct in a diff
- **SH1136** — No console file suppresses set-state-in-effect or refs any more: each effect's state is derived, recorded per input or remounted, refs are written after commit, and the three helper exports moved to lib modules (design §LXXII.24 recorded in `docs/agents/console-ui.md`).
- **SH1140** — The fetch guard sees a service built in the call and one held under any name, and the login form it then found aborts both mount reads on unmount (design §LXXII.26 recorded in `docs/agents/console-ui.md`).
- 🗑 **SH1161** — superseded by SH1102: The six findings are code.renamed resolving Shio's prose against the vendored roadkeep's own modules, so the entries were never stale; SH1102 already tracks that cause.
- **SH1164** — The theme script is a data block now, so React's dev build stops reporting it and the dev-server console check fails only on real faults (design §LXXII.28 recorded in `docs/agents/console-ui.md`).
- **SH1166** — Both editors seed their form through useForm values, so no Controller updates during render, and a scan fails on the next render-phase form write (design §LXXII.29 recorded in `docs/agents/console-ui.md`).
- **SH1167** — The post editor reads its site's layout bindings first, so the live preview asks only for a type the site renders as a page and says why otherwise (design §LXXII.30 recorded in `docs/agents/console-ui.md`).
- **SH1168** — The user form starts from empty-string defaults and merges the loaded user over them, so no input is ever uncontrolled and a new field needs a default (design §LXXII.31 recorded in `docs/agents/console-ui.md`).
- **SH1169** — The explorer takes the shell's full column and fills what the header leaves, so it ends inside the window and the page no longer scrolls (design §LXXII.32 recorded in `docs/agents/console-ui.md`).
- **SH1170** — The console check records a request that never connected with its URL and error, and leaves out the reads the console cancels on purpose (design §LXXII.33 recorded in `docs/agents/console-ui.md`).
- **SH1171** — The route cost counts reads and not the held change streams, and gates only the jar: a dev-server run prints its findings as notes and exits clean (design §LXXII.34 recorded in `docs/agents/build.md`).
- **SH1172** — The route budget is re-seeded from a healthy jar, reads are counted by path, and a ceiling below the shell's floor is refused; a jar run reports no finding (design §LXXII.35 recorded in `docs/agents/build.md`).
- **SH1176** — The provisioner reads the change count where the apply puts it, so its log says how much a run wrote: changed=45 on a clean instance (design §LXXII.36 recorded in `docs/agents/blueprints.md`).
- **SH1053** — Every console page has one main, a skip link first and focus on the new page's title, held by a live probe; busy buttons keep focus and every spinner is heard (design §LXXII.11 recorded in `docs/agents/console-ui.md`).
- **SH1054** — Axe runs on every console route and at phone and tablet widths with zero serious findings, the document names its language, dark: follows the theme, and jsx-a11y lints (design §LXXII.12 recorded in `docs/agents/console-ui.md`).
- **SH1051** — Shio's accent clears 4.5:1 on both grounds, measured on every test run, and primary is claimed through its base inputs, so the rail marker and buttons carry the brand (design §LXXII.9 recorded in `docs/agents/console-ui.md`).

## Block BH — One content model, many languages

- **SH1056** — A site declares its languages on either door, the pack and the CDA report them, and the console edits the policy and offers only the declared languages as translations (design §LXXIII.1 recorded in `docs/agents/content-api.md`).
- **SH1123** — SH1056's delivery half: the site read carries the policy, and an undeclared site is described by the rows the token reads, so a production switcher never offers a draft-only language.
- **SH1059** — Each browser row keeps its locale as a chip beside the type, and the checkbox, title and actions all name the row with it, so a page and its translation are two different rows.
- **SH1057** — The public segment selects a page's translation and a declared site is addressed in its own tag; with SH1127 and SH1129 every delivery read and the client can ask for a locale (design §LXXIII.2 superseded: the furl-plus-locale finder it named cannot reach a translation at its own URL, so the segment selects through the translation group) (design §LXXIII.2 recorded in `docs/agents/renderer.md`).
- **SH1127** — SH1057's CDA half: the three listings and the client take a locale as a database predicate, so a pt-br page of fifty holds fifty pt-br posts and totalPosts counts them.
- **SH1129** — SH1057's GraphQL half: posts carry both fields and postByUrl and posts take locale; a page reads its groups in one query, 5 statements at 5 rows or 25 against 105 per row.
- **SH1058** — shio_read, the file projection and the console's languages menu each say a translation has fallen behind its source, and say nothing when it has not (design §LXXIII.3 superseded: translatedFrom would put a digest in a file with nothing to compare it against, so the projection carries translationStale, the fact a reader can act on) (design §LXXIII.3 recorded in `docs/agents/renderer.md`).
- **SH1060** — Coverage is a filter on every surface, a read per site, and a console board where a missing cell is the gesture that starts the translation (design §LXXIII.5 recorded in `docs/agents/content-api.md`).
- **SH1131** — SH1060's read half: GET /site/{id}/coverage answers a row per page and a cell per language — current, stale or missing with addresses — from two queries whatever the site holds.
- **SH1061** — The source sits beside the translation, and a field checked against it says so as a note an agent reads, with the panes stacking behind a toggle where there is no room for two (design §LXXIII.6 recorded in `docs/agents/console-ui.md`).
- **SH1062** — A curator asks the connected agent for a translation from a board cell, a whole row, a locale column or the translation workspace: each is a request note on the draft it names, the cell reads requested until the agent answers, and nothing is published by asking (design §LXXIII.7 superseded: a new translate note kind carrying the locale was unneeded, because the draft the request hangs on already carries its locale and translation group) (design §LXXIII.7 recorded in `docs/agents/mcp.md`).
- **SH1125** — the browser's locale chip marks the row whose language the site **declared** as its default, on the chip and in every accessible name a row gives — SH1059's design asked for it "where the site's enabled set exists" and it did not exist then, so once SH1056 gave the console `GET /api/v2/site/{id}/locales` a folder holding a page in English and in Portuguese still said which row was which and not which one came first, which is the question a curator deleting one of them is actually asking; `declared` is the whole rule and it is SH1056's distinction rather than a nicety — a site that chose nothing still reports a default, the locale its content happens to be written in, so `declaredDefaultLocale` marks nothing for an undeclared policy and the folder then says which language each row is and stays silent about which came first, which is the honest answer and the assertion worth having; the flag is computed once per listing from one `useSiteLocalePolicy(siteId)` cached under the key the query layer already uses for the site, rather than at each of the four places a label is built, and the word for "default" is passed into the pure `rowLabel` already translated because a hard-coded one would be an English word in a Portuguese console; the spreadsheet view's `getRowLabel` carries it too, since leaving the table as the one view without the mark is the half-migration this repository keeps finding — and SH1059's and SH1020's extractors were followed to the new signature rather than loosened, both having been regexes that would keep passing against a call that had lost the argument
- **SH1128** — a post's `availableLocales` comes from the rows in the states the reader reads — `PUBLISHED` for a production token, both for a preview token — which is SH1123's rule brought down a level: the group read asked for no state, and `translate` creates the sibling as a DRAFT, so the moment a curator started a Portuguese translation every production token's read of the English page said it exists in `pt-br` and a switcher built from that field linked to a page the same token gets a 404 for, for as long as the translation was being written; SH1129 had carried the old rule into GraphQL deliberately so the two surfaces agreed while this was open, and both move together now — by the **token** rather than by the request's `state=`, because the question the field answers is which of these a reader can follow a link to and the credential decides that, so a preview token looking at published rows still sees the draft translation it can fetch; and the single-post path reads through SH1129's batch instead of loading whole rows through `findByTranslationGroupId`, so there is one query carrying the state rule rather than two that agree until somebody changes one, with the single read getting cheaper on the way since the batch selects two columns where the finder loaded documents — driven from both surfaces, because they were two different queries before this and that is exactly how they could have diverged: a published English page with a draft-only `pt-br` sibling reports `["en"]` to production and `["en","pt-br"]` to preview, on REST and on GraphQL, and both assertions fail against the old rule
- **SH1130** — verify's content group warns locale-declared-unwritten for a declared locale no published content is written in, naming the language the fallback serves, and locale-undeclared-content for the mirror (design §LXXIII.10 recorded in `docs/agents/renderer.md`).

## Block BI — The areas this round did not reach

- **SH1063** — One routing table read answers whether what this instance publishes is findable, and it reaches a resource, the CLI, the console card and verify — with the per-page answer on the read an agent already makes (design §LXXIV.1 superseded: the last indexed instant is left out and declared as absent: nothing writes one, so reporting it is a column and a write per publish to argue for with a measurement) (design §LXXIV.1 recorded in `docs/agents/turing.md`).
- **SH1064** — A rename can keep its old address answering: `post.redirect` writes a published Redirect at the vacated path (302, `data.permanent:true` for a 301, refused where a page still answers), and a move's own report now hands over that op with the address filled in. `verify` gains `url-orphaned` — an error where `link-unresolved` is a warning, because the revision table proves the path was a page here and a published page still links to it — and clearing it is the op the finding names. `shio redirects` lists the table with the orphans under it and exits 1 on one; the console's publish dialog offers the redirect, ticked, exactly when an address stops answering, composing the same op rather than copying it (design §LXXIV.2 superseded: the console has no rename dialog to put the offer in — a post's URL is changed by post.move on the agent surface, and the console's only path to one is a rollback restoring an older revision's URL, so the count and the tick landed on SH996's publish dialog, which is where that case surfaces) (design §LXXIV.2 recorded in `docs/agents/agent-surface.md`).
- **SH1065** — `shio export site:<name> [--out]` resolves the address on the agent surface and streams the zip off the strictly id-keyed console route, so the export of an address-native product is reachable with an address. The manifest's `elsewhere` names both halves (`shio import <file> | shio export site:<name>`), the console's download now saves the server's own filename instead of composing a second one, and what a package carries — site, folders, posts in both states, their post-types, the site's notes — and what it does not — users, tokens, revisions, releases, other sites' notes, the bytes of uploaded files — is written down beside the endpoint, with promotion named as a release's job rather than a zip's (design §LXXIV.3 superseded: two of the three surfaces it asked for were already decided — the console has had a Download action on the site page since Block AR, so there was no button to add, and an MCP resource is refused for the reason SH268 refused an import tool: a resource carrying the bytes is the base64 megabyte, and one carrying a pointer is the manifest entry written twice) (design §LXXIV.3 recorded in `docs/agents/cli.md`).
- **SH1067** — `siteConversion` is declared and classified, so the census can now be asked whether an agent can replicate a site and has to answer. The answer is CLI-only with a falsifier, and it is not CLI-only all the way down: composing the document reads captured markup out of the file tree (SH268's boundary), while applying it is an ordinary `/agent/apply` write — so the manifest points at `shio convert --out <file>`, the seam where an MCP client finishes a replication with `shio_apply` and nothing new. An instance that grows a capture service flips the key and the row with it (design §LXXIV.5 superseded: the arc was not unclassified — `siteCapture` (SH377) and `conversionProposal` (SH379) have carried keys since they shipped, and the hole was the third act; and the reach it sketched (a resource plus a request the instance records) needs a worker on the server for the half the server must not do, so the census took the other branch the design allowed, an exception with a reason and a falsifier) (design §LXXIV.5 recorded in `docs/agents/replication.md`).
- **SH1068** — The docs gate now checks documented op names, MCP resource URIs and verify --checks groups against readers derived from source, and each reader must find a planted name or fail (design §LXXIV.6 recorded in `docs/agents/cli.md`).
- **SH1069** — Every manifest feature key has a row in vigletdocs COVERAGE.md naming its page, the unnamed-key ceiling is zero so a new key without one fails, and this round's ships are named and described on their pages (design §LXXIV.7 recorded in `docs/agents/docs-process.md`).
- **SH1066** — A Forms page on the rail lists a site's submissions through submission=true and edits the site's form destination, types, origins and switch; agents find the same rows with shio_find, and verify names a form whose folder is gone (design §LXXIV.4 superseded: per-row archive and mark-as-spam became one trash action, since a post has no archive state and SH970 had chosen trash, and the caption stays the post type's title and summary rather than a form setting) (design §LXXIV.4 recorded in `docs/agents/console-ui.md`).
- **SH1103** — A gate stamp carries a digest of the ledger and coverage mirror it ran against, so a ship after a green run leaves the stamp stale in both comparators.
- **SH1104** — /agent/editable and its insertable catalogue are budgeted separately, measured on a page that renders through a layout, with the fixture seeded after the other responses so no budget's baseline moved.
- **SH1121** — `landing`'s PageLayout wraps its section loop in `<main>` and makes the first section's heading an `<h1>` through the `@first` frame `getRelation` has published since SH772 — the same two rules `checks=a11y` named on `marketing-site`, which was repaired only because the headline benchmark happened to apply it while `landing` had no benchmark and so nothing reported it — and the half worth keeping is `ShBlueprintAccessibilityTest`, which reads its subjects out of the registry rather than naming three packages: every blueprint whose content declares a `PageLayout` is applied to a fresh site with the parameters its own manifest requires, and `verify(site, "a11y", 200)` has to report nothing, so a blueprint that gains a layout joins the test by existing and one that ships a broken layout fails the day it lands, while the three that carry their markup in `files/app/layout.tsx` are absent from the subjects because nothing in them declares a layout — which confirms by construction what §LXXIV.11 said was worth confirming; it spends a context slot deliberately (`DECLARED_CONTEXTS` 78→79, `maxSize` 81→82), the cheaper answer of sharing the sibling's database being refused by `ShBenchmarkIsolationLintTest` as the shared fixture wearing isolation's clothes
- **SH1122** — the pull half: `readRemoteFolders` asks for `sites` beside the `sitemap` it was already asking for — on the first page of each site's walk and no other, because the rows do not paginate and a settled pull's request count is guarded, which SH398 proved by catching the version that fetched the pack itself and went from twelve requests to thirteen — and `reconcileSiteSettings` merges the four settings **per key** under `reconcileNotes`' rule rather than `reconcileFolders`', which is the whole of it: a folder marker records that a folder exists, the server's fact, so the server wins and no conflict is possible, while every key of a site marker is something somebody chose, so a value the tree moved on its own survives a read and a key both sides moved is reported as `<site>#<key>` with the file left exactly as it was — copying the folder rule would have made a pull silently overwrite a url an agent had just authored; per key for `assetMeta`'s reason and written per file because a marker is one document, so a site with any conflicted key is left alone rather than half each side's; `content-base.json` grows a `sites` section merged over what it held, absent in an older snapshot reading as "never agreed about any setting", and §LXXIV.12's round trip is four tests of which the middle two are the ones that would have caught the wrong rule
- **SH1160** — the context pack's site row carries `furl`, `description` and `localePolicy` beside the url and the three locale fields it already had, which is what a `_site.md` needs and what SH1122 recorded as its blocker — the alternative being the console's whole-entity site read, which answers the 5 MB `postTypeLayout` column along with them, so reading four short strings that way is a P3 regression rather than a detail; `localePolicy` is the **stored** document rather than a reconstruction, because the three discovery fields each omit what says the ordinary thing (a default matching the instance's, a single-locale list) and carry no fallback chain at all, so a tree rebuilding a policy from them would write four of the marker's five keys and call it a round trip — it is built by `ShSiteLocales.toNode()`, which `toJson` now delegates to, so that document has one spelling rather than two that agree until a key moves; and the measurement is two numbers because the first says nothing: `response.context.json` did not move by a single token (all three are NON_NULL and the benchmark's site has none of them), so `measureConfiguredSiteRow` measures a site that HAS been configured, at 30 tokens against a new `response.context.site-row` ceiling of 40, on the JSON row and not the terse one — terse deliberately carries none of it, being the cheap form of the call that replaces a session, and a guard over that row would have been a guard over a row the change never touched
- **SH1133** — The CDA serves each site's redirect table and ShioClient.getRedirects reads it; create-shio-app's middleware answers a moved path with its 301 or 302; url-orphaned and shio redirects name the table a front end must read (design §LXXIV.13 recorded in `docs/agents/content-api.md`).
- **SH1134** — A site export writes each File post's bytes to files/<postId> and the import stores them under the post's new id, counting them in arrived.files and naming a listed file with no bytes as file-bytes-missing (design §LXXIV.14 superseded: it said the import already restored files/, and it restored nothing, so both halves were written) (design §LXXIV.14 recorded in `docs/agents/content-api.md`).
- **SH1135** — shio convert records each applied round as a site-scoped memory note naming the source, the counts, the plan's digest and the command that reruns it, and the console's site page shows it (design §LXXIV.15 recorded in `docs/agents/replication.md`).
- **SH1144** — The console check's provisioning applies marketing-site with mergePostTypes, so a clean instance's bootstrap Page gains the blueprint's fields and the site fills instead of being refused (design §LXXIV.16 recorded in `docs/agents/blueprints.md`).
- **SH1163** — A blueprint refused for fields an existing type lacks now answers blueprint-needs-merge, naming each type, its missing fields and the opt-in that adds them (design §LXXIV.17 superseded: its preferred fix, reseeding the vocabulary's Page, was measured out: nextjs-starter's Page differs again, so no one seed matches every package) (design §LXXIV.17 recorded in `docs/agents/blueprints.md`).
- **SH1173** — Preview and delivery prefixes spell the site as a path segment, and a link already in the preview carries editor=true, so the click-through keeps its bridge (design §LXXIV.18 recorded in `docs/agents/renderer.md`).
- **SH1174** — The drive hears the publish write and names its outcome, and matches the success it was shown twice; against the jar it publishes and all 72 probes pass (design §LXXIV.19 superseded: the silence was not a refusal: the publish succeeded, and a toast and the dock both said so) (design §LXXIV.19 recorded in `docs/agents/console-ui.md`).
- **SH1175** — Section fields declare their own type's widget and the bridge reads a plain field as text, so two editor saves leave ordinary spaces and no entity (design §LXXIV.20 recorded in `docs/agents/renderer.md`).
- **SH1177** — pnpm peers check runs on every pnpm test, and jsx-a11y's stale eslint range is the one named exception, which fails its own test once the plugin admits eslint 10 (design §LXXIV.21 recorded in `docs/agents/build.md`).
- **SH1102** — roadkeep lint exits clean in Shio with no baseline on 0.2.511, which fixed RK1707 and RK1708, and its workflow now runs on every push and pull request (design §LXXIV.8 recorded in `.github/workflows/roadkeep.yml`).
- **SH1181** — The Java build prints no deprecation warning: the ten deprecated calls use their Jackson 3, Testcontainers 2 and resources-plugin replacements, and a lint fails on any that comes back (design §LXXV.1 recorded in `docs/agents/build.md`).
- **SH1183** — The Java gate is green on a runner with no React build: a stub SPA shell on the test classpath, and an assertion that the shell resolves from it and not from a stale build (design §LXXV.2 recorded in `docs/agents/build.md`).
